project.name: git
project.description: Git, the distributed version control system (v2.56.1). This graph covers the C sources at the repository root plus builtin/, refs/, odb/, xdiff/ and reftable/. Shell, Perl, contrib, t/ and docs are excluded.

nodes.name: abspath.c
nodes.summary: Path helpers that turn relative paths into absolute ones and resolve symlinks by hand (strbuf_realpath with MAXSYMLINKS), plus prefix_filename for paths given relative to a subdirectory of the work tree.

nodes.name: is_directory
nodes.summary: Reports whether a path is a directory using stat(), deliberately following symlinks (not for tracked content).

nodes.name: strip_last_component
nodes.summary: Removes the final path component from a strbuf, used while walking up during '..' handling.

nodes.name: get_next_component
nodes.summary: Splits the next path component off the front of a 'remaining' strbuf into 'next'.

nodes.name: get_root_part
nodes.summary: Seeds the resolved path with the root (such as '/' or a drive prefix) of the remaining path.

nodes.name: strbuf_realpath_1
nodes.summary: Core component-by-component realpath loop that expands symlinks (bounded by MAXSYMLINKS) and tolerates missing trailing components when REALPATH_MANY_MISSING is set.

nodes.name: strbuf_realpath
nodes.summary: Public wrapper that resolves a path to its canonical absolute form in a strbuf, optionally dying on error.

nodes.name: strbuf_realpath_forgiving
nodes.summary: Variant of strbuf_realpath that allows any number of missing trailing components.

nodes.name: real_pathdup
nodes.summary: Returns a heap-allocated canonical path for a given path, or NULL (or die) on failure.

nodes.name: absolute_path
nodes.summary: Returns an absolute path built from the current working directory without resolving symlinks, in a static buffer.

nodes.name: absolute_pathdup
nodes.summary: Heap-allocated variant of absolute_path.

nodes.name: prefix_filename
nodes.summary: Joins a command-line prefix (the subdirectory git was run from) and an argument into a path relative to the repository work tree.

nodes.name: prefix_filename_except_for_dash
nodes.summary: Like prefix_filename but leaves a literal '-' (stdin/stdout) untouched.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_absolute_path
nodes.summary: Appends the absolute form of a path to a strbuf.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_real_path
nodes.summary: Appends the canonical real path of a path to a strbuf.

nodes.name: archive-tar.c
nodes.summary: Tar backend of git archive: writes ustar records in 10 KiB blocked output, emits pax extended headers for long paths or sizes and the global header holding the commit ID, and can pipe the stream through filters such as gzip (tar.gz).

nodes.name: do_write_blocked
nodes.summary: Buffers output into BLOCKSIZE blocks and flushes each full block to stdout, padding as the tar format requires.

nodes.name: write_trailer
nodes.summary: Writes the zero records that end a tar archive and pads the final block.

nodes.name: stream_blocked
nodes.summary: Streams a blob's contents from the object database into tar blocks without loading it all in memory.

nodes.name: strbuf_append_ext_header
nodes.summary: Appends one pax extended header record ('len key=value') to a strbuf.

nodes.name: ustar_header_chksum
nodes.summary: Computes and stores the ustar header checksum field.

nodes.name: get_path_prefix
nodes.summary: Splits a long path into the ustar prefix and name fields at a directory boundary.

nodes.name: prepare_header
nodes.summary: Fills a ustar header (mode, size, mtime, type) from a tree entry's mode and the archive arguments.

nodes.name: write_extended_header
nodes.summary: Writes a pax extended-header record block for entries whose metadata do not fit ustar fields.

nodes.name: write_tar_entry
nodes.summary: Writes one tree entry (file, symlink or directory) as tar records, reading blob contents from the object database and choosing extended headers when needed.

nodes.name: write_global_extended_header
nodes.summary: Writes the pax global header that stores the commit object ID of the archived tree.

nodes.name: tar_filter_config
nodes.summary: Parses tar.<format>.command and tar.<format>.remote config keys to register filter-based archivers.

nodes.name: git_tar_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for tar.umask and the tar.<format> settings.

nodes.name: write_tar_archive
nodes.summary: archiver callback that writes a full tar archive by walking the tree with write_archive_entries.

nodes.name: write_tar_filter_archive
nodes.summary: Runs the configured filter command (for example gzip) as a child process and feeds the tar stream through it.

nodes.name: init_tar_archiver
nodes.summary: Registers the 'tar' and 'tgz' archivers and the config-defined filter archivers with the archive registry.

nodes.name: archive-zip.c
nodes.summary: ZIP backend of git archive: writes local headers, optional streaming data descriptors, deflate or stored entries, the central directory and ZIP64 trailers, converting git file modes and commit time to ZIP/DOS metadata.

nodes.name: copy_le16
nodes.summary: Stores a 16-bit value little-endian into a header field.

nodes.name: copy_le32
nodes.summary: Stores a 32-bit value little-endian into a header field.

nodes.name: copy_le64
nodes.summary: Stores a 64-bit value little-endian into a header field.

nodes.name: write_zip_data_desc
nodes.summary: Writes the data descriptor that follows streamed entries, using the ZIP64 form when sizes exceed 32 bits.

nodes.name: has_only_ascii
nodes.summary: Checks whether a path consists only of ASCII bytes to decide whether to set the UTF-8 flag.

nodes.name: entry_is_binary
nodes.summary: Peeks at blob content to guess whether the entry should be flagged as binary rather than text.

nodes.name: write_zip_entry
nodes.summary: Writes one archive entry: builds the local header, deflates or stores the blob from the object database, records a central-directory entry and handles symlinks, directories and ZIP64 extras.

nodes.name: write_zip64_trailer
nodes.summary: Writes the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record and locator.

nodes.name: write_zip_trailer
nodes.summary: Writes the central directory end record, switching to ZIP64 when counts or offsets overflow.

nodes.name: dos_time
nodes.summary: Converts a git timestamp to the DOS date and time fields used in ZIP headers.

nodes.name: archive_zip_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for the zip archiver settings.

nodes.name: write_zip_archive
nodes.summary: archiver callback that writes a full ZIP archive by walking the tree and then the trailer.

nodes.name: init_zip_archiver
nodes.summary: Registers the 'zip' archiver in the archive registry.

nodes.name: zip_local_header
nodes.summary: On-disk layout of a ZIP local file header.

nodes.name: zip_dir_trailer
nodes.summary: On-disk layout of the ZIP end-of-central-directory record.

nodes.name: zip64_dir_trailer
nodes.summary: On-disk layout of the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record.

nodes.name: archive.c
nodes.summary: Format-independent core of git archive: parses command-line arguments, resolves a tree-ish to a tree, applies export-ignore and export-subst attributes and pathspecs, walks the tree to feed entries to the chosen archiver backend, and keeps the archiver registry.

nodes.name: register_archiver
nodes.summary: Adds an archiver backend (tar, zip, etc.) to the registry by name.

nodes.name: init_archivers
nodes.summary: Registers the built-in tar and zip archivers.

nodes.name: format_subst
nodes.summary: Expands $Format:...$ placeholders using pretty-format when export-subst is set on a blob.

nodes.name: write_archive_entry
nodes.summary: Callback for read_tree that reads a blob, applies export-subst and line-ending conversion, and passes it to the archiver's entry writer.

nodes.name: queue_directory
nodes.summary: Queues a directory entry so it can be written after its contents are known.

nodes.name: write_directory
nodes.summary: Flushes queued directory entries to the archiver in order.

nodes.name: queue_or_write_archive_entry
nodes.summary: Decides whether a tree entry is written immediately or queued, honoring export-ignore and pathspec matches.

nodes.name: write_archive_entries
nodes.summary: Walks the tree of the chosen commit with read_tree and writes every matching entry, including the extra files added with --add-file.

nodes.name: reject_entry
nodes.summary: Tree-walk callback that records which pathspec entries were matched.

nodes.name: reject_outside
nodes.summary: Checks that a pathspec argument does not lie outside the repository work tree.

nodes.name: path_exists
nodes.summary: Reports whether a path exists in the given tree, used to validate pathspecs.

nodes.name: parse_pathspec_arg
nodes.summary: Parses the trailing path arguments into a pathspec and validates them against the tree.

nodes.name: parse_treeish_arg
nodes.summary: Resolves the <tree-ish> argument (and --remote prefix) to a tree object and commit with their timestamps.

nodes.name: add_file_cb
nodes.summary: Option callback for --add-file and --add-virtual-file.

nodes.name: parse_archive_args
nodes.summary: Parses archive options such as --format, --prefix, --output, --worktree-attributes and compression level and selects the archiver.

nodes.name: write_archive
nodes.summary: Public entry point for git archive and upload-archive: parses arguments, resolves the tree-ish and pathspec and runs the selected archiver's write_archive callback.

nodes.name: match_extension
nodes.summary: Matches a filename's extension against a known format suffix.

nodes.name: archive.h
nodes.summary: Public API of the archive subsystem: archiver_args describing what to archive, the archiver backend struct with its write_archive callback and flags, and the per-entry callback type shared by the tar and zip backends.

nodes.name: attr.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of gitattributes: git_attr names, attr_check requests, git_check_attr and git_all_attrs lookups against the index or work tree, attribute direction, and the pattern and match_attr structures of parsed attribute lines.

nodes.name: annotate.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git annotate', a thin alias that builds an argument vector with '-c' and forwards it to cmd_blame.

nodes.name: cmd_annotate
nodes.summary: Prepends 'annotate -c' to the arguments, copies the vector (since cmd_blame modifies it) and calls cmd_blame.

nodes.name: apply.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git apply' entry point that initialises an apply_state, parses options, and delegates to the patch machinery in apply.c.

nodes.name: cmd_apply
nodes.summary: Sets up apply_state, falls back to the default hash algorithm outside a repository, parses options, checks state and calls apply_all_patches.

nodes.name: check-ref-format.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git check-ref-format' that validates a ref name against the ref naming rules and can normalise it or check a branch name.

nodes.name: check_ref_format_branch
nodes.summary: Checks that a name is a valid branch name and prints the short form.

nodes.name: cmd_check_ref_format
nodes.summary: Parses --normalize, --allow-onelevel and --refspec-pattern, then calls check_refname_format on the argument and prints the normalised name when asked.

nodes.name: fsmonitor--daemon.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git fsmonitor--daemon' (start, run, stop, status): a long-running per-repository daemon that listens to file system events and answers IPC queries about which paths changed since a token, so git status can skip scanning the work tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Most of the file is wrapped in HAVE_FSMONITOR_DAEMON_BACKEND; the #else branch only dies with 'not supported on this platform'. It uses pthreads: a listener thread, a health thread and an IPC thread pool.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for fsmonitor.ipcthreads, fsmonitor.starttimeout and fsmonitor.announcestartup.

nodes.name: do_as_client__send_stop
nodes.summary: Acts as an IPC client that asks a running daemon to quit and waits for it to go away.

nodes.name: do_as_client__status
nodes.summary: Acts as an IPC client that reports whether a daemon is listening for this repository.

nodes.name: with_lock__wait_for_cookie
nodes.summary: Creates a cookie file in the .git directory and waits until the listener thread sees its event, proving earlier file system events have been processed.

nodes.name: with_lock__mark_cookies_seen
nodes.summary: Marks cookies as seen when their events arrive from the listener.

nodes.name: with_lock__abort_all_cookies
nodes.summary: Wakes every waiting cookie with an abort result during shutdown.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_new_token_data
nodes.summary: Allocates a new token and the first batch that identifies a point in the stream of file system events.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_batch__new
nodes.summary: Allocates an empty batch of changed paths.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_batch__free_list
nodes.summary: Frees a linked list of batches.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_batch__add_path
nodes.summary: Adds a changed path to a batch.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_batch__combine
nodes.summary: Merges one batch's paths into another when older batches are collapsed.

nodes.name: with_lock__truncate_old_batches
nodes.summary: Drops or merges old batches so memory use stays bounded while keeping tokens answerable.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_free_token_data
nodes.summary: Frees a token and its batch list.

nodes.name: with_lock__do_force_resync
nodes.summary: Starts a new token epoch so clients must do a full scan.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_force_resync
nodes.summary: Takes the main lock and forces a resync, called when events may have been lost.

nodes.name: with_lock__format_response_token
nodes.summary: Formats a token string (daemon ID and sequence number) for a response.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_parse_client_token
nodes.summary: Parses the token sent by a client into a daemon ID and sequence number.

nodes.name: do_handle_client
nodes.summary: Serves one IPC request: validates the client token, waits for a cookie, then replies with the paths changed since that token or a trivial 'full scan' answer.

nodes.name: handle_client
nodes.summary: simple-ipc application callback that handles 'quit' and query messages from a client.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_classify_path_workdir_relative
nodes.summary: Classifies a work-tree-relative path as inside .git, inside the work tree, or outside.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_classify_path_gitdir_relative
nodes.summary: Classifies a path relative to the .git directory (cookie files and others).

nodes.name: fsmonitor_classify_path_absolute
nodes.summary: Classifies an absolute path from a file system event against the work tree and git dir.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_publish
nodes.summary: Publishes the batch of changed paths from the listener thread and starts a new token.

nodes.name: fsm_health__thread_proc
nodes.summary: Thread procedure for the health thread that watches the process and file system state.

nodes.name: fsm_listen__thread_proc
nodes.summary: Thread procedure that runs the platform file system listener.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_run_daemon_1
nodes.summary: Starts the IPC thread pool, the listener thread and the health thread, then waits for shutdown and joins them.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_run_daemon
nodes.summary: Initialises daemon state and the IPC path, runs the daemon and cleans up when it stops.

nodes.name: try_to_run_foreground_daemon
nodes.summary: Runs the daemon in the current process, optionally detaching the console.

nodes.name: bg_wait_cb
nodes.summary: Callback used while polling a spawned background daemon.

nodes.name: try_to_start_background_daemon
nodes.summary: Spawns 'fsmonitor--daemon run' as a detached child and waits until it is ready or times out.

nodes.name: cmd_fsmonitor__daemon
nodes.summary: Dispatches start, run, stop and status subcommands after loading config and verifying that the repository is compatible with fsmonitor.

nodes.name: mailinfo.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git mailinfo' that reads one e-mail message and splits it into commit metadata printed on stdout, a message body file and a patch file, as used by git am.

nodes.name: parse_opt_explicit_encoding
nodes.summary: Option callback for --encoding.

nodes.name: parse_opt_quoted_cr
nodes.summary: Option callback for --quoted-cr that selects how to handle CR before LF in quoted mail.

nodes.name: cmd_mailinfo
nodes.summary: Parses options, sets up a mailinfo structure and calls mailinfo() to separate message and patch.

nodes.name: mailsplit.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git mailsplit' that splits an mbox file or Maildir into numbered single-message files, the first step of git am.

nodes.name: is_from_line
nodes.summary: Recognises an mbox 'From ' separator line.

nodes.name: is_gtfrom
nodes.summary: Detects '>From ' quoting inside a message body.

nodes.name: split_one
nodes.summary: Copies one message from the input to a numbered output file.

nodes.name: populate_maildir_list
nodes.summary: Reads the cur and new directories of a Maildir into a sorted list.

nodes.name: maildir_filename_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares Maildir file names so messages split in delivery order.

nodes.name: split_maildir
nodes.summary: Splits each message of a Maildir into numbered files.

nodes.name: split_mbox
nodes.summary: Splits an mbox stream into numbered files, deciding where messages begin.

nodes.name: cmd_mailsplit
nodes.summary: Parses the output directory, numbering and mbox options and runs split_mbox or split_maildir over the inputs.

nodes.name: merge-recursive.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git merge-recursive' (and its merge-subtree variant) low-level merge driver that takes base commits, a head and a remote and runs the ort merge machinery.

nodes.name: cmd_merge_recursive
nodes.summary: Parses merge bases and the two heads from arguments, initialises merge_options and runs the merge, returning conflict status.

nodes.name: multi-pack-index.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git multi-pack-index' with subcommands write, compact, verify, expire and repack that manage the multi-pack index (MIDX) spanning several packfiles of an object directory.

nodes.name: parse_object_dir
nodes.summary: Option callback for --object-dir that resolves the object directory.

nodes.name: git_multi_pack_index_write_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for multi-pack-index settings such as bitmaps and preferred pack.

nodes.name: read_packs_from_stdin
nodes.summary: Reads the list of pack names from stdin for write --stdin-packs.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index_write
nodes.summary: Writes a multi-pack index (optionally with a reachability bitmap) for the object directory.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index_compact
nodes.summary: Compacts a range of MIDX layers into a single layer.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index_verify
nodes.summary: Verifies the multi-pack index against the packs it covers.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index_expire
nodes.summary: Removes packfiles that no longer contain any object referenced by the index.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index_repack
nodes.summary: Repacks small packs in the index into a new pack up to a batch size.

nodes.name: cmd_multi_pack_index
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the write, compact, verify, expire and repack subcommands.

nodes.name: show-index.c
nodes.summary: Builtin 'git show-index' that reads a packfile index (.idx) from stdin, version 1 or 2, and prints each object's offset, ID and CRC.

nodes.name: cmd_show_index
nodes.summary: Reads the idx header and fan-out table, then prints entries for version 1 or version 2 (with CRC32 and 64-bit offset table) layouts.

nodes.name: cbtree.c
nodes.summary: Crit-bit tree implementation that allocates nothing internally: lookup, insertion and prefix iteration over caller-owned nodes keyed by an arbitrary byte string, used for object ID prefix lookups.

nodes.name: cb_descend
nodes.summary: Recursively visits every leaf below an internal node, stopping when the callback returns non-zero.

nodes.name: cb_each
nodes.summary: Finds the subtree sharing a key prefix and iterates over all nodes in it with a callback.

nodes.name: cbtree.h
nodes.summary: Declarations for the crit-bit tree: cb_node, cb_tree with a key offset, inline cb_init, and the lookup, insert and each-with-prefix functions.

nodes.name: chunk-format.c
nodes.summary: Shared reader and writer for chunk-based file formats (used by the commit-graph and multi-pack-index): a table of contents of chunk IDs and offsets followed by chunk data, with helpers to pair chunks with in-memory pointers.

nodes.name: free_chunkfile
nodes.summary: Frees a chunkfile and its chunk table.

nodes.name: get_num_chunks
nodes.summary: Returns the number of chunks registered.

nodes.name: add_chunk
nodes.summary: Registers a chunk ID with its expected size and write callback.

nodes.name: write_chunkfile
nodes.summary: Writes the table of contents and then each chunk through the hashfile, checking that the written size matches the recorded one.

nodes.name: read_table_of_contents
nodes.summary: Parses and validates the chunk table of contents from a mapped file, rejecting malformed or out-of-range entries.

nodes.name: pair_chunk_fn
nodes.summary: Callback that stores a pointer to a chunk's data in a caller-provided slot.

nodes.name: pair_chunk
nodes.summary: Associates a chunk ID with a pointer to its data in the mapped file.

nodes.name: read_chunk
nodes.summary: Invokes a callback on a chunk's data by ID.

nodes.name: oid_version
nodes.summary: Maps the repository hash algorithm to its format version number.

nodes.name: chunk_info
nodes.summary: Table entry holding a chunk ID, expected size and write callback.

nodes.name: chunkfile
nodes.summary: State of a chunk file being written, holding the hashfile and chunk list.

nodes.name: color.c
nodes.summary: Terminal colour support: parses colour specifications from config (names, 256-colour, RGB and attributes like bold) into ANSI escape sequences, decides whether to colour output (auto, always, never, isatty, pager), and provides colour-aware printf wrappers.

nodes.name: get_hex_color
nodes.summary: Parses a #rrggbb colour specification.

nodes.name: parse_ansi_color
nodes.summary: Parses a basic or bright ANSI colour name.

nodes.name: parse_color
nodes.summary: Parses a single colour token such as 'red', '12' or '#ff0000'.

nodes.name: parse_attr
nodes.summary: Parses an attribute token such as bold, dim, ul or reverse.

nodes.name: color_parse_mem_1
nodes.summary: Core routine that turns a multi-word colour specification into an escape sequence.

nodes.name: color_parse_mem
nodes.summary: Parses a colour specification given as pointer and length.

nodes.name: color_parse
nodes.summary: Parses a colour config value into an escape sequence.

nodes.name: color_parse_quietly
nodes.summary: Parses a colour value without emitting an error.

nodes.name: git_config_colorbool
nodes.summary: Interprets always, never, auto and boolean forms of colour config values.

nodes.name: check_auto_color
nodes.summary: Checks whether stdout is a tty and TERM allows colour.

nodes.name: want_color_fd
nodes.summary: Decides whether to use colour for a given file descriptor, caching the result.

nodes.name: git_color_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for color.ui.

nodes.name: color_print_strbuf
nodes.summary: Writes a strbuf to a file with a colour prefix and reset suffix.

nodes.name: color_vfprintf
nodes.summary: va_list printf with colour start and reset around the formatted text.

nodes.name: color_fprintf
nodes.summary: printf-style output wrapped in a colour sequence.

nodes.name: color_fprintf_ln
nodes.summary: Like color_fprintf but appends a newline after the reset sequence.

nodes.name: color_is_nil
nodes.summary: Tests whether a colour string is the empty 'no colour' value.

nodes.name: color
nodes.summary: Parsed colour (unspecified, normal, ANSI, 256 or 24-bit RGB) used when building escape sequences.

nodes.name: common-exit.c
nodes.summary: Process-exit hook that git wraps around exit(): checks that no unreported bug() calls were left and emits the trace2 exit event.

nodes.name: check_bug_if_BUG
nodes.summary: Aborts with BUG() if bug() was called without a matching BUG_if_bug() before exit.

nodes.name: common_exit
nodes.summary: Masks the exit code to 8 bits, checks for pending bug() reports and records the trace2 command-exit event.

nodes.name: common-init.h
nodes.summary: One-line header declaring init_git(), the process-wide initialisation called before cmd_main.

nodes.name: common-main.c
nodes.summary: Real main() of every git program: runs init_git, calls the program-specific cmd_main and exits through the exit wrapper.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Initialises process state with init_git(argv), calls cmd_main(argc, argv) and exits with its result.

nodes.name: convert.c
nodes.summary: Content conversion between work tree and object database: CRLF/LF normalisation (text, eol, core.autocrlf), working-tree-encoding re-encoding, $Id$ ident expansion, clean/smudge filters (single command and long-running filter processes), and streaming filters.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses stream_filter_vtbl structs of function pointers (null, lf_to_crlf, cascade, ident) as a hand-written vtable for streaming conversion.

nodes.name: gather_stats
nodes.summary: Counts CR, LF, NUL and printable characters in a buffer to classify it.

nodes.name: convert_is_binary
nodes.summary: Decides if gathered stats look binary.

nodes.name: gather_convert_stats
nodes.summary: Returns a string describing a buffer's line-ending style.

nodes.name: output_eol
nodes.summary: Maps an eol setting to the line ending bytes to write.

nodes.name: check_global_conv_flags_eol
nodes.summary: Checks safe-CRLF round-trip flags when converting to git.

nodes.name: has_crlf_in_index
nodes.summary: Checks whether the indexed version of a path already contains CRLF.

nodes.name: validate_encoding
nodes.summary: Validates a buffer against a declared working-tree-encoding for round-trip safety.

nodes.name: check_roundtrip
nodes.summary: Tests whether an encoding is subject to the core.checkRoundtripEncoding list.

nodes.name: encode_to_git
nodes.summary: Re-encodes working-tree content to UTF-8 for storing in the object database.

nodes.name: encode_to_worktree
nodes.summary: Re-encodes UTF-8 content to the working-tree-encoding on checkout.

nodes.name: crlf_to_git
nodes.summary: Applies CRLF to LF conversion when adding content to git, with auto detection and safecrlf.

nodes.name: crlf_to_worktree
nodes.summary: Converts LF to CRLF on checkout.

nodes.name: filter_buffer_or_fd
nodes.summary: Runs an external filter command with the buffer or file descriptor as input.

nodes.name: apply_single_file_filter
nodes.summary: Applies a per-file clean or smudge command and captures its output.

nodes.name: handle_filter_error
nodes.summary: Interprets the status a long-running filter returns for a file.

nodes.name: apply_multi_file_filter
nodes.summary: Talks the long-running filter protocol over pkt-line to a persistent sub-process, with optional delay.

nodes.name: async_query_available_blobs
nodes.summary: Asks delayed filters which blobs are now ready during checkout.

nodes.name: apply_filter
nodes.summary: Chooses and runs a configured filter driver for a path.

nodes.name: read_convert_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads filter.<driver>.* settings.

nodes.name: ident_to_git
nodes.summary: Collapses $Id: ...$ back to $Id$.

nodes.name: ident_to_worktree
nodes.summary: Expands $Id$ to include the blob object ID.

nodes.name: convert_attrs
nodes.summary: Loads attributes of a path (text, eol, ident, filter, working-tree-encoding) into a conv_attrs.

nodes.name: reset_parsed_attributes
nodes.summary: Frees cached attribute check data.

nodes.name: would_convert_to_git_filter_fd
nodes.summary: Tells whether content would be changed when added from a file descriptor.

nodes.name: convert_to_git
nodes.summary: Entry point for converting a work-tree buffer to its stored form (filter, encoding, EOL, ident).

nodes.name: convert_to_git_filter_fd
nodes.summary: Same conversion applied to a file descriptor's content.

nodes.name: convert_to_working_tree_ca_internal
nodes.summary: Applies smudge, EOL, ident and encoding conversions for checkout.

nodes.name: async_convert_to_working_tree_ca
nodes.summary: Checkout conversion that allows a delayed filter.

nodes.name: convert_to_working_tree_ca
nodes.summary: Synchronous checkout conversion.

nodes.name: renormalize_buffer
nodes.summary: Converts content to git form then back, used by merge to renormalise.

nodes.name: lf_to_crlf_filter_fn
nodes.summary: Streaming LF to CRLF conversion filter.

nodes.name: cascade_filter_fn
nodes.summary: Chains two stream filters.

nodes.name: ident_filter_fn
nodes.summary: Streaming $Id$ expansion filter.

nodes.name: free_stream_filter
nodes.summary: Releases a stream filter chain.

nodes.name: stream_filter
nodes.summary: Feeds data through a streaming filter.

nodes.name: init_checkout_metadata
nodes.summary: Fills checkout metadata (ref, tree, commit) sent to filters.

nodes.name: clone_checkout_metadata
nodes.summary: Copies checkout metadata.

nodes.name: classify_conv_attrs
nodes.summary: Classifies conversion attributes into text, binary, or other for diff and blame decisions.

nodes.name: text_stat
nodes.summary: Counters used to classify a buffer as binary, CRLF or LF text.

nodes.name: convert_driver
nodes.summary: Configured clean/smudge filter driver with command, process and required flags.

nodes.name: cascade_filter
nodes.summary: Streaming filter that chains two filters.

nodes.name: ident_filter
nodes.summary: Streaming filter state for $Id$ expansion.

nodes.name: convert.h
nodes.summary: Public API for work-tree/object-database conversion: eol and autocrlf enums, conv_attrs, convert_to_git, convert_to_working_tree, delayed checkout, checkout metadata and stream filter interfaces.

nodes.name: ctype.c
nodes.summary: Defines the locale-independent sane_ctype table that classifies each ASCII byte (space, alpha, digit, glob and regex specials, pathspec magic, control, punctuation).

nodes.name: date.c
nodes.summary: Date and time handling for git: parses many human, ISO 8601, RFC 2822 and relative formats into timestamp and timezone offset, formats dates in modes (default, relative, iso, raw, human, strftime), and implements approxidate for fuzzy phrases like 'yesterday 5pm'.

nodes.name: tm_to_time_t
nodes.summary: mktime-like conversion from struct tm to time_t without normalising tm_wday or tm_yday.

nodes.name: gm_time_t
nodes.summary: Converts a timestamp with a timezone offset to a UTC-adjusted time_t.

nodes.name: local_time_tzoffset
nodes.summary: Computes the local timezone offset in minutes for a time_t.

nodes.name: local_tzoffset
nodes.summary: Local timezone offset for a git timestamp.

nodes.name: get_time
nodes.summary: Gets the current time, honouring GIT_TEST_DATE_NOW.

nodes.name: show_date_relative
nodes.summary: Formats the age of a timestamp as '3 days ago' style text.

nodes.name: date_mode_from_type
nodes.summary: Builds a date_mode from a simple type constant.

nodes.name: show_date_normal
nodes.summary: Formats the default git date style.

nodes.name: show_date
nodes.summary: Formats a timestamp and timezone according to a date_mode.

nodes.name: match_alpha
nodes.summary: Matches month, weekday, timezone and keyword words while parsing a date.

nodes.name: set_date
nodes.summary: Validates and sets year/month/day on a struct tm.

nodes.name: match_multi_number
nodes.summary: Parses numeric forms such as hh:mm:ss, mm/dd/yy and dd.mm.yy.

nodes.name: match_digit
nodes.summary: Parses an alphanumeric token starting with digits as a date, time or timestamp component.

nodes.name: match_tz
nodes.summary: Parses a timezone offset like +0200.

nodes.name: parse_date_basic
nodes.summary: Core date parser that fills a timestamp and offset from a string, or returns -1.

nodes.name: parse_expiry_date
nodes.summary: Parses expiry strings including 'never' and 'now'.

nodes.name: parse_date
nodes.summary: Parses a date and writes it back as an object-header 'timestamp offset' string.

nodes.name: parse_date_format
nodes.summary: Parses a --date= format name into a date_mode.

nodes.name: datestamp
nodes.summary: Writes the current time in git's raw date format.

nodes.name: approxidate_alpha
nodes.summary: Handles words such as yesterday, noon, tea, ago and weekday names in approxidate.

nodes.name: approxidate_digit
nodes.summary: Handles numeric tokens in approxidate.

nodes.name: approxidate_str
nodes.summary: Loops over tokens of a fuzzy date string, accumulating changes to a struct tm.

nodes.name: approxidate_careful
nodes.summary: Parses a date by strict rules first and falls back to approximate parsing, reporting errors.

nodes.name: decorate.c
nodes.summary: Open-addressing hash table that attaches an arbitrary pointer (a decoration) to an object, keyed by object ID hash, with growth at two thirds load.

nodes.name: hash_obj
nodes.summary: Hashes an object's ID into a bucket index.

nodes.name: insert_decoration
nodes.summary: Inserts or replaces a decoration using linear probing.

nodes.name: grow_decoration
nodes.summary: Reallocates the table at about 1.5 times the size and reinserts all entries.

nodes.name: add_decoration
nodes.summary: Adds or replaces the decoration for an object, growing the table as needed.

nodes.name: lookup_decoration
nodes.summary: Returns the decoration for an object or NULL.

nodes.name: clear_decoration
nodes.summary: Frees the table, optionally calling a callback on each decoration.

nodes.name: diff-delta.c
nodes.summary: Binary delta generation used for packfiles: indexes the source buffer with a Rabin-style rolling hash over 16-byte windows and emits copy and insert instructions to encode the target against it.

nodes.name: create_delta_index
nodes.summary: Builds the hash index of a source buffer: hashes each 16-byte block with Rabin polynomials into bucketed entries limited by HASH_LIMIT.

nodes.name: free_delta_index
nodes.summary: Frees a delta index.

nodes.name: sizeof_delta_index
nodes.summary: Returns the memory size of a delta index.

nodes.name: create_delta
nodes.summary: Matches the target buffer against the index and writes delta opcodes (copy from source and insert literal data), stopping if the delta would exceed max_size.

nodes.name: delta_index
nodes.summary: Hash index over a source buffer: bucket table of index_entry lists used to find matching blocks.

nodes.name: diffcore-break.c
nodes.summary: Diffcore transformation for -B: splits a modified file pair that changed too much into delete plus create so rename and copy detection can reuse the content, and merges them back when no match was found.

nodes.name: should_break
nodes.summary: Decides whether a filepair has been rewritten enough (by score and literal copy counts) to be broken.

nodes.name: diffcore_break
nodes.summary: Walks the diff queue and splits qualifying modifications into a deletion and creation pair.

nodes.name: merge_broken
nodes.summary: Merges a broken pair back into one modification when the halves are still adjacent.

nodes.name: diffcore_merge_broken
nodes.summary: Final pass that re-joins broken pairs that were not claimed by rename or copy detection.

nodes.name: diffcore-delta.c
nodes.summary: Estimates how much content was copied between two blobs by hashing line- or 64-byte chunks into a span hash and comparing counts, for similarity scoring in rename detection.

nodes.name: spanhash_cmp
nodes.summary: Orders span hash entries by hash value.

nodes.name: diffcore_count_changes
nodes.summary: Counts bytes copied and literal bytes added between source and destination, building and caching span hashes of each.

nodes.name: spanhash
nodes.summary: Single bucket of a span hash holding a hash value and its occurrence count.

nodes.name: spanhash_top
nodes.summary: Header of a span hash table with size and entries.

nodes.name: diffcore-order.c
nodes.summary: Implements the -O<orderfile> diff option: reads glob patterns from a file and reorders the diff queue so paths matching earlier patterns come first.

nodes.name: prepare_order
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the order file into an array of patterns.

nodes.name: match_order
nodes.summary: Finds the index of the first order pattern matching a path.

nodes.name: compare_objs_order
nodes.summary: qsort comparison using pattern index then original position.

nodes.name: order_objects
nodes.summary: Sorts objects by order file position.

nodes.name: diffcore_order
nodes.summary: Reorders the queued filepairs of the diff by the order file.

nodes.name: diffcore-rotate.c
nodes.summary: Implements --rotate-to and --skip-to for diff: rotates the diff queue so output begins at a given path, optionally dropping the paths before it.

nodes.name: diffcore_rotate
nodes.summary: Finds the target path in the diff queue and rebuilds the queue starting from it, appending or discarding the earlier entries.

nodes.name: fetch-negotiator.c
nodes.summary: Factory for fetch negotiators: picks the default (consecutive), skipping or noop negotiation algorithm from repository settings.

nodes.name: fetch_negotiator_init
nodes.summary: Chooses and initialises the negotiator implementation according to the fetch negotiation algorithm setting.

nodes.name: fetch_negotiator_init_noop
nodes.summary: Initialises a negotiator that never sends 'have' lines.

nodes.name: fetch-negotiator.h
nodes.summary: Interface of a fetch negotiator: a struct of callbacks (known_common, add_tip, next, ack, have_sent, release) used to decide which 'have' commits to send to the server.

nodes.name: add-interactive.c
nodes.summary: Implements the menu-driven `git add -i` interactive mode: it lists staged and unstaged changes from the index and worktree, lets the user pick files by number or unique prefix, and dispatches to status, update, revert, add-untracked, patch, diff and help commands.
nodes.languageNotes: C file that uses function-pointer command tables (command_t) and an item-list abstraction (prefix_item_list over string_list) to build a small text UI; many structs are file-local.

nodes.name: add-interactive.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the interactive add UI: declares struct add_i_state (repository plus interactive config) and the init/clear/run_add_i entry points used by git add and git checkout/commit.

nodes.name: advice.h
nodes.summary: Declares the advice subsystem: the enum advice_type of every hint Git can print, the advise/advise_if_enabled helpers that honour advice.* configuration, and canned messages for conflict resolution and sparse-checkout situations.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only declarations; the enum plus a matching advice_setting array in advice.c is the extension point for a new hint.

nodes.name: init_add_i_state
nodes.summary: Initialises an add_i_state for a repository and loads the interactive color and patch settings from config.

nodes.name: clear_add_i_state
nodes.summary: Releases the interactive state that init_add_i_state set up.

nodes.name: find_unique_prefixes
nodes.summary: Computes for every item in a prefix_item_list the shortest prefix that is unique among the items, so the user can select by typing a prefix.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Prints a numbered, optionally multi-column list of items with a header, marking which items are currently selected.

nodes.name: list_and_choose
nodes.summary: Core prompt loop of the interactive UI: shows the item list, reads the user's answer (numbers, ranges, prefixes, negation, help), and updates the selection flags.

nodes.name: collect_changes_cb
nodes.summary: Diff callback that records, for each changed path, its added/deleted line counts into a pathname map for either the staged or unstaged side.

nodes.name: get_modified_files
nodes.summary: Runs a diff of HEAD against the index and of the index against the worktree, merging both results into a sorted list of file_items with staged and unstaged summaries.

nodes.name: print_file_item
nodes.summary: Renders one file entry of the status list, showing staged and unstaged add/delete counts and the path with its unique prefix highlighted.

nodes.name: run_status
nodes.summary: The `status` command: refreshes the file list from get_modified_files and prints it.

nodes.name: run_update
nodes.summary: The `update` command: lets the user choose modified files and stages them by updating the index entries from the worktree.

nodes.name: revert_from_diff
nodes.summary: Diff callback used by `revert` that restores a path's index entry to the HEAD version, or removes it when it was newly added.

nodes.name: run_revert
nodes.summary: The `revert` command: lets the user pick staged files and resets their index entries back to HEAD, then writes the index under a lock.

nodes.name: get_untracked_files
nodes.summary: Scans the worktree with dir_struct for untracked, non-ignored files matching the pathspec and puts them into an item list.

nodes.name: run_add_untracked
nodes.summary: The `add untracked` command: lets the user choose untracked files and adds them to the index.

nodes.name: run_patch
nodes.summary: The `patch` command: lets the user choose files with changes and hands them to run_add_p for hunk-level staging.

nodes.name: run_diff
nodes.summary: The `diff` command: shows the staged diff (index against HEAD) for the files the user selects, using the revision machinery.

nodes.name: run_add_i
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git add -i`: builds the command table, refreshes and reads the index, shows status, then loops on the main menu dispatching the chosen command until the user quits.

nodes.name: prefix_item_list
nodes.summary: List of selectable items plus a sorted index used to match each by a unique prefix.

nodes.name: file_item
nodes.summary: One changed file in the interactive status list, holding its staged and unstaged add/delete counts.

nodes.name: command_item
nodes.summary: One menu command of git add -i, wrapping the function pointer that runs it.

nodes.name: apply.c
nodes.summary: Core of `git apply`: parses unified and git-style diffs (including renames, mode changes and binary patches) into patch/fragment structures, checks them against the worktree or index, applies hunks with fuzz and whitespace handling, optionally falls back to a three-way merge, and writes results or .rej files.
nodes.languageNotes: Large C file organised as a pipeline: parse_chunk builds a patch list, check_patch_list validates, apply_data/apply_fragments rewrite the image, write_out_results commits to disk. Uses a hash table of file names (fn_table) to track in-memory results across patches.

nodes.name: add.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git add`: updates the index from the worktree for the given pathspecs (add, update, remove, intent-to-add, renormalize, chmod), batches object writes in an odb transaction, and delegates to interactive/patch/edit modes.

nodes.name: check-ignore.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git check-ignore`: for each path (from argv or stdin) it consults the ignore rules (.gitignore, exclude files) via dir_struct and reports whether and by which pattern the path is ignored.

nodes.name: git_apply_config
nodes.summary: Reads apply.whitespace, apply.ignorewhitespace and merge-related config into the repository's config values.

nodes.name: parse_whitespace_option
nodes.summary: Parses a --whitespace value (nowarn, warn, error, fix, error-all) into the apply_state's ws_error_action.

nodes.name: init_apply_state
nodes.summary: Initialises an apply_state for a repository, setting defaults and loading apply config.

nodes.name: clear_apply_state
nodes.summary: Frees the lists and buffers owned by an apply_state.

nodes.name: check_apply_state
nodes.summary: Validates the combination of options in an apply_state (index vs cached vs three-way, reverse, check) and resolves defaults.

nodes.name: read_patch_file
nodes.summary: Reads the whole patch input from a file descriptor into a strbuf and ensures it is NUL terminated.

nodes.name: guess_p_value
nodes.summary: Guesses the -p strip level for a traditional patch by comparing the old/new names against the current directory.

nodes.name: has_epoch_timestamp
nodes.summary: Decides whether a traditional diff header's timestamp is the epoch, which marks a file as created or deleted.

nodes.name: parse_traditional_patch
nodes.summary: Parses the `---`/`+++` header lines of a traditional unified diff and fills in the old and new names and the creation/deletion flags.

nodes.name: gitdiff_verify_name
nodes.summary: Checks that the file name given on a git-style `diff --git` header matches the names on the rename/copy/---/+++ lines.

nodes.name: gitdiff_index
nodes.summary: Parses the `index <old>..<new> <mode>` line of a git diff header, recording the pre- and post-image object ids.

nodes.name: parse_git_diff_header
nodes.summary: Parses an extended git diff header block (rename, copy, mode, index, binary lines) by dispatching each line to a gitdiff_* handler; returns the header length.

nodes.name: recount_diff
nodes.summary: Recomputes a hunk's line counts by scanning its body, used for --recount and for hand-edited patches.

nodes.name: find_header
nodes.summary: Scans forward through patch text to find the next file header, deciding whether it is a git diff, traditional diff or garbage, and returns its offset.

nodes.name: record_ws_error
nodes.summary: Records a whitespace error found on an added line and prints it according to the whitespace policy.

nodes.name: parse_fragment
nodes.summary: Parses the body of one hunk, counting context, added and removed lines against the header and recording whitespace errors.

nodes.name: parse_single_patch
nodes.summary: Parses every hunk fragment that follows a file header into a patch's fragment list and computes line statistics.

nodes.name: parse_binary
nodes.summary: Parses a `GIT binary patch` section (base85 literal or delta) into forward and reverse binary fragments.

nodes.name: parse_chunk
nodes.summary: Parses one complete per-file chunk of the patch: finds its header, parses the git header, text hunks or binary data, and returns the bytes consumed.

nodes.name: reverse_patches
nodes.summary: Turns each parsed patch into its reverse, swapping names, modes, object ids and hunk directions for `git apply -R`.

nodes.name: show_stats
nodes.summary: Prints the --stat style diffstat line for one patch, scaling the add/delete bars.

nodes.name: match_fragment
nodes.summary: Checks whether a hunk's preimage matches the image at a candidate position, with optional whitespace-insensitive and fuzzy matching.

nodes.name: find_pos
nodes.summary: Searches the image forward and backward from the expected line for a position where a hunk matches, honouring the leading/trailing anchors.

nodes.name: update_image
nodes.summary: Replaces the matched lines of the image with the hunk's postimage and shifts the line bookkeeping.

nodes.name: apply_one_fragment
nodes.summary: Applies a single hunk to an in-memory image: builds pre/post images, applies whitespace fixes, finds its position and updates the image.

nodes.name: apply_binary_fragment
nodes.summary: Applies one binary fragment (literal or delta) to produce the new blob contents.

nodes.name: apply_binary
nodes.summary: Applies a binary patch: verifies the preimage object id from the index line, then applies the forward or reverse fragment.

nodes.name: apply_fragments
nodes.summary: Applies all fragments of a patch in order to the image, or applies the binary fragment for binary patches.

nodes.name: three_way_merge
nodes.summary: Merges the preimage, the current file and the patched result via ll_merge, resolving trivial cases first.

nodes.name: try_threeway
nodes.summary: Fallback for `git apply --3way`: rebuilds the preimage from the index line's blob, applies the patch to it, and three-way merges with the current file.

nodes.name: apply_data
nodes.summary: Applies a patch to the loaded preimage image, trying a plain apply first and then the three-way fallback if enabled.

nodes.name: check_preimage
nodes.summary: Verifies that the file a patch modifies exists (in index or worktree) with a matching mode, and loads its old content.

nodes.name: check_to_create
nodes.summary: Checks that a patch which creates a file does not collide with an existing worktree or index entry.

nodes.name: check_unsafe_path
nodes.summary: Rejects patch paths that are unsafe, such as ones escaping the repository or touching .git.

nodes.name: check_patch
nodes.summary: Runs all checks for one patch (preimage, destination, symlink traversal, mode) and applies its fragments, updating the in-memory file table.

nodes.name: check_patch_list
nodes.summary: Runs check_patch over every patch in the list and fails if any would not apply.

nodes.name: build_fake_ancestor
nodes.summary: Builds a temporary index from the `index` lines of the patch so that `git am --3way` can use a merge base made of pre-image blobs.

nodes.name: create_one_file
nodes.summary: Creates one file in the worktree with its new content, handling symlinks, gitlinks and file-versus-directory conflicts.

nodes.name: write_out_one_result
nodes.summary: Writes one patch's result: removes the old file, creates the new one, or updates in place, and updates the index when requested.

nodes.name: write_out_one_reject
nodes.summary: Writes the hunks that failed to apply into a `<path>.rej` file in unified diff format.

nodes.name: write_out_results
nodes.summary: Writes every patch's result, collecting rejects, and reports whether any hunk was rejected.

nodes.name: apply_patch
nodes.summary: Applies one patch input end to end: reads it, parses all chunks, checks them, updates the index under lock, and writes results.

nodes.name: apply_all_patches
nodes.summary: Public driver that applies every patch file named in argv (or stdin) and then prints stats and summaries.

nodes.name: apply_parse_options
nodes.summary: Defines and parses the command-line options of git apply into the apply_state.

nodes.name: chmod_pathspec
nodes.summary: Implements --chmod=+x/-x by changing the executable bit of every index entry matching the pathspec.

nodes.name: renormalize_tracked_files
nodes.summary: Implements --renormalize: re-adds tracked files so that line-ending and clean filters are applied again.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Refreshes index entries matching the pathspec and reports paths that do not exist or are ignored.

nodes.name: interactive_add
nodes.summary: Runs interactive staging: calls run_add_p for --patch, otherwise run_add_i for --interactive.

nodes.name: edit_patch
nodes.summary: Implements `git add --edit`: generates a diff of worktree changes, opens it in the editor, and applies the edited patch to the index with apply.

nodes.name: add_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads add.ignore-errors and add.interactive.* settings.

nodes.name: check_embedded_repo
nodes.summary: Warns, with advice, when a path being added is a nested git repository that would be added as a gitlink.

nodes.name: add_files
nodes.summary: Adds every file collected by the dir scan to the index, handling ignore errors and intent-to-add, inside an odb transaction.

nodes.name: add_resolved_files
nodes.summary: Adds files that are tracked or newly resolved through a diff-style scan, used for -u and -A.

nodes.name: cmd_add
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git add`: parses options, dispatches to interactive/edit modes, builds the pathspec, scans the worktree, adds or updates entries, and writes the locked index.

nodes.name: output_pattern
nodes.summary: Prints a path and, in verbose mode, the ignore pattern (source file, line, pattern) that matched it, in plain or NUL-terminated form.

nodes.name: check_ignore
nodes.summary: Checks each path against the ignore rules using last_matching_pattern on a dir_struct and prints the matches.

nodes.name: check_ignore_stdin_paths
nodes.summary: Reads paths from stdin line by line (NUL or newline terminated) and checks each one with check_ignore.

nodes.name: cmd_check_ignore
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git check-ignore`: validates option combinations, sets up the repository and ignore rules, and runs the check.

nodes.name: fragment
nodes.summary: One hunk of a patch: old/new line positions and counts, the hunk text, and flags for leading/trailing context.

nodes.name: image
nodes.summary: In-memory view of a file's content as an array of lines with hashes and flags, which hunks are applied against.

nodes.name: checkout--worker.c
nodes.summary: Hidden helper command `git checkout--worker` that runs as a child process of parallel checkout: it reads work items over pkt-line from the parent, writes the corresponding cache entries to the worktree, and reports the results back.

nodes.name: checkout-index.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command `git checkout-index`: copies files from the index to the working tree (or to temporary files), either named explicitly, listed on stdin, or all entries, with stage and force handling and optional parallel checkout.

nodes.name: checkout.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git checkout`, `git switch` and `git restore`: switching branches (two-way tree merge of HEAD, index and worktree through unpack_trees), creating or resetting branches, detaching HEAD, and restoring paths from the index or a tree-ish, with conflict, sparse-checkout and orphan handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Three porcelain commands share one checkout_opts struct and checkout_main(); switch_branches and checkout_paths are the two main paths (branch switch versus path restore).

nodes.name: packet_to_pc_item
nodes.summary: Decodes one pkt-line payload from the parent into a parallel_checkout_item, rebuilding the cache entry, conversion attributes and encoding.

nodes.name: report_result
nodes.summary: Sends a work item's result (status, errno, stat data) back to the parent over pkt-line.

nodes.name: worker_loop
nodes.summary: Main loop of the worker: reads items until a flush packet, writes each to the worktree with write_pc_item, and reports results.

nodes.name: cmd_checkout__worker
nodes.summary: Entry point of the hidden `checkout--worker` command: parses options and runs worker_loop.

nodes.name: write_tempfile_record
nodes.summary: Prints the temporary-file mapping records emitted by `checkout-index --temp`, in newline or NUL-terminated form.

nodes.name: checkout_file
nodes.summary: Checks out one named path from the index (all stages with --stage=all), with skip-worktree, sparse-directory and unmerged diagnostics.

nodes.name: checkout_all
nodes.summary: Checks out every entry of the index, queueing items for parallel checkout when it is enabled.

nodes.name: option_parse_stage
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --stage that accepts a stage number 1-3 or `all`.

nodes.name: cmd_checkout_index
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git checkout-index`: parses options, holds and refreshes the index, checks out named, stdin or all paths, then commits the lock.

nodes.name: post_checkout_hook
nodes.summary: Runs the post-checkout hook with the old and new commit ids and a flag saying whether it was a branch switch.

nodes.name: try_update_sparse_directory
nodes.summary: Updates a sparse-directory index entry to match the target tree without expanding the sparse index.

nodes.name: update_some
nodes.summary: tree-walk callback that copies matching blob entries from a tree into the index during `checkout <tree-ish> -- <paths>`.

nodes.name: checkout_stage
nodes.summary: Checks out one unmerged stage (ours or theirs) of a path from the index into the worktree.

nodes.name: checkout_merged
nodes.summary: Recreates the three-way merge result of a conflicted path (checkout --merge) by running ll_merge over stages 1-3 and writing the result.

nodes.name: mark_ce_for_checkout_overlay
nodes.summary: Marks index entries that match the pathspec for checkout in overlay mode, where files missing from the source are left alone.

nodes.name: mark_ce_for_checkout_no_overlay
nodes.summary: Marks entries for checkout in no-overlay mode (restore), where tracked files absent from the source tree are removed.

nodes.name: checkout_worktree
nodes.summary: Writes the marked index entries to the worktree, using parallel checkout when enabled, and updates the sparse-checkout and stat information.

nodes.name: checkout_paths
nodes.summary: Handles `checkout <tree-ish> -- <paths>` and `restore`: updates the index and/or worktree for matching paths, handling patch mode, unmerged entries and --merge/--ours/--theirs.

nodes.name: reset_tree
nodes.summary: Forces the index and worktree to a tree with a one-way unpack_trees (used for --force and --discard-changes).

nodes.name: merge_working_tree
nodes.summary: Performs the two-way merge of old HEAD tree, new branch tree, index and worktree through unpack_trees, then writes the locked index and shows local changes.

nodes.name: update_refs_for_switch
nodes.summary: After a switch, creates the new branch if requested, points HEAD at the new ref or detaches it, writes reflog entries, and reports tracking status.

nodes.name: suggest_reattach
nodes.summary: Lists commits that would become unreachable when leaving a detached HEAD, with advice on how to keep them.

nodes.name: orphaned_commit_warning
nodes.summary: Warns about commits that would be lost on leaving the old HEAD, using a revision walk over refs that excludes reachable commits.

nodes.name: switch_branches
nodes.summary: Main branch-switch routine: resolves old and new branch info, merges the working tree, updates refs and HEAD, and runs the post-checkout hook.

nodes.name: git_checkout_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for checkout.* (guess, workers, thresholds, defaultRemote) and the common diff and submodule options.

nodes.name: setup_new_branch_info_and_source_tree
nodes.summary: Resolves the starting point of a switch into a commit and tree, parsing the name as a revision.

nodes.name: parse_branchname_arg
nodes.summary: Disambiguates the argument list of `git checkout` into a branch, tree-ish and paths, including DWIM creation of a tracking branch from a unique remote branch.

nodes.name: die_if_some_operation_in_progress
nodes.summary: Aborts a branch switch with a clear message if a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect is in progress.

nodes.name: checkout_branch
nodes.summary: Validates a branch checkout request (flags, detached, unborn branch, branch in use elsewhere) and then calls switch_branches.

nodes.name: checkout_main
nodes.summary: Shared driver for checkout, switch and restore: parses the target, applies option rules and decides between checkout_paths and checkout_branch.

nodes.name: cmd_checkout
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git checkout`: sets up checkout_opts and parse-options, then calls checkout_main.

nodes.name: cmd_switch
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git switch`: its own option table (-c, -C, --orphan, --detach, --guess) layered on checkout_main.

nodes.name: cmd_restore
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git restore`: options for --source, --staged and --worktree layered on checkout_main in no-overlay mode.

nodes.name: checkout_opts
nodes.summary: All options shared by checkout, switch and restore: branch creation flags, patch mode, overlay, merge, sources and pathspec.

nodes.name: branch_info
nodes.summary: Describes a branch being left or entered: name, full refname, resolved commit and object id.

nodes.name: add-patch.c
nodes.summary: Implements the interactive hunk selector behind `git add -p`, `git stash -p`, `git reset -p`, `git checkout -p` and `git restore -p`: it runs a diff, splits it into per-file hunks, prompts the user to stage/discard/split/edit each hunk, and feeds the chosen hunks back to `git apply`.
nodes.languageNotes: Large state-machine style C file: one `struct add_p_state` is threaded through every helper, and per-mode behaviour is table-driven through `struct patch_mode` instances (add, stash, reset, checkout, worktree variants).

nodes.name: patch_mode
nodes.summary: Descriptor of one patch mode (apply and check arguments, diff command, prompt strings, help text); a static instance exists for each of add, stash, reset, checkout and worktree modes.

nodes.name: hunk_header
nodes.summary: Parsed numeric `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` hunk header, with offsets into the plain and colored text buffers.

nodes.name: hunk
nodes.summary: One hunk of a file diff: its text ranges, parsed header, number of ways it can be split, and the user decision (undecided, use, skip).

nodes.name: add_p_state
nodes.summary: Whole-session state of the interactive patch loop: repository, index, config, the plain and colored diff buffers, the per-file diff array and the selected patch mode.

nodes.name: interactive_config_init
nodes.summary: Reads interactive.*, color and diff settings from config and the command-line options into a `struct interactive_config`.

nodes.name: interactive_config_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the strings owned by an `interactive_config`.

nodes.name: parse_diff
nodes.summary: Runs the mode-specific `git diff` as a child process (plain and colored, optionally through the interactive diff filter) and parses the output into `file_diff` and `hunk` records.

nodes.name: merge_hunks
nodes.summary: Merges adjacent selected hunks into a single hunk, recomputing the combined header, so that they can be applied together.

nodes.name: reassemble_patch
nodes.summary: Concatenates the file diff header and all hunks marked for use into one patch text suitable for `git apply`.

nodes.name: split_hunk
nodes.summary: Splits a hunk with several change blocks separated by context lines into smaller hunks, rewriting their headers (and the colored copy).

nodes.name: edit_hunk_manually
nodes.summary: Opens the hunk in the user's editor, then re-reads the edited text as the replacement hunk.

nodes.name: recount_edited_hunk
nodes.summary: Recomputes the line counts of an edited hunk header so a hand-edited hunk still forms a valid unified diff.

nodes.name: edit_hunk_loop
nodes.summary: Loops over hand-editing a hunk until `git apply --check` accepts it or the user abandons the edit.

nodes.name: apply_for_checkout
nodes.summary: For checkout-style modes, verifies the patch applies to both index and worktree with `git apply --check` and then applies it, using child processes.

nodes.name: apply_patch
nodes.summary: Applies the accumulated selected hunks of a file by piping them to `git apply` with the mode's arguments.

nodes.name: display_hunks
nodes.summary: Prints a paged summary of hunk numbers with their decision marks and one-line summaries.

nodes.name: patch_update_file
nodes.summary: Main per-file prompt loop: renders each hunk, reads a key (y, n, q, a, d, j, k, g, /, s, e and so on), updates hunk decisions and navigates between hunks and files.

nodes.name: run_add_p_common
nodes.summary: Shared driver: parses the diff, walks every file through `patch_update_file`, applies deferred patches and reports when nothing changed or only binary files changed.

nodes.name: run_add_p
nodes.summary: Public entry point of the patch-mode UI: selects the `patch_mode` for the requested `add_p_mode`, sets up state from the repository index and runs the interactive loop.

nodes.name: run_add_p_index
nodes.summary: Variant of `run_add_p` that works on a caller-provided index and index file, always in staging mode.

nodes.name: add-patch.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the interactive patch UI: option and config structs, the add_p_mode and flag enums, and the run_add_p entry points used by add, stash, reset, checkout and the interactive add.

nodes.name: interactive_options
nodes.summary: Command-line overrides for diff context, inter-hunk context and auto-advance, with an INIT macro of -1 defaults.

nodes.name: interactive_config
nodes.summary: Resolved interactive configuration: colors for header, help, prompt and diff lines, single-key mode, diff filter and algorithm, context sizes.

nodes.name: add_p_mode
nodes.summary: Enum of patch modes: ADD_P_ADD, ADD_P_STASH, ADD_P_RESET, ADD_P_CHECKOUT, ADD_P_WORKTREE.

nodes.name: advice.c
nodes.summary: Implements the "hint:" advice system: a table of advice.* config keys, color settings, and helpers that print multi-line hints and canned messages for conflicts, detached HEAD, sparse paths and other situations.

nodes.name: vadvise
nodes.summary: Formats an advice message and prints each line to stderr prefixed with a colored "hint:", optionally appending instructions for turning the advice off.

nodes.name: advise
nodes.summary: Prints an unconditional hint message to stderr.

nodes.name: advice_enabled
nodes.summary: Tells whether an advice type is enabled by advice.* config and the global GIT_ADVICE environment switch.

nodes.name: advise_if_enabled
nodes.summary: Prints a hint only when its advice type is enabled, adding the "turn off with advice.<key>" footer when the user has not set it explicitly.

nodes.name: git_default_advice_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that parses color.advice, color.advice.hint and each advice.<name> boolean into the advice settings table.

nodes.name: list_config_advices
nodes.summary: Adds every known advice.* config key to a string list for command-line completion.

nodes.name: error_resolve_conflict
nodes.summary: Reports that an operation (commit, merge, pull, rebase, ...) cannot proceed because of unmerged files, with advice on how to resolve.

nodes.name: die_resolve_conflict
nodes.summary: Calls error_resolve_conflict and then exits.

nodes.name: die_conclude_merge
nodes.summary: Dies telling the user to conclude an in-progress merge with `git commit` first.

nodes.name: die_ff_impossible
nodes.summary: Dies with advice when a fast-forward-only operation is impossible.

nodes.name: advise_on_updating_sparse_paths
nodes.summary: Lists pathspecs that matched paths outside the sparse-checkout definition and suggests --sparse or changing sparsity rules.

nodes.name: detach_advice
nodes.summary: Prints the long "detached HEAD" explanation shown after checking out a non-branch commit.

nodes.name: advise_on_moving_dirty_path
nodes.summary: Advises about paths that were moved but still have local changes in the worktree.

nodes.name: alias.c
nodes.summary: Resolves command aliases from the `alias.*` configuration (both `alias.name` and `[alias "name"] command` forms), lists them, and provides shell-like splitting and quoting of an alias command line into argv.

nodes.name: config_alias_data
nodes.summary: Callback data for the alias config walk: the alias being looked up, the found value, and the accumulated list when listing.

nodes.name: config_alias_cb
nodes.summary: Config callback that recognizes both alias syntaxes, matches case-insensitively or exactly, and stores or lists the alias value.

nodes.name: alias_lookup
nodes.summary: Reads early config and returns the command string defined for an alias name, or NULL.

nodes.name: list_aliases
nodes.summary: Collects all configured alias names into a string list (used by help and completion).

nodes.name: quote_cmdline
nodes.summary: Builds a single shell-style quoted command line out of an argv array.

nodes.name: split_cmdline
nodes.summary: Splits an alias command line into argv in place, honoring single and double quotes and backslash escapes; reports an errno-style code on unbalanced quotes.

nodes.name: split_cmdline_strerror
nodes.summary: Translates a split_cmdline error code into a message.

nodes.name: alias.h
nodes.summary: Declares alias lookup, alias listing, and the command-line quoting and splitting helpers.

nodes.name: apply.h
nodes.summary: Public API of the patch-application engine behind `git apply` and `git am`: the apply_state option block, the per-file struct patch, and the entry points that parse options, parse git diff headers and apply patches to the worktree and index.

nodes.name: apply_ws_error_action
nodes.summary: Enum selecting how whitespace errors are handled: ignore, warn, die or correct.

nodes.name: apply_state
nodes.summary: All options and runtime state of a patch application: index and cached mode, check and reject flags, three-way fallback, whitespace handling, lock file, strip level and the list of parsed patches.

nodes.name: patch
nodes.summary: One file-level patch parsed from a diff: old and new names and modes, creation/deletion/rename flags, the linked list of fragments (hunks), the result buffer and three-way stage ids.

nodes.name: release_patch
nodes.summary: Declaration: free a struct patch and its fragments.

nodes.name: bisect.c
nodes.summary: Core of `git bisect`: computes the commit that best halves the remaining candidate range in the commit DAG (weights, distances, skip handling), checks good/bad ancestry, checks out the next revision, reads bisect state from refs/bisect and the BISECT_* files, and cleans the state up.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a commit-slab for per-commit weights and temporarily reuses object flag bits (COUNTED, TREESAME, UNINTERESTING) while walking the commit DAG.

nodes.name: commit_dist
nodes.summary: Pair of a commit and its distance from the midpoint, used to sort bisection candidates.

nodes.name: count_distance
nodes.summary: Counts tree-changing commits reachable from an entry by walking first parents and recursing into merge parents, marking visited commits COUNTED.

nodes.name: count_interesting_parents
nodes.summary: Counts parents that are not UNINTERESTING (only the first when first-parent bisection is on).

nodes.name: approx_halfway
nodes.summary: Decides whether a commit's weight is close enough to half of the candidates to stop searching early.

nodes.name: best_bisection
nodes.summary: Picks the candidate whose reach is closest to half of all tree-changing commits.

nodes.name: best_bisection_sorted
nodes.summary: Builds a distance-sorted list of candidates (used when skipped commits require alternates) and decorates them with their distance.

nodes.name: do_find_bisection
nodes.summary: Computes the weight (number of reachable candidates) of every commit in topological order, resolving merges with count_distance, and returns the best midpoint.

nodes.name: find_bisection
nodes.summary: Public bisection routine: reverses the revision list, drops UNINTERESTING commits, and returns the commit (or sorted list) that best splits the range along with its reach and the total count.

nodes.name: register_ref
nodes.summary: Callback for refs/bisect/* that records bad, good and skip revisions into global state.

nodes.name: read_bisect_refs
nodes.summary: Iterates over refs/bisect/ to load the current bad commit and the good and skipped sets.

nodes.name: filter_skipped
nodes.summary: Removes commits listed as skipped from the candidate list, remembering which were tried; optionally keeps them when show_all is set.

nodes.name: managed_skipped
nodes.summary: Applies filter_skipped to the candidate list when any commits were marked skip.

nodes.name: bisect_rev_setup
nodes.summary: Builds the rev-list arguments (bad revision positive, good revisions negative) and sets up a rev_info for the bisection walk.

nodes.name: bisect_common
nodes.summary: Prepares the revision walk and marks tree edges uninteresting.

nodes.name: error_if_skipped_commits
nodes.summary: Reports the list of skipped commits when nothing but skipped commits remain to be tested.

nodes.name: bisect_checkout
nodes.summary: Records the chosen revision in BISECT_EXPECTED_REV, then either updates BISECT_HEAD (no-checkout) or runs `git checkout`, and prints the commit subject.

nodes.name: handle_bad_merge_base
nodes.summary: Explains the case where the merge base is the bad commit (a good revision is not an ancestor of bad) and exits with an error.

nodes.name: check_merge_bases
nodes.summary: Computes merge bases between bad and good commits and reports problems such as a skipped or bad merge base.

nodes.name: check_good_are_ancestors_of_bad
nodes.summary: Verifies, and caches in BISECT_ANCESTORS_OK, that all good revisions are ancestors of the bad one; otherwise handles merge-base checks.

nodes.name: show_commit
nodes.summary: Prints the found first bad commit using a diff-tree style log output.

nodes.name: read_bisect_terms
nodes.summary: Reads custom bad/good terms from BISECT_TERMS, defaulting to "bad" and "good".

nodes.name: bisect_next_all
nodes.summary: Main bisect step: loads bisect state, validates ancestry, runs the bisection walk, announces remaining steps or the first bad commit, and checks out the next test commit.

nodes.name: estimate_bisect_steps
nodes.summary: Estimates the number of remaining bisection steps from the candidate count (roughly log2).

nodes.name: bisect_clean_state
nodes.summary: Deletes refs/bisect/*, BISECT_HEAD, BISECT_EXPECTED_REV and all BISECT_* state files so a bisect session ends cleanly.

nodes.name: bisect.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the bisection engine: result codes, the find_bisection and filter_skipped helpers used by rev-list --bisect, and the state, checkout and cleanup functions used by the bisect builtin.

nodes.name: bisect_error
nodes.summary: Enum of bisect result codes (OK, FAILED, only skipped left, merge-base check, no testable commit, and the internal success codes).

nodes.name: bisect_state
nodes.summary: Counters of good and bad revisions found in the bisect state.

nodes.name: blame.c
nodes.summary: Engine of `git blame`: maintains a scoreboard of line ranges ("blame entries") attributed to suspect commits, walks history, diffs each commit against its parents to pass blame upward, detects moved and copied lines with line fingerprints, honors ignore-revs, and uses commit-graph Bloom filters to skip commits that did not touch the path.
nodes.languageNotes: Blame entries are singly linked lists of line ranges that are split, sorted and coalesced; `blame_origin` objects are reference-counted and kept per commit in a commit-slab.

nodes.name: blame_bloom_data
nodes.summary: Per-blame Bloom filter query data: the filter settings and the Bloom keys derived from the path being blamed.

nodes.name: fingerprint
nodes.summary: Multiset of character-pair counts for one line, used to estimate similarity between lines of different commits.

nodes.name: blame_line_tracker
nodes.summary: Tracks a source line number and its mapped parent line during ignore-diff processing.

nodes.name: blame_chunk_cb_data
nodes.summary: Callback context passed while walking diff hunks for one parent.

nodes.name: blame_list
nodes.summary: Array element pairing a blame entry with a split destination during copy and move detection.

nodes.name: get_blame_suspects
nodes.summary: Returns the list of blame_origin suspects attached to a commit via the commit slab.

nodes.name: blame_origin_decref
nodes.summary: Drops a reference to a blame_origin and frees its blob, fingerprints and links when the count reaches zero.

nodes.name: make_origin
nodes.summary: Allocates a blame_origin for (commit, path) and links it into the commit's suspect list.

nodes.name: get_origin
nodes.summary: Finds or creates the blame_origin of a commit for a given path.

nodes.name: fake_working_tree_commit
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic commit representing the working tree (or --contents file) so uncommitted lines can be blamed.

nodes.name: find_line_starts
nodes.summary: Scans a buffer and returns the array of line start offsets.

nodes.name: get_line_fingerprints
nodes.summary: Computes fingerprints for a range of lines.

nodes.name: fingerprint_similarity
nodes.summary: Returns the similarity score between two line fingerprints.

nodes.name: find_best_line_matches
nodes.summary: Computes the best matching lines between the parent and target version for fuzzy ignore-rev handling.

nodes.name: fuzzy_find_matching_lines_recurse
nodes.summary: Recursively matches lines in ignored changes by fingerprint to map them back to the parent.

nodes.name: fill_origin_blob
nodes.summary: Loads the blob of the file at the origin commit into memory (through the object database and text conversion).

nodes.name: blame_sort_final
nodes.summary: Sorts the final blame entries by line number.

nodes.name: blame_coalesce
nodes.summary: Merges adjacent blame entries with the same suspect and consecutive lines.

nodes.name: queue_blames
nodes.summary: Adds a suspect's new entries to its commit and pushes the commit on the scoreboard priority queue.

nodes.name: maybe_changed_path
nodes.summary: Uses the commit-graph Bloom filter of a commit to rule out commits that cannot have touched the blamed path.

nodes.name: add_bloom_key
nodes.summary: Hashes a path into a Bloom key and appends it to the blame Bloom data.

nodes.name: find_origin
nodes.summary: Finds the origin of the file in a parent commit by diffing the parent tree against its own and reading the blob id of the same path.

nodes.name: find_rename
nodes.summary: Detects whether the file was renamed in the parent by running diff with rename detection and returns the origin at the old name.

nodes.name: split_overlap
nodes.summary: Splits a blame entry around the portion of lines taken by a split range.

nodes.name: split_blame
nodes.summary: Divides an entry among split parts, distributing the pieces to their blamed parents.

nodes.name: guess_line_blames
nodes.summary: For ignored commits, guesses which parent line each target line came from.

nodes.name: ignore_blame_entry
nodes.summary: Handles a blame entry changed by an ignored revision, passing blame to the parent by line or fingerprint.

nodes.name: blame_chunk
nodes.summary: Processes one diff chunk: splits entries that overlap it, passing unchanged parts to the parent and keeping changed parts with the target.

nodes.name: pass_blame_to_parent
nodes.summary: Diffs a target origin against its parent and runs blame_chunk on each hunk to move blame to the parent.

nodes.name: blame_entry_score
nodes.summary: Scores how many alphanumeric characters an entry has, used to decide whether a move or copy is significant.

nodes.name: find_copy_in_blob
nodes.summary: Looks for lines of an entry inside another file blob to detect copied lines (-C).

nodes.name: find_move_in_parent
nodes.summary: Detects lines moved within the same file between target and parent (-M).

nodes.name: find_copy_in_parent
nodes.summary: Searches other files changed in the parent commit for copied code (-C, -C -C).

nodes.name: pass_whole_blame
nodes.summary: Hands all remaining entries to the parent when the blob is identical.

nodes.name: distribute_blame
nodes.summary: Sorts newly blamed entries by suspect and queues them to the respective parent commits.

nodes.name: pass_blame
nodes.summary: Core step per commit: for each parent finds the origin, diffs, passes blame upward, then applies move and copy detection to what remains.

nodes.name: assign_blame
nodes.summary: Main blame loop: pops commits from the priority queue and calls pass_blame until all lines are attributed; commits left with lines become "guilty".

nodes.name: init_scoreboard
nodes.summary: Zero-initializes a blame scoreboard.

nodes.name: setup_scoreboard
nodes.summary: Resolves the final commit (or reverse initial commit), reads the file contents, builds the line index and the first blame entry for the whole file.

nodes.name: setup_blame_bloom_data
nodes.summary: Allocates Bloom filter settings and keys for the path so commits can be pre-filtered.

nodes.name: cleanup_scoreboard
nodes.summary: Frees the scoreboard buffers, entries and Bloom data.
