nodes.name: blame_entry_prepend
nodes.summary: Allocates a new blame entry for a range and prepends it to a list.

nodes.name: blame_nth_line
nodes.summary: Returns a pointer to line n in the scoreboard's final buffer.

nodes.name: blame.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the blame engine: the blame_origin (a file version at a commit), blame_entry (a line range attributed to a suspect) and blame_scoreboard structs, plus the functions that set up, run and clean up a blame computation.

nodes.name: blame_origin
nodes.summary: A particular version of the blamed file at a commit: reference count, commit, blob id and contents, line fingerprints and the list of entries still suspected on it.

nodes.name: blame_entry
nodes.summary: A run of lines (source and result line numbers, count) currently attributed to a suspect origin, linked in a list.

nodes.name: blame_scoreboard
nodes.summary: Whole blame state: final commit and buffer, revision walk, priority queue of commits, entries, ignore list, move/copy scores, debug counters and Bloom data.

nodes.name: blame_origin_incref
nodes.summary: Inline helper that increments the reference count of a blame_origin.

nodes.name: bloom.c
nodes.summary: Implements changed-path Bloom filters for the commit-graph: seeded murmur3 hashing (v1 and v2), loading filters from the commit-graph chunks, computing one by diffing a commit with its first parent, upgrading old-version filters, and membership tests for a path.
nodes.languageNotes: Filters are cached per commit in a commit-slab; hash version 1 had a sign-extension bug for bytes with the high bit set, so v2 is a corrected murmur3 and filters containing high-bit paths cannot be upgraded.

nodes.name: pathmap_hash_entry
nodes.summary: Hashmap entry holding a changed path string while deduplicating paths and their leading directories for a filter.

nodes.name: check_bloom_offset
nodes.summary: Validates that a Bloom index offset lies inside the commit-graph Bloom data chunk.

nodes.name: load_bloom_filter_from_graph
nodes.summary: Fills a bloom_filter from the commit-graph chunks (indexes and data) for the commit at a graph position.

nodes.name: murmur3_seeded_v2
nodes.summary: Correct implementation of seeded 32-bit murmur3 hashing used for Bloom keys.

nodes.name: murmur3_seeded_v1
nodes.summary: Legacy murmur3 variant with the signed-char bug kept for reading version-1 filters.

nodes.name: bloom_key_fill
nodes.summary: Computes the k hash positions of a path and stores them in a bloom_key.

nodes.name: bloom_key_clear
nodes.summary: Frees a bloom_key.

nodes.name: add_key_to_filter
nodes.summary: Sets the bits of a key in a filter, using modulo of the filter bit length.

nodes.name: init_bloom_filters
nodes.summary: Initializes the per-commit Bloom filter slab.

nodes.name: deinit_bloom_filters
nodes.summary: Frees the filter slab and each filter's data.

nodes.name: bloom_keyvec_new
nodes.summary: Builds a vector of keys for a path and each of its leading directories.

nodes.name: bloom_keyvec_free
nodes.summary: Frees a bloom_keyvec and its keys.

nodes.name: init_truncated_large_filter
nodes.summary: Marks a filter as "too large" (a single all-ones word) when a commit changes more paths than the limit.

nodes.name: has_entries_with_high_bit
nodes.summary: Checks if a tree contains paths with bytes above 0x7f, which the v1 hash handled incorrectly.

nodes.name: commit_tree_has_high_bit_paths
nodes.summary: Applies has_entries_with_high_bit to the tree of a commit.

nodes.name: upgrade_filter
nodes.summary: Rehashes an old-version filter into the new hash version when the data allows it.

nodes.name: get_bloom_filter
nodes.summary: Returns the cached or graph-loaded filter of a commit if its hash version matches the configured one.

nodes.name: get_or_compute_bloom_filter
nodes.summary: Returns the commit's Bloom filter from the slab or commit-graph; if allowed, computes it by diffing against the first parent, adding changed paths and their directories, with truncation for large changes.

nodes.name: bloom_filter_contains
nodes.summary: Tests whether all hash positions of a key are set in a filter ("maybe present") or not ("definitely absent").

nodes.name: bloom_filter_contains_vec
nodes.summary: Tests a vector of keys, returning true only when every key may be present.

nodes.name: test_bloom_murmur3_seeded
nodes.summary: Test hook exposing the murmur3 hash for the unit tests.

nodes.name: bloom.h
nodes.summary: Interface of the changed-path Bloom filter code: filter settings, filter and key structs, and functions to fill keys, load or compute a commit's filter and test paths against it.

nodes.name: bloom_filter_settings
nodes.summary: Parameters of a Bloom filter: hash version, number of hashes, bits per entry and maximum changed paths before a filter is declared too large.

nodes.name: bloom_filter
nodes.summary: A Bloom filter: bit data pointer, length in bytes, version and the buffer to free.

nodes.name: bloom_key
nodes.summary: Hash positions computed for one path, ready to test or add to a filter.

nodes.name: bloom_keyvec
nodes.summary: Array of bloom_key for a path and its parent directories.

nodes.name: bloom_filter_computed
nodes.summary: Flag enum telling how a filter was obtained (not computed, computed, truncated large, truncated empty, upgraded).

nodes.name: branch.c
nodes.summary: Branch creation and upstream-tracking logic behind `git branch`, `checkout -b` and `switch -c`: validates branch names, resolves the start point, writes the new ref in a transaction, configures branch.<name>.remote/merge, tracks which branches are checked out in other worktrees, and recurses into submodules.

nodes.name: tracking
nodes.summary: Collects the remote refspec, matched source refs and match count while searching for an upstream.

nodes.name: checked_out_branch
nodes.summary: Record of a branch name and the path of the worktree (or kind of operation: checkout, rebase, bisect) that has it checked out.

nodes.name: find_tracked_branch
nodes.summary: Per-remote callback that matches the start point against a remote's fetch refspecs to find the tracked remote ref.

nodes.name: should_setup_rebase
nodes.summary: Decides whether branch.<name>.rebase should be set for a given origin.

nodes.name: install_branch_config_multiple_remotes
nodes.summary: Writes branch.<name>.remote, .merge and optionally .rebase to config for one or more upstream refs, with warnings and instructions on failure.

nodes.name: install_branch_config
nodes.summary: Single-remote convenience wrapper that installs tracking config for a branch.

nodes.name: inherit_tracking
nodes.summary: Copies the upstream configuration of another branch (BRANCH_TRACK_INHERIT).

nodes.name: setup_tracking
nodes.summary: Finds the upstream of the new branch from the start point (or inherited) and writes the tracking config; dies with advice when the information is ambiguous.

nodes.name: read_branch_desc
nodes.summary: Reads branch.<name>.description from config into a strbuf.

nodes.name: validate_branchname
nodes.summary: Checks a branch name with check_branch_ref and returns the full refs/heads name; true if the branch already exists.

nodes.name: register_checked_out_branch
nodes.summary: Records that a worktree has a branch checked out.

nodes.name: prepare_checked_out_branches
nodes.summary: Scans all worktrees (HEAD, rebase, bisect states) and fills a map from branch to the worktree path using it.

nodes.name: branch_checked_out
nodes.summary: Returns the worktree path that has the given branch checked out, if any.

nodes.name: branch_bisecting
nodes.summary: Returns the worktree path that is bisecting on the given branch, if any.

nodes.name: validate_new_branchname
nodes.summary: Validates a new branch name and checks it is not already checked out elsewhere; with force an existing branch may be reset.

nodes.name: dwim_branch_start
nodes.summary: Resolves the start point (name, ref or commit), determining the object id and, for remote-tracking refs, the real ref for tracking.

nodes.name: create_branch
nodes.summary: Creates a new branch ref via a ref transaction, writing the reflog message, and sets up tracking when requested.

nodes.name: dwim_and_setup_tracking
nodes.summary: Resolves the start point and sets up tracking for an already-existing branch.

nodes.name: submodule_create_branch
nodes.summary: Creates the branch inside one submodule by running a child `git branch` there.

nodes.name: create_branches_recursively
nodes.summary: Creates the branch in the superproject and all populated submodules at their gitlink commits, rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: remove_merge_branch_state
nodes.summary: Deletes MERGE_HEAD, MERGE_RR, MERGE_MSG, MERGE_MODE and the autostash state.

nodes.name: remove_branch_state
nodes.summary: Removes merge, cherry-pick and revert sequencer state when switching branches.

nodes.name: die_if_checked_out
nodes.summary: Dies when the branch is already checked out in another worktree.

nodes.name: branch.h
nodes.summary: Interface for creating branches, setting up upstream tracking, validating branch names and querying which branches are checked out in other worktrees.

nodes.name: branch_track
nodes.summary: Enum of tracking modes: unspecified, never, remote, always, explicit, override, inherit, simple.

nodes.name: builtin.h
nodes.summary: Central header listing the cmd_* entry point of every built-in Git command, plus helpers such as is_builtin and setup_auto_pager that git.c uses to dispatch commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Every built-in has the uniform signature `int cmd_foo(int argc, const char **argv, const char *prefix, struct repository *repo)`; the return value becomes the process exit status.

nodes.name: is_builtin
nodes.summary: Declaration: tells whether a command name is a built-in.

nodes.name: fast-export.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git fast-export`, which walks a revision range and serializes blobs, commits, tags and ref resets as a git fast-import stream with marks. It also supports anonymizing paths, refs, identities and messages, signature and re-encoding policies, and marks files for incremental export.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses decorations (struct decoration idnums) to map in-memory objects to numeric marks, and hashmaps keyed by original strings to produce stable anonymized replacements.

nodes.name: parse_opt_sign_mode
nodes.summary: Option callback that parses --signed-tags/--signed-commits values into a sign_mode, rejecting the *-if-invalid variants that fast-export cannot honour.

nodes.name: parse_opt_tag_of_filtered_mode
nodes.summary: Option callback mapping --tag-of-filtered-object to abort, drop or rewrite behaviour for tags whose target was excluded by path filtering.

nodes.name: parse_opt_reencode_mode
nodes.summary: Option callback mapping --reencode to yes, no or abort for commits that carry an encoding header.

nodes.name: anonymized_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison function for anonymized_entry records, comparing either against a bounded key (path component) or against another entry by original string.

nodes.name: add_anonymized_entry
nodes.summary: Inserts an original-to-anonymized string mapping into a hashmap (lazily initializing it) and frees any entry it replaces.

nodes.name: anonymize_str
nodes.summary: Looks up the replacement for a string first in user-supplied --anonymize-map seeds, then in the per-context cache, and otherwise generates and caches a new token with the supplied generator.

nodes.name: anonymize_path
nodes.summary: Anonymizes a slash-separated path one component at a time so that sibling paths share an anonymized parent directory.

nodes.name: rewrite_commit
nodes.summary: Follows first parents of a commit that is TREESAME to its parent to find the nearest exported ancestor, used when a tag or ref points at a commit that path filtering skipped.

nodes.name: export_blob
nodes.summary: Writes a `blob` command to the stream for an object id: reads and verifies the blob from the object database (or fabricates content when anonymizing), assigns it the next mark and emits its data once.

nodes.name: depth_first
nodes.summary: qsort comparator for diff filepairs that orders deeper paths before their parent directory and renames last, so file replacements inside directories are emitted correctly.

nodes.name: print_path
nodes.summary: Prints a path in fast-import syntax, quoting it when needed and optionally anonymizing each component.

nodes.name: show_filemodify
nodes.summary: Diff-queue callback that emits `D`, `R`, `C` and `M` filechange lines for a commit, referencing blobs by mark (or by raw id for gitlinks and --no-data) and tracking already changed paths to keep renames and copies valid.

nodes.name: anonymize_refname
nodes.summary: Anonymizes a ref name while preserving standard prefixes such as refs/heads/ and refs/tags/ so tags stay tags.

nodes.name: anonymize_ident_line
nodes.summary: Rewrites an author, committer or tagger header to a generic User N identity while keeping the timestamp, because dates influence traversal order.

nodes.name: find_commit_multiline_header
nodes.summary: Reads a possibly multi-line commit header (for example gpgsig) from a raw commit buffer and returns it with continuation spaces removed.

nodes.name: append_signatures_for_header
nodes.summary: Collects every gpgsig or gpgsig-sha256 header of a commit into a list tagged with its hash algorithm.

nodes.name: handle_commit
nodes.summary: Exports one commit: parses author, committer, encoding and signature headers, diffs its tree against the first parent (or the empty tree), exports referenced blobs, then prints the `commit` command with parent marks, filechanges and message.

nodes.name: handle_tag
nodes.summary: Exports an annotated tag as a `tag` command, handling nested tags, tags of trees, signed-tag policy and tags whose target was filtered out.

nodes.name: get_commit
nodes.summary: Resolves a command-line revision entry to a commit, peeling nested tag objects and remembering each tag ref for later export.

nodes.name: get_tags_and_duplicates
nodes.summary: Scans command-line revisions to resolve full ref names, apply refspecs, export directly named blobs and register refs that need a final reset or tag record.

nodes.name: handle_tags_and_duplicates
nodes.summary: After the commit walk, emits `tag` and `reset` commands so every requested ref ends up pointing at the right exported commit or is deleted.

nodes.name: export_marks
nodes.summary: Writes the mark-to-commit-id table to the --export-marks file for later incremental exports.

nodes.name: import_marks
nodes.summary: Reads a marks file, verifies each id is a commit in the object database, and restores the mark numbers so an export can continue where it stopped.

nodes.name: handle_deletes
nodes.summary: Emits `reset` commands with a null object id for refspecs that have an empty source, which delete refs in the importer.

nodes.name: parse_opt_anonymize_map
nodes.summary: Option callback for --anonymize-map from:to that preloads a fixed anonymization seed.

nodes.name: cmd_fast_export
nodes.summary: Entry point of git fast-export: parses options, sets up a topological reversed revision walk with a diff callback, loads marks, runs handle_commit for each commit, then emits tags, resets and exports marks.

nodes.name: anonymized_entry
nodes.summary: Hashmap entry holding an original string and its anonymized replacement, with a flexible array member for the original text.

nodes.name: fmt-merge-msg.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git fmt-merge-msg`, which reads FETCH_HEAD style lines from a file or stdin and prints the default merge commit message, optionally with a shortlog of merged commits. It is a thin command wrapper around fmt_merge_msg() in fmt-merge-msg.c.

nodes.name: cmd_fmt_merge_msg
nodes.summary: Entry point of git fmt-merge-msg: parses --log, --message, --into-name and --file, reads the input, fills fmt_merge_msg_opts and calls fmt_merge_msg() to build the message written to stdout.

nodes.name: for-each-ref.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git for-each-ref`, listing refs that match patterns with sorting, filtering (merged, contains, points-at) and a user-defined --format. The shared for_each_ref_core() is also reused by other ref-listing commands.

nodes.name: for_each_ref_core
nodes.summary: Shared implementation that parses ref-listing options, validates the format and sorting, collects patterns from argv or stdin, and calls filter_and_format_refs() to print the matching refs.

nodes.name: cmd_for_each_ref
nodes.summary: Entry point of git for-each-ref that supplies its usage text to for_each_ref_core().

nodes.name: for-each-repo.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git for-each-repo`, which reads a list of repository paths from a multi-valued config key and runs the same git command in each one, optionally continuing after failures.

nodes.name: run_command_on_repo
nodes.summary: Runs `git -C <path> <args>` as a child process in one repository after expanding the path and sanitizing repo-specific environment variables.

nodes.name: cmd_for_each_repo
nodes.summary: Entry point of git for-each-repo: parses --config and --keep-going, fetches every value of the config key and runs the command in each repository.

nodes.name: get-tar-commit-id.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git get-tar-commit-id`, which reads the first two 512-byte records of a tar stream produced by git archive and prints the commit id stored in the pax global header comment.

nodes.name: cmd_get_tar_commit_id
nodes.summary: Reads the ustar header and extended global header from stdin, validates the `comment=` length against known hash sizes and writes the embedded commit id to stdout.

nodes.name: help.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git help`: lists commands, guides and config variables, and shows the documentation for a command as a man page, info page or HTML page using the configured viewer, resolving aliases and git-prefixed page names first.

nodes.name: set_config_vars
nodes.summary: Cuts a config variable name at the first `*` or `<` placeholder so completion lists contain only the fixed prefix.

nodes.name: set_config_sections
nodes.summary: Reduces a config variable name to its section (the part before the first dot) for shell completion output.

nodes.name: list_config_help
nodes.summary: Prints known configuration variable names, expanding slot placeholders for advice, color, and fsck keys and sorting the unique result in human, variable or section mode.

nodes.name: parse_help_format
nodes.summary: Converts a help.format value (man, info, web, html) into the help_format enum or dies on unknown names.

nodes.name: check_emacsclient_version
nodes.summary: Runs `emacsclient --version` and verifies it is at least version 22 before WoMan is used to show a man page.

nodes.name: exec_woman_emacs
nodes.summary: Replaces the process with emacsclient evaluating (woman ...) to display a man page.

nodes.name: exec_man_konqueror
nodes.summary: Opens a man page in a new Konqueror tab through kfmclient when a display is available.

nodes.name: add_man_viewer_info
nodes.summary: Parses man.<tool>.path and man.<tool>.cmd config keys and registers custom man viewer commands.

nodes.name: git_help_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading help.format, help.htmlpath, man.viewer and man.<tool>.* keys, delegating everything else to git_default_config.

nodes.name: cmd_to_page
nodes.summary: Maps a command name to its documentation page name (git, git-<cmd>, gitfoo or scalar).

nodes.name: setup_man_path
nodes.summary: Prepends Git's man directory to MANPATH, keeping a trailing colon so system pages remain reachable.

nodes.name: exec_viewer
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the man, woman, konqueror or custom-command viewer implementation by name.

nodes.name: show_man_page
nodes.summary: Tries each configured man viewer, then GIT_MAN_VIEWER, then plain man, and dies if none succeeds.

nodes.name: get_html_page_path
nodes.summary: Builds the path or URL of the HTML documentation page, checking the file exists for local paths.

nodes.name: check_git_cmd
nodes.summary: Resolves the help target: a real git command, an alias (printing its definition or following its first word), or an unknown name.

nodes.name: no_help_format
nodes.summary: Reports a usage error when a help format option is combined with a mode that cannot use it.

nodes.name: cmd_help
nodes.summary: Entry point of git help: picks a listing mode (all commands, guides, config, interfaces, completion helpers) or resolves the requested command and shows its man, info or web page.

nodes.name: slot_expansion
nodes.summary: Describes a config key family whose placeholder (for example <slot>) is expanded by a callback that lists the real names.

nodes.name: history.c
nodes.summary: Implements the experimental `git history` command with drop, fixup, reword and split subcommands. Each rewrites one commit by building new commit and tree objects, replays descendant commits with the replay machinery, and updates branches through a ref transaction.

nodes.name: fill_commit_message
nodes.summary: Writes COMMIT_EDITMSG with the original message plus a status-style summary of the tree change, launches the editor and returns the cleaned message.

nodes.name: commit_tree_ext
nodes.summary: Creates a rewritten commit with a new tree and parents while keeping the original author and extra headers, stripping signatures and encoding, and optionally letting the user edit the message.

nodes.name: commit_tree_with_edited_message
nodes.summary: Rewrites a commit keeping its tree and parents but with an edited message, computing the old tree from the first parent.

nodes.name: parse_ref_action
nodes.summary: Option callback for --update-refs choosing between updating all descendant branches or only HEAD.

nodes.name: revwalk_contains_merges
nodes.summary: Checks via a --min-parents=2 revision walk whether any commit to be replayed is a merge, which is not yet supported.

nodes.name: setup_revwalk
nodes.summary: Configures a reversed topological ancestry-path walk over descendants of the rewritten commit, limited to HEAD or all branches, and rejects merges.

nodes.name: handle_ref_update
nodes.summary: Either prints an update line (dry run) or adds a ref update to the transaction.

nodes.name: compute_pending_ref_updates
nodes.summary: Replays descendants onto the rewritten commit with replay_revisions() and additionally queues updates for local refs and HEAD that point at the original commit.

nodes.name: apply_pending_ref_updates
nodes.summary: Applies queued ref updates in one atomic ref transaction, or only prints them for a dry run.

nodes.name: handle_reference_updates
nodes.summary: Computes and then applies the ref updates that follow a history rewrite.

nodes.name: commit_became_empty
nodes.summary: Reports whether a rewritten tree equals the tree of the commit's parent, meaning the commit has become empty.

nodes.name: parse_opt_empty
nodes.summary: Option callback for --empty selecting drop, keep or abort for commits that become empty.

nodes.name: cmd_history_fixup
nodes.summary: Implements `history fixup`: writes the staged index as a tree, three-way merges it into the target commit with merge-ort, handles a commit that becomes empty, and replays descendants.

nodes.name: cmd_history_reword
nodes.summary: Implements `history reword`: opens an editor for the target commit message, recreates the commit and replays descendants.

nodes.name: write_ondisk_index
nodes.summary: Builds an index file from a tree object by unpacking it into an index and writing it under a lock, used as a temporary index for splitting.

nodes.name: split_commit
nodes.summary: Splits a commit into two: applies selected hunks (interactive add -p) onto the parent tree to form the first commit, then recreates the original tree as the second.

nodes.name: cmd_history_split
nodes.summary: Implements `history split`: validates the commit is not a merge, splits it and replays descendants.

nodes.name: update_worktree
nodes.summary: Moves the working tree and index from the old HEAD to the new HEAD, with an optional dry-run check.

nodes.name: find_head_tree_change
nodes.summary: Determines whether the planned ref updates move HEAD to a commit with a different tree.

nodes.name: cmd_history_drop
nodes.summary: Implements `history drop`: replays descendants onto the commit's parent, dry-run merges the worktree change and then applies ref and worktree updates.

nodes.name: cmd_history
nodes.summary: Entry point of git history that dispatches to the drop, fixup, reword and split subcommands.

nodes.name: hook.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git hook` with `run` and `list` subcommands, letting users run all hooks registered for an event (hooks directory and config-defined hooks) or list them with scope and disabled state.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Implements `git hook list`: validates the hook event name, loads traditional and configured hooks with list_hooks() and prints each with optional config scope and disabled markers.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Implements `git hook run`: parses --jobs, --ignore-missing and --to-stdin, collects hook arguments after `--` and calls run_hooks_opt() for the event.

nodes.name: cmd_hook
nodes.summary: Entry point of git hook that dispatches to the run or list subcommand.

nodes.name: interpret-trailers.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git interpret-trailers`, which adds, rewrites or extracts structured trailers (such as Signed-off-by) in commit messages read from files or stdin, optionally editing files in place through a temporary file.

nodes.name: new_trailers_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the list of --trailer items collected from the command line.

nodes.name: option_parse_trailer
nodes.summary: Option callback that records a --trailer value together with the current --where, --if-exists and --if-missing settings.

nodes.name: parse_opt_parse
nodes.summary: Option callback implementing --parse as an alias for --only-trailers --only-input --unfold.

nodes.name: read_input_file
nodes.summary: Reads a message from a named file or stdin into a strbuf and ensures it ends with a newline.

nodes.name: interpret_trailers
nodes.summary: Processes one input: reads it, runs process_trailers() with the new trailers and writes the result to stdout or atomically replaces the file via a tempfile rename.

nodes.name: cmd_interpret_trailers
nodes.summary: Entry point of git interpret-trailers: parses options, rejects incompatible combinations and processes each file or stdin.

nodes.name: last-modified.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git last-modified`, which reports, for every path in a commit's tree, the most recent commit that changed it. It walks history with a priority queue, carries a bitmap of still-unresolved paths per commit, and uses Bloom filters from the commit-graph to skip diffs.
nodes.languageNotes: Each commit holds a bitmap (via a commit slab) of paths whose last change is not found yet. Paths that are TREESAME to a parent are handed to that parent, and whatever remains active at a commit was changed there.

nodes.name: last_modified_entry_hashcmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison function that matches entries by path string.

nodes.name: last_modified_release
nodes.summary: Frees the path hashmap, Bloom keys, revision state and path array of a last_modified run.

nodes.name: add_path_from_diff
nodes.summary: Diff callback that adds every path of the target tree to the hashmap with its blob id and a Bloom key.

nodes.name: populate_paths_from_revs
nodes.summary: Diffs the single requested commit against the empty tree to collect all paths whose last change must be found.

nodes.name: last_modified_emit
nodes.summary: Prints a commit id (with ^ for boundary commits) and the path, newline or NUL terminated.

nodes.name: mark_path
nodes.summary: Reports a path as resolved for the current commit if the blob matches the wanted version and removes it from the hashmap.

nodes.name: last_modified_diff
nodes.summary: Diff callback that marks every non-deleted path of a commit's diff as last modified there.

nodes.name: maybe_changed_path
nodes.summary: Uses the commit's changed-path Bloom filter to decide whether any still-active path might have changed, avoiding a tree diff.

nodes.name: process_parent
nodes.summary: Diffs a commit with one parent (unless Bloom filters rule it out), passes TREESAME active paths to the parent's bitmap and queues the parent when it still has active paths.

nodes.name: last_modified_run
nodes.summary: Main loop: seeds a priority queue ordered by generation number and date, pops commits, handles boundary (--not) commits, propagates active paths through parents and marks the remaining paths at each commit.

nodes.name: last_modified_init
nodes.summary: Sets up revision options, parses revisions, loads Bloom settings and builds the path hashmap and indexed path array.

nodes.name: cmd_last_modified
nodes.summary: Entry point of git last-modified: parses options such as --recursive, --show-trees and -z, then initializes and runs the walk.

nodes.name: last_modified_entry
nodes.summary: Hashmap record for one tracked path: its wanted blob id, Bloom key and index into the bitmap.

nodes.name: last_modified
nodes.summary: State of a last-modified run: revision info, tracked path hashmap, path array, per-commit active-path bitmaps and a scratch bitmap.

nodes.name: log.c
nodes.summary: Implements the history-display and patch-generation commands: `git log`, `git show`, `git whatchanged`, `git reflog` display, `git format-patch` (cover letters, numbering, threading, range-diff, base commit) and `git cherry`. They share a revision walk plus log-tree output pipeline, configured by log.* and format.* settings.
nodes.languageNotes: cmd_log_init_defaults and cmd_log_init_finish bracket setup_revisions so one init path serves log, show and reflog. format-patch reuses log_tree_commit with mail-oriented rev_info settings.

nodes.name: parse_decoration_style
nodes.summary: Maps a log.decorate or --decorate value (short, full, auto, no) to a decoration style, treating auto as interactive-dependent.

nodes.name: log_config_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes a log_config and sets defaults: show root commits, encode email headers, use the mailmap, subject prefix PATCH, default patch file name length and an auto-selected decoration style.

nodes.name: decorate_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for --decorate[=style] that sets the decoration style.

nodes.name: log_line_range_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for -L that records a line range and file for line-level history tracing.

nodes.name: cmd_log_init_defaults
nodes.summary: Applies log configuration defaults (pretty format, follow renames, abbreviation, date mode, signature display) to a rev_info.

nodes.name: set_default_decoration_filter
nodes.summary: Builds the default decoration filter from log.excludeDecoration, log.initialDecorationSet and ref namespaces when no explicit filter was given.

nodes.name: cmd_log_init
nodes.summary: Wrapper that applies the log defaults and then parses options and sets up revisions, shared by log and show.

nodes.name: cmd_log_init_finish
nodes.summary: Parses log options, calls setup_revisions, loads notes, mailmap and ref decorations, sets up -L line tracing and starts the pager.

nodes.name: cmd_log_walk_no_free
nodes.summary: Runs the revision walk: prepares it, calls log_tree_commit for each commit, frees commit buffers to save memory and returns the diff exit code.

nodes.name: cmd_log_walk
nodes.summary: Wrapper around cmd_log_walk_no_free that also frees diff options afterwards.

nodes.name: git_log_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for log.* and format.* variables, falling back to git_diff_ui_config.

nodes.name: cmd_whatchanged
nodes.summary: Entry point of the deprecated `git whatchanged`, implemented as a raw-diff log walk.

nodes.name: show_tagger
nodes.summary: Prints the Tagger line of an annotated tag in the chosen date and commit format.

nodes.name: show_blob_object
nodes.summary: Writes a blob's content to stdout, applying textconv when requested.

nodes.name: show_tag_object
nodes.summary: Reads a tag object and prints its header lines and message for `git show`.

nodes.name: show_tree_object
nodes.summary: read_tree callback printing one tree entry name for `git show` on a tree.

nodes.name: cmd_show
nodes.summary: Entry point of git show: resolves each argument and dispatches on object type (blob, tag followed to its target, tree listing, or commit shown with a diff).

nodes.name: cmd_log_reflog
nodes.summary: Entry point for `git reflog show`, equal to `git log -g --abbrev-commit --pretty=oneline`.

nodes.name: cmd_log
nodes.summary: Entry point of git log: initializes revision options and runs the log walk.

nodes.name: format_config_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a format_config on top of log_config defaults: cover text from the description message, automatic numbering, empty To/Cc/header lists and a .patch suffix.

nodes.name: parse_cover_from_description
nodes.summary: Parses format.coverFromDescription values (default, none, message, subject, auto) into the cover_from_description enum or dies.

nodes.name: add_header
nodes.summary: Adds a format.headers value to extra email headers.

nodes.name: git_format_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for format.* variables used by format-patch (headers, thread, numbered, to, cc, signature, suffix, cover letter).

nodes.name: open_next_file
nodes.summary: Opens the next output patch file, named by number, commit subject or cover-letter, inside the output directory.

nodes.name: get_patch_ids
nodes.summary: For a range a..b, computes patch ids for all commits in b..a so equivalent commits can be recognized.

nodes.name: gen_message_id
nodes.summary: Generates a Message-ID from a base, timestamp and committer identity for email threading.

nodes.name: find_branch_name
nodes.summary: Finds the branch name that a single positive revision argument refers to, if its tip equals the ref, for cover-letter descriptions.

nodes.name: show_diffstat
nodes.summary: Prints a diffstat and summary between an origin and head commit for the cover letter.

nodes.name: prepare_cover_text
nodes.summary: Builds the cover letter subject and body, optionally from the branch description.

nodes.name: generate_shortlog_cover_letter
nodes.summary: Fills the cover letter commit list with a shortlog grouped by author.

nodes.name: generate_commit_list_cover
nodes.summary: Fills the cover letter commit list using a user pretty-format for each commit.

nodes.name: make_cover_letter
nodes.summary: Writes the cover letter: headers, subject and body, commit list, diffstat, optional interdiff and range-diff.

nodes.name: clean_message_id
nodes.summary: Trims whitespace and angle brackets from a message id supplied with --in-reply-to.

nodes.name: get_base_commit
nodes.summary: Determines the base commit for --base (explicit, auto from upstream, or merge-base of the series) and validates it is an ancestor and not in the series.

nodes.name: prepare_bases
nodes.summary: Collects patch ids of prerequisite commits between the base and the series for the base-commit trailer.

nodes.name: print_bases
nodes.summary: Prints the base-commit and prerequisite-patch-id lines.

nodes.name: infer_range_diff_ranges
nodes.summary: Infers the two revision ranges for --range-diff from the previous version and current series.

nodes.name: cmd_format_patch
nodes.summary: Entry point of git format-patch: parses a large option set, walks the commit range, handles cover letter, numbering, threading, base commit, signature and per-patch output through log_tree_commit.

nodes.name: add_pending_commit
nodes.summary: Resolves a revision name to a commit and adds it to a revision walk with flags.

nodes.name: print_commit
nodes.summary: Prints one git cherry line with the + or - sign and abbreviated id, optionally with the subject.

nodes.name: collect_diff_blob_oids
nodes.summary: Collects blob ids from one commit's diff (skipping binary drivers) for prefetching in partial clones.

nodes.name: prefetch_cherry_blobs
nodes.summary: In a partial clone, gathers blobs of commits whose patch-id headers collide and fetches them in one request from the promisor remote.

nodes.name: cmd_cherry
nodes.summary: Entry point of git cherry: compares commits of head against upstream by patch id and prints + for commits not present upstream and - for those that are.

nodes.name: log_config
nodes.summary: Settings loaded from log.* and format.* config for log, show and reflog commands.

nodes.name: format_config
nodes.summary: Settings loaded from format.* config for format-patch (numbering, threading, headers, cover letter, signature).

nodes.name: ls-tree.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git ls-tree`, which lists the entries of a tree object (mode, type, object id, optional size and path) with recursion, pathspec limiting, NUL termination and a custom --format.

nodes.name: expand_objectsize
nodes.summary: Appends a blob's size (or - for non-blobs) to the output line, padded for the %(objectsize:padded) placeholder.

nodes.name: show_recursive
nodes.summary: Decides whether a tree entry should be descended into, either because of -r or because a pathspec reaches below it.

nodes.name: show_tree_fmt
nodes.summary: Generic read_tree callback that expands %(objectmode), %(objecttype), %(objectname), %(objectsize) and %(path) in a --format string for each entry.

nodes.name: show_tree_common
nodes.summary: Shared early checks for the fast-path callbacks: skips blobs under -d and decides recursion.

nodes.name: show_tree_common_default_long
nodes.summary: Prints the path part of a tree entry relative to the prefix, quoted or NUL terminated.

nodes.name: show_tree_default
nodes.summary: Fast-path callback printing the default `mode type id<TAB>path` line.

nodes.name: show_tree_long
nodes.summary: Fast-path callback for --long that adds the blob size column.

nodes.name: show_tree_name_only
nodes.summary: Fast-path callback for --name-only that prints only paths.

nodes.name: show_tree_object
nodes.summary: Fast-path callback for --object-only that prints only object ids.

nodes.name: cmd_ls_tree
nodes.summary: Entry point of git ls-tree: parses options, resolves the tree-ish, builds the pathspec and runs read_tree with the callback matching the chosen output mode.

nodes.name: ls_tree_options
nodes.summary: Options of a ls-tree run: recursion flags, pathspec, prefix, abbreviation length and format string.

nodes.name: merge-base.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git merge-base`, finding best common ancestors of commits in the commit graph, with modes for all bases, octopus bases, independent heads, is-ancestor checks and fork-point lookup in a ref's reflog.

nodes.name: show_merge_base
nodes.summary: Computes merge bases of the first commit against the others with repo_get_merge_bases_many_dirty and prints one or all of them.

nodes.name: get_commit_reference
nodes.summary: Resolves a revision name to a commit object or dies with a clear message.

nodes.name: handle_independent
nodes.summary: Implements --independent by reducing a list of commits to those not reachable from the others.

nodes.name: handle_octopus
nodes.summary: Implements --octopus by computing merge bases for an n-way merge and reducing them.

nodes.name: handle_is_ancestor
nodes.summary: Implements --is-ancestor, returning exit status 0 when the first commit is reachable from the second.

nodes.name: handle_fork_point
nodes.summary: Implements --fork-point by looking at the reflog of a ref to find where a commit forked from it.

nodes.name: cmd_merge_base
nodes.summary: Entry point of git merge-base: parses mode options and dispatches to the matching handler or the default merge-base listing.

nodes.name: merge-file.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git merge-file`, a standalone three-way file merge using the xdiff library. It merges two modified versions against a common ancestor, with conflict markers, diff3 or zdiff3 styles, favor options and an --object-id mode that reads and writes blobs.

nodes.name: label_cb
nodes.summary: Option callback collecting up to three -L labels for the conflict markers.

nodes.name: set_diff_algorithm
nodes.summary: Applies a named diff algorithm to xdiff parameter flags.

nodes.name: diff_algorithm_cb
nodes.summary: Option callback for --diff-algorithm that validates and sets the algorithm.

nodes.name: cmd_merge_file
nodes.summary: Entry point of git merge-file: loads the three inputs from files or blobs, rejects binary data, runs xdl_merge and writes the result to a file, stdout or a new blob object.

nodes.name: merge-ours.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git merge-ours`, the built-in merge strategy that keeps the current tree unchanged: it only checks that the index matches HEAD and exits with status 0 so the caller records a merge commit.

nodes.name: cmd_merge_ours
nodes.summary: Reads the index and returns 2 if it differs from HEAD, otherwise 0, so the merge keeps the current tree.

nodes.name: merge.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git merge`: resolves the commits to merge, detects up-to-date and fast-forward cases, tries merge strategies (ort, recursive, octopus, resolve, ours, subtree) with state stashing and restoring, then writes the merge commit, MERGE_HEAD state files and merge message, or reports conflicts.
nodes.languageNotes: The control flow in cmd_merge is a ladder of cases: unborn HEAD, up-to-date, fast-forward, trivial in-index merge, then a real merge by trying each strategy in turn and picking the one with the fewest conflicts.

nodes.name: option_parse_message
nodes.summary: Option callback for -m that appends paragraphs to the merge message.

nodes.name: option_read_message
nodes.summary: Option callback for -F that reads a merge message from a file.

nodes.name: get_strategy
nodes.summary: Looks up a merge strategy by name among built-in strategies or external git-merge-* commands and exits with a list of available names if unknown.

nodes.name: save_state
nodes.summary: Refreshes the index and runs `git stash create` to save local changes so a strategy can be undone.

nodes.name: read_empty
nodes.summary: Runs read-tree to move from the empty tree to a commit when merging into an unborn branch.

nodes.name: reset_hard
nodes.summary: Runs read-tree --reset -u to restore the index and working tree to a commit.

nodes.name: restore_state
nodes.summary: Resets to HEAD and reapplies the stashed local changes, then reloads the index.

nodes.name: squash_message
nodes.summary: Writes SQUASH_MSG containing the log of the commits being squash-merged.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Completes a merge: updates HEAD with a reflog message, runs auto maintenance, shows a diffstat and runs the post-merge hook.

nodes.name: merge_name
nodes.summary: Builds the FETCH_HEAD-style description line (branch, tag, remote-tracking branch or commit) used to generate the merge message.

nodes.name: parse_branch_merge_options
nodes.summary: Parses branch.<name>.mergeoptions by splitting the string and running it through parse_options.

nodes.name: git_merge_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for merge.diffstat, merge.ff, merge.verifySignatures, merge.autostash, merge.defaultToUpstream, pull.twohead, pull.octopus, commit.cleanup, commit.gpgsign and branch.<name>.mergeoptions, then delegating to fmt_merge_msg_config and the diff UI config.

nodes.name: read_tree_trivial
nodes.summary: Runs unpack_trees with threeway_merge in trivial-only mode over the base, HEAD and remote trees to attempt an in-index merge.

nodes.name: try_merge_strategy
nodes.summary: Runs one merge strategy: merge-ort for ort, recursive and subtree under an index lock, or an external merge command for others.

nodes.name: count_unmerged_entries
nodes.summary: Counts index entries at conflict stages above zero.

nodes.name: add_strategies
nodes.summary: Adds strategies from a configured list or from the defaults for two-head or octopus merges.

nodes.name: prepare_to_commit
nodes.summary: Runs pre-merge-commit, prepare-commit-msg and commit-msg hooks, writes MERGE_HEAD and MERGE_MSG, optionally launches the editor and cleans the message.

nodes.name: merge_trivial
nodes.summary: Creates the merge commit for a successful trivial in-index merge.

nodes.name: finish_automerge
nodes.summary: Writes the merged tree and creates the merge commit with the right parents after a strategy merged cleanly.

nodes.name: suggest_conflicts
nodes.summary: Appends a conflict hint to MERGE_MSG, runs rerere and tells the user to resolve conflicts and commit.

nodes.name: evaluate_result
nodes.summary: Counts differing files and unmerged entries so the best of several strategies can be chosen.

nodes.name: setup_with_upstream
nodes.summary: Builds the merge arguments from the current branch's configured upstream remote-tracking branches.

nodes.name: write_merge_heads
nodes.summary: Writes MERGE_HEAD with the ids being merged and MERGE_MODE for no-ff.

nodes.name: default_edit_option
nodes.summary: Decides whether to open the editor by default, based on -m, GIT_MERGE_AUTOEDIT and whether stdin and stdout are the same tty.

nodes.name: reduce_parents
nodes.summary: Reduces remote heads to independent tips and notes whether HEAD is already contained in one of them.

nodes.name: prepare_merge_message
nodes.summary: Calls fmt_merge_msg to generate the default merge message from the collected names.

nodes.name: handle_fetch_head
nodes.summary: Parses FETCH_HEAD, keeping only entries not marked not-for-merge, and returns the commits to merge.

nodes.name: collect_parents
nodes.summary: Resolves the commit arguments (or FETCH_HEAD) into the list of merge heads and builds the merge message names.

nodes.name: merging_a_throwaway_tag
nodes.summary: Detects a merge of an annotated tag that is not already stored locally, which forbids fast-forward so the signature is kept.

nodes.name: cmd_merge
nodes.summary: Entry point of git merge: handles --abort, --quit and --continue, collects merge heads, finds merge bases, then takes the unborn, up-to-date, fast-forward, trivial or real-merge path, trying strategies and finishing with a commit or conflict message.

nodes.name: strategy
nodes.summary: Merge strategy name with attribute flags (default two-head, default octopus, no fast-forward, no trivial).

nodes.name: show-ref.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git show-ref`: lists refs (with their object ids) from the ref store filtered by pattern, --branches/--tags/--head, and offers --verify, --exists and --exclude-existing modes.

nodes.name: stripspace.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git stripspace`, which reads stdin and either strips whitespace and comment lines or prefixes every line with the comment character.

nodes.name: symbolic-ref.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git symbolic-ref`: reads, creates or deletes symbolic refs such as HEAD, with safety checks that keep HEAD inside refs/.

nodes.name: tag.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git tag`: lists tags through the ref-filter machinery, deletes and verifies tags, and creates lightweight or annotated (optionally GPG-signed) tag objects, then updates refs/tags/* in a ref transaction.

nodes.name: show_one
nodes.summary: Prints one ref as "<abbrev oid> <name>" (or just the hash), dies if the object is missing from the object database, and optionally prints the peeled value of an annotated tag as "<name>^{}".

nodes.name: show_ref
nodes.summary: Callback for ref iteration that accepts a ref when it is HEAD (with --head) or its name ends with one of the given patterns on a path component boundary, then prints it with show_one.

nodes.name: cmd_show_ref__exclude_existing
nodes.summary: Reads ref names from stdin, strips a trailing ^{}, drops lines that do not match the prefix or are malformed, and prints only those that do not already exist in the local ref store.

nodes.name: cmd_show_ref__verify
nodes.summary: Implements --verify: each argument must be a safe, readable full ref name; it is read from the ref store and shown, otherwise the command dies or returns 1 under --quiet.

nodes.name: cmd_show_ref__patterns
nodes.summary: Default listing mode: iterates over all refs, or only refs/heads/ and refs/tags/ when --branches/--tags are given, and shows those matching the patterns.

nodes.name: cmd_show_ref__exists
nodes.summary: Implements --exists: checks whether exactly one ref exists by reading the raw ref without resolving it, returning 2 when it is missing and 1 on other errors.

nodes.name: hash_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for -s/--hash that sets hash_only and parses the optional abbreviation length.

nodes.name: cmd_show_ref
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: defines the options, reads config, rejects incompatible modes and dispatches to the exclude-existing, verify, exists or patterns implementation.

nodes.name: cmd_stripspace
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: reads all of stdin into a strbuf, applies strbuf_stripspace (optionally removing comment lines) or comments every line, and writes the result to stdout.

nodes.name: check_symref
nodes.summary: Resolves a ref without recursing (unless asked), dies or returns 1 if it is not a symbolic ref, and optionally prints its target, shortened to an unambiguous name.

nodes.name: cmd_symbolic_ref
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: with one argument shows a symref, with two sets it (refusing to point HEAD outside refs/ or to an invalid name), and with -d deletes a non-HEAD symref.

nodes.name: list_tags
nodes.summary: Builds the default `%(refname:lstrip=2)` format (optionally with message lines) and calls filter_and_format_refs over refs/tags with the chosen sorting.

nodes.name: for_each_tag_name
nodes.summary: Maps each argument to refs/tags/<name>, reads it from the ref store and calls the callback, reporting names that do not exist.

nodes.name: collect_tags
nodes.summary: Callback that appends a tag ref and a copy of its object id to a string_list, used to batch deletions.

nodes.name: delete_tags
nodes.summary: Deletes the named tags in one refs_delete_refs call and prints "Deleted tag ... (was <abbrev>)" for each tag that is actually gone.

nodes.name: verify_tag
nodes.summary: Callback for `git tag -v` that verifies one tag signature with gpg_verify_tag and optionally pretty-prints it with a ref format.

nodes.name: do_sign
nodes.summary: Signs the tag buffer with the configured signing key and, in a compat-hash (SHA-1/SHA-256) repository, also converts and signs the buffer for the other algorithm and records the compat object id.

nodes.name: git_tag_config
nodes.summary: Config callback handling tag.gpgsign, tag.sort, tag.forcesignannotated, column.* and color settings before falling back to git_default_config.

nodes.name: write_tag_body
nodes.summary: Reads an existing tag object, strips its signature and header, and writes only its message body to a file descriptor, used to prefill the editor when a tag is re-created with -f.

nodes.name: build_tag_object
nodes.summary: Optionally signs the buffer and writes the final tag object into the object database, returning its object id.

nodes.name: create_tag
nodes.summary: Creates an annotated tag object: validates the target type, writes the header (object, type, tag, tagger), gathers the message from -m/-F/editor/trailers, cleans it up and writes the object, leaving the message in TAG_EDITMSG on failure.

nodes.name: create_reflog_msg
nodes.summary: Builds the reflog message for a new tag, honouring GIT_REFLOG_ACTION or describing the target as "tag: tagging <abbrev> (<commit subject>, <date>)" depending on object type.

nodes.name: parse_msg_arg
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for -m that appends each message paragraph, separated by a blank line, into a strbuf.

nodes.name: cmd_tag
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: selects list, delete, verify or create mode, applies sorting, column and signing options, and creates the tag by updating refs/tags/<name> in a ref transaction.

nodes.name: create_tag_options
nodes.summary: Options controlling tag creation: whether a message was given, whether to use the editor, signing and message cleanup mode.

nodes.name: update-ref.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git update-ref`: updates or deletes a single ref safely, or runs a scripted batch of update/create/delete/verify/symref commands from stdin inside one atomic ref transaction with start/prepare/commit/abort control.

nodes.name: update-server-info.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git update-server-info`, a thin wrapper that regenerates the info/refs and objects/info/packs files used by dumb HTTP transports.

nodes.name: var.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git var`: prints logical Git variables (author and committer identity, editor, pager, default branch, shell path, config and attribute file locations) through a table of reader callbacks.

nodes.name: verify-commit.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git verify-commit`: resolves each argument to a commit, parses it and checks its GPG/SSH signature, printing the result.

nodes.name: verify-pack.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git verify-pack`: normalizes each pack name to <name>.pack and runs `git index-pack --verify` on it, optionally printing statistics, to validate packfile integrity.

nodes.name: verify-tag.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git verify-tag`: resolves tag names and verifies their signatures with gpg_verify_tag, optionally printing the tag through a ref-filter format string.

nodes.name: write-tree.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git write-tree`: writes the current index out as tree objects (optionally for a subdirectory prefix) and prints the root tree object id.

nodes.name: parse_arg
nodes.summary: Reads one whitespace-terminated, possibly C-quoted argument from the line and appends the unquoted text to a strbuf.

nodes.name: parse_refname
nodes.summary: Parses a ref name argument from stdin input (quoted in text mode, NUL-terminated with -z) and returns it as an allocated string after checking the ref name format.

nodes.name: parse_next_refname
nodes.summary: Skips the argument separator and parses the next ref name, returning NULL if no argument follows.

nodes.name: parse_next_arg
nodes.summary: Parses the next generic argument in text or -z binary mode and returns it as an allocated string, dying on malformed quoting or terminators.

nodes.name: parse_next_oid
nodes.summary: Parses the next argument as an object id (or an empty string/zero id where allowed), die with an informative message for bad values, and reports whether an argument was present.

nodes.name: print_rejected_refs
nodes.summary: Callback that prints one rejected update in the "rejected <ref> <new> <old> <reason>" format used by --batch-updates.

nodes.name: handle_ref_transaction_error
nodes.summary: Dies on generic transaction errors but, when batch updates are allowed, prints rejected updates and continues.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_update
nodes.summary: Parses an `update <ref> <new-oid> [<old-oid>]` stdin command and queues it in the ref transaction.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_symref_update
nodes.summary: Parses a `symref-update` command (ref, new target, optional old target or old oid) and queues a symbolic ref update.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_create
nodes.summary: Parses a `create <ref> <new-oid>` command and queues a creation that requires the ref not to exist.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_symref_create
nodes.summary: Parses a `symref-create` command and queues creation of a symbolic ref.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_delete
nodes.summary: Parses a `delete <ref> [<old-oid>]` command and queues the deletion in the transaction.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_symref_delete
nodes.summary: Parses a `symref-delete` command and queues deletion of a symbolic ref, optionally checking its old target.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_verify
nodes.summary: Parses a `verify <ref> [<old-oid>]` command that asserts the ref value at commit time.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_symref_verify
nodes.summary: Parses a `symref-verify` command asserting a symbolic ref target.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_prepare
nodes.summary: Handles the `prepare` command by locking and preparing the ref transaction so that every update is checked before commit.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_abort
nodes.summary: Handles the `abort` command by aborting the current ref transaction.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_commit
nodes.summary: Handles the `commit` command by committing the transaction, printing rejected updates and freeing it.

nodes.name: update_refs_stdin
nodes.summary: Reads commands line by line from stdin, dispatches them through the command table with a small state machine (open, started, prepared, closed) and commits or aborts the ref transaction at the end.

nodes.name: cmd_update_ref
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: updates or deletes one ref directly with an optional old-value check, or switches to the stdin transaction mode.

nodes.name: cmd_update_server_info
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point that parses --force and calls update_server_info on the repository.

nodes.name: git_config_val_global
nodes.summary: Returns the global config file locations (XDG and user), normalized, one per line, for the GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL variable.

nodes.name: list_vars
nodes.summary: Prints every readable logical variable as name=value, splitting multi-valued ones on newlines.

nodes.name: get_git_var
nodes.summary: Looks up a logical variable by name in the git_vars table.

nodes.name: show_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for `git var -l` that prints every config key and value and then delegates to git_default_config.

nodes.name: cmd_var
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: with -l lists all config and logical variables, otherwise prints the value of one logical variable.

nodes.name: run_gpg_verify
nodes.summary: Checks the signature of a commit with check_commit_signature and prints the verification output.

nodes.name: verify_commit
nodes.summary: Resolves a name to an object, requires it to be a commit and verifies its signature.

nodes.name: cmd_verify_commit
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: parses --verbose/--raw and verifies each commit argument, ignoring SIGPIPE from gpg.

nodes.name: verify_one_pack
nodes.summary: Normalizes a pack name (.idx, .pack or bare) and spawns `git index-pack --verify[-stat]` as a child process, printing ok or bad in verbose mode.

nodes.name: cmd_verify_pack
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point that runs verify_one_pack for every pack argument and returns non-zero if any fails.

nodes.name: cmd_verify_tag
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: resolves each tag name to an object id, verifies its signature with gpg_verify_tag and optionally prints it using --format.

nodes.name: cmd_write_tree
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point: calls write_index_as_tree on the current index (honouring --missing-ok and --prefix), prints the resulting tree object id and maps failures to messages.

nodes.name: command_options
nodes.summary: Per-run options for stdin commands, including whether individual update failures are allowed (--batch-updates).

nodes.name: parse_cmd
nodes.summary: Table entry that binds a stdin command name to its parser function, argument count and the transaction state it moves to.

nodes.name: git_var
nodes.summary: Descriptor of a logical Git variable: name, reader function and whether it can have several values.

nodes.name: color.h
nodes.summary: Public API for terminal color handling: color config parsing, the git_colorbool tri-state, want_color checks and color-aware fprintf helpers, plus the ANSI color constants.

nodes.name: column.c
nodes.summary: Lays out a list of strings into columns or rows sized to the terminal width (with optional dense packing), parses column.* configuration and can pipe output through `git column` as a child filter.

nodes.name: column.h
nodes.summary: Declares the column layout API (COL_* option flags, struct column_options, print_columns, config and parse-options hooks, column filter start/stop) used by tag, branch, status and friends.

nodes.name: combine-diff.c
nodes.summary: Implements combined diff for merge commits (`git diff -c`, `--cc`, `--combined-all-paths`): finds paths touched relative to every parent, diffs each parent against the merge result, coalesces the lost lines and prints combined hunks or raw output.

nodes.name: layout
nodes.summary: Computes cell width, number of columns and rows for equally sized cells given the table width and padding.

nodes.name: compute_column_width
nodes.summary: Finds the widest cell in each column for the current rows and columns arrangement.

nodes.name: shrink_columns
nodes.summary: Dense layout: repeatedly reduces the row count to add columns until the table no longer fits the terminal width.

nodes.name: display_cell
nodes.summary: Prints one table cell with indent, trailing padding or a newline depending on the layout mode.

nodes.name: display_table
nodes.summary: Measures every string, chooses the layout (optionally dense) and prints the table row-wise or column-wise.

nodes.name: print_columns
nodes.summary: Public entry that normalizes column options and prints the list as plain lines or as a column or row table according to colopts.

nodes.name: finalize_colopts
nodes.summary: Resolves the "auto" column mode to enabled or disabled depending on whether stdout is a tty or a pager is active.

nodes.name: parse_option
nodes.summary: Parses one column option word (always, never, auto, plain, column, row, dense, with optional "no" prefix) into the colopts bit field.

nodes.name: parse_config
nodes.summary: Parses a space or comma separated column mode string; setting a layout without an enable flag implies "always".

nodes.name: git_column_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for column.ui and column.<command> keys, setting colopts for a given command.

nodes.name: parseopt_column_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --column and --no-column.

nodes.name: run_column_filter
nodes.summary: Starts `git column --raw-mode=...` as a child process and redirects stdout through it so the command output is laid out in columns.

nodes.name: stop_column_filter
nodes.summary: Finishes the column filter child and restores the original stdout.

nodes.name: intersect_paths
nodes.summary: Intersects the set of changed paths of the next parent diff with the running list, keeping paths changed against every parent and recording per-parent mode, oid and status.

nodes.name: match_string_spaces
nodes.summary: Compares two lines ignoring differences in whitespace according to the xdiff whitespace flags.

nodes.name: coalesce_lines
nodes.summary: Merges the removed lines of a new parent into the accumulated lost lines using a longest common subsequence match, tracking which parents had each line.

nodes.name: grab_blob
nodes.summary: Reads the content of a blob (or a subproject line, deleted blob, or textconv output) for a given oid and mode.

nodes.name: append_lost
nodes.summary: Appends a line removed from a parent to the bucket of lost lines attached to a result line.

nodes.name: consume_hunk
nodes.summary: xdiff hunk callback that records the hunk header positions and chooses the bucket for lost lines.

nodes.name: consume_line
nodes.summary: xdiff line callback that records "-" lines as lost lines and flags "+" lines as present in the merge result.

nodes.name: combine_diff
nodes.summary: Diffs one parent blob against the merge result with xdiff, filling the per-line state (sline) and line numbers for that parent.

nodes.name: give_context
nodes.summary: Marks lines within the context window around interesting lines so that hunks include surrounding context.

nodes.name: make_hunks
nodes.summary: Decides which lines belong to hunks, and in dense mode (`--cc`) drops hunks where only one parent differs or all differences are identical.

nodes.name: dump_sline
nodes.summary: Prints combined hunks with "@@@" headers, per-parent +/- columns, lost lines and optional colors.

nodes.name: reuse_combine_diff
nodes.summary: Copies the combined diff state of an identical parent instead of diffing it again.

nodes.name: show_combined_header
nodes.summary: Prints the "diff --combined" header with index line, modes and file names.

nodes.name: show_patch_diff
nodes.summary: Produces the combined patch for one path: reads the merge result (from the object database or working tree), diffs it against each parent, builds hunks and prints them or a binary notice.

nodes.name: show_raw_diff
nodes.summary: Prints the combined raw format line with N colons, parent modes and oids, per-parent status letters and the path.

nodes.name: show_combined_diff
nodes.summary: Public entry that prints a combined diff path in raw, name-only or patch form depending on the diff options.

nodes.name: combined_pair
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a diff_filepair with N entries on the one side and the merge result on the other for format callbacks.

nodes.name: handle_combined_callback
nodes.summary: Builds a diff queue of combined pairs and invokes the diff format callback.

nodes.name: find_paths_generic
nodes.summary: Finds changed paths by running a full pairwise diff (with rename and other diffcore transforms) against each parent and intersecting the results.

nodes.name: find_paths_multitree
nodes.summary: Finds paths changed relative to all parents in one simultaneous multi-tree walk, the faster path when no diffcore transforms are requested.

nodes.name: combined_objfind
nodes.summary: Filters combined paths to those whose blob (or a parent blob) is in the --find-object set.

nodes.name: diff_tree_combined
nodes.summary: Public driver for diffing a merge commit against all its parents: finds common changed paths, prints the log header, and shows each path in raw, stat or combined patch form.

nodes.name: diff_tree_combined_merge
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that gathers the saved parents of a merge commit and calls diff_tree_combined.

nodes.name: combine_diff_path_new
nodes.summary: Allocates a combine_diff_path with room for the per-parent records.

nodes.name: column_data
nodes.summary: Working state of a column layout: the list, options, row and column counts and the cell lengths and widths.

nodes.name: colopt
nodes.summary: Table entry mapping a column option name to its bit value and mask.

nodes.name: lline
nodes.summary: A line removed from one or more parents, linked into the lost-line list of a result line with a bit map of parents.

nodes.name: sline
nodes.summary: State of one surviving line of the merge result: lost lines before it, a flag word with per-parent bits and per-parent line numbers.

nodes.name: combine_diff_state
nodes.summary: xdiff callback state for diffing one parent against the merge result.

nodes.name: git_colorbool
nodes.summary: Tri-state color setting (unknown, never, always, auto) derived from config or options.

nodes.name: column_options
nodes.summary: Layout options for print_columns: width, padding, indent string and newline string.

nodes.name: commit-graph.h
nodes.summary: Declares the commit-graph file API: the in-memory struct commit_graph with its chunks, lookups of commit data and generation numbers, writing, verifying and splitting commit-graph files.

nodes.name: commit-reach.c
nodes.summary: Commit reachability algorithms over the commit DAG: paint-down-to-common merge base search, redundant-head removal, is-descendant checks, `--contains` tag algorithm, can-all-from-reach, ahead/behind counting and branch base finding, accelerated by commit-graph generation numbers.

nodes.name: compare_commits_by_gen
nodes.summary: Orders commits by generation number, then commit date, for sorting commit arrays.

nodes.name: paint_queue_get
nodes.summary: Pops the next commit from the paint-down priority queue and applies generation cutoffs and early-exit conditions.

nodes.name: paint_down_to_common
nodes.summary: Core merge-base walk: paints commits reachable from one side PARENT1 and the other PARENT2 using a generation/date priority queue, collects commits painted both, and marks their parents STALE.

nodes.name: merge_bases_many
nodes.summary: Handles trivial cases, parses the inputs, runs paint_down_to_common and returns the non-stale common ancestors.

nodes.name: get_octopus_merge_bases
nodes.summary: Computes merge bases for more than two commits by folding pairwise merge bases over the input list.

nodes.name: remove_redundant_no_gen
nodes.summary: Reduces a set of commits to the independent ones (dropping commits reachable from another) using repeated paint-down walks when generation numbers are unavailable.

nodes.name: remove_redundant_with_gen
nodes.summary: Removes redundant commits using generation numbers to bound walks, sorting inputs by generation and raising the minimum generation as stale tips are found.

nodes.name: remove_redundant
nodes.summary: Chooses between the generation-number and the plain algorithm to filter redundant commits.

nodes.name: get_merge_bases_many_0
nodes.summary: Shared implementation of the merge base queries: finds candidates, clears flags if requested and removes redundant results.

nodes.name: repo_get_merge_bases_many
nodes.summary: Public API returning all merge bases of one commit against several others.

nodes.name: repo_get_merge_bases_many_dirty
nodes.summary: Same as repo_get_merge_bases_many but leaves traversal flags set on commits for the caller.

nodes.name: repo_get_merge_bases
nodes.summary: Public API returning the merge bases of two commits.

nodes.name: repo_is_descendant_of
nodes.summary: Tells whether a commit descends from any commit in a list, using can_all_from_reach with commit-graph generation numbers when enabled or merge bases otherwise.

nodes.name: repo_in_merge_bases_many
nodes.summary: Tells whether a commit is an ancestor of one of the reference commits, via merge base computation with generation cutoffs.

nodes.name: repo_in_merge_bases
nodes.summary: Single-reference version of repo_in_merge_bases_many.

nodes.name: reduce_heads

nodes.name: commit_tree

nodes.name: rev_collect
nodes.summary: Collects commits found in reflog entries into a stack for fork-point calculation.

nodes.name: commit.h
