nodes.summary: Connects to the daemon and sends the since-token to get changed paths, handling states by spawning the daemon once when nobody listens, then retrying while waiting for the socket to appear; wrapped in trace2 regions.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_ipc__send_command
nodes.summary: Connects to an already running daemon and sends a command verb, dying with a message if the daemon is not running or the send fails.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_settings
nodes.summary: Private per-repository fsmonitor settings: mode, incompatibility reason and hook path, allocated lazily.

nodes.name: check_remote
nodes.summary: Checks whether the worktree is on a remote filesystem and, unless fsmonitor.allowRemote is true, reports it as incompatible.

nodes.name: check_for_incompatible
nodes.summary: Decides whether fsmonitor can be used: bare repositories fail, and with OS support it also runs the remote check and the platform fsm_os__incompatible check.

nodes.name: alloc_settings
nodes.summary: Allocates a zeroed settings struct defaulting to disabled mode and untested reason.

nodes.name: lookup_fsmonitor_settings
nodes.summary: Resolves settings from core.fsmonitor: a boolean selects IPC or disabled, any other string is a hook path, and when unset GIT_TEST_FSMONITOR is consulted.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__get_mode
nodes.summary: Returns the fsmonitor mode, loading settings if needed.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__get_hook_path
nodes.summary: Returns the fsmonitor hook path, loading settings if needed.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__set_ipc
nodes.summary: Switches to IPC mode if the repository passes the compatibility checks, otherwise records the incompatibility.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__set_hook
nodes.summary: Switches to hook mode with a copy of the hook path if compatible, otherwise records the incompatibility.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__set_disabled
nodes.summary: Sets mode to disabled with reason OK and clears the hook path.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__set_incompatible
nodes.summary: Sets mode to incompatible and stores the reason.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__get_reason
nodes.summary: Returns the stored incompatibility reason, loading settings if needed.

nodes.name: fsm_settings__get_incompatible_msg
nodes.summary: Builds a translated message for each incompatibility reason (bare, error, remote, VFS, missing Unix sockets) and returns it as an allocated string.

nodes.name: gettext.h
nodes.summary: Thin internationalization layer: defines the _(), Q_() and N_() macros/inlines that mark and look up translatable strings, becoming no-ops when NO_GETTEXT is set.
nodes.languageNotes: FORMAT_PRESERVING uses __attribute__((format_arg(n))) so the compiler can still type-check printf-style format strings that pass through _().

nodes.name: git-compat-util.h
nodes.summary: Portability and safety layer that nearly every Git source file includes first: platform and libc includes, compiler attribute macros (NORETURN, format checking), die/error/warning prototypes, overflow-checked size arithmetic (st_add, st_mult), allocation helpers (ALLOC_GROW, CALLOC_ARRAY), skip_prefix, and the BUG() assertion macro.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy preprocessor use: platform #ifdef ladders, and macros such as ALLOC_GROW and COPY_ARRAY that infer the element size from the pointer type.

nodes.name: git-zlib.c
nodes.summary: Wrappers around zlib inflate/deflate that Git uses for loose objects and packfiles: tracks byte counters as size_t, clamps each zlib call to a 1 GB window, cross-checks zlib's totals against its own, and dies or reports with readable messages on init errors.

nodes.name: git-zlib.h
nodes.summary: Declares git_zstream, a zlib stream with size_t counters, and the git_inflate_* and git_deflate_* entry points used by the object database and pack code.
Translates a message id through gettext when localization is enabled, returns the id unchanged otherwise, and keeps the empty string empty.

nodes.name: Q_
nodes.summary: Plural-aware translation: picks singular or plural form by count, via ngettext when localization is on.

nodes.name: skip_prefix_impl
nodes.summary: Implementation behind skip_prefix(): if the string starts with the prefix, stores the remainder in out and returns true.

nodes.name: git_open_cloexec
nodes.summary: Opens a file with close-on-exec set, portable across platforms.

nodes.name: st_add
nodes.summary: Adds two size_t values and dies on overflow, protecting allocation size computations.

nodes.name: st_mult
nodes.summary: Multiplies two size_t values and dies on overflow.

nodes.name: ALLOC_GROW
nodes.summary: Macro that grows a heap array geometrically ((alloc+16)*3/2) when nr exceeds the allocation, using overflow-checked REALLOC_ARRAY.

nodes.name: regexec_buf
nodes.summary: Runs regexec on a length-delimited buffer using REG_STARTEND so the text need not be NUL-terminated.

nodes.name: git_zstream
nodes.summary: Wrapper struct around z_stream that keeps avail_in, avail_out, total_in and total_out as size_t plus next_in and next_out pointers.

nodes.name: zerr_to_string
nodes.summary: Maps a zlib status code to a short English description used in error messages.

nodes.name: zlib_pre_call
nodes.summary: Copies Git's size_t stream fields into the z_stream, capping buffer sizes to 1 GB and counters to uLong before each zlib call.

nodes.name: zlib_post_call
nodes.summary: After a zlib call, verifies zlib's totals match Git's own accounting (BUG on mismatch) and updates the size_t counters and pointers.

nodes.name: git_inflate_init
nodes.summary: Initializes inflation and dies with the zlib message if it fails.

nodes.name: git_inflate_init_gzip_only
nodes.summary: Initializes inflation with windowBits 15+16 so only gzip data is accepted.

nodes.name: git_inflate_end
nodes.summary: Ends inflation and reports an error if inflateEnd fails.

nodes.name: git_inflate
nodes.summary: Calls inflate in a loop (never passing Z_FINISH unless all input is supplied) while output remains and progress is made; dies on out-of-memory and reports other errors.

nodes.name: git_deflate_bound
nodes.summary: Returns the worst-case compressed size, using a stored-block formula for sizes above uLong on Windows.

nodes.name: git_deflate_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes the stream and initializes deflation at the given level, dying on failure.

nodes.name: do_git_deflate_init
nodes.summary: Shared initializer for deflateInit2 with a chosen windowBits value.

nodes.name: git_deflate_init_gzip
nodes.summary: Initializes deflation producing gzip framing (windowBits 15+16).

nodes.name: git_deflate_init_raw
nodes.summary: Initializes deflation producing raw data with no header or trailer (windowBits -15).

nodes.name: git_deflate_abort
nodes.summary: Calls deflateEnd and returns the status without printing an error.

nodes.name: git_deflate_end
nodes.summary: Aborts the stream and reports an error if deflateEnd fails.

nodes.name: git_deflate_end_gently
nodes.summary: Calls deflateEnd and returns the status, leaving reporting to the caller.

nodes.name: git_deflate
nodes.summary: Calls deflate in a loop like git_inflate, dying on out-of-memory and reporting other errors.

nodes.name: grep.c
nodes.summary: Search engine behind git grep and the --grep/--author log filters: compiles patterns (BRE, ERE, fixed, PCRE2) into a boolean expression tree, matches lines in files, blobs or buffers, and handles context lines, function-name headers, colors, textconv and binary detection.
nodes.languageNotes: The USE_LIBPCRE2 #ifdef swaps in a real PCRE2 implementation (compile_pcre2_pattern, pcre2match, free_pcre2_pattern) or stubs; GIT_PCRE2_VERSION_10_xx macros guard JIT workarounds.

nodes.name: parse_pattern_type_arg
nodes.summary: Maps default, basic, extended, fixed or perl to a grep_pattern_type, dying on anything else.

nodes.name: grep_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads grep.extendedRegexp, grep.patternType, grep.lineNumber, grep.column, grep.fullName and color.grep.* slots into a grep_opt.

nodes.name: grep_init
nodes.summary: Overwrites a grep_opt with GREP_OPT_INIT defaults, binds the repository and resets the pattern list tails.

nodes.name: create_grep_pat
nodes.summary: Allocates a grep_pat with a copy of the pattern text and its origin, number, token and header field.

nodes.name: do_append_grep_pat
nodes.summary: Appends a pattern to a list and splits multi-line patterns at newlines into separate patterns.

nodes.name: append_header_grep_pattern
nodes.summary: Adds a header-field pattern (author, committer or reflog) to the header list and enables the reflog filter when relevant.

nodes.name: append_grep_pattern
nodes.summary: Appends a NUL-terminated body pattern by delegating to append_grep_pat.

nodes.name: append_grep_pat
nodes.summary: Creates a pattern with given length and token and appends it to the main pattern list.

nodes.name: grep_opt_dup
nodes.summary: Copies a grep_opt and rebuilds its pattern list so another thread can own it.

nodes.name: compile_regexp_failed
nodes.summary: Formats where a pattern came from and dies with the regex compilation error.

nodes.name: is_fixed
nodes.summary: Returns true if a pattern contains no regex metacharacters, so a literal search suffices.

nodes.name: compile_pcre2_pattern
nodes.summary: Compiles a pattern with PCRE2 (JIT where possible), choosing UTF and case-insensitive options and locale tables, and dies on compile errors.

nodes.name: pcre2match
nodes.summary: Executes a compiled PCRE2 pattern over a line, using JIT or the interpreter and mapping the result to regmatch_t.

nodes.name: compile_fixed_regexp
nodes.summary: Without PCRE2, quotes a fixed string into a basic regex and compiles it with regcomp.

nodes.name: compile_regexp
nodes.summary: Chooses a pattern dialect, handles fixed strings and PCRE, and otherwise compiles the pattern with regcomp using ERE or BRE flags.

nodes.name: compile_pattern_atom
nodes.summary: Recursive-descent parser step: parses a pattern atom or a parenthesized group into an expression node.

nodes.name: compile_pattern_not
nodes.summary: Parses an optional --not operator in front of an atom.

nodes.name: compile_pattern_and
nodes.summary: Parses a chain of --and operators, building AND nodes.

nodes.name: compile_pattern_or
nodes.summary: Parses the lowest-precedence level where adjacent expressions are ORed.

nodes.name: prep_header_patterns
nodes.summary: Compiles header patterns and groups them by header field into an OR-tree combined into one expression.

nodes.name: grep_splice_or
nodes.summary: Replaces the TRUE leaf of the header expression's rightmost OR chain with another expression.

nodes.name: compile_grep_patterns
nodes.summary: Compiles every pattern atom with compile_regexp and builds the pattern expression tree when operators, all-match, no-body-match or header patterns require it.

nodes.name: free_pattern_expr
nodes.summary: Recursively frees an expression tree.

nodes.name: free_grep_pat
nodes.summary: Frees a pattern list, releasing PCRE2 or regex objects and pattern text.

nodes.name: free_grep_patterns
nodes.summary: Frees both pattern lists and the expression tree of a grep_opt.

nodes.name: patmatch
nodes.summary: Matches one pattern against a range with PCRE2 or regexec_buf, returning 1, 0 or -1 on error.

nodes.name: headerless_match_one_pattern
nodes.summary: Matches a pattern at the right context and, with -w, re-checks word boundaries and retries later positions on the line.

nodes.name: match_one_pattern
nodes.summary: Matches one pattern, first checking the header prefix (author, committer, reflog) and stripping timestamps for header patterns.

nodes.name: match_expr_eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates the expression tree for a line with short-circuiting, tracking the earliest match column and collecting per-node hits when needed.

nodes.name: match_line
nodes.summary: Evaluates the expression tree if there is one, or ORs over the simple pattern list, returning whether the line hit and the first match column.

nodes.name: match_next_pattern
nodes.summary: Finds the leftmost-longest match among patterns for highlighting.

nodes.name: grep_next_match
nodes.summary: Returns the next match in a line across header or body patterns, optionally filtered by header field.

nodes.name: show_line_header
nodes.summary: Prints the filename, line number and column prefix of an output line with colors and separators.

nodes.name: show_line
nodes.summary: Prints a matching or context line, highlighting matches with color, and handles --only-matching.

nodes.name: show_pre_context
nodes.summary: Prints the lines before a hit (context before, function header or function body) by rewinding in the buffer.

nodes.name: should_lookahead
nodes.summary: Decides whether the look-ahead optimization is safe: only for plain patterns with no expression tree and no inversion.

nodes.name: look_ahead
nodes.summary: Searches the whole remaining buffer for the earliest hit and skips straight to its line, tracking line numbers.

nodes.name: fill_textconv_grep
nodes.summary: Loads the grep_source, or runs its textconv filter through a fake diff_filespec when a textconv driver exists.

nodes.name: grep_source_1
nodes.summary: Main per-source search loop: applies textconv and binary handling, iterates lines with optional look-ahead, applies invert, count and max-count, and prints hits and context.

nodes.name: grep_source
nodes.summary: Runs one or two passes of grep_source_1: a hit-collecting pass first when all-match or no-body-match is in effect, then the real pass.

nodes.name: grep_source_init_buf
nodes.summary: Initializes a grep_source over an in-memory buffer.

nodes.name: grep_buffer
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that greps a raw buffer and cleans up.

nodes.name: grep_source_init_file
nodes.summary: Initializes a grep_source to read a file from disk.

nodes.name: grep_source_init_oid
nodes.summary: Initializes a grep_source to read a blob by object id from a repository.

nodes.name: grep_source_clear
nodes.summary: Frees name, path and identifier and clears the data.

nodes.name: grep_source_clear_data
nodes.summary: Frees the loaded buffer for file and OID sources and leaves caller-owned buffers alone.

nodes.name: grep_source_load_oid
nodes.summary: Reads a blob's contents from the object database into the source buffer.

nodes.name: grep_source_load_file
nodes.summary: Reads a regular file into memory with lstat, open and read_in_full.

nodes.name: grep_source_load
nodes.summary: Loads the source contents once, dispatching on its type (file, blob or buffer).

nodes.name: grep_source_load_driver
nodes.summary: Finds the userdiff driver for the source's path (default driver as fallback) under the attribute mutex.

nodes.name: grep_source_is_binary
nodes.summary: Decides if a source is binary from the userdiff driver or by scanning its buffer.

nodes.name: grep.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the grep engine: pattern and expression structures, the grep_opt option block with its GREP_OPT_INIT defaults, the grep_source abstraction (file, blob OID or buffer), and functions to append patterns, compile them and run a search.

nodes.name: hash-lookup.c
nodes.summary: Lookup helpers for sorted tables of object ids: oid_pos does an interpolation-assisted binary search over an abstract OID table, and bsearch_hash searches a packfile-index-style table using its 256-entry fanout.

nodes.name: hash.c
nodes.summary: Hash algorithm abstraction: builds the hash_algos table (unknown, SHA-1, unsafe SHA-1, SHA-256) with per-algorithm init/update/final function pointers, the empty-tree, empty-blob and null OIDs, context lifecycle wrappers, and lookup of an algorithm by name, format id or digest length.

nodes.name: grep_pat_token
nodes.summary: Token kinds in a grep pattern list: pattern atoms (generic, head, body) and the operators AND, parentheses, NOT and OR.

nodes.name: grep_pattern_type
nodes.summary: Pattern dialects supported by grep: unspecified, basic, extended, fixed and PCRE.

nodes.name: grep_pat
nodes.summary: One compiled pattern: its text, origin, token and header field, a POSIX regex or PCRE2 objects, and flags such as fixed, ignore_case and word_regexp.

nodes.name: grep_expr
nodes.summary: Node of the boolean expression tree built from patterns (atom, not, and, or, true) with a hit counter.

nodes.name: grep_opt
nodes.summary: Complete option and state block of a grep run: pattern lists and expression, output flags (line numbers, columns, context, colors, count, name-only), binary handling, limits and the output callback.

nodes.name: grep_source
nodes.summary: Abstraction of something to grep: a file, a blob identified by OID, or an in-memory buffer, with name, path for attributes and userdiff driver.

nodes.name: oid_pos
nodes.summary: Binary search over a table of object ids accessed through a callback, with interpolation on the leading bytes to pick the first probe; returns the position or a negative insert position.

nodes.name: bsearch_hash
nodes.summary: Searches a table of fixed-stride hashes using the first-byte fanout table to narrow the range, and returns the index or the insert position.

nodes.name: null_oid
nodes.summary: Returns the null OID of the given algorithm.

nodes.name: empty_tree_oid_hex
nodes.summary: Returns the hex of the algorithm's empty tree OID in a static buffer.

nodes.name: hash_algo_ptr_by_number
nodes.summary: Bounds-checked access to the hash_algos table.

nodes.name: git_hash_alloc
nodes.summary: Allocates an uninitialized hash context on the heap.

nodes.name: git_hash_free
nodes.summary: Frees a heap-allocated hash context.

nodes.name: git_hash_init
nodes.summary: Calls the algorithm's init function and marks the context active.

nodes.name: git_hash_clone
nodes.summary: Clones one active context into another through the algorithm's clone function, with BUG checks.

nodes.name: git_hash_update
nodes.summary: Dispatches update to the algorithm, with a BUG if the context is inactive.

nodes.name: git_hash_final
nodes.summary: Finalizes the hash into bytes and deactivates the context.

nodes.name: git_hash_final_oid
nodes.summary: Finalizes into a struct object_id (with algo set) and deactivates the context.

nodes.name: git_hash_discard
nodes.summary: Releases an active context without producing output.

nodes.name: hash_algo_by_name
nodes.summary: Linear search of the algorithm table by name.

nodes.name: hash_algo_by_id
nodes.summary: Linear search of the algorithm table by four-byte format id.

nodes.name: hash_algo_by_length
nodes.summary: Linear search of the algorithm table by raw digest size.

nodes.name: unsafe_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Returns the faster unsafe variant of an algorithm if it has one, else the algorithm itself.

nodes.name: oid_common_prefix_hexlen
nodes.summary: Returns how many leading hex characters two object ids share, counting half bytes.

nodes.name: hash.h
nodes.summary: Core hash and object-id header: selects the SHA-1 and SHA-256 backends, defines struct object_id, git_hash_ctx and git_hash_algo, and provides the inline OID helpers (oidcmp, oideq, oidcpy, oidread, is_null_oid) used throughout Git.

nodes.name: hex-ll.c
nodes.summary: Defines the hexval_table lookup table for hexadecimal digits and hex_to_bytes, a dependency-free converter from hex text to bytes.

nodes.name: hex-ll.h
nodes.summary: Low-level hexadecimal helpers with no repository dependencies: hexval, hex2chr and the hex_to_bytes prototype.

nodes.name: hex.c
nodes.summary: Converts between hexadecimal text and object ids: parses hex into struct object_id for a given or any known hash algorithm, and formats hashes or OIDs as hex using a small ring of static buffers or a caller buffer.

nodes.name: object_id
nodes.summary: The object name type: a fixed-size hash buffer (large enough for SHA-256) plus a 32-bit algorithm id.

nodes.name: get_oid_result
nodes.summary: Result codes for object name resolution: found, missing object, ambiguous short name, and symlink-related failures.

nodes.name: git_hash_ctx
nodes.summary: Hash computation context: pointer to the algorithm, a union of SHA-1, unsafe SHA-1 and SHA-256 states, and an active flag.

nodes.name: git_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Descriptor of a hash algorithm: name, format id, raw and hex sizes, block size, init/clone/update/final/discard function pointers, and the empty tree, empty blob and null OIDs.

nodes.name: hashcmp
nodes.summary: Compares two raw hashes, specialized for the two possible digest sizes.

nodes.name: oidcmp
nodes.summary: Three-way comparison of two object ids over the maximum hash width.

nodes.name: oideq
nodes.summary: Tests two object ids for equality.

nodes.name: oidcpy
nodes.summary: Copies an object id including its algorithm field.

nodes.name: oidread
nodes.summary: Builds an object id from a raw hash buffer, zero-padding to the maximum width and setting the algorithm.

nodes.name: oidclr
nodes.summary: Zeroes an object id and sets its algorithm.

nodes.name: oid_set_algo
nodes.summary: Sets the algorithm field of an object id from an algorithm pointer.

nodes.name: is_null_oid
nodes.summary: Tests whether an object id is all zeros.

nodes.name: hexval
nodes.summary: Looks up the value (0 to 15, or negative) of a hex digit in hexval_table.

nodes.name: hex2chr
nodes.summary: Converts two hex digits to one byte, returning a negative value on bad input without reading past short strings.

nodes.name: hex_to_bytes
nodes.summary: Converts pairs of hex digits to bytes using hexval and fails if any digit is invalid.

nodes.name: get_hash_hex_algop
nodes.summary: Decodes rawsz bytes of hex into a hash buffer for the given algorithm, returning -1 on bad digits.

nodes.name: get_hash_hex
nodes.summary: Decodes hex to a raw hash using the repository's default algorithm.

nodes.name: get_oid_hex_algop
nodes.summary: Parses hex into an object_id for a given algorithm, zero-padding and setting the algo field.

nodes.name: get_oid_hex_any
nodes.summary: Tries each known algorithm from longest to shortest and returns the algorithm number that parsed, or unknown.

nodes.name: get_oid_hex
nodes.summary: Parses hex into an object_id using the repository's default algorithm.

nodes.name: parse_oid_hex_algop_impl
nodes.summary: Parses a hex object id for an algorithm and sets the end pointer after the digits.

nodes.name: parse_oid_hex_any
nodes.summary: Parses a hex object id of any supported algorithm and advances the end pointer.

nodes.name: parse_oid_hex
nodes.summary: Parses a hex object id with the default algorithm and advances the end pointer.

nodes.name: hash_to_hex_algop_r
nodes.summary: Formats raw hash bytes as lowercase hex into a caller buffer, defaulting to the repository hash when the algorithm is unset.

nodes.name: oid_to_hex_r
nodes.summary: Formats an object id as hex into a caller-provided buffer.

nodes.name: hash_to_hex_algop
nodes.summary: Formats raw hash bytes as hex into one of four rotating static buffers.

nodes.name: hash_to_hex
nodes.summary: Formats a raw hash as hex using the default algorithm and a rotating static buffer.

nodes.name: oid_to_hex
nodes.summary: Returns the hex of an object id in a rotating static buffer; the most common way to print an OID.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_oid_hex
nodes.summary: Appends the hex of an object id to a strbuf.

nodes.name: json-writer.c
nodes.summary: Incremental JSON writer: builds objects and arrays into a strbuf with correct commas, string escaping, optional pretty-printing and sub-writer embedding, and uses a stack of open brackets to catch misuse with BUG().

nodes.name: kwset.c
nodes.summary: Multiple-keyword set matcher copied from GNU grep (Aho-Corasick and Commentz-Walter style trie, with Boyer-Moore for a single keyword). The diff pickaxe code uses it for fast fixed-string searches.
nodes.languageNotes: K&R-style C with register variables and the obstack allocator; the trie stores reversed keywords so the search can skip ahead from the right.

nodes.name: kwset.h
nodes.summary: Declares the keyword-set API (kwsalloc, kwsincr, kwsprep, kwsexec, kwsfree) and struct kwsmatch, plus the lowercase translation table for case-insensitive search.

nodes.name: levenshtein.c
nodes.summary: Implements a weighted Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance (swap, substitution, insertion, deletion costs) using only three rows of the distance matrix.

nodes.name: levenshtein.h
nodes.summary: Declares the weighted levenshtein() edit-distance function.

nodes.name: line-range.c
nodes.summary: Parser for the -L line-range option of git log -L and git blame -L: accepts line numbers, +N/-N offsets, /regex/ anchors and :funcname ranges, using the userdiff funcname patterns to find function boundaries.

nodes.name: linear-assignment.c
nodes.summary: Implements the Jonker-Volgenant shortest-augmenting-path algorithm for the dense linear assignment problem, used to pair up columns and rows at minimum total cost.

nodes.name: kwsmatch
nodes.summary: Result of a keyword search: index of the matching keyword and the offset and size of the match.

nodes.name: jw_init
nodes.summary: Resets a json_writer to its blank initial state.

nodes.name: jw_release
nodes.summary: Releases the writer's output and bracket-stack strbufs.

nodes.name: append_quoted_string
nodes.summary: Appends a JSON string with quotes and escapes for quotes, backslash, control characters and \uXXXX.

nodes.name: begin
nodes.summary: Opens an object or array, pushing the bracket onto the open stack.

nodes.name: assert_in_object
nodes.summary: BUG() unless the innermost open container is an object.

nodes.name: assert_in_array
nodes.summary: BUG() unless the innermost open container is an array.

nodes.name: maybe_add_comma
nodes.summary: Emits a comma before every member except the first at each level.

nodes.name: fmt_double
nodes.summary: Appends a double with a given number of decimal places.

nodes.name: object_common
nodes.summary: Common prefix of every object member: assert, comma, pretty newline and indent, quoted key and colon.

nodes.name: array_common
nodes.summary: Common prefix of every array element: assert, comma, pretty newline and indent.

nodes.name: jw_object_begin
nodes.summary: Starts a JSON object, compact or pretty.

nodes.name: jw_object_string
nodes.summary: Adds a string member to the current object.

nodes.name: jw_object_double
nodes.summary: Adds a floating-point member with the given precision.

nodes.name: increase_indent
nodes.summary: Copies a pretty JSON buffer, adding extra indentation after each newline.

nodes.name: kill_indent
nodes.summary: Copies a pretty JSON buffer into compact form by dropping newlines and following indentation.

nodes.name: append_sub_jw
nodes.summary: Embeds another finished writer's JSON, re-indenting or compacting it to match the parent's mode.

nodes.name: jw_object_sub_jw
nodes.summary: Adds a finished sub-writer as an object member.

nodes.name: jw_object_inline_begin_object
nodes.summary: Starts a nested object as a member of the current object.

nodes.name: jw_array_begin
nodes.summary: Starts a JSON array, compact or pretty.

nodes.name: jw_array_string
nodes.summary: Appends a string element to the current array.

nodes.name: jw_array_sub_jw
nodes.summary: Appends a finished sub-writer as an array element.

nodes.name: jw_array_argv
nodes.summary: Appends each string of a NULL-terminated argv as array elements.

nodes.name: jw_is_terminated
nodes.summary: Returns true when every opened object and array has been closed.

nodes.name: jw_end
nodes.summary: Closes the innermost object or array and emits the matching bracket, with pretty newline.

nodes.name: tree
nodes.summary: Node of a balanced binary tree holding the labelled edges that leave one trie node.

nodes.name: trie
nodes.summary: Trie node for a set of reversed keywords: accepting index, outgoing edge tree, parent, Aho-Corasick failure link and shift values.

nodes.name: kwset
nodes.summary: Opaque keyword-set object: obstack, trie, min and max depth, delta table, root children cache and the single-keyword target for Boyer-Moore.

nodes.name: kwsalloc
nodes.summary: Allocates a keyword set with an empty root trie node on an obstack and stores the optional translation table.

nodes.name: kwsincr
nodes.summary: Inserts one keyword (reversed) into the trie, creating nodes and keeping the edge trees balanced, and tracks min and max depth.

nodes.name: treefails
nodes.summary: Computes Aho-Corasick failure links for the children in an edge tree by walking the parent's failure chain.

nodes.name: treedelta
nodes.summary: Fills the delta (skip) table entries for the labels of an edge tree.

nodes.name: hasevery
nodes.summary: Tests whether one edge tree contains every label of another.

nodes.name: kwsprep
nodes.summary: Finishes the set: builds the level-order queue, failure function, shift values and delta table, or picks the single-keyword Boyer-Moore target.

nodes.name: bmexec
nodes.summary: Boyer-Moore search used when the set has exactly one keyword and no translation.

nodes.name: cwexec
nodes.summary: Commentz-Walter style search over the trie for several keywords, returning the leftmost longest match.

nodes.name: kwsexec
nodes.summary: Dispatches to bmexec for a single keyword or cwexec otherwise and fills the kwsmatch result.

nodes.name: kwsfree
nodes.summary: Frees the obstack and the keyword set.

nodes.name: levenshtein
nodes.summary: Dynamic-programming Damerau-Levenshtein distance keeping three rows, with separate costs for swap, substitution, addition and deletion.

nodes.name: parse_loc
nodes.summary: Parses one endpoint of a -L range: a number, +N/-N offset or /regex/ anchor, resolving it to a line number via a line callback.

nodes.name: match_funcname
nodes.summary: Decides if a line starts a function, using the userdiff funcname matcher or a simple alpha, underscore or dollar heuristic.

nodes.name: find_funcname_matching_regexp
nodes.summary: Scans forward for a line matching the regex that also looks like a function header.

nodes.name: parse_range_funcname
nodes.summary: Handles the :funcname form of -L: finds the function line from the anchor via the userdiff driver and extends the range to the next function.

nodes.name: parse_range_arg
nodes.summary: Parses a full -L argument (begin,end or :funcname) into 1-based begin and end lines, swapping them when reversed.

nodes.name: skip_range_arg
nodes.summary: Skips over a -L range argument without resolving lines and returns the pointer after it.

nodes.name: compute_assignment
nodes.summary: Jonker-Volgenant solver: column reduction, reduction transfer, augmenting row reduction and shortest-path augmentation fill column2row and row2column at minimum cost.

nodes.name: linear-assignment.h
nodes.summary: Declares compute_assignment and the COST_MAX bound that keeps cost sums from overflowing int.

nodes.name: lockfile.c
nodes.summary: Implements Git's lock files (path.lock) used for atomic updates of refs, the index and config: resolves symlinks, creates the lock with an accompanying pid file, retries with randomized quadratic backoff, reports who holds a lock, and commits or rolls back.

nodes.name: loose.c
nodes.summary: Maintains the loose-object-idx file that maps object ids between the repository hash algorithm and the compatibility hash algorithm (SHA-1 and SHA-256 interop) for loose objects, with in-memory khash maps and a locked, appended on-disk format.

nodes.name: loose.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct loose_object_map (two khash maps, to_compat and to_storage) and the functions that load, query, extend, write and clear the loose-object id mapping.

nodes.name: ls-refs.c
nodes.summary: Server side of the protocol v2 ls-refs command: reads the client's arguments (peel, symrefs, ref-prefix, unborn), walks matching refs while honoring hidden-ref config and namespaces, and writes one pkt-line per ref with optional symref-target and peeled values.

nodes.name: loose_object_map
nodes.summary: Pair of khash maps relating object ids in the storage hash algorithm and in the compatibility hash algorithm.

nodes.name: trim_last_path_component
nodes.summary: Removes the final path component from a strbuf, keeping the preceding slash.

nodes.name: resolve_symlink
nodes.summary: Follows a chain of symlinks (up to 5) and replaces the path with the real target so locks are created next to it.

nodes.name: create_lock_pid_file
nodes.summary: Creates path.lock.pid-style file recording the owner's pid with O_EXCL, if pid files are enabled.

nodes.name: read_lock_pid
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the pid stored in a lock's pid file.

nodes.name: lock_file
nodes.summary: Creates the .lock tempfile (after optionally resolving symlinks) and its pid file, returning the descriptor or -1.

nodes.name: lock_file_timeout
nodes.summary: Retries lock_file with randomized quadratic backoff until a timeout, only on EEXIST.

nodes.name: unable_to_lock_message
nodes.summary: Builds the 'Unable to create ...lock' message, adding the holding pid and a hint about removing a stale lock.

nodes.name: unable_to_lock_die
nodes.summary: Dies with the unable-to-lock message.

nodes.name: hold_lock_file_for_update_timeout_mode
nodes.summary: Takes a lock using the global repository.

nodes.name: repo_hold_lock_file_for_update_timeout_mode
nodes.summary: Takes a lock with timeout and mode, optionally dying or reporting when it fails.

nodes.name: get_locked_file_path
nodes.summary: Returns the path being locked by stripping .lock from the lock tempfile's path.

nodes.name: commit_lock_file
nodes.summary: Deletes the pid file and renames the lock file over the target, atomically publishing the new content.

nodes.name: rollback_lock_file
nodes.summary: Deletes the pid file and the lock file, discarding changes.

nodes.name: loose_object_map_init
nodes.summary: Allocates a loose_object_map with two empty khash maps.

nodes.name: insert_oid_pair
nodes.summary: Inserts a copied OID value under a key in a khash map unless the key exists.

nodes.name: insert_loose_map
nodes.summary: Adds both directions of an OID pair to the maps and registers the compat OID in the loose oidtree cache.

nodes.name: loose_object_map_load
nodes.summary: Seeds the maps with the empty tree, empty blob and null OIDs, then parses loose-object-idx (header line and 'oid compat_oid' lines).

nodes.name: repo_read_loose_object_map
nodes.summary: Loads the loose object map of every files-based object source.

nodes.name: repo_write_loose_object_map
nodes.summary: Writes the whole map to loose-object-idx under a lock file, skipping empty tree and blob entries, and commits it.

nodes.name: write_one_object
nodes.summary: Appends one OID pair line to loose-object-idx while holding its lock, writing the header if the file is new.

nodes.name: repo_add_loose_object_map
nodes.summary: Inserts an OID pair in memory and persists it when it is new.

nodes.name: repo_loose_object_map_oid
nodes.summary: Looks up the counterpart OID in the other hash algorithm across all object sources.

nodes.name: loose_object_map_clear
nodes.summary: Frees all stored OIDs, both khash maps and the container.

nodes.name: unborn_config
nodes.summary: Reads lsrefs.unborn (advertise, allow or ignore), defaulting to advertise, and dies on bad values.

nodes.name: ref_match
nodes.summary: Returns true if the refname starts with any of the client's ref-prefix values, or when none were given.

nodes.name: ls_refs_data
nodes.summary: Per-request state of ls-refs: peel and symrefs flags, requested prefixes, output buffer, hidden refs and unborn flag.

nodes.name: send_ref
nodes.summary: Formats one ref as 'oid name' (or 'unborn name') with optional symref-target and peeled fields, skipping hidden or non-matching refs, and writes it as a pkt-line.

nodes.name: send_possibly_unborn_head
nodes.summary: Sends HEAD, and for an unborn HEAD that is a symref sends 'unborn' when the client asked for it.

nodes.name: ls_refs_config
nodes.summary: Config callback collecting uploadpack hide-refs settings.

nodes.name: ls_refs
nodes.summary: Handles a v2 ls-refs request: reads arguments from pkt-lines, sends HEAD, enumerates refs for the requested prefixes through send_ref and ends with a flush packet.

nodes.name: ls_refs_advertise
nodes.summary: Adds 'unborn' to the capability advertisement when lsrefs.unborn is advertise.

nodes.name: mailinfo.c
nodes.summary: Core of git mailinfo and git am's email parsing: reads RFC 2822 headers, decodes MIME encodings (quoted-printable, base64, RFC 2047 words, format=flowed), handles multipart boundaries and in-body headers, splits the message into commit message and patch, and prints Author/Email/Subject/Date.

nodes.name: mailinfo.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct mailinfo (parser state for one email), the quoted-CR policy enum, and the setup_mailinfo, mailinfo and clear_mailinfo entry points.

nodes.name: merge-ll.c
nodes.summary: Low-level three-way file merge: selects a merge driver per path from the merge and conflict-marker-size gitattributes, runs the built-in text (xdiff), binary or union drivers or a user-defined external command, optionally renormalizes inputs, and offers helpers to detect conflict markers.

nodes.name: quoted_cr_action
nodes.summary: Enum for what to do with CRLF line endings found in a quoted-printable or MIME body: unset, nowarn, warn or strip.

nodes.name: mailinfo
nodes.summary: Parser state for one email: input/output/patch files, parsed name and email, header and body options (scissors, in-body headers, charset), MIME boundary stack, transfer encoding and accumulated log message.

nodes.name: cleanup_space
nodes.summary: Collapses runs of whitespace in a strbuf to single spaces.

nodes.name: get_sane_name
nodes.summary: Falls back to the email address when the display name is empty, too long or contains @ < >.

nodes.name: parse_bogus_from
nodes.summary: Fallback parser for a 'Name <addr>' From line without a proper @ address.

nodes.name: unquote_comment
nodes.summary: Copies an RFC 2822 parenthesized comment with nesting and backslash escapes.

nodes.name: unquote_quoted_string
nodes.summary: Copies a quoted string, resolving backslash escapes.

nodes.name: unquote_quoted_pair
nodes.summary: Removes quoting from a header line while preserving comments.

nodes.name: handle_from
nodes.summary: Extracts the author name and email from a From header, handling quoted pairs, comments and angle-bracket forms.

nodes.name: slurp_attr
nodes.summary: Extracts a MIME attribute value (such as boundary= or charset=) from a header line.

nodes.name: handle_content_type
nodes.summary: Processes Content-Type: pushes multipart boundaries and records format=flowed, delsp and charset.

nodes.name: cleanup_subject
nodes.summary: Strips Re: prefixes and, unless kept, bracketed tags like [PATCH] from the subject.

nodes.name: is_format_patch_separator
nodes.summary: Recognizes the fake 'From <sha> Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001' line written by format-patch.

nodes.name: decode_q_segment
nodes.summary: Decodes quoted-printable text (and RFC 2047 underscores).

nodes.name: decode_b_segment
nodes.summary: Decodes base64 text.

nodes.name: convert_to_utf8
nodes.summary: Re-encodes a line from the declared charset to the metainfo charset.

nodes.name: decode_header
nodes.summary: Decodes RFC 2047 encoded-words (=?charset?Q|B?...?=) in a header into the output charset.

nodes.name: check_header
nodes.summary: Tests a line against From, Subject and Date plus Content-Type, Content-Transfer-Encoding and Message-ID headers and stores or handles the value.

nodes.name: is_inbody_header
nodes.summary: Returns whether a line looks like an in-body header (From, Subject or Date).

nodes.name: decode_transfer_encoding
nodes.summary: Decodes a line by the current Content-Transfer-Encoding (quoted-printable or base64).

nodes.name: patchbreak
nodes.summary: Detects where the commit message ends and the patch begins (diff -, Index:, ---).

nodes.name: is_scissors_line
nodes.summary: Heuristically recognizes a scissors line such as '-- >8 --'.

nodes.name: check_inbody_header
nodes.summary: Handles in-body header lines, including continuations, [PATCH] subjects and >From separators.

nodes.name: handle_commit_msg
nodes.summary: Processes a line of the commit message part: in-body headers, charset conversion, scissors reset, patch-break detection, and appends to the log message.

nodes.name: handle_filter
nodes.summary: Routes each line to commit-message handling first and to the patch file once the patch begins.

nodes.name: is_rfc2822_header
nodes.summary: Checks that a line is shaped like an RFC 2822 header (field name then colon) or an mbox From line.

nodes.name: read_one_header_line
nodes.summary: Reads one logical header, unfolding continuation lines, and reports false at the end of the header block.

nodes.name: find_boundary
nodes.summary: Skips input lines until the next multipart boundary.

nodes.name: handle_boundary
nodes.summary: Processes a multipart boundary: pops finished sections, resets encoding and reads the part's headers.

nodes.name: handle_filter_flowed
nodes.summary: Handles format=flowed text (soft line breaks, space-stuffing, signature separator) and quoted CRLF before filtering.

nodes.name: handle_body
nodes.summary: Main body loop: walks boundaries, decodes transfer encodings and feeds complete lines to the filter.

nodes.name: handle_info
nodes.summary: Prints the final Author, Email, Subject and Date lines (preferring in-body headers when a patch exists) with cleanup.

nodes.name: mailinfo
nodes.summary: Top-level routine: opens the message and patch files, parses the email headers and body, writes the commit message and prints the header summary.

nodes.name: mailinfo_parse_quoted_cr_action
nodes.summary: Parses nowarn, warn or strip into the quoted CR action.

nodes.name: git_mailinfo_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for mailinfo.scissors and mailinfo.quotedCR, deferring other keys to the default config.

nodes.name: setup_mailinfo
nodes.summary: Zeroes and initializes a mailinfo, sets defaults and reads config.

nodes.name: clear_mailinfo
nodes.summary: Releases all buffers, header data and the boundary stack of a mailinfo.

nodes.name: ll_merge_driver
nodes.summary: Descriptor of a low-level merge driver: name, description, merge function pointer, recursive-driver name and (for external drivers) a command line.

nodes.name: load_merge_attributes
nodes.summary: Lazily creates the attribute check for merge and conflict-marker-size.

nodes.name: reset_merge_attributes
nodes.summary: Frees the cached merge attribute check.

nodes.name: ll_binary_merge
nodes.summary: Built-in binary merge: no content merge, takes ours, theirs or the ancestor depending on options, otherwise reports a binary conflict.

nodes.name: ll_xdl_merge
nodes.summary: Built-in text three-way merge through xdl_merge, falling back to the binary driver for large or binary inputs.

nodes.name: ll_union_merge
nodes.summary: Text merge that keeps both sides' lines instead of conflicting.

nodes.name: create_temp
nodes.summary: Writes a merge input to a temporary file for an external driver.

nodes.name: ll_ext_merge
nodes.summary: Runs a user-configured merge driver command with %O %A %B %L %P placeholders and reads the result back from the A file.

nodes.name: read_merge_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading merge.default and merge.<name>.name, driver, recursive.

nodes.name: initialize_ll_merge
nodes.summary: Loads merge driver config once.

nodes.name: find_ll_merge_driver
nodes.summary: Maps a merge attribute value to a driver: set means text, unset uses merge.default, then user and built-in drivers by name.

nodes.name: normalize_file
nodes.summary: Applies line-ending normalization to a merge input.

nodes.name: ll_merge
nodes.summary: Entry point of low-level merge: normalizes inputs if asked, reads merge and marker-size attributes, picks a driver (the recursive variant for virtual ancestors) and runs it.

nodes.name: ll_merge_marker_size
nodes.summary: Reads the conflict-marker-size attribute for a path with validation and default.

nodes.name: is_conflict_marker_line
nodes.summary: Tests whether a line is a conflict marker (<<<<, ====, >>>> or ||||) of the given size.

nodes.name: has_conflict_markers
nodes.summary: Scans a file for conflict markers, stopping at binary content.

nodes.name: merge-ort-wrappers.c
nodes.summary: Compatibility wrappers that let older callers use the merge-ort engine through merge_ort_nonrecursive, merge_ort_recursive and merge_ort_generic: they check that the index matches HEAD, run the in-core merge, and switch the working tree and index to the result.

nodes.name: unclean
nodes.summary: Checks that the index matches HEAD's tree before a merge and reports the files that would be overwritten.

nodes.name: merge_ort_nonrecursive
nodes.summary: Runs merge-ort for one merge base: checks cleanliness, handles already-up-to-date, merges in core and switches to the result.

nodes.name: merge_ort_recursive
nodes.summary: Runs the recursive (multi-base) merge-ort merge and switches the worktree and index to the result.

nodes.name: get_ref
nodes.summary: Resolves an object id to a commit, peeling tags and wrapping a bare tree in a virtual commit.

nodes.name: merge_ort_generic
nodes.summary: Generic merge entry point taking OIDs: resolves commits and bases, locks the index, runs the recursive merge and writes the index.

nodes.name: graph.c
nodes.summary: Implements the ASCII commit graph drawn by git log --graph. A small state machine (padding, skip, pre-commit, pre-root, commit, post-merge, collapsing) tracks the columns of in-flight parent commits and emits one text line at a time, so the revision walk output can be decorated with branch lines.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a function-local state enum with a big switch in graph_next_line; column arrays are swapped (columns/new_columns, mapping/old_mapping) on each commit rather than reallocated.

nodes.name: parse_graph_colors_config
nodes.summary: Splits the log.graphColors comma-separated string into a strvec of validated color escape codes.

nodes.name: graph_set_column_colors
nodes.summary: Installs the global array of column colors used when drawing graph lines.

nodes.name: diff_output_prefix_callback
nodes.summary: Diff output_prefix callback that builds the graph prefix for the current line so diff output lines up under the graph.

nodes.name: graph_setup_line_prefix
nodes.summary: Registers the graph prefix callback on a diff_options when none is set, so graph lines can be prefixed even without a graph object.

nodes.name: graph_read_config
nodes.summary: Reads log.graphColors and falls back to the built-in ANSI color list for the graph.

nodes.name: graph_init
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes a git_graph for a rev_info, reads color config, sizes the column arrays and hooks the diff output prefix callback.

nodes.name: graph_clear
nodes.summary: Frees all arrays owned by a git_graph and the graph itself.

nodes.name: graph_ensure_capacity
nodes.summary: Grows the column and mapping arrays by doubling until they can hold the requested number of columns.

nodes.name: graph_is_interesting
nodes.summary: Decides whether a commit will be printed in the graph (lookahead, boundary, UNINTERESTING and revision-limit rules).

nodes.name: next_interesting_parent
nodes.summary: Walks the parent list from a given parent and returns the next one that the graph will display.

nodes.name: first_interesting_parent
nodes.summary: Returns the first parent of the current commit that is shown in the graph, or NULL if there is none.

nodes.name: graph_find_commit_color
nodes.summary: Finds the color of the existing column that is waiting for the given commit.

nodes.name: graph_find_new_column_by_commit
nodes.summary: Linear search of new_columns for the column that already tracks a commit.

nodes.name: graph_insert_into_new_columns
nodes.summary: Places a parent commit into new_columns (reusing a column if it is already tracked) and records the mapping from old column to new column.

nodes.name: graph_update_columns
nodes.summary: Recomputes the column layout for the next commit: swaps arrays, inserts the parents of the current commit and builds the old-to-new column mapping used by later lines.

nodes.name: graph_num_expansion_rows
nodes.summary: Number of extra rows needed before a merge commit with many parents (two per dashed parent).

nodes.name: graph_pop_lookahead
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the oldest commit from the two-slot lookahead buffer.

nodes.name: graph_get_lookahead_room
nodes.summary: Reports how many free slots remain in the lookahead buffer.

nodes.name: graph_push_lookahead
nodes.summary: Appends a commit to the lookahead buffer used to peek at upcoming commits.

nodes.name: graph_is_visual_root_candidate
nodes.summary: True when a commit has no displayed parents and is not a boundary commit, so it may start a new visual root.

nodes.name: graph_is_visual_root
nodes.summary: Combines candidate status, column state and lookahead flags to decide whether the commit is drawn as a visual root.

nodes.name: graph_peek_next_visible
nodes.summary: Uses the lookahead buffer to fill flags about the next visible commit (visible, visual root, has column).

nodes.name: graph_update
nodes.summary: Advances the graph to a new commit: counts displayed parents, updates columns, computes visual-root cascade and chooses the next output state.

nodes.name: graph_is_mapping_correct
nodes.summary: Sanity check that the column mapping array only moves columns left by at most one position per row.

nodes.name: graph_pad_horizontally
nodes.summary: Pads a graph line with spaces up to the graph width so messages line up.

nodes.name: graph_output_padding_line
nodes.summary: Emits a line that only carries the vertical column lines (no commit).

nodes.name: graph_width
nodes.summary: Returns the display width of the graph columns for the current commit, used to align messages and wrapping.

nodes.name: graph_output_skip_line
nodes.summary: Emits the ... line shown when commits were hidden between two displayed commits and moves to the next state.

nodes.name: graph_output_pre_commit_line
nodes.summary: Emits an expansion row that widens the columns to the right of an octopus merge commit.

nodes.name: graph_output_commit_char
nodes.summary: Writes the symbol for the commit (o for boundary, otherwise the revision mark such as * or <).

nodes.name: graph_draw_octopus_merge
nodes.summary: Draws the horizontal dashes joining the extra parents of an octopus merge.

nodes.name: graph_output_commit_line
nodes.summary: Emits the line that contains the commit symbol and the other column lines, and picks the next state (post-merge, collapsing or padding).

nodes.name: graph_output_post_merge_line
nodes.summary: Emits the row after a merge commit that fans the parent lines out to their columns.

nodes.name: graph_output_collapsing_line
nodes.summary: Emits one row of lines collapsing toward the left using the old and new column mappings, including horizontal edges.

nodes.name: graph_output_pre_root_line
nodes.summary: Emits the connecting row drawn before a visual root commit that needs indentation.

nodes.name: graph_next_line
nodes.summary: Public step function: switches on the current state, writes the next graph line into a strbuf and returns whether it was the commit line.

nodes.name: graph_padding_line
nodes.summary: Produces a padding line that keeps columns intact, with extra spacing for commits with many parents.

nodes.name: graph_is_commit_finished
nodes.summary: True once all graph lines for the current commit were output (state is padding).

nodes.name: graph_show_commit
nodes.summary: Prints graph lines up to and including the commit line, preceded by any line prefix.

nodes.name: graph_show_oneline
nodes.summary: Prints exactly one graph line, used for lines of the commit message and header.

nodes.name: graph_show_padding
nodes.summary: Prints a graph padding line to the diff output file.

nodes.name: graph_show_remainder
nodes.summary: Prints the remaining graph lines for the commit after its message has been written.

nodes.name: graph_show_strbuf
nodes.summary: Writes a multi-line strbuf, inserting a graph line before each line after the first.

nodes.name: graph_show_commit_msg
nodes.summary: Writes a commit message with graph columns beside every line and then flushes any remaining graph lines.

nodes.name: column
nodes.summary: One column of the graph: the parent commit it is waiting for, its color index and whether it came from a non-first merge parent.

nodes.name: graph_state
nodes.summary: Enum of the line kinds the graph state machine can emit (padding, skip, pre-commit, pre-root, commit, post-merge, collapsing).

nodes.name: graph_line
nodes.summary: Output buffer plus running display width for the line currently being assembled.

nodes.name: git_graph
nodes.summary: Full state of the graph renderer: current commit, rev_info, column and mapping arrays, expansion row, lookahead buffer and visual-root bookkeeping.

nodes.name: graph_lookahead_flags
nodes.summary: Flags produced by peeking at the next visible commit (is it visible, a visual root, does it already have a column).

nodes.name: graph.h
nodes.summary: Public API of the commit graph renderer used by git log --graph: create and clear a graph, feed it commits, pull graph lines one at a time and print them beside commit messages, plus a small lookahead buffer used by the revision walk.

nodes.name: help.c
nodes.summary: Implements the help machinery of the git command: listing builtin and external commands from command-list.h and PATH, printing categorized command lists, suggesting the closest command (Levenshtein distance and help.autocorrect) for a mistyped name, suggesting refs, and git version output.
nodes.languageNotes: Command names are stored as flexible-array structs; the len field is reused to hold a Levenshtein similarity score while ranking suggestions.

nodes.name: drop_prefix
nodes.summary: Strips the git- or gitfoo- style prefix from a command name depending on its category.

nodes.name: extract_cmds
nodes.summary: Copies the entries of the generated command_list table whose category matches a mask into a new array.

nodes.name: print_command_list
nodes.summary: Prints command names and their one-line help aligned to a common column width.

nodes.name: print_cmd_by_category
nodes.summary: Builds, sorts and prints commands grouped under each category heading and reports the longest name.

nodes.name: add_cmdname
nodes.summary: Appends a name to a cmdnames list, allocating the flexible-array entry.

nodes.name: cmdnames_release
nodes.summary: Frees every entry and the array of a cmdnames list.

nodes.name: uniq
nodes.summary: Removes adjacent duplicate names from a sorted cmdnames list.

nodes.name: exclude_cmds
nodes.summary: Removes from a sorted list every name that also appears in a second sorted list.

nodes.name: pretty_print_cmdnames
nodes.summary: Prints a cmdnames list in columns using the column.ui configuration.

nodes.name: list_commands_in_dir
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for executable files with the git- prefix and adds their names to a list.

nodes.name: load_command_list
nodes.summary: Builds the list of builtin plus git-exec-path commands and the list of other commands found along PATH, sorted and de-duplicated.

nodes.name: get_colopts
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads column.* options for command list output.

nodes.name: list_commands
nodes.summary: Prints the available main and external commands in columns for git help -a style output.

nodes.name: list_common_cmds_help
nodes.summary: Prints the short list of common Git commands grouped by purpose.

nodes.name: list_all_main_cmds
nodes.summary: Fills a string list with all main commands (builtin and in exec-path).

nodes.name: list_all_other_cmds
nodes.summary: Fills a string list with commands found on PATH outside the exec path.

nodes.name: list_cmds_by_category
nodes.summary: Appends all commands of a named category to a string list, dying on an unknown category.

nodes.name: list_cmds_by_config
nodes.summary: Applies completion.commands config, adding or removing (-name) entries on a command list.

nodes.name: list_guides_help
nodes.summary: Prints the list of Git concept guides.

nodes.name: list_user_interfaces_help
nodes.summary: Prints user-facing repository, command and file interfaces.

nodes.name: list_developer_interfaces_help
nodes.summary: Prints file formats, protocols and other developer interfaces.

nodes.name: list_all_cmds_help_external_commands
nodes.summary: Prints the External commands section for git help --all.

nodes.name: list_all_cmds_help_aliases
nodes.summary: Prints the Command aliases section built from configured aliases, aligned with the longest name.

nodes.name: list_all_cmds_help
nodes.summary: Prints the full help --all output: categorized commands, then optionally external commands and aliases.

nodes.name: is_in_cmdlist
nodes.summary: Linear membership test of a name in a cmdnames list.

nodes.name: parse_autocorrect
nodes.summary: Parses help.autocorrect values (bool, prompt, never, immediate, show) into an internal mode.

nodes.name: git_unknown_cmd_config
nodes.summary: Early-config callback that reads help.autocorrect and collects alias names.

nodes.name: add_cmd_list
nodes.summary: Moves all entries of one cmdnames list into another.

nodes.name: help_unknown_cmd
nodes.summary: Handles an unknown command: loads all commands and aliases, ranks them by Levenshtein distance, and either autocorrects, prompts, or prints did-you-mean suggestions and exits.

nodes.name: get_version_info
nodes.summary: Writes git version and optional build details (cpu, commit, library versions, hash backends, ref format) into a strbuf.

nodes.name: cmd_version
nodes.summary: Entry point of git version: parses --build-options and prints the version info.

nodes.name: append_similar_ref
nodes.summary: Ref iteration callback that collects remote-tracking refs whose last component matches a base name.

nodes.name: guess_refs
nodes.summary: Iterates all refs to find remote branches with the same short name as a mistyped ref.

nodes.name: help_unknown_ref
nodes.summary: Prints an error for an unknown ref with did-you-mean candidates from remotes and exits.

nodes.name: category_description
nodes.summary: Pairs a command category bitmask with the heading text printed above that group of commands.

nodes.name: help_unknown_cmd_config
nodes.summary: Holds the parsed help.autocorrect setting and the list of alias names while reading early config.

nodes.name: help.h
nodes.summary: Declares the command listing and help helpers (cmdnames lists, categorized command printing, unknown command and ref suggestions, version info) and a few inline helpers and macros for building config name lists for completion.

nodes.name: cmdnames
nodes.summary: Sorted list of command names (flexible-array entries) used when discovering builtin, exec-path and PATH commands.

nodes.name: load_builtin_commands
nodes.summary: Declared here and defined in the main git program: loads the builtin command names into a cmdnames list.

nodes.name: line-log.c
nodes.summary: Implements git log -L (line-level history): parses -L ranges, keeps per-commit sets of line ranges per file in a decoration, and walks history by diffing each commit against its parent and mapping the ranges across the diff hunks to find commits that touched those lines.
nodes.languageNotes: Range sets are sorted vectors of half-open ranges; set union, difference and shifting by diff hunks are hand-written merge loops over two sorted arrays.

nodes.name: range_set_init
nodes.summary: Initializes an empty range set, optionally pre-allocating space.

nodes.name: range_set_release
nodes.summary: Frees the range array of a range set and zeroes it.

nodes.name: range_set_append_unsafe
nodes.summary: Appends a range at the end without checking order against the previous range.

nodes.name: range_set_append
nodes.summary: Appends a range, asserting that it starts at or after the end of the last range.

nodes.name: range_cmp
nodes.summary: qsort comparator ordering ranges by start line.

nodes.name: range_set_check_invariants
nodes.summary: Asserts that ranges are non-empty, sorted and non-overlapping.

nodes.name: sort_and_merge_range_set
nodes.summary: Sorts a range set and merges overlapping or touching ranges in place.

nodes.name: range_set_union
nodes.summary: Computes the union of two sorted range sets with a two-pointer merge.

nodes.name: range_set_difference
nodes.summary: Computes the set difference of two sorted range sets.

nodes.name: search_line_log_data
nodes.summary: Finds the line_log_data entry for a path in a path-sorted list and optionally reports the insertion point.

nodes.name: line_log_data_insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a new range for a path, appending to an existing entry or creating a new sorted list node.

nodes.name: collect_diff_cb
nodes.summary: xdiff hunk callback that appends the parent and target ranges of each hunk.

nodes.name: collect_diff
nodes.summary: Runs xdi_diff with zero context to record the pre-image and post-image ranges of each hunk.

nodes.name: dump_diff_ranges
nodes.summary: Debug helper that prints the parent and target ranges of a diff.

nodes.name: diff_ranges_filter_touched
nodes.summary: Selects the diff hunks that overlap at least one interesting range in the target.

nodes.name: range_set_shift_diff
nodes.summary: Shifts line numbers in a range set by the cumulative added and removed lines of the diff.

nodes.name: range_set_map_across_diff
nodes.summary: Maps interesting ranges from the target file to the parent file across a diff, returning the touched hunks.

nodes.name: check_single_commit
nodes.summary: Verifies that -L is used with exactly one starting commit and returns it.

nodes.name: fill_blob_sha1
nodes.summary: Looks up a path in a commit tree and fills a diff_filespec with the blob oid and mode.

nodes.name: fill_line_ends
nodes.summary: Reads a blob and records the byte offset of each line end plus the line count.

nodes.name: nth_line
nodes.summary: Callback returning a pointer to the start of the nth line of a file buffer.

nodes.name: parse_lines
nodes.summary: Parses all -L arguments into a sorted list of per-file line ranges for a commit, validating bounds against the real file.

nodes.name: line_log_data_copy_one
nodes.summary: Deep copies a single line_log_data node.

nodes.name: line_log_data_copy
nodes.summary: Deep copies a linked list of line_log_data nodes.

nodes.name: line_log_data_merge
nodes.summary: Merges two path-sorted line_log_data lists, taking the union of ranges for equal paths.

nodes.name: add_line_range
nodes.summary: Stores or merges the line ranges to track for a commit in the line_log_data decoration of the rev_info.

nodes.name: lookup_line_range
nodes.summary: Returns the tracked line ranges for a commit, if any.

nodes.name: same_paths_in_pathspec_and_range
nodes.summary: Checks whether a pathspec already lists exactly the paths of the ranges.

nodes.name: parse_pathspec_from_ranges
nodes.summary: Builds a pathspec from the file paths mentioned in the -L ranges.

nodes.name: line_log_init
nodes.summary: Public setup: finds the start commit, parses -L args, registers the ranges and sets the pathspec on rev_info.

nodes.name: filter_diffs_for_paths
nodes.summary: Reduces the queued diff to filepairs touching tracked paths, optionally keeping deletions.

nodes.name: diff_might_be_rename
nodes.summary: Checks if the queued diff contains an addition that rename detection could pair.

nodes.name: queue_diffs
nodes.summary: Runs a tree diff between a commit and its parent, applies rename detection, and keeps only tracked paths.

nodes.name: process_diff_filepair
nodes.summary: For one filepair with tracked ranges, diffs the blobs and maps the ranges to the parent version; returns whether lines changed.

nodes.name: process_all_files
nodes.summary: Runs process_diff_filepair on every queued filepair and records the resulting diffs on the range list.

nodes.name: line_log_queue_pairs
nodes.summary: Queues the stored filepairs and their line ranges of a commit into the global diff queue for output.

nodes.name: bloom_filter_check
nodes.summary: Uses the changed-path Bloom filter of a commit to see if tracked paths may have changed, so unchanged commits can be skipped.

nodes.name: process_ranges_ordinary_commit
nodes.summary: Handles a single-parent commit: diffs against the parent and propagates ranges to it.

nodes.name: process_ranges_merge_commit
nodes.summary: Handles a merge commit: tries each parent, and if one parent shows no change follows only that parent.

nodes.name: line_log_process_ranges_arbitrary_commit
nodes.summary: Public entry: processes one commit's ranges (bloom check, merge or ordinary path) and marks the commit TREESAME if nothing changed.

nodes.name: line_log_rewrite_one
nodes.summary: Parent rewrite callback that skips TREESAME parents so the printed history only contains changing commits.

nodes.name: line_log_filter
nodes.summary: Filters the commit list down to commits that changed tracked lines, then rewrites parents.

nodes.name: line_log_free
nodes.summary: Clears the line_log_data decoration and frees all stored range lists.

nodes.name: collect_diff_cbdata
nodes.summary: Callback state that points at the diff_ranges being filled while xdiff reports hunks.

nodes.name: nth_line_cb
nodes.summary: State for the line-number lookup callback: the blob, its line count and an array of line end offsets.

nodes.name: line-log.h
nodes.summary: Declares the data structures and API of line-level history (git log -L): range sets, per-file tracked ranges and the functions that initialize, filter and free line-log state on a rev_info.

nodes.name: diff_ranges
nodes.summary: A diff encoded as the pair of pre-image and post-image range sets of its hunks.

nodes.name: line_log_data
nodes.summary: Linked list node of tracked files, each with its path, line ranges, filepair and diff ranges, kept sorted by path.

nodes.name: line-range.h
nodes.summary: Declares parse_range_arg and skip_range_arg, which parse the begin,end or :funcname parts of a -L argument against a file through a line-lookup callback.

nodes.name: log-tree.c
nodes.summary: Glue between the revision walk and commit output for git log, show and format-patch: loads ref decorations, prints the commit header and message through the pretty printer, runs the per-commit diff (including merge, combined and remerge diffs) and tracks --follow pathspecs across history.

nodes.name: parse_decorate_color_config
nodes.summary: Config handler for color.decorate.<slot> that parses the color for a decoration slot.

nodes.name: add_name_decoration
nodes.summary: Attaches a ref name and decoration type to an object in the global decoration table.

nodes.name: get_name_decoration
nodes.summary: Looks up the ref decorations of an object, loading all ref decorations on first use.

nodes.name: match_ref_pattern
nodes.summary: Matches a ref name against a decoration filter pattern (glob or prefix).

nodes.name: ref_filter_match
nodes.summary: Applies the include, exclude and config-exclude pattern lists to decide if a ref is decorated.

nodes.name: add_ref_decoration
nodes.summary: Ref iteration callback: classifies the ref (head, tag, local, remote, replace) and records it, peeling annotated tags.

nodes.name: load_ref_decorations

nodes.name: load_branch_decorations

nodes.name: format_decorations

nodes.name: show_decorations
nodes.summary: Prints the source ref (if any) and decorations of a commit to the log output.

nodes.name: fmt_output_subject

nodes.name: fmt_output_commit
nodes.summary: Builds the patch file name for a commit by formatting its %f sanitized subject.

nodes.name: fmt_output_email_subject
nodes.summary: Writes the Subject: header with [PATCH n/m] style numbering into a strbuf.

nodes.name: log_write_email_headers
nodes.summary: Prints the From, Message-ID, References and MIME headers that begin each format-patch email.

nodes.name: show_sig_lines
nodes.summary: Prints signature verification output lines with color and graph prefix.

nodes.name: show_signature
nodes.summary: Verifies the GPG signature of a commit and prints the result.

nodes.name: which_parent
nodes.summary: Returns the index of a given commit among the parents of a commit, or -1.

nodes.name: show_one_mergetag
nodes.summary: Verifies and prints one mergetag header (a signed tag merged into the commit).

nodes.name: show_diff_of_diff
nodes.summary: Prints interdiff or range-diff output after a format-patch commit when requested.

nodes.name: show_log
nodes.summary: Prints the log header of a commit: abbreviated oid or full commit line, decorations, signature, notes, then the pretty-printed message with graph columns.

nodes.name: log_tree_diff_flush
nodes.summary: Runs diffcore, prints the log header once when there is diff output, and flushes the diff queue.

nodes.name: setup_additional_headers
nodes.summary: Restricts the remerge path-message map to the pathspec and attaches it to diff options.

nodes.name: cleanup_additional_headers
nodes.summary: Releases the additional path headers installed for a remerge diff.

nodes.name: do_remerge_diff
nodes.summary: Re-does a two-parent merge in memory with merge-ort in a temporary object directory and diffs it against the real merge result.

nodes.name: remember_follow_pathspec
nodes.summary: Stores the current path of a followed file for a commit in a commit slab.

nodes.name: recall_follow_pathspec
nodes.summary: Reads back the followed path stored for a commit.

nodes.name: release_follow_pathspec_slab
nodes.summary: Frees the commit slab used for --follow bookkeeping.

nodes.name: propagate_follow_pathspec_to_parent
nodes.summary: Runs a rename-following diff between a merge commit and a parent to compute the path to follow in that parent.

nodes.name: log_tree_diff
nodes.summary: Decides which diffs to show for a commit (root, merge variants, each parent) and runs the diff and flush for it.

nodes.name: log_tree_commit
nodes.summary: Public entry for showing one commit: applies --follow path, shows diff and header, interdiff, then records paths for parents.

nodes.name: decoration
nodes.summary: Global decoration table mapping objects to the chain of ref names that point at them.

nodes.name: log-tree.h
nodes.summary: Declares the log output entry points (log_tree_commit, show_log, decoration formatting, patch file name helpers) and the log_info and decoration option structs.

nodes.name: log_info
nodes.summary: The commit and optional parent currently being shown by the log machinery.

nodes.name: decoration_filter
nodes.summary: Include, exclude and config-exclude ref pattern lists that restrict which refs are shown as decorations.

nodes.name: decoration_options
nodes.summary: Strings (prefix, suffix, separator, pointer, tag) that customize decoration formatting.

nodes.name: mailmap.c
nodes.summary: Implements the .mailmap mechanism: parses mailmap files, the mailmap.file and mailmap.blob configuration and the repository .mailmap into a sorted string_list, then maps an author or committer name and email to their canonical form.
nodes.languageNotes: Each email key owns a mailmap_entry with a nested name-keyed string_list, giving a two-level lookup (email, then optionally name) with case-insensitive comparison.

nodes.name: free_mailmap_entry
nodes.summary: Frees one mailmap_entry including its nested name map.

nodes.summary: Inserts a mapping from an old name and email to a new name and email into the two-level map.

nodes.name: parse_name_and_email
nodes.summary: Splits a Name <email> segment of a mailmap line in place and returns the remainder of the line.

nodes.name: read_mailmap_line
nodes.summary: Parses one mailmap line (one or two name and email pairs) and adds the mapping.

nodes.name: read_mailmap_file
nodes.summary: Reads a mailmap file from disk (optionally refusing symlinks) line by line.

nodes.name: read_mailmap_string
nodes.summary: Parses a mailmap held in a writable memory buffer line by line, splitting at newlines.

nodes.name: read_mailmap_blob
nodes.summary: Reads a mailmap from a blob named by a revision such as HEAD:.mailmap.

nodes.name: read_mailmap
nodes.summary: Loads the combined mailmap: the work tree .mailmap, the mailmap.blob (HEAD:.mailmap for bare repos) and mailmap.file.

nodes.summary: Frees all entries of a mailmap string_list.

nodes.name: lookup_prefix
nodes.summary: Case-insensitive lookup of a string of given length in the sorted map, tolerating a longer unterminated key.

nodes.name: map_user
nodes.summary: Maps an email and name to their mailmap replacements, in place, and reports whether a mapping applied.

nodes.summary: A replacement name and email pair; either field may be NULL.

nodes.name: mailmap_entry
nodes.summary: Top-level mailmap record for an old email: a default replacement plus a nested map keyed by old name.

nodes.name: mailmap.h
nodes.summary: Declares the mailmap API: reading mailmap files, blobs and repository configuration into a string_list and mapping a name and email to their canonical identity.

nodes.name: merge-ort.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the ort merge strategy: merge_options and merge_result structs and functions to merge in memory (recursive with merge bases or a single base tree), then switch the work tree and index to the result or inspect conflicts.

nodes.name: merge_result
nodes.summary: Outcome of an in-core merge: clean flag, result tree, path messages and private data for later update steps.

nodes.name: merge_options
nodes.summary: Configuration of a merge: ref names for markers, rename detection, xdiff options, verbosity and internal state.

nodes.name: stage_info
nodes.summary: Object id, mode and stage number of one index entry of a conflicted path.

nodes.name: mergesort.h

nodes.name: notes-merge.h

nodes.name: notes_merge_options
nodes.summary: Settings of a notes merge: refs, commit message buffer, verbosity, strategy and whether a notes merge work tree exists.

nodes.name: notes-utils.c

nodes.summary: Commits each rewritten notes tree and frees the rewrite configuration.

nodes.name: notes-utils.h
nodes.summary: Declares helpers on top of the notes API: creating and committing notes commits, the notes merge strategy enum and the structure and functions used to copy notes when commits are rewritten.

nodes.name: notes_merge_strategy
nodes.summary: The conflict resolution strategies of git notes merge (manual, ours, theirs, union, cat_sort_uniq).

nodes.name: notes.c

nodes.name: note_tree_search
nodes.summary: Descends the radix tree by nibbles toward a key, loading subtrees on demand, and returns the slot where the key lives or would live.

nodes.name: note_tree_find
nodes.summary: Returns the leaf for a key if a matching note exists in the tree.

nodes.name: note_tree_consolidate
nodes.summary: Collapses an internal node with a single note child back into its parent slot.

nodes.name: note_tree_remove
nodes.summary: Removes the note for a key and consolidates empty internal nodes up the path.

nodes.name: note_tree_insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a note or subtree entry, splitting leaf slots into internal nodes and combining on conflict with the configured combine function.

nodes.name: note_tree_free
nodes.summary: Recursively frees an entire notes tree.

nodes.name: add_non_note

nodes.name: load_subtree

nodes.name: for_each_note_helper
nodes.summary: Recursive traversal over all notes, optionally yielding subtrees and unpacking them lazily.

nodes.name: tree_write_stack_init_subtree
nodes.summary: Pushes a new subtree buffer onto the write stack.

nodes.name: tree_write_stack_finish_subtree
nodes.summary: Writes the nested subtree objects of the write stack to the object database and adds their entries to the parent.

nodes.name: write_each_note_helper
nodes.summary: Adds one note entry to the correct nested subtree buffer, managing subtree opening and closing.

nodes.name: write_each_non_note_until
nodes.summary: Writes preserved non-note entries that sort before a given note path.

nodes.summary: odb_source callback that updates the mtime of a loose object file so it is not pruned as old.

nodes.name: close_loose_object
nodes.summary: Finalizes a written loose object file: fsyncs it (batched in a transaction or immediately, depending on config) and closes the descriptor.

nodes.name: create_tmpfile
nodes.summary: Creates a tmp_obj_XXXXXX file in the same directory as the final object path, creating the fan-out directory on demand to avoid cross-directory renames.

nodes.name: start_loose_object_common
nodes.summary: Starts writing a loose object: creates the tmpfile, initializes zlib deflate and the hash contexts (plus a compatibility-algorithm context), and feeds in the object header.

nodes.name: write_loose_object_common
nodes.summary: Inner loop step of loose writing: deflates input, updates the hash contexts and writes the compressed bytes to the file.

nodes.name: end_loose_object_common
nodes.summary: Ends the zlib stream and finalizes the computed object id (and compatibility id).

nodes.name: write_loose_object
nodes.summary: Writes one loose object from an in-memory buffer: deflates header and data into a tmpfile while hashing, verifies the id matches, fsyncs, optionally sets mtime and renames it into place.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose_write_object
nodes.summary: odb_source callback that formats the object header, writes the loose object and records the mapping to its compatibility-algorithm id if given.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose_write_object_stream
nodes.summary: Writes a loose object from an input stream when the id is not yet known: streams data through deflate and the hashes into a tmpfile in the objects dir, then freshens or renames it to the final fan-out path.

nodes.name: fsck_loose
nodes.summary: Verifies one loose object during fsck by reading it and comparing the real hash to the path, then hands type, size and contents to the fsck object callback.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose_fsck
nodes.summary: odb_source callback that walks all loose files with progress, running fsck_loose per object and flagging unexpected files and corruption.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose_new
nodes.summary: Allocates a loose source, initializes the base odb_source, wires up every backend callback, registers chdir notification for relative paths and loads the loose object map.

nodes.name: source-loose.h
nodes.summary: Declares the loose-object-only object database source (one zlib-compressed file per object), including its readdir cache bitmap, oidtree cache and loose object map, plus a checked downcast.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose
nodes.summary: Loose backend struct: embeds odb_source, caches readdir results in an oidtree guarded by a 256-bit subdir_seen bitmap for fast existence and abbreviation checks, and holds the map between object ids of different hash algorithms.

nodes.name: odb_source_loose_downcast
nodes.summary: Inline cast from odb_source to odb_source_loose that BUGs when the source type is not ODB_SOURCE_LOOSE.

nodes.name: source.c
nodes.summary: Common helpers for the odb_source abstraction: maps source types to names, creates the default (files) source, and initializes, frees and releases the shared base fields of a source.

nodes.name: odb_source_type_to_name
