nodes.summary: Maps an odb_source_type enum value to its string name (unknown, files, loose, packed, in-memory), BUGging if a name is missing from the table.

nodes.name: odb_source_new
nodes.summary: Creates a new object source for the given odb and path; currently always a files source (loose plus packfiles).

nodes.name: odb_source_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the shared base fields of an odb_source: owning odb, type, locality and a copy of the path.

nodes.name: odb_source_free
nodes.summary: Frees a source by calling its type-specific free callback (NULL is a no-op).

nodes.name: odb_source_release
nodes.summary: Releases the base-owned memory of a source (its path); called by backends from their own free routines.

nodes.name: source.h
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract object database source interface: the source type enum, the odb_source struct with its table of backend callbacks (read, stream, iterate, write, transactions, alternates, optimize, pack generation, fsck) and inline wrappers that dispatch to them.
nodes.languageNotes: Polymorphism in C: odb_source holds function pointers and the static inline odb_source_* wrappers call through them, so backends (files, loose, packed, in-memory) can be swapped without callers knowing.

nodes.name: odb_source_type
nodes.summary: Enum of source backends: unknown, files (loose plus packfiles), loose, packed and in-memory.

nodes.name: odb_source
nodes.summary: Base struct of an object database source (primary or alternate): linked list pointer, path hash entry, owning odb, type, local flag, will_destroy flag, path and callbacks for free, close, create_on_disk, prepare, read_object_info, read_object_stream, for_each_object, count_objects, find_abbrev_len, freshen_object, write_object, write_object_stream, begin_transaction, alternates, optimize, generate_pack and fsck.

nodes.name: odb_source_prepare
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper calling the source prepare callback, optionally flushing caches.

nodes.name: odb_source_read_object_info
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that asks a source for object metadata or content through its read_object_info callback.

nodes.name: odb_source_read_object_stream
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that opens a streaming reader for an object via the source callback.

nodes.name: odb_source_for_each_object
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that iterates the objects of a source through its for_each_object callback.

nodes.name: odb_source_count_objects
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that counts objects in a source (approximate or exact).

nodes.name: odb_source_find_abbrev_len
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that finds the abbreviation length needed to keep an id unique within a source.

nodes.name: odb_source_freshen_object
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that bumps an object mtime in the source to protect it from pruning.

nodes.name: odb_source_write_object
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that writes an object buffer of a given type to the source, with optional compat id, mtime and flags.

nodes.name: odb_source_write_object_stream
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that writes an object from a stream, returning the computed object id.

nodes.name: odb_source_begin_transaction
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that starts an object database transaction on the source.

nodes.name: odb_source_optimize
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that triggers backend optimization (repacking and similar).

nodes.name: odb_source_fsck
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper that runs the backend integrity check.

nodes.name: transaction.c
nodes.summary: Generic object database transaction layer: begin, commit and finalize a single pending transaction on the odb, and forward stream writes, pack writes and environment setup to the transaction callbacks.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_begin
nodes.summary: Starts a transaction on the primary source unless one is already pending, and records it on the object database.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_commit
nodes.summary: Commits the pending transaction through its commit callback (asserting it is the odb current one) and clears the pending pointer.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_finalize
nodes.summary: Runs the optional finalize callback and frees the transaction object.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_write_object_stream
nodes.summary: Forwards a streamed object write to the transaction callback.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_write_pack
nodes.summary: Forwards writing an incoming pack file descriptor to the transaction callback.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_env
nodes.summary: Asks the transaction to contribute environment variables (for child processes); a NULL transaction is a no-op.

nodes.name: oid-array.c
nodes.summary: Growable array of object ids with lazy sorting, binary-search lookup, iteration (all or unique), filtering and clearing; used wherever Git collects sets of object ids.

nodes.name: oid_array_append
nodes.summary: Appends an object id (setting a default hash algorithm if unset) and marks the array unsorted.

nodes.name: void_hashcmp
nodes.summary: qsort comparator that orders object ids first by hash algorithm and then by raw hash bytes.

nodes.name: oid_array_sort
nodes.summary: Sorts the array once (skipped if already sorted).

nodes.name: oid_array_lookup
nodes.summary: Sorts the array if needed and binary-searches it for an object id using oid_pos.

nodes.name: oid_array_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the storage and resets the counters.

nodes.name: oid_array_for_each
nodes.summary: Calls a callback on every entry in current order without sorting, stopping at the first non-zero return.

nodes.name: oid_array_for_each_unique
nodes.summary: Sorts, then calls a callback once per distinct object id, skipping duplicates.

nodes.name: oid_array_filter
nodes.summary: Removes in place the entries for which a predicate callback returns false.

nodes.name: oidmap.c
nodes.summary: Hash map keyed by object id built on the generic hashmap: init, put, get, remove and clear (optionally freeing entries).

nodes.name: oidmap_neq
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback that tests two entries or an entry and a key for object id inequality.

nodes.name: oidmap_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the underlying hashmap with the object id comparison function.

nodes.name: oidmap_clear
nodes.summary: Clears the map, freeing entries with free() when requested.

nodes.name: oidmap_clear_with_free
nodes.summary: Iterates all entries applying a custom free callback, then clears the hashmap.

nodes.name: oidmap_get
nodes.summary: Looks up an entry by object id using the id-derived hash.

nodes.name: oidmap_remove
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the entry for an object id, initializing the map lazily.

nodes.name: oidmap_put
nodes.summary: Inserts or replaces an entry keyed by its object id and returns the old one.

nodes.name: oidtree.c
nodes.summary: Stores object ids in a critbit tree backed by a memory pool, giving ordered storage and efficient enumeration of all ids sharing a hex prefix; used for abbreviation and loose object caches.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds struct cb_node as the first member of oidtree_node and recovers the container with container_of, an intrusive-tree idiom.

nodes.name: oidtree_node
nodes.summary: Tree node: an embedded critbit node, the object id key and an optional data pointer.

nodes.name: oidtree_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the critbit tree keyed on the oid field and its memory pool.

nodes.name: oidtree_clear
nodes.summary: Discards the memory pool and reinitializes the tree.

nodes.name: oidtree_insert
nodes.summary: Allocates a node from the pool and inserts the object id with its payload, overwriting data of a pre-existing entry.

nodes.name: oidtree_lookup
nodes.summary: Finds the node for an exact object id by building a key of the right length and calling cb_lookup.

nodes.name: oidtree_contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether the tree holds the given object id.

nodes.name: oidtree_get
nodes.summary: Returns the payload pointer stored with an object id, or NULL.

nodes.name: iter
nodes.summary: Per-node filter for prefix iteration: checks the hash algorithm and the last odd nibble before calling the user callback.

nodes.name: oidtree_each
nodes.summary: Iterates all ids whose hex prefix (of any length, including odd nibble counts) matches the given id, via cb_each.

nodes.name: oidtree.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the oidtree: a critbit-tree set of object ids with payloads supporting init, clear, insert, lookup and prefix enumeration.

nodes.name: oidtree
nodes.summary: Struct holding the critbit tree and the memory pool its nodes are allocated from.

nodes.name: packfile-list.c
nodes.summary: Singly linked list of packfiles with head and tail pointers: clear, remove, prepend, append (optionally skipping duplicate check) and finding the pack that contains an object id.

nodes.name: packfile_list_clear
nodes.summary: Frees every list entry and resets head and tail (packs themselves are not freed).

nodes.name: packfile_list_remove_internal
nodes.summary: Unlinks and returns the entry holding a given pack, fixing head and tail pointers.

nodes.name: packfile_list_remove
nodes.summary: Removes a pack from the list and frees its entry.

nodes.name: packfile_list_prepend
nodes.summary: Moves or adds a pack at the head of the list (most recently used first).

nodes.name: packfile_list_append
nodes.summary: Adds a pack at the tail, removing an existing entry first unless the duplicate check is skipped.

nodes.name: packfile_list_find_oid
nodes.summary: Walks the list and returns the first pack whose index contains the object id.

nodes.name: packfile-list.h
nodes.summary: Declares the packfile_list linked list types and its operations.

nodes.name: packfile_list
nodes.summary: List header with head and tail pointers to entries.

nodes.name: packfile_list_entry
nodes.summary: List node holding the next pointer and a packed_git.

nodes.name: parse-options.c
nodes.summary: Git command-line option parser: matches short, long, negated, abbreviated, alias and subcommand options against a struct option table, stores typed values (bit, int, string, callback and so on), enforces command-mode exclusivity, drives shell completion output, and prints usage help.

nodes.name: optbug
nodes.summary: Reports a programming error in an option table entry through bug().

nodes.name: optname
nodes.summary: Formats a human-readable name of an option (switch, option or no- form) for error messages.

nodes.name: get_arg
nodes.summary: Obtains an option argument from the attached text, a default or the next argv entry, or errors if it is missing.

nodes.name: do_get_int_value
nodes.summary: Reads an integer from a target pointer according to its declared byte precision.

nodes.name: set_int_value
nodes.summary: Writes an integer into the option target honoring its precision and rejecting values that do not fit.

nodes.name: do_get_value
nodes.summary: Core of option handling: validates unset/no-arg rules and applies the option by type (bit, negbit, countup, set int, string, filename, callback, integer with git_parse_signed, unsigned with git_parse_unsigned).

nodes.name: parse_opt_cmdmode_list
nodes.summary: Linked list that tracks the value of each PARSE_OPT_CMDMODE variable and which option last changed it, used to detect conflicting command modes.

nodes.name: build_cmdmode_list
nodes.summary: Scans the option table and builds the list of command-mode targets with their initial values.

nodes.name: get_value
nodes.summary: Applies an option via do_get_value and then checks that no two command-mode options changed the same variable, erroring with "cannot be used together".

nodes.name: parse_short_opt
nodes.summary: Matches one short option character (or a numeric option) from the current argument.

nodes.name: is_alias
nodes.summary: Tells whether two options belong to the same alias group.

nodes.name: register_abbrev
nodes.summary: Records an abbreviated-option candidate and marks the match ambiguous when two distinct non-alias options match.

nodes.name: parse_long_opt
nodes.summary: Matches a --long option: handles no- negation, exact match, "=value", unique abbreviations and ambiguity errors.

nodes.name: parse_nodash_opt
nodes.summary: Matches options flagged PARSE_OPT_NODASH that appear as a bare letter without a dash.

nodes.name: parse_subcommand
nodes.summary: Matches an argument to a registered subcommand and stores its handler function.

nodes.name: check_typos
nodes.summary: Suggests "--option" when a user typed an option with a single dash that looks like a long option, and exits with 129.

nodes.name: parse_options_check
nodes.summary: Validates an option table for programmer mistakes (duplicate short names, invalid flag combinations, bad help strings, and so on).

nodes.name: parse_options_check_harder
nodes.summary: Additional check that long option names are unique within a table.

nodes.name: parse_options_start_1
nodes.summary: Initializes a parse context from argc/argv and flags, rejects incompatible flag combinations, and builds the command-mode list.

nodes.name: parse_options_start
nodes.summary: Public initializer that zeroes the context and starts parsing.

nodes.name: show_negated_gitcomp
nodes.summary: Prints --no-xxx completion words for options that have an unset form (shell completion helper).

nodes.name: show_gitcomp
nodes.summary: Prints all option names for git-completion.bash and returns PARSE_OPT_COMPLETE.

nodes.name: preprocess_options
nodes.summary: Duplicates the option array substituting OPTION_ALIAS entries with copies of their source options and records alias groups.

nodes.name: free_preprocessed_options
nodes.summary: Frees the preprocessed option array and the help strings made for aliases.

nodes.name: parse_options_step
nodes.summary: Main iteration over argv: classifies each argument as non-option, subcommand, -h/help, completion helper, short, long, "--" or unknown and dispatches to the specific parser.

nodes.name: parse_options_end
nodes.summary: Finishes parsing by compacting the remaining arguments and returning the new argc.

nodes.name: parse_options
nodes.summary: High-level entry point: preprocesses options, runs parse_options_step, handles help, errors and unknown options (printing usage), and returns the count of remaining arguments.

nodes.name: usage_argh
nodes.summary: Prints the argument placeholder of an option (like <path>) in usage text, honoring optional-argument forms.

nodes.name: usage_with_options_internal
nodes.summary: Builds and prints the full usage message: usage lines, option groups with aligned help text and alias and hidden-option handling, to stdout or stderr.

nodes.name: usage_with_options
nodes.summary: Prints usage to stderr and exits with code 129.

nodes.name: show_usage_with_options_if_asked
nodes.summary: Handles a lone -h or --help-all argument by printing usage to stdout and exiting 0.

nodes.name: usage_msg_opt
nodes.summary: Prints an error message and then usage, then exits.

nodes.name: usage_msg_optf
nodes.summary: printf-style variant of usage_msg_opt.

nodes.name: die_for_incompatible_opt4
nodes.summary: Dies with a message listing up to four options that were used together but are mutually incompatible.

nodes.name: parse.c
nodes.summary: Parses numeric and boolean values from strings and environment variables, with k/m/g unit suffixes and overflow checks: the primitives behind git config values and command-line integers.

nodes.name: get_unit_factor
nodes.summary: Maps a k, m or g suffix (case-insensitive) to 1024, 1024^2 or 1024^3; 0 if the suffix is unknown.

nodes.name: git_parse_signed
nodes.summary: Parses a signed integer with an optional unit suffix, setting errno to EINVAL or ERANGE and returning 0 on bad or overflowing input.

nodes.name: git_parse_unsigned
nodes.summary: Parses an unsigned integer with unit suffix, rejecting negatives and multiplication overflow.

nodes.name: git_parse_int
nodes.summary: Parses an int through git_parse_signed with the int maximum.

nodes.name: git_parse_int64
nodes.summary: Parses an int64_t through git_parse_signed.

nodes.name: git_parse_uint
nodes.summary: Parses an unsigned int through git_parse_unsigned.

nodes.name: git_parse_ulong
nodes.summary: Parses an unsigned long through git_parse_unsigned.

nodes.name: git_parse_ssize_t
nodes.summary: Parses a ssize_t through git_parse_signed.

nodes.name: git_parse_size_t
nodes.summary: Parses a size_t through git_parse_unsigned.

nodes.name: git_parse_double
nodes.summary: Parses a double using strtod and applies a unit suffix factor.

nodes.name: git_parse_maybe_bool_text
nodes.summary: Recognizes true/yes/on and false/no/off words (and NULL as true, empty as false) and returns -1 otherwise.

nodes.name: git_parse_maybe_bool
nodes.summary: Parses a boolean from text or, failing that, from an integer (non-zero is true), returning -1 on error.

nodes.name: git_env_bool
nodes.summary: Reads an environment variable as a boolean with a default, dying on a bad value.

nodes.name: git_env_ulong
nodes.summary: Reads an environment variable as an unsigned long with a default, dying if it cannot be parsed.

nodes.name: parse.h
nodes.summary: Declares the value-parsing helpers for integers with unit suffixes, doubles, booleans and environment variables.

nodes.name: patch-delta.c
nodes.summary: Applies a delta (as produced by diff-delta) to a base buffer to reconstruct the target: the delta decoder used for deltified objects in packfiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a local macro (PARSE_CP_PARAM) and goto-based error labels placed inside the final if-block for shared cleanup.

nodes.name: patch_delta
nodes.summary: Validates the delta header against the source size, then replays copy commands (offset and size encoded in flag bits) and insert commands into a freshly allocated buffer, failing on corruption, bad sizes or reserved opcode 0.

nodes.name: prio-queue.c
nodes.summary: Binary-heap priority queue with a user comparator and stable tie-breaking by insertion counter; with no comparator it behaves as a LIFO stack. Used by revision walking.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares two heap slots with the user callback, breaking ties by insertion order for stability.

nodes.name: prio_queue_reverse
nodes.summary: Reverses a LIFO queue in place (BUG if a comparator is set).

nodes.name: clear_prio_queue
nodes.summary: Frees the array and resets all counters.

nodes.name: sift_down_root
nodes.summary: Restores the heap property by pushing the root element down to its proper place.

nodes.name: prio_queue_put
nodes.summary: Inserts an item (or replaces the pending-removed root) and bubbles it up; LIFO queues just append.

nodes.name: prio_queue_get
nodes.summary: Returns the next item, lazily deferring the heap repair via get_pending so a following put can reuse the slot.

nodes.name: prio_queue_peek
nodes.summary: Returns the next item without removing it.

nodes.name: prompt.c
nodes.summary: Prompts the user for input (such as credentials): runs a GIT_ASKPASS, core.askPass or SSH_ASKPASS helper if requested, falls back to the terminal, and offers an interactive line reader.

nodes.name: do_askpass
nodes.summary: Runs the askpass helper program with the prompt and reads its first line of output (at most 20 bytes initially) as the answer.

nodes.name: git_prompt
nodes.summary: Obtains an answer by askpass program if enabled and available, otherwise from the terminal unless GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT disables it; dies if no input could be read.

nodes.name: git_read_line_interactively
nodes.summary: Flushes stdout and reads one line from stdin into a strbuf.

nodes.name: rebase.c
nodes.summary: Parses the textual value of pull.rebase and branch.<name>.rebase into an enum rebase_type (false, true, merges, interactive or invalid).

nodes.name: rebase_parse_value
nodes.summary: Turns a config string into REBASE_FALSE/TRUE/MERGES/INTERACTIVE (accepting m and i abbreviations), warns that preserve was replaced by merges, and returns REBASE_INVALID otherwise.

nodes.name: rebase.h
nodes.summary: Declares enum rebase_type and the parser for rebase configuration values.

nodes.name: rebase_type
nodes.summary: Enum of rebase modes: invalid, false, true, merges and interactive.

nodes.name: debug.c
nodes.summary: Debugging decorator for ref storage backends: wraps a real ref_store and logs every operation (transactions, reads, iteration, reflogs, fsck) through the GIT_TRACE_REFS trace key before delegating.
nodes.languageNotes: Decorator pattern in C: refs_be_debug is a ref_storage_be vtable whose functions call the corresponding function of the wrapped backend and trace the result.

nodes.name: debug_ref_store
nodes.summary: Wrapper store: a base ref_store plus the pointer to the real store being traced.

nodes.name: maybe_debug_wrap_ref_store
nodes.summary: Wraps a ref store in the debug backend when GIT_TRACE_REFS is enabled, otherwise returns it unchanged.

nodes.name: debug_transaction_prepare
nodes.summary: Delegates ref transaction prepare to the real backend and traces the result and error.

nodes.name: print_update
nodes.summary: Traces one ref update: refname, old and new object ids, flags and type.

nodes.name: print_transaction
nodes.summary: Traces every update of a ref transaction.

nodes.name: debug_transaction_finish
nodes.summary: Delegates transaction finish, then traces the updates and result.

nodes.name: debug_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Wrapping iterator holding the real iterator being traced.

nodes.name: debug_ref_iterator_advance
nodes.summary: Advances the wrapped iterator and traces the ref name or end.

nodes.name: debug_ref_iterator_begin
nodes.summary: Starts iteration on the real backend and wraps the iterator for tracing.

nodes.name: debug_read_raw_ref
nodes.summary: Reads a raw ref through the real backend and traces the object id, referent, type or errno.

nodes.name: debug_read_symbolic_ref
nodes.summary: Reads a symbolic ref through the real backend and traces its target.

nodes.name: debug_reflog_expire
nodes.summary: Delegates reflog expiry to the real backend with tracing wrappers for the prepare, prune and cleanup callbacks.

nodes.name: refs_be_debug
nodes.summary: The ref_storage_be instance named "debug" that maps each backend operation to its tracing wrapper.

nodes.name: ref-cache.c
nodes.summary: In-memory cache of references organized as a tree of lazily filled directories with sorted entries, binary-search lookup, prefix-aware priming, and an iterator that walks refs in lexicographic order.

nodes.name: add_entry_to_dir
nodes.summary: Appends an entry to a directory, keeping the sorted marker if entries arrive in order.

nodes.name: get_ref_dir
nodes.summary: Returns a directory entry subdir, first filling it lazily via the cache fill callback if it is still incomplete.

nodes.name: create_ref_entry
nodes.summary: Allocates a ref entry with name, object id, flags and optional symbolic referent.

nodes.name: create_ref_cache
nodes.summary: Creates a ref cache whose root directory starts out incomplete and optionally lazily fills via a callback.

nodes.name: free_ref_entry
nodes.summary: Frees a ref or directory entry recursively without triggering lazy loading.

nodes.name: free_ref_cache
nodes.summary: Frees the whole cache and its tree.

nodes.name: create_dir_entry
nodes.summary: Allocates a directory entry (flagged DIR and INCOMPLETE) for a given dirname with trailing slash.

nodes.name: search_ref_dir
nodes.summary: Sorts a directory if needed and binary-searches for a name slice, returning its index or -1.

nodes.name: search_for_subdir
nodes.summary: Finds a subdirectory entry directly within a directory and loads it.

nodes.name: find_containing_dir
nodes.summary: Walks the path components of a refname down the directory tree to find the directory that should hold it.

nodes.name: is_dup_ref
nodes.summary: Detects duplicate ref names, dying on conflicting ids and warning for harmless duplicates.

nodes.name: sort_ref_dir
nodes.summary: Sorts a directory entries by name and removes duplicates.

nodes.name: overlaps_prefix
nodes.summary: Classifies a directory relative to a prefix: contains, within or excludes.

nodes.name: prime_ref_dir
nodes.summary: Recursively loads all loose-ref directories that may contain refs matching a prefix.

nodes.name: cache_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over the cache: a base ref_iterator, a stack of directory levels, the prefix and flags.

nodes.name: cache_ref_iterator_advance
nodes.summary: Moves to the next ref by walking the directory stack depth-first in sorted order, honoring prefix state and descending into subdirectories.

nodes.name: cache_ref_iterator_set_prefix
nodes.summary: Resets the iterator to start at the directory containing a prefix, optionally priming it.

nodes.name: cache_ref_iterator_seek
nodes.summary: Positions the iterator at a given refname by descending the directory tree, or sets a prefix.

nodes.name: cache_ref_iterator_begin
nodes.summary: Creates a ref_iterator over the cache with an optional prefix and priming.

nodes.name: ref-cache.h
nodes.summary: Defines the ref cache data structures (ref_cache, ref_value, ref_dir, ref_entry with REF_DIR and REF_INCOMPLETE flags) and the functions to build, search and iterate them.

nodes.name: ref_cache
nodes.summary: Cache root: root directory entry, owning ref_store and lazy fill callback.

nodes.name: ref_value
nodes.summary: Value of a cached ref: object id and symbolic referent.

nodes.name: ref_dir
nodes.summary: A directory level of refs: growable array of entries, sorted prefix count and back pointer to cache; loose dirs are read lazily.

nodes.name: ref_entry
nodes.summary: Either a ref (value) or a subdirectory (subdir), discriminated by the REF_DIR flag, with a flexible full-name field.

nodes.name: refspec.c
nodes.summary: Parses and applies refspecs (the "+src:dst" mappings used by fetch and push), including glob patterns, negative refspecs and matching refspecs, and maps ref names through them.

nodes.name: parse_refspec
nodes.summary: Parses one refspec string into a refspec_item: leading + or ^, src and dst split at the last colon, glob rules, and validity of each side differently for fetch, push and negative refspecs.

nodes.name: refspec_item_init_fetch
nodes.summary: Initializes a refspec_item from a fetch refspec string.

nodes.name: refspec_item_init_push
nodes.summary: Initializes a refspec_item from a push refspec string.

nodes.name: refspec_item_clear
nodes.summary: Frees a refspec_item strings and resets its flags.

nodes.name: refspec_init_fetch
nodes.summary: Initializes an empty fetch refspec list.

nodes.name: refspec_init_push
nodes.summary: Initializes an empty push refspec list.

nodes.name: refspec_append
nodes.summary: Parses a refspec string and appends it to a refspec list, dying if it is invalid.

nodes.name: refspec_appendf
nodes.summary: printf-style variant of refspec_append.

nodes.name: refspec_appendn
nodes.summary: Appends several refspec strings.

nodes.name: refspec_clear
nodes.summary: Clears all items and frees the list.

nodes.name: valid_fetch_refspec
nodes.summary: Tells whether a string is a valid fetch refspec.

nodes.name: refspec_ref_prefixes
nodes.summary: Computes ref prefixes (for ls-remote style filtering) implied by non-negative refspecs.

nodes.name: match_refname_with_pattern
nodes.summary: Matches a refname against a pattern with one "*" and optionally builds the replacement name for the dst side.

nodes.name: refspec_match
nodes.summary: Tests a refname against a single refspec item (pattern or exact).

nodes.name: refname_matches_negative_refspec_item
nodes.summary: Returns whether a refname is excluded by any negative refspec.

nodes.name: refspec_find_negative_match
nodes.summary: Determines whether a query (by src or dst) maps to a name excluded by negative refspecs, applying positive patterns in reverse.

nodes.name: refspec_find_all_matches
nodes.summary: Collects every mapped name for a query across all refspecs.

nodes.name: refspec_find_match
nodes.summary: Finds the first refspec mapping for a src or dst query, copying the force flag, or -1 if none or negated.

nodes.name: apply_negative_refspecs
nodes.summary: Removes from a ref map list the refs that match negative refspecs.

nodes.name: apply_refspecs
nodes.summary: Maps a source name through the refspecs to its destination name.

nodes.name: scalar.c
nodes.summary: The Scalar command-line tool for large repositories: clone (partial clone with sparse-checkout), register/unregister enlistments, apply recommended config, run maintenance tasks, diagnose and delete, built on running git subcommands.

nodes.name: setup_enlistment_directory
nodes.summary: Locates the enlistment root (with an optional src/ worktree), changes into it, sets up the git directory and returns the root path.

nodes.name: run_git
nodes.summary: Runs a git subcommand built from a NULL-terminated list of arguments.

nodes.name: scalar_config
nodes.summary: A recommended config key, value and whether it is overwritten on reconfigure.

nodes.name: set_scalar_config
nodes.summary: Writes a config key into the repo config file with a "set by scalar" comment.

nodes.name: set_config_if_missing
nodes.summary: Sets a recommended config value if it is unset (or overwritable on reconfigure) and traces whether it was created or existed.

nodes.name: set_recommended_config
nodes.summary: Applies the list of recommended settings for large repos (untracked cache, commit-graph, fetch and index tuning, fsmonitor when supported) and a log.excludeDecoration entry.

nodes.name: toggle_maintenance
nodes.summary: Runs "git maintenance start" or "unregister --force".

nodes.name: add_or_remove_enlistment
nodes.summary: Adds or removes the worktree in the global scalar.repo setting if not already in the desired state.

nodes.name: start_fsmonitor_daemon
nodes.summary: Starts the fsmonitor daemon unless it is already listening.

nodes.name: stop_fsmonitor_daemon
nodes.summary: Stops the fsmonitor daemon if it is listening.

nodes.name: register_dir
nodes.summary: Registers the current directory as an enlistment, sets recommended config and optionally starts maintenance and the fsmonitor daemon.

nodes.name: unregister_dir
nodes.summary: Turns off maintenance and removes the enlistment registration.

nodes.name: set_config
nodes.summary: printf-style helper that sets a config entry from a "key=value" string.

nodes.name: remote_default_branch
nodes.summary: Finds the default branch of a remote with "git ls-remote --symref" (falling back to the local default) and returns its name.

nodes.name: delete_enlistment
nodes.summary: Unregisters, moves out of the directory, stops fsmonitor and recursively deletes an enlistment.

nodes.name: load_builtin_commands
nodes.summary: Dummy implementation that dies, needed only to link get_version_info().

nodes.name: cmd_clone
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar clone": git init, remote config for a blobless partial clone, sparse-checkout, tuned config, fetch (with full-clone fallback), branch tracking, checkout and registration.

nodes.name: cmd_diagnose
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar diagnose" by running "git diagnose" into a timestamped zip under .scalarDiagnostics.

nodes.name: cmd_list
nodes.summary: Lists registered enlistments by reading scalar.repo values.

nodes.name: cmd_register
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar register" with an optional --no-maintenance.

nodes.name: get_scalar_repos
nodes.summary: Config callback that collects scalar.repo values into a list.

nodes.name: remove_deleted_enlistment
nodes.summary: Removes scalar.repo and maintenance.repo entries for a worktree that no longer exists.

nodes.name: cmd_reconfigure
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar reconfigure": reapplies recommended config to one or all registered enlistments, adjusting maintenance and cleaning stale entries.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar run <task>" mapping tasks (config, commit-graph, fetch, loose-objects, pack-files, all) to "git maintenance run --task".

nodes.name: cmd_unregister
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar unregister", forgiving when the worktree no longer exists.

nodes.name: cmd_delete
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar delete", refusing to delete the current directory.

nodes.name: cmd_help
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar help" by running "git help scalar".

nodes.name: cmd_version
nodes.summary: Implements "scalar version" with optional Git version and build options.

nodes.name: cmd_main
nodes.summary: Entry point: handles -C and -c, dispatches to the matching builtin subcommand, otherwise prints usage.

nodes.name: sh-i18n--envsubst.c
nodes.summary: Stripped-down port of gettext envsubst: reads a shell format string, finds $VAR and ${VAR} references and substitutes only the listed environment variables from stdin to stdout; used by the git-sh-i18n shell fallbacks.

nodes.name: cmd_main
nodes.summary: Handles argument modes (substitute listed variables on stdin, or --variables to print them) and closes stderr reporting failure.

nodes.name: find_variables
nodes.summary: Scans a string for $NAME or ${NAME} (ASCII identifiers) and calls a callback for each valid variable.

nodes.name: sorted_string_list_member
nodes.summary: Binary-searches a sorted string list for membership.

nodes.name: note_variables
nodes.summary: Collects variables found in a string into a sorted set for later substitution.

nodes.name: subst_from_stdin
nodes.summary: Copies stdin to stdout, replacing $VAR and ${VAR} with environment values when the variable is in the allowed set.

nodes.name: sha1dc_git.c
nodes.summary: Glue between Git and the collision-detecting SHA-1 library (sha1dc): init with safe-hash off, a Final that dies on detecting a collision attack, and an Update that splits inputs larger than INT_MAX.

nodes.name: git_SHA1DCInit
nodes.summary: Initializes the SHA-1 context with safe-hash disabled (compiled only with an external sha1dc).

nodes.name: git_SHA1DCFinal
nodes.summary: Finalizes the digest and dies with the hash if sha1dc reports a collision attack.

nodes.name: git_SHA1DCUpdate
nodes.summary: Feeds data into the context in INT_MAX-sized chunks to match Git size_t interface.

nodes.name: sha1dc_git.h
nodes.summary: Selects the sha1dc header (external, submodule or bundled) and maps the platform_SHA1 macros to the Git wrappers.

nodes.name: sigchain.c
nodes.summary: Stack of signal handlers per signal: push installs a handler and remembers the previous one, pop restores it, with helpers to push or pop the common termination signals.

nodes.name: sigchain_signal
nodes.summary: Per-signal record of saved previous handlers with count and capacity.

nodes.name: sigchain_push
nodes.summary: Installs a handler for a signal and saves the previous handler on its stack.

nodes.name: sigchain_pop
nodes.summary: Restores the previously saved handler of a signal.

nodes.name: sigchain_push_common
nodes.summary: Pushes a handler for SIGINT, SIGHUP, SIGTERM, SIGQUIT and SIGPIPE.

nodes.name: sigchain_pop_common
nodes.summary: Pops the handlers for the common termination signals.

nodes.name: simple-ipc.h
nodes.summary: API of Git simple IPC over named pipes or Unix domain sockets: client connect and send, and a threaded server with an application callback, available only when SUPPORTS_SIMPLE_IPC; used by the fsmonitor daemon.

nodes.name: ipc_active_state
nodes.summary: Enum of the state of an IPC endpoint: listening, not listening, invalid path, path not found or other error.

nodes.name: ipc_client_connect_options
nodes.summary: Client options: wait if the server is busy or not yet present, and disallow chdir for Unix sockets.

nodes.name: ipc_client_connection
nodes.summary: Handle of a client connection wrapping a file descriptor.

nodes.name: ipc_server_opts
nodes.summary: Server options: number of threads and the chdir restriction.

nodes.name: ipc_get_active_state
nodes.summary: Declares a probe of whether a server is listening on a path.

nodes.name: ipc_client_try_connect
nodes.summary: Declares connecting to the daemon with retry options and returning a connection handle.

nodes.name: ipc_client_close_connection
nodes.summary: Declares closing a client connection.

nodes.name: ipc_client_send_command_to_connection
nodes.summary: Declares a synchronous send and receive on an existing connection.

nodes.name: ipc_client_send_command
nodes.summary: Declares connecting and exchanging one message with a server at a path.

nodes.name: ipc_server_init_async
nodes.summary: Declares creating a server thread pool with an application callback.

nodes.name: ipc_server_start_async
nodes.summary: Declares starting the initialized server pool.

nodes.name: ipc_server_stop_async
nodes.summary: Declares gently shutting down the server pool.

nodes.name: ipc_server_await
nodes.summary: Declares waiting for all server threads to finish.

nodes.name: ipc_server_free
nodes.summary: Declares freeing server resources.

nodes.name: ipc_server_run
nodes.summary: Declares a synchronous wrapper that runs the server until shutdown or error.

nodes.name: split-index.c
nodes.summary: Implements the split index: a shared base index plus a small index of changes, serialized in the "link" extension with EWAH delete and replace bitmaps, including merging the base back, preparing entries to write, and discarding.

nodes.name: init_split_index
nodes.summary: Creates the split_index struct for an index (refusing sparse index) with refcount 1.

nodes.name: read_link_extension
nodes.summary: Reads the "link" extension: base index hash plus EWAH delete and replace bitmaps, with corruption checks.

nodes.name: write_link_extension
nodes.summary: Writes the base oid and the serialized delete and replace bitmaps.

nodes.name: mark_base_index_entries
nodes.summary: Stores a 1-based position in each base entry so shared entries can be identified.

nodes.name: move_cache_to_base_index
nodes.summary: Turns the current in-memory index into the shared base index, transferring the memory pool.

nodes.name: mark_entry_for_delete
nodes.summary: EWAH bit callback that marks the entry at a position for removal.

nodes.name: replace_entry
nodes.summary: EWAH bit callback that replaces a base entry with the stripped-name entry stored in the split index.

nodes.name: merge_base_index
nodes.summary: Merges the base index with the split index: copy base entries, apply replace and delete bitmaps, then add the remaining new entries.

nodes.name: compare_ce_content
nodes.summary: Compares the on-disk-relevant content (flags, stat data, oid) of two cache entries.

nodes.name: prepare_to_write_split_index
nodes.summary: Decides which entries go to the split index: sets delete and replace bitmaps against the base, detects racy and modified entries, and swaps cache for the entries to write.

nodes.name: finish_writing_split_index
nodes.summary: Restores the full cache after writing and frees the bitmaps.

nodes.name: discard_split_index
nodes.summary: Drops a reference to the split index and frees it and its base when the refcount hits zero.

nodes.name: save_or_free_index_entry
nodes.summary: Marks a base-shared entry as removed or discards an unshared one.

nodes.name: replace_index_entry_in_base
nodes.summary: Replaces an entry in the base index with a new entry sharing its position.

nodes.name: add_split_index
nodes.summary: Enables split index mode on an index.

nodes.name: remove_split_index
nodes.summary: Disables split index mode, handing the base memory pool to the main index.

nodes.name: stable-qsort.c
nodes.summary: Stable merge sort (git_stable_qsort) simplified from glibc qsort, used where equal elements must keep their original order.

nodes.name: msort_with_tmp
nodes.summary: Recursive top-down merge sort that uses a temporary buffer to merge two sorted halves.

nodes.name: git_stable_qsort
nodes.summary: Allocates a temporary buffer and runs the merge sort.

nodes.name: basics.c
nodes.summary: Foundation utilities of the reftable library: pluggable allocator hooks, the growable reftable_buf string buffer, a callback-driven binary search, parsing of newline-separated table name lists, and hash-size lookup.

nodes.name: reftable_malloc
nodes.summary: Allocates memory through the user-installed allocator hook when one is set, otherwise malloc; returns NULL for a zero-size request.

nodes.name: reftable_realloc
nodes.summary: Resizes an allocation through the installed hook or realloc; a zero size frees the pointer and returns NULL.

nodes.name: reftable_free
nodes.summary: Frees memory with the installed free hook or the standard free.

nodes.name: reftable_calloc
nodes.summary: Allocates a zeroed array after checking that nelem * elsize does not overflow, going through reftable_malloc.

nodes.name: reftable_strdup
nodes.summary: Duplicates a C string with reftable_malloc so the copy can be released with reftable_free.

nodes.name: reftable_set_alloc
nodes.summary: Public hook that lets an embedder replace the malloc, realloc and free functions used by the whole reftable library.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_init
nodes.summary: Resets a reftable_buf to the empty REFTABLE_BUF_INIT state without freeing anything.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_release
nodes.summary: Frees the storage of a reftable_buf and reinitializes it so it can be reused.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_reset
nodes.summary: Empties a buffer (length 0, NUL terminated) while keeping its allocation for reuse.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_setlen
nodes.summary: Truncates a buffer to a shorter length and re-terminates it; returns -1 if the new length is larger than the current one.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two buffers byte-wise with memcmp over the common length and then by length; this ordering defines how ref names and record keys sort in a table.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_add
nodes.summary: Appends len arbitrary bytes to a buffer, growing it with REFTABLE_ALLOC_GROW and keeping a trailing NUL byte.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_addstr
nodes.summary: Appends a C string to a buffer by delegating to reftable_buf_add.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_detach
nodes.summary: Transfers ownership of the buffer memory to the caller and reinitializes the buffer.

nodes.name: binsearch
nodes.summary: Generic binary search that returns the smallest index at which a predicate callback turns true, aborting with size on a negative callback result; block iterators use it to pick a restart point.

nodes.name: free_names
nodes.summary: Frees a NULL-terminated array of malloced strings and the array itself.

nodes.name: names_length
nodes.summary: Counts the entries of a NULL-terminated array of names.

nodes.name: parse_names
nodes.summary: Splits a newline-separated buffer such as the stack list file tables.list into a NULL-terminated array of duplicated names, discarding empty lines and rejecting input that lacks a final newline.

nodes.name: names_equal
nodes.summary: Compares two NULL-terminated name arrays element by element; the stack uses it to detect whether tables.list changed between reads.

nodes.name: common_prefix_size
nodes.summary: Returns how many leading bytes two buffers share, which is the basis of the prefix compression of record keys.

nodes.name: hash_size
nodes.summary: Maps a reftable_hash id (SHA-1 or SHA-256) to the object id byte length, aborting on an unknown id.

nodes.name: basics.h
nodes.summary: Internal basics header: declares the reftable_buf operations, allocator wrappers and array-growth macros (REFTABLE_ALLOC_ARRAY, REFTABLE_ALLOC_GROW), big-endian put/get helpers, binary search and name-list helpers, and bans direct malloc/free inside the library.

nodes.name: block.c
nodes.summary: Implements reftable blocks: the block_writer that packs prefix-compressed records plus a restart table into a fixed-size block (zlib-compressing log blocks), and the block reader and block_iter that validate, inflate, seek and iterate records inside one block.

nodes.name: header_size
nodes.summary: Returns the reftable file header size: 24 bytes for format version 1 and 28 for version 2.

nodes.name: footer_size
nodes.summary: Returns the reftable file footer size: 68 bytes for version 1 and 72 for version 2.

nodes.name: block_writer_register_restart
nodes.summary: Accounts for a freshly encoded record: decides whether it is a restart point (up to MAX_RESTARTS), checks that record plus restart table still fit into the block, stores the restart offset and remembers the key as last_key.

nodes.name: block_writer_init
nodes.summary: Prepares a block_writer to fill a caller-provided buffer with one record type: writes the block type byte, sets the default restart interval of 16, and lazily creates the zlib deflate stream (level 9).

nodes.name: block_writer_type
nodes.summary: Returns the block type character stored at the start of the block being written.

nodes.name: block_writer_add
nodes.summary: Encodes one record (prefix-compressed key followed by its encoded value) into the current block and registers the restart point; returns REFTABLE_ENTRY_TOO_BIG_ERROR when the block is full so the caller can flush it.

nodes.name: block_writer_finish
nodes.summary: Seals the block by appending the 3-byte restart offsets and the 2-byte restart count, storing the block length in the header and, for log blocks, zlib-compressing the whole body; returns the final block size.

nodes.name: read_block
nodes.summary: Reads sz bytes at offset off from a block source, clamping to the source size and releasing previously held data first.

nodes.name: reftable_block_init
nodes.summary: Loads one block from a block source: validates the type byte, reads the declared size, inflates zlib-compressed log blocks, checks the restart table bounds and fills in the reftable_block metadata (type, restart offset, restart count, full block size).

nodes.name: reftable_block_release
nodes.summary: Releases the zlib inflate stream, the uncompressed buffer and the underlying block data and zeroes the block.

nodes.name: reftable_block_type
nodes.summary: Returns the type byte (ref, log, obj or index) of a loaded block.

nodes.name: reftable_block_first_key
nodes.summary: Decodes the first key of a block (stored without a prefix); table seeking compares it with the wanted key to find the block that may contain it.

nodes.name: block_iter_init
nodes.summary: Attaches a block_iter to a block and positions it before the first record.

nodes.name: block_iter_seek_start
nodes.summary: Rewinds a block iterator to the first record of its block and clears the remembered last key.

nodes.name: restart_needle_less
nodes.summary: Binary-search predicate that decodes the (unprefixed) key at a restart point and compares it with the needle, flagging format errors through its argument struct.

nodes.name: block_iter_next
nodes.summary: Decodes the next record of the block by applying the prefix-compressed key delta to last_key and decoding the value; returns 1 at the end of the block.

nodes.name: block_iter_reset
nodes.summary: Clears a block iterator so it no longer refers to a block.

nodes.name: block_iter_close
nodes.summary: Releases the iterator scratch buffers.

nodes.name: block_iter_seek_key
nodes.summary: Positions the iterator at the first record whose key is >= the wanted key: binary searches the restart points, then scans forward linearly inside that restart interval.

nodes.name: block_iter_seek_void
nodes.summary: Vtable adapter that turns a wanted record into its key and seeks the block iterator, rejecting records of a different type.

nodes.name: reftable_block_init_iterator
nodes.summary: Allocates a block_iter and installs it behind the generic reftable_iterator vtable (seek, next, close).

nodes.name: block_writer_release
nodes.summary: Frees the zlib stream, restart array, compression buffer and scratch buffers owned by a block_writer.

nodes.name: block.h
nodes.summary: Declares block_writer (accumulates records, restart offsets and optional zlib state for one block) and block_iter (cursor over one loaded block) together with their operations, and the header and footer size helpers.

nodes.name: block_writer
nodes.summary: Writer state for one block: output buffer, restart offsets, last key, zlib stream and entry count, reused across blocks to avoid allocations.

nodes.name: block_iter
nodes.summary: Cursor over a loaded block holding the offset of the next entry and the last decoded key used for prefix decompression.

nodes.name: blocksource.c
nodes.summary: Block source abstraction of reftable: thin dispatch wrappers over a vtable of size/read/release/close operations, with two backends, an in-memory buffer and a read-only mmap of a table file.
nodes.languageNotes: Polymorphism through a vtable of function pointers (struct reftable_block_source_vtable) with in-memory and mmap backends.

nodes.name: block_source_release_data
nodes.summary: Returns block data to its source through the vtable release_data hook and clears the block descriptor.

nodes.name: block_source_close
nodes.summary: Closes a block source via its vtable and clears it; a no-op for a zero-initialized source.

nodes.name: block_source_read_data
nodes.summary: Reads size bytes at offset off through the source vtable and records the owning source in the returned block data.

nodes.name: block_source_size
nodes.summary: Returns the total length of the underlying resource through the vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_buf_read_data
nodes.summary: Buffer-backed read: allocates a fresh block and copies the requested range out of the in-memory reftable_buf.

nodes.name: block_source_from_buf
nodes.summary: Wraps an in-memory reftable_buf as a block source with the buffer vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_block_source_from_file
nodes.summary: Opens a table file read-only, maps it with reftable_mmap and exposes it as a block source whose reads are zero-copy slices of the mapping; returns REFTABLE_NOT_EXIST_ERROR when the file is missing.

nodes.name: blocksource.h
nodes.summary: Internal block source API: close, read, size and release operations plus a constructor wrapping an in-memory buffer.

nodes.name: constants.h
nodes.summary: Tiny constants header: MAX_RESTARTS (65535), DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE (4096) and DEFAULT_GEOMETRIC_FACTOR (2).

nodes.name: error.c
nodes.summary: Translates reftable_error codes (I/O, format, lock, API misuse, zlib, empty table, refname, entry too big, outdated, out of memory) into human-readable strings.

nodes.name: reftable_error_str
nodes.summary: Maps a reftable_error code to a descriptive message and formats unknown codes into a static buffer.

nodes.name: fsck.c
nodes.summary: Consistency checks for a reftable stack: validates that every table file name follows the <min>-<max>-<hash>.ref/.log pattern and reports problems through caller-supplied callbacks.

nodes.name: table_has_valid_name
nodes.summary: Parses a table file name as hex min update index, hex max update index and hex hash suffix followed by .ref or .log and returns whether it matches.

nodes.name: table_check_name
nodes.summary: Per-table check that reports REFTABLE_FSCK_ERROR_TABLE_NAME through the report callback when the table name is invalid.

nodes.name: table_checks
nodes.summary: Runs the list of per-table check functions on one table and ORs together their results.

nodes.name: reftable_fsck_check
nodes.summary: Walks every table of a reftable_stack, emits a verbose message for it and runs the table checks, reporting findings through the callbacks.

nodes.name: iter.c
nodes.summary: Generic reftable iterator plumbing: dispatch through the reftable_iterator vtable, an empty iterator, a ref iterator filtered by object id, an iterator that follows object-index offsets, and the public ref and log seek/next helpers.

nodes.name: iterator_seek
nodes.summary: Dispatches a seek on a reftable_iterator to its vtable implementation.

nodes.name: iterator_next
nodes.summary: Dispatches a next call on a reftable_iterator to its vtable implementation.

nodes.name: iterator_set_empty
nodes.summary: Installs a vtable on the iterator that yields no entries, used when a lookup finds nothing.

nodes.name: filtering_ref_iterator_next
nodes.summary: Pulls ref records from an inner iterator and returns only those whose value, or peeled value for annotated tags, equals the wanted object id; used for reverse lookups in tables without an object index.

nodes.name: iterator_from_filtering_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Installs the filtering ref iterator vtable on an iterator.

nodes.name: indexed_table_ref_iter_next_block
nodes.summary: Loads the next ref block listed in the object-index offsets of an indexed iterator, or marks it finished.

nodes.name: indexed_table_ref_iter_next
nodes.summary: Walks the blocks named by the object index and yields ref records whose value or peeled value matches the wanted object id.

nodes.name: indexed_table_ref_iter_new
nodes.summary: Creates an iterator over the ref blocks at the given offsets (from an o-section record) for one object id and loads the first block.

nodes.name: iterator_from_indexed_table_ref_iter
nodes.summary: Installs the indexed-table iterator vtable on an iterator.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_destroy
nodes.summary: Closes an iterator through its vtable, clears the ops pointer and frees the iterator state.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_seek_ref
nodes.summary: Builds a ref record with the wanted name and seeks the iterator to it.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_next_ref
nodes.summary: Returns the next ref record from an iterator of ref type.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_seek_log_at
nodes.summary: Seeks a log iterator to the reflog entry of a ref at a given update index; log keys sort newest first.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_seek_log
nodes.summary: Seeks a log iterator to the newest reflog entry of a ref by using the maximum update index.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_next_log
nodes.summary: Returns the next log record from an iterator of log type.

nodes.name: iter.h
nodes.summary: Declares the reftable_iterator vtable (seek, next, close), the filtering ref iterator and the indexed table ref iterator, and helpers to install them on a generic iterator.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator_vtable
nodes.summary: Virtual function table with seek, next and close callbacks that every reftable iterator kind implements.

nodes.name: filtering_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Iterator state wrapping an inner ref iterator plus the object id used to filter refs.

nodes.name: indexed_table_ref_iter
nodes.summary: Iterator that follows block offsets from the object index, holding the table, wanted oid, offset list, current block and block iterator.

nodes.name: merged.c
nodes.summary: Merges several reftable tables into one logical sorted view: a priority-queue based merged iterator in which newer tables shadow older ones, with optional suppression of deletion tombstones.

nodes.name: merged_iter_close
nodes.summary: Releases the priority queue and destroys every sub-iterator and its record.

nodes.name: merged_iter_advance_subiter
nodes.summary: Advances one sub-iterator and pushes its new current record onto the priority queue.

nodes.name: merged_iter_seek
nodes.summary: Clears the priority queue, seeks every sub-iterator to the wanted record and re-queues the ones that have entries.

nodes.name: merged_iter_next_entry
nodes.summary: Pops the smallest record from the queue, drops older duplicates with the same key from other tables and swaps the winner into the output; records the sub-iterator to advance lazily on the next call.

nodes.name: merged_iter_next_void
nodes.summary: Vtable next that loops over merged entries and skips deletion tombstones when suppress_deletions is set.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_new
nodes.summary: Builds a merged table over an array of tables after verifying all use the expected hash id, and computes the overall min and max update index.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_free
nodes.summary: Frees a merged table object (not its member tables).

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_max_update_index
nodes.summary: Returns the highest update index across the merged tables.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_min_update_index
nodes.summary: Returns the lowest update index across the merged tables.

nodes.name: merged_table_init_iter
nodes.summary: Creates one sub-iterator per table for a record type and wraps them in a merged_iter installed on the caller iterator.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_init_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over all ref records of a merged table.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_init_log_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over all log (reflog) records of a merged table.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table_hash_id
nodes.summary: Returns the object hash algorithm used by the merged tables.

nodes.name: merged_subiter
nodes.summary: One member of a merged iterator: the sub-iterator over a single table and its current record.

nodes.name: merged_iter
nodes.summary: State of a merged iterator: sub-iterators, priority queue, suppress_deletions flag and the sub-iterator to advance next.

nodes.name: merged.h
nodes.summary: Defines struct reftable_merged_table (array of tables, hash id, deletion suppression flag, update index range) and declares merged_table_init_iter.

nodes.name: reftable_merged_table
nodes.summary: Logical union of several tables with newer tables shadowing older ones, holding the table array, hash id, suppress_deletions flag and min/max update index.

nodes.name: pq.c
nodes.summary: Binary min-heap used by the merged iterator, ordering entries by record key and breaking ties so that records from newer tables win.

nodes.name: pq_less
nodes.summary: Compares two queue entries by record key and, for equal keys, by sub-iterator index so the newer table is preferred.

nodes.name: merged_iter_pqueue_remove
nodes.summary: Pops the top of the heap, moves the last element to the root and sifts it down.

nodes.name: merged_iter_pqueue_add
nodes.summary: Appends an entry to the heap array and sifts it up to restore heap order.

nodes.name: merged_iter_pqueue_release
nodes.summary: Frees the heap array and zeroes the queue.

nodes.name: pq.h
nodes.summary: Declares the priority queue (min-heap of pq_entry) used by the merged iterator with add, remove, release, comparison and inline top and is-empty helpers.

nodes.name: pq_entry
nodes.summary: Heap element: the index of the source sub-iterator and a pointer to its current record.

nodes.name: merged_iter_pqueue
nodes.summary: Heap array with length and capacity.

nodes.name: record.c
nodes.summary: Defines the four reftable record kinds (ref, log, obj, index) with their key derivation, copy, equality, comparison and binary encode/decode, plus varint and prefix-compressed key coding and a vtable that dispatches generic reftable_record operations by type.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a hand-written vtable (struct of function pointers) per record type plus a tagged union, a C idiom for polymorphism.

nodes.name: get_var_int
nodes.summary: Decodes a reftable varint (7 bits per byte, continuation bit, offset-by-one scheme) from a string_view and returns the bytes consumed, or -1 on truncation or overflow.

nodes.name: put_var_int
nodes.summary: Encodes a 64-bit value as a reftable varint into a string_view, failing with REFTABLE_ENTRY_TOO_BIG_ERROR if it does not fit.

nodes.name: reftable_is_block_type
nodes.summary: Returns whether a byte is one of the valid block type characters (ref, log, obj, index).

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_val1
nodes.summary: Returns the first object id of a ref record (the value of a VAL1 ref or the unpeeled value of a VAL2 tag) or NULL otherwise.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_val2
nodes.summary: Returns the peeled target object id of a VAL2 (annotated tag) ref record or NULL for other types.

nodes.name: decode_string
nodes.summary: Decodes a varint length-prefixed string from a buffer view into a reftable_buf and returns the bytes consumed.

nodes.name: encode_string
nodes.summary: Encodes a C string as a varint length followed by its bytes into a string_view.

nodes.name: reftable_encode_key
nodes.summary: Writes a record key as prefix length, suffix length shifted left by 3 bits combined with the 3-bit value type, and the key suffix, compressed against the previous key.

nodes.name: reftable_decode_keylen
nodes.summary: Reads prefix length, suffix length and value type of a key header from a view without decoding the key bytes.

nodes.name: reftable_decode_key
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the full key from last_key plus the prefix length and suffix bytes read from the view, returning the value-type bits.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_copy_from
nodes.summary: Deep-copies a ref record (refname, update index and value or symref target depending on value type) into the destination.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_release
nodes.summary: Frees the refname and symref target of a ref record and zeroes it.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes the value part of a ref record: update index varint followed by one hash, two hashes (tag plus peeled), a length-prefixed symref target, or nothing for a deletion.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a ref record from its key and value bytes, reading the update index, then a hash, two hashes or a symref string according to the value type.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record_copy_from
nodes.summary: Deep-copies an object-index record including its hash prefix and offsets array.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes an object-index record as a count (when 0 or at least 8) followed by delta-encoded block offsets.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes an object-index record: hash prefix from the key and the offset list from varint deltas, taking the count from the value type or an explicit varint.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record_equal_void
nodes.summary: Compares two object-index records by hash prefix and offsets.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record_cmp_void
nodes.summary: Orders two object-index records by hash prefix.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_key
nodes.summary: Builds the sort key of a reflog entry as the NUL-terminated refname followed by the bit-inverted big-endian update index, so newer entries sort first.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_copy_from
nodes.summary: Deep-copies a reflog record including old and new object ids, committer name, email, time, timezone offset and message.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_release
nodes.summary: Frees the strings of a log record (refname, name, email, message) and zeroes it.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes a reflog update: old and new hash, committer name, email, varint time, 16-bit timezone offset and message; deletions encode to nothing.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a reflog record from its key and compressed-block payload, parsing hashes, committer identity, time, timezone and message and recovering the update index from the inverted key suffix.

nodes.name: null_streq
nodes.summary: String equality that treats two NULL pointers as equal.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_cmp_void
nodes.summary: Orders two log records by key (refname, then update index descending).

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_equal
nodes.summary: Compares two log records field by field including old and new hash, name, email, time, timezone and message.

nodes.name: reftable_index_record_copy_from
nodes.summary: Copies an index record (block offset and last key of the indexed block).

nodes.name: reftable_index_record_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes an index record as the varint offset of the indexed block.

nodes.name: reftable_index_record_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes an index record: the last key comes from the record key and the block offset from a varint.

nodes.name: reftable_record_key
nodes.summary: Computes the sort key of any record by dispatching on the record type through the vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_record_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes the value of any record through its type vtable and returns the bytes written.

nodes.name: reftable_record_copy_from
nodes.summary: Copies a record of any type using the type-specific copy function.

nodes.name: reftable_record_val_type
nodes.summary: Returns the 3-bit value type of a record, e.g. ref deletion, val1, val2 or symref.

nodes.name: reftable_record_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a record of any type from its key, value type and payload bytes through the vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_record_release
nodes.summary: Releases the resources of a record through its vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_record_is_deletion
nodes.summary: Returns whether a record is a deletion tombstone, dispatching by type.

nodes.name: reftable_record_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares the keys of two records of the same type and reports an API error if types differ.

nodes.name: reftable_record_equal
nodes.summary: Tests two records of the same type for full equality through the vtable.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_equal
nodes.summary: Compares two ref records by name, update index, value type and value hashes or symref target.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_compare_name
nodes.summary: qsort-style comparator ordering ref records by refname.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record_is_deletion
nodes.summary: Returns whether a ref record is a deletion tombstone.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_compare_key
nodes.summary: qsort-style comparator ordering log records by refname and then update index descending.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record_is_deletion
nodes.summary: Returns whether a log record is a deletion tombstone.

nodes.name: reftable_record_data
nodes.summary: Returns a pointer to the union member of a reftable_record that matches its type.

nodes.name: reftable_record_vtable
nodes.summary: Selects the reftable_record_vtable (ref, log, index or obj) that matches the record type.

nodes.name: reftable_record_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes a record and sets its type, initializing the buffer of index records.

nodes.name: record.h
nodes.summary: Declares the record layer: string_view, the varint and prefix-compressed key coding functions, the per-type record vtable, index and object records, the tagged-union reftable_record and the generic record operations.

nodes.name: string_view
nodes.summary: Non-owning pointer and length pair describing a byte range, advanced with string_view_consume while encoding or decoding.

nodes.name: reftable_record_vtable
nodes.summary: Per-record-type function table (key, copy_from, val_type, encode, decode, release, is_deletion, equal, cmp).

nodes.name: reftable_index_record
nodes.summary: Index record pointing at a block via its offset and last key.

nodes.name: reftable_obj_record
nodes.summary: Object-index record: object id prefix and the block offsets where refs to it occur.

nodes.name: reftable_record
nodes.summary: Tagged union over ref, log, obj and index records, so blocks and iterators handle all record kinds generically.

nodes.name: reftable-basics.h
nodes.summary: Public header with the reftable_buf string buffer struct, the reftable_hash enum (SHA-1 and SHA-256 ids) and the reftable_set_alloc allocator hook.

nodes.name: reftable_buf
nodes.summary: Growable NUL-terminated byte buffer (alloc, len, buf) used for keys, paths and scratch data throughout the library.

nodes.name: reftable_hash
nodes.summary: Hash algorithm ids (REFTABLE_HASH_SHA1, REFTABLE_HASH_SHA256) stored in tables.

nodes.name: reftable-blocksource.h
nodes.summary: Public header defining reftable_block_source with its vtable (size, read_data, release_data, close), the reftable_block_data descriptor and the file-based constructor.

nodes.name: reftable_block_source
nodes.summary: Handle to a readable table storage: a vtable pointer plus opaque argument.

nodes.name: reftable_block_data
nodes.summary: Block bytes returned by a source together with the source that owns them.

nodes.name: reftable_block_source_vtable
nodes.summary: Operations of a block source: size, read_data, release_data and close.

nodes.name: reftable-error.h
nodes.summary: Public header with the reftable_error enum (I/O, format, not exist, lock, API, zlib, empty table, refname, entry too big, outdated, out of memory) and reftable_error_str.

nodes.name: reftable_error
nodes.summary: Negative error codes returned by reftable functions such as REFTABLE_IO_ERROR and REFTABLE_LOCK_ERROR.

nodes.name: reftable-fsck.h
nodes.summary: Public header for reftable consistency checking: the error enum, the reftable_fsck_info report struct, callback types and reftable_fsck_check.

nodes.name: reftable_fsck_error
nodes.summary: Kinds of problems fsck can report; currently an invalid table name.

nodes.name: reftable_fsck_info
nodes.summary: Report passed to the fsck callback with the error kind, message and table path.

nodes.name: reftable-merged.h
nodes.summary: Public API of merged tables: construct a merged table from a table array, create ref or log iterators, query update index range and hash id, and free it.

nodes.name: reftable-record.h
nodes.summary: Public definitions of ref records (deletion, val1, val2 for peeled tags, symref) and log records (deletion or update with old/new hash, committer, time, timezone, message) together with accessors, release and equality helpers.

nodes.name: reftable_ref_record
nodes.summary: A ref entry: refname, update index, value type and a union holding one hash, tag plus peeled hash, or a symref target.

nodes.name: reftable_log_record
nodes.summary: A reflog entry: refname, update index, deletion or update with old and new object id, committer name, email, time, timezone offset and message.

nodes.name: reftable-table.h
nodes.summary: Public API of a single table: struct reftable_table (name, source, size, hash id, block size, update index range, section offsets, refcount) plus constructor, refcounting, iterators, reverse lookup by oid and a raw block iterator.

nodes.name: reftable_table_offsets
nodes.summary: Offsets of one section (presence flag, section start and index start).

nodes.name: reftable_table
nodes.summary: An opened reftable file with its block source, size, hash id, block size, update index range, section offsets and refcount.

nodes.name: reftable_table_iterator
nodes.summary: Opaque handle to a block-level iterator over a table.

nodes.name: stack.c
nodes.summary: Implements the reftable_stack, the on-disk directory of tables listed in tables.list: reloading with retry, atomic additions under a lock, geometric auto-compaction and explicit compaction with table locks, reading refs and logs, and cleanup of stale tables.

nodes.name: stack_filename
nodes.summary: Builds the full path of a table inside the stack directory.

nodes.name: reftable_write_data
nodes.summary: Writes a whole buffer to a file descriptor, retrying on EAGAIN and EINTR.

nodes.name: fd_read_lines
nodes.summary: Reads a whole file through a descriptor and parses it into a NULL-terminated array of lines.

nodes.name: read_lines
nodes.summary: Opens a file by name and reads its lines into a names array, used to read tables.list.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_init_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over the refs of the stack via its merged table.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_init_log_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over the reflog entries of the stack via its merged table.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_merged_table
nodes.summary: Returns the merged table view over all tables currently loaded by the stack.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_destroy
nodes.summary: Frees a stack: drops table references (unlinking tables no longer listed in tables.list), closes the list file descriptor and frees paths.

nodes.name: stack_copy_tables
nodes.summary: Copies the array of table pointers of the stack so a reload can reuse still-valid open tables.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_reload_once
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the stack from a list of table names: reuses already open tables, opens new ones through block sources, creates a new merged table and swaps it in, releasing or unlinking tables that disappeared.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_reload_maybe_reuse
nodes.summary: Reload loop that reads tables.list, retries with randomized backoff for up to three seconds when a listed table has vanished because of concurrent compaction, and keeps the list file open to detect later changes.

nodes.name: reftable_new_stack
nodes.summary: Creates a stack object for a directory, defaults the hash to SHA-1, sets the tables.list path and performs the initial reload.

nodes.name: stack_uptodate
nodes.summary: Checks whether the loaded tables still match tables.list (by stat inode comparison, then by table names), returning positive if a reload is needed.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_reload
nodes.summary: Public reload: reloads the stack if tables.list changed on disk.

nodes.name: reftable_addition_close
nodes.summary: Removes new tables created by an uncommitted addition, frees its state and releases the tables.list lock.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_init_addition
nodes.summary: Starts an addition: takes the tables.list.lock lock file, applies default permissions, reloads if the stack is stale and records the next update index.

nodes.name: stack_try_add
nodes.summary: Runs a full addition cycle: initialize (lock), write the new table via callback, commit and close.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_add
nodes.summary: Public one-shot API that atomically adds a new table written by a callback to the stack.

nodes.name: reftable_addition_destroy
nodes.summary: Closes and frees a reftable_addition.

nodes.name: reftable_addition_commit
nodes.summary: Commits an addition: writes the old plus new table names into the locked tables.list, fsyncs, renames the lock file into place, reloads the stack and triggers best-effort auto-compaction.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_addition_new
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes a reftable_addition that holds the stack lock so several tables can be added in one transaction.

nodes.name: reftable_addition_add
nodes.summary: Writes one new table through a callback into a temp file, closes the reftable writer, validates the update index range, renames it to its <min>-<max> name and records it in the addition.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_next_update_index
nodes.summary: Returns the update index one above the highest index in the stack, the minimum for the next table.

nodes.name: stack_write_compact
nodes.summary: Merges a range of tables with a merged iterator and writes all refs (dropping deletions when compacting from the bottom) and logs (honoring expiry config) into the new table via a reftable writer.

nodes.name: stack_compact_locked
nodes.summary: Writes the compacted output for a table range to a temp file named by its update-index range using a reftable writer.

nodes.name: stack_compact_range
nodes.summary: Compacts tables [first, last] into one: locks tables.list and each input table, compacts without the list lock, then re-locks and verifies the range is unchanged before renaming the new table in and rewriting tables.list; best-effort mode shrinks the range on lock conflicts.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_compact_all
nodes.summary: Public API that compacts every table of the stack into a single table.

nodes.name: suggest_compaction_segment
nodes.summary: Computes the table range to compact to restore a geometric size sequence: scans from the newest table back to find the segment end where size[i-1] < size[i] * factor, then extends the start backwards while the preceding table is smaller than the accumulated bytes times the factor.

nodes.name: stack_segments_for_compaction
nodes.summary: Collects table sizes (minus header overhead) and asks suggest_compaction_segment for the segment to compact.

nodes.name: update_segment_if_compaction_required
nodes.summary: Decides whether compaction is needed: never with fewer than two tables, always when the geometric heuristic is off, otherwise only if the suggested segment is non-empty; fills in the segment.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_compaction_required
nodes.summary: Public API that reports whether the stack should be compacted.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_auto_compact
nodes.summary: Compacts the segment suggested by the geometric heuristic in best-effort mode; called after every commit.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_compaction_stats
nodes.summary: Returns the accumulated compaction statistics (attempts, failures, bytes, entries written).

nodes.name: reftable_stack_read_ref
nodes.summary: Looks up one ref by name through a merged ref iterator, returning 1 when the ref is missing or deleted.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_read_log
nodes.summary: Looks up the newest reflog entry of a ref through a merged log iterator.

nodes.name: remove_maybe_stale_table
nodes.summary: Opens an unlisted table file, reads its max update index and unlinks it if it is not newer than the stack.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_clean_locked
nodes.summary: Scans the table directory and removes .ref files that are not part of the current stack and are stale.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_clean
nodes.summary: Takes the stack lock via an addition and removes stale tables from the directory.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_hash_id
nodes.summary: Returns the hash algorithm of the stack.

nodes.name: reftable_addition
nodes.summary: State of a transaction that adds tables to a stack while holding the tables.list lock, tracking new table names and the next update index.

nodes.name: stack.h
nodes.summary: Defines struct reftable_stack (list file, lock, directory, options, loaded tables, merged table, compaction stats) and struct segment, and declares read_lines and suggest_compaction_segment.

nodes.name: reftable_stack
nodes.summary: Stack of tables in one directory tracked by tables.list, with the loaded table array, merged table view, lock state, options and compaction statistics.

nodes.name: segment
nodes.summary: Half-open range of tables to compact together with the total byte size.

nodes.name: system.c
nodes.summary: Glue between the self-contained reftable library and Git: random numbers, temporary files, lock files, fsync, millisecond clock and mmap are implemented on top of Git lockfile, tempfile, trace and wrapper APIs.
nodes.languageNotes: Adapter layer: the reftable library is written to be reusable outside Git, so every OS and Git dependency is isolated here.

nodes.name: reftable_rand
nodes.summary: Returns a random 32-bit value from Git git_rand, used for retry backoff jitter.

nodes.name: tmpfile_from_pattern
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary file from a mkstemp-style pattern using Git mks_tempfile and exposes path and fd.

nodes.name: tmpfile_close
nodes.summary: Closes the temporary file descriptor via close_tempfile_gently.

nodes.name: tmpfile_delete
nodes.summary: Deletes the temporary file with delete_tempfile.

nodes.name: tmpfile_rename
nodes.summary: Atomically renames the temporary file to its final path with rename_tempfile.

nodes.name: flock_acquire
nodes.summary: Takes a Git lock file (path.lock) for a target path with an optional timeout, mapping EEXIST to REFTABLE_LOCK_ERROR.

nodes.name: flock_close
nodes.summary: Closes the lock file descriptor without releasing the lock.

nodes.name: flock_release
nodes.summary: Rolls back and frees the lock file, removing the lock.

nodes.name: flock_commit
nodes.summary: Commits the lock file by renaming it over the target, publishing the new content atomically.

nodes.name: reftable_fsync
