nodes.summary: Flushes a descriptor to disk with fsync_component for the reference component, honoring core.fsync settings.

nodes.name: reftable_time_ms
nodes.summary: Returns the current time in milliseconds from getnanotime.

nodes.name: reftable_mmap
nodes.summary: Maps a file read-only with xmmap_gently and records base and size.

nodes.name: reftable_munmap
nodes.summary: Unmaps a mapping created by reftable_mmap and zeroes the descriptor.

nodes.name: system.h
nodes.summary: Declares the platform layer reftable needs: random numbers, temp files (reftable_tmpfile), file locks (reftable_flock), fsync, clock and mmap, implemented in system.c on Git APIs.

nodes.name: reftable_tmpfile
nodes.summary: Handle to a temporary file with path, descriptor and private implementation pointer.

nodes.name: reftable_flock
nodes.summary: Handle to a held lock file with path, descriptor and private implementation pointer.

nodes.name: reftable_mmap
nodes.summary: Read-only memory mapping with base pointer and size.

nodes.name: table.c
nodes.summary: Reads a single reftable file: parses and CRC-checks the footer, locates the ref, obj and log sections, and provides table iterators that seek via linear block scanning or the multi-level index, plus reverse lookup of refs by object id.

nodes.name: table_offsets_for
nodes.summary: Returns the section offsets descriptor (ref, log or obj) for a block type.

nodes.name: reftable_table_hash_id
nodes.summary: Returns the hash algorithm of the table.

nodes.name: reftable_table_name
nodes.summary: Returns the file name associated with the table.

nodes.name: parse_footer
nodes.summary: Parses the table footer: checks the REFT magic, compares footer and header, reads block size, update index range, hash id (v2), section and index offsets, verifies the CRC-32 and derives which sections are present.

nodes.name: table_iter_next_in_block
nodes.summary: Advances within the current block and rebases ref update indexes onto the table min update index.

nodes.name: table_init_block
nodes.summary: Loads the block at an offset in the table through reftable_block_init, honoring the first-block header offset.

nodes.name: table_iter_next_block
nodes.summary: Loads the next block after the current one, marking the iterator finished at the end of the section.

nodes.name: table_iter_next
nodes.summary: Yields the next record, moving block by block when the current block is exhausted.

nodes.name: table_iter_seek_to
nodes.summary: Positions the iterator at a block offset and type.

nodes.name: table_iter_seek_start
nodes.summary: Seeks to the start of a section, or of its index when requested.

nodes.name: table_iter_seek_linear
nodes.summary: Finds the block containing a key by scanning blocks until the first key exceeds the wanted key, then seeks inside the preceding block.

nodes.name: table_iter_seek_indexed
nodes.summary: Seeks through the multi-level index: linear search in the top index level, descend through index records to a leaf block, then seek the key inside it.

nodes.name: table_iter_seek
nodes.summary: Seeks to a record using the section index when it exists, otherwise a linear block scan.

nodes.name: table_init_iter
nodes.summary: Creates a table iterator for a record type, returning an empty iterator when the section is absent.

nodes.name: reftable_table_init_ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over the ref section of a table.

nodes.name: reftable_table_init_log_iterator
nodes.summary: Initializes an iterator over the log section of a table.

nodes.name: reftable_table_new
nodes.summary: Opens a table from a block source: reads and validates the header, determines the format version, reads the footer and parses it, taking ownership of the source.

nodes.name: reftable_table_incref
nodes.summary: Increments the reference count of a table.

nodes.name: reftable_table_decref
nodes.summary: Decrements the reference count and frees the table and closes its source at zero.

nodes.name: reftable_table_refs_for_indexed
nodes.summary: Reverse lookup using the object index: seeks the o-section record for the oid prefix and iterates only the ref blocks it names.

nodes.name: reftable_table_refs_for_unindexed
nodes.summary: Reverse lookup without an object index: scans every ref and filters by object id.

nodes.name: reftable_table_refs_for
nodes.summary: Finds refs pointing at an object id, using the object index if present.

nodes.name: reftable_table_max_update_index
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum update index recorded in the table footer.

nodes.name: reftable_table_min_update_index
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum update index recorded in the table footer.

nodes.name: reftable_table_iterator_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a block-level iterator over all blocks of a table.

nodes.name: reftable_table_iterator_release
nodes.summary: Releases a table iterator created by reftable_table_iterator_init.

nodes.name: reftable_table_iterator_next
nodes.summary: Returns the next block of the table, used by consumers that inspect the raw blocks.

nodes.name: table_iter
nodes.summary: Iterator over one table section: table, record type, block offset, loaded block and block iterator.

nodes.name: table.h
nodes.summary: Internal table API: table name accessor, table_init_iter that creates an iterator for a record type, and table_init_block.

nodes.name: tree.c
nodes.summary: Minimal unbalanced binary search tree (search, insert, in-order walk, free) used by the writer to build the inverse object-id to ref-block index.

nodes.name: tree_search
nodes.summary: Recursively looks up a key in the binary search tree with a comparison callback and returns the node or NULL.

nodes.name: tree_insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a key into the tree, allocating a node when absent, and returns the existing or new node.

nodes.name: infix_walk
nodes.summary: Visits the tree in sorted (in-order) sequence and calls an action on each key.

nodes.name: tree_free
nodes.summary: Recursively frees all nodes of the tree (not the keys).

nodes.name: tree.h
nodes.summary: Declares the simple binary search tree (tree_node plus search, insert, in-order walk and free) used for the writer object index.

nodes.name: tree_node
nodes.summary: Binary tree node holding an opaque key and left and right children.

nodes.name: writer.c
nodes.summary: The reftable writer: it streams sorted ref and log records into blocks, tracks stats and padding, builds multi-level indexes and the inverse object-id index, and finally writes the footer with a CRC-32.

nodes.name: writer_reftable_block_stats
nodes.summary: Selects the per-block-type statistics struct (ref, obj, index or log) of the writer.

nodes.name: padded_write
nodes.summary: Writes data through the writer callback after flushing any pending zero padding, and queues new padding for the next write.

nodes.name: options_set_defaults
nodes.summary: Fills in default restart interval 16 and block size 4096 when unset.

nodes.name: writer_write_header
nodes.summary: Fills the file header or footer prefix: REFT magic, version, block size, update index range and, for version 2, the hash format id.

nodes.name: writer_reinit_block_writer
nodes.summary: Starts a new block of the given type, reserving space for the file header in the first block.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_new
nodes.summary: Creates a writer with write and flush callbacks, a hash id and options, allocating the block buffer and the first ref block writer.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_set_limits
nodes.summary: Sets the min and max update index of the table; must be called before the first record is written.

nodes.name: writer_release
nodes.summary: Frees the writer block buffer, block writer, index and key buffers.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_free
nodes.summary: Releases and frees a writer.

nodes.name: writer_index_hash
nodes.summary: Records that an object id occurs in the current ref block by adding the block offset to its entry in the inverse object-id tree.

nodes.name: writer_add_record
nodes.summary: Adds one record: enforces strictly ascending keys, switches blocks when the type changes, and flushes and re-adds when the block is full, failing if the record cannot fit an empty block.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_add_ref
nodes.summary: Adds a ref record after validating the name and update index range, rebases the update index and indexes its object ids for the obj section.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_add_refs
nodes.summary: Sorts an array of ref records by name and adds them in order.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_add_log_verbatim
nodes.summary: Adds a log record without message normalization, first finishing the ref section if still open.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_add_log
nodes.summary: Adds a reflog entry after checking limits, normalizing the message to exactly one trailing newline and rejecting multi-line messages.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_add_logs
nodes.summary: Sorts an array of log records by key and adds them in order.

nodes.name: writer_finish_section
nodes.summary: Flushes the last block of a section and, when it has many blocks, writes a multi-level index, recording index statistics.

nodes.name: update_common
nodes.summary: Tree walk callback that computes the longest common prefix of adjacent object ids to choose the shortest unique obj prefix length.

nodes.name: write_object_record
nodes.summary: Tree walk callback that writes one object-index record, flushing the block when full and dropping offsets if still too large.

nodes.name: writer_dump_object_index
nodes.summary: Writes the obj section: computes the object id prefix length, walks the object-id tree in order writing obj records and finishes the section with its index.

nodes.name: writer_finish_public_section
nodes.summary: Finishes the current ref or log section and, after refs, writes the object index unless disabled, then frees the object tree.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_close
nodes.summary: Finishes the table: finalizes sections, writes the footer with section and index offsets and a CRC-32 (or an empty header), flushes and frees the writer; returns REFTABLE_EMPTY_TABLE_ERROR for an empty table.

nodes.name: writer_flush_nonempty_block
nodes.summary: Finishes the current block (restart table, compression), applies padding, updates stats, writes the file header with the first block and appends an index record for the block.

nodes.name: reftable_writer_stats
nodes.summary: Returns the statistics (blocks, entries, index offsets, object id length) of the table written.

nodes.name: obj_index_tree_node
nodes.summary: Entry of the writer object-id tree: a hash and the offsets of ref blocks containing it.

nodes.name: writer.h
nodes.summary: Defines struct reftable_writer, the full state of a table writer: write and flush callbacks, key and scratch buffers, offsets, update index limits, options, block writer, pending index and object-id tree, and stats.

nodes.name: reftable_writer
nodes.summary: State of an in-progress table: output callbacks, current block writer, pending index records, object-id tree, update index limits, options and stats.

nodes.name: merge-ll.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the low-level three-way file merge: the ll_merge_options struct, the ll_merge_result enum and ll_merge(), a thin wrapper over xdl_merge that picks a merge driver from gitattributes and reports conflicts with marker lines.
nodes.languageNotes: The header documents the calling sequence in a doc comment: prepare options, fill three mmfile_t buffers, call ll_merge, read result_buf. LL_MERGE_OPTIONS_INIT is a designated initializer macro.

nodes.name: ll_merge_options
nodes.summary: Options for a single-file merge: virtual-ancestor handling, ours/theirs/union variant, renormalization, extra conflict marker size, conflict style and xdiff flags.

nodes.name: ll_merge_result
nodes.summary: Enum of results of ll_merge: error, ok, conflict and binary conflict.

nodes.name: merge-ort.c
nodes.summary: Implementation of the "ort" (Ostensibly Recursive's Twin) merge strategy, the default for git merge. It walks the three trees at once, records per-path state in a strmap, detects file and directory renames, merges contents, resolves or records conflicts, writes the result tree and can update the index and working tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure in-core design: merge_incore_nonrecursive()/merge_incore_recursive() produce a tree and a conflict list in merge_result without touching the index; merge_switch_to_result() later updates the index and working tree. All per-path data lives in opt->priv->paths (strmap of merged_info/conflict_info) with strings interned in a mem_pool so pointer comparison can replace strcmp.

nodes.name: clear_or_reinit_internal_opts
nodes.summary: Frees or partially resets every strmap, strintmap and strset held in merge_options_internal (paths, conflicted, rename caches) so the structure can be released or reused for the next merge in a rebase or cherry-pick sequence.

nodes.name: format_commit
nodes.summary: Appends an indented one-line description of a commit (abbreviated hash and subject, or "virtual <name>" for synthesized merge-base commits) to a strbuf for the "merging common ancestors" messages.

nodes.name: path_msg
nodes.summary: Printf-style recorder for merge messages: files each message under its primary path with a conflict/info type, skips hints when recording headers and messages from inner recursive merges, and stores the formatted text for later display or for remerge-diff headers.

nodes.name: pool_alloc_filespec
nodes.summary: Allocates a diff_filespec from a mem_pool, reusing the caller's path string, as a pool-based variant of alloc_filespec used when building rename-detection pairs.

nodes.name: pool_diff_queue
nodes.summary: Creates a diff_filepair in a mem_pool from two filespecs and optionally appends it to a diff queue, mirroring diff_queue() but with pool allocation.

nodes.name: unique_path
nodes.summary: Builds a path name of the form "path~branch" (with "/" in the branch flattened to "_" and a numeric suffix on clashes) that does not exist in opt->priv->paths, used when a conflicting file must be moved aside.

nodes.name: traverse_trees_wrapper_callback
nodes.summary: Callback installed during the first, buffering pass of traverse_trees_wrapper(): saves each (mask, dirmask, names) tuple into renames->callback_data and bumps dir_rename_mask when a file appears in a directory needing rename detection.

nodes.name: traverse_trees_wrapper
nodes.summary: Wraps traverse_trees(): first reads all entries of a directory while only recording them, which lets merge-ort learn about added files (for directory rename detection) before it runs the real collect_merge_info_callback on each saved entry.

nodes.name: setup_path_info
nodes.summary: Allocates a merged_info (resolved) or conflict_info (unresolved) from the pool for a path, fills in the three stage versions, masks, directory name and basename offset, and registers it in opt->priv->paths.

nodes.name: add_pair
nodes.summary: Records an added or deleted path as a diff_filepair in renames->pairs[side], skipping deletions that cannot be rename sources according to match_mask and dir_rename_mask and updating relevant_sources.

nodes.name: collect_rename_info
nodes.summary: Updates dir_rename_mask for the current directory and, for each side that deleted or added the path, calls add_pair so that rename detection later has the candidate sources and targets.

nodes.name: collect_merge_info_callback
nodes.summary: Per-entry callback of the three-way tree walk: derives filemask, dirmask, match_mask and D/F conflict state, trivially resolves paths where two sides agree, otherwise creates a conflict_info via setup_path_info and recurses into subdirectories (deferring some for rename optimization).

nodes.name: resolve_trivial_directory_merge
nodes.summary: Resolves a directory entry in favor of the side that changed it when the other side matches the merge base, and clears the matching stages from filemask, dirmask and D/F conflict flags.

nodes.name: handle_deferred_entries
nodes.summary: After the first traversal, revisits directories whose entries were deferred: for every path that rename detection now needs, it re-walks the trees to fill in the missing per-path info before rename detection runs.

nodes.name: collect_merge_info
nodes.summary: First phase of a merge: parses the base and two side trees, sets up traverse_info and walks the three trees together with collect_merge_info_callback, then handles deferred entries.

nodes.name: find_first_merges
nodes.summary: Finds the earliest merge commits that include both submodule commits a and b by running a rev-list --merges --ancestry-path query, used to suggest a submodule merge resolution.

nodes.name: merge_submodule
nodes.summary: Three-way merges a submodule gitlink: opens the submodule repository, checks that both sides fast-forward from the base, resolves by fast-forwarding when one contains the other, otherwise searches for a merge commit suggestion, and records submodule-specific conflict types.

nodes.name: initialize_attr_index
nodes.summary: Builds a fake index_state holding only .gitattributes, since renormalize_buffer needs an index to read attributes and merge-ort has none of its own.

nodes.name: merge_3way
nodes.summary: Runs ll_merge for one path: reads the three blobs, labels the conflict markers with branch names (and "merged common ancestors" for virtual bases), applies renormalization and merge options, and returns the merged buffer.

nodes.name: handle_content_merge
nodes.summary: Merges one path's file mode and content: trivially picks the changed side, calls merge_3way for regular files, merge_submodule for gitlinks and a variant-dependent choice for symlinks, optionally writes the result blob, and reports whether it was clean.

nodes.name: path_in_way
nodes.summary: Tells whether a path would be in the way of moving a renamed file there, i.e. it already exists cleanly or is a file or directory on the relevant side.

nodes.name: apply_dir_rename
nodes.summary: Returns a new path in which the leading directory (rename_info->key) is replaced by its renamed directory (rename_info->value), handling renames into the repository root.

nodes.name: handle_path_level_conflicts
nodes.summary: Applies a directory rename to one path and checks the collisions map; if the new location would collide with another path it reports a CONFLICT_DIR_RENAME_COLLISION and returns NULL, otherwise returns the new path.

nodes.name: get_provisional_directory_renames
nodes.summary: Collapses dir_rename_count (old dir to {new dir to count}) into dir_renames by picking the unique new directory with the highest count, and flags ties as ambiguous so no directory rename is applied.

nodes.name: handle_directory_level_conflicts
nodes.summary: Removes from both sides' directory rename maps any directory that was renamed on both sides, because the two renames conflict.

nodes.name: check_dir_renamed
nodes.summary: Looks up the nearest parent directory of a path in the dir_renames map by stripping trailing components one at a time.

nodes.name: compute_collisions
nodes.summary: Precomputes, for every path moved by an implicit directory rename, which sources map to the same target path so later steps can detect add/add style collisions caused by merged directories.

nodes.name: free_collisions
nodes.summary: Releases the collisions map built by compute_collisions, including its source_files lists and the interned new path strings.

nodes.name: check_for_directory_rename
nodes.summary: Decides whether an added or renamed file should be moved by an implicit directory rename: finds the renamed parent, handles exclusions and collisions and returns the new path or NULL, recording a conflict or hint message.

nodes.name: apply_directory_rename_modifications
nodes.summary: Moves a conflict_info from its old path to the directory-renamed path in opt->priv->paths, preserving directory pointer identity, adding missing parent directory entries and fixing masks and stages.

nodes.name: process_renames
nodes.summary: Turns each detected rename pair into per-path merge state: moves stage information to the new path, handles rename/delete, rename/rename(1to2 and 2to1) and rename/add collisions, does content merges for the renamed file and records the matching conflicts.

nodes.name: resolve_diffpair_statuses
nodes.summary: Sets the status (added, deleted, renamed) of each diff_filepair in a queue, a simplified copy of diff_resolve_rename_copy() which is static in diff.c.

nodes.name: prune_cached_from_relevant
nodes.summary: Removes from relevant_sources every path already covered by cached rename pairs or cached irrelevant entries, so rename detection is not redone for them.

nodes.name: use_cached_pairs
nodes.summary: Re-injects cached rename pairs from an earlier merge (in a rebase or cherry-pick sequence) into a diff queue as ready-made rename pairs when their targets are still valid.

nodes.name: cache_new_pair
nodes.summary: Stores a newly found rename (old path to new path) in cached_pairs and records the target name in cached_target_names for reuse by the next merge.

nodes.name: possibly_cache_new_pair
nodes.summary: Decides whether a diff pair from this merge should be cached for later merges (renames, directory-rename moves, or deletions that are no longer relevant) and calls cache_new_pair or records irrelevance.

nodes.name: detect_regular_renames
nodes.summary: Runs git's diffcore rename machinery on one side's add/delete pairs: prunes cached entries, configures diff options (rename score, limit, minimal), calls diffcore_rename_extended and records whether the rename limit was exceeded.

nodes.name: collect_renames
nodes.summary: Walks the renames found on one side, applies implicit directory renames where applicable via check_for_directory_rename, and collects the resulting rename pairs for process_renames.

nodes.name: detect_and_process_renames
nodes.summary: Top-level rename phase: detects renames on both sides, computes directory renames and collisions, collects renames, sorts them and processes them into merge state, honoring cached results and redo logic.

nodes.name: sort_dirs_next_to_their_children
nodes.summary: String comparison that sorts a directory name as if it had a trailing slash, so a directory appears right before the files beneath it in the reverse-order processing pass.

nodes.name: read_oid_strbuf
nodes.summary: Reads a blob object from the object database into a strbuf, reporting an error message through path_msg when the object is missing or is not a blob.

nodes.name: blob_unchanged
nodes.summary: Compares two blob versions for equality after optional renormalization (line ending and attribute conversion), so merges can ignore changes that only reflect normalization.

nodes.name: tree_entry_order
nodes.summary: qsort comparator that orders merged tree entries with base_name_compare using each entry's mode, giving git's canonical tree entry order.

nodes.name: write_tree
nodes.summary: Sorts the collected directory entries in canonical order, serializes them into raw tree object format (mode, name, hash) and writes the tree object to the object database.

nodes.name: record_entry_for_tree
nodes.summary: Appends a non-null merged entry (basename and result version) to the list of versions that will become the current directory's tree object.

nodes.name: write_completed_directory
nodes.summary: Called while processing paths in reverse order: detects when a directory's entries are all done, writes its tree object (or marks it empty/null), and maintains a stack of offsets into the pending versions list.

nodes.name: process_entry
nodes.summary: Resolves one path after rename handling: deals with directory/file conflicts, mode and type conflicts, add/add, modify/delete and ordinary content merges (via handle_content_merge), setting the final result or recording stage information for the index.

nodes.name: prefetch_for_content_merges
nodes.summary: Before content merges, collects blob ids of conflicted regular files and batch-fetches the missing ones from the promisor remote in one request (partial clone support).

nodes.name: process_entries
nodes.summary: Final phase: sorts all paths, prefetches blobs, then walks them in reverse order calling process_entry and write_completed_directory, finishing with the top-level result tree object id.

nodes.name: checkout
nodes.summary: Switches the index and working tree from the previous tree to the merge result tree with unpack_trees in two-way mode, honoring the "merge" porcelain error messages.

nodes.name: record_conflicted_index_entries
nodes.summary: After checkout, rewrites index entries for conflicted paths as stage 1/2/3 entries (removing the stage-0 entry), expanding sparse index entries as needed, so that the index reflects the unresolved merge.

nodes.name: print_submodule_conflict_suggestion
nodes.summary: Prints advice for resolving submodule merge conflicts, listing git add/merge steps for each conflicted submodule that has a usable suggestion.

nodes.name: merge_display_update_messages
nodes.summary: Prints the recorded merge messages (conflicts and info) sorted by path to stdout or the caller's stream, with a detailed mode, and then submodule advice.

nodes.name: merge_get_conflicted_files
nodes.summary: Fills a string_list with each conflicted path and a stage_info (stage number, mode, oid) per present side, giving callers the unmerged entries without touching the index.

nodes.name: merge_switch_to_result
nodes.summary: Applies an in-core merge result: optionally checks out the result tree and records conflicted index entries, then displays messages and finalizes the result.

nodes.name: merge_finalize
nodes.summary: Cleans up after a merge: resets attribute direction if renormalizing and frees the internal state stored in result->priv.

nodes.name: shift_tree_object
nodes.summary: Applies the "subtree" merge option: shifts one tree relative to another with shift_tree or shift_tree_by and returns the matching tree object.

nodes.name: make_virtual_commit
nodes.summary: Creates an in-memory commit object that points to a given tree with a descriptive label, used for the virtual merge base in recursive merges.

nodes.name: merge_start
nodes.summary: Validates merge_options and allocates and initializes merge_options_internal (memory pool, strmaps, rename caches, conflict maps) before a merge begins.

nodes.name: merge_check_renames_reusable
nodes.summary: Determines whether renames cached from the previous merge may be reused because the new base and sides are related to the old ones (cherry-pick and rebase sequences), setting cached_pairs_valid_side.

nodes.name: move_opt_priv_to_result_priv
nodes.summary: Moves opt->priv into result->priv at the end of the outermost merge so the rename cache can survive for the next merge.

nodes.name: merge_ort_nonrecursive_internal
nodes.summary: Core merge of three trees: collects merge info, detects and processes renames, processes all entries to produce the result tree, redoes the pass if the rename cache requires it, and fills merge_result.

nodes.name: merge_ort_internal
nodes.summary: Handles the recursive case: if there are several merge bases, merges them pairwise into a virtual commit via nested calls, then merges the two heads against that virtual base.

nodes.name: merge_incore_nonrecursive
nodes.summary: Public API: three-way merges two trees against a given base in core, with rename cache checks and merge_result bookkeeping.

nodes.name: merge_incore_recursive
nodes.summary: Public API: merges two commits in core using all given merge bases (or computing them), creating virtual merge bases recursively when there are several.

nodes.name: merge_recursive_config
nodes.summary: Reads merge-related configuration (merge.verbosity, rename limit, renormalize, merge.renames, directoryRenames, conflictstyle) into merge_options.

nodes.name: init_merge_options
nodes.summary: Zeroes and sets default merge_options values (rename detection, verbosity, histogram diff) and applies config and GIT_MERGE_VERBOSITY.

nodes.name: init_ui_merge_options
nodes.summary: Initializes merge_options for porcelain use, including user-interface config handling.

nodes.name: init_basic_merge_options
nodes.summary: Initializes merge_options for plumbing or internal callers that should not read UI config.

nodes.name: copy_merge_options
nodes.summary: Shallow-copies merge_options from one struct to another.

nodes.name: clear_merge_options
nodes.summary: Releases merge_options resources; currently a no-op because copies are shallow.

nodes.name: parse_merge_opt
nodes.summary: Parses one -X strategy option string (ours, theirs, subtree, patience, histogram, diff-algorithm, renormalize, find-renames, rename-threshold, etc.) into merge_options.

nodes.name: rename_info
nodes.summary: Per-merge rename-detection state: diff pairs for each side, removed directories, directory rename counts and final directory renames, relevant sources, deferred traversal data and caches that let renames be reused across merges.

nodes.name: merge_options_internal
nodes.summary: Private state of one merge: the paths strmap of merged_info/conflict_info, conflicted and conflicts maps, memory pool, rename_info, attribute index, recursion depth and the stack of current directory names.

nodes.name: merged_info
nodes.summary: Per-path merge result for a cleanly merged path: result version (mode and oid), clean flag, basename offset and interned directory name.

nodes.name: conflict_info
nodes.summary: Extends merged_info with the three input versions, per-stage path names, D/F and path conflict flags and filemask, dirmask and match_mask for unresolved paths.

nodes.name: deferred_traversal_data
nodes.summary: Data that lets collect_merge_info postpone entries whose rename relevance is unknown: trivially resolvable paths and a set of possible trivial merges.

nodes.name: directory_versions
nodes.summary: Accumulator used while writing result trees: list of entries per directory, stack of offsets and the last directory seen.

nodes.name: name-hash.c
nodes.summary: Maintains the in-memory hash tables of an index_state: name_hash for cache entries and dir_hash for directories, built lazily (optionally with multiple threads) and used for fast, optionally case-insensitive, lookup of file and directory names.
nodes.languageNotes: Threaded initialization runs in two phases: several "dir" threads build dir_hash guarded by 32 bucket-partitioned mutexes and park per-entry results in a lazy_entry array, then one "name" thread fills name_hash while the main thread updates directory ref-counts.

nodes.name: dir_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: hashmap comparison callback for dir_hash entries: equal when the lengths match and the names compare equal ignoring case.

nodes.name: hash_dir_entry
nodes.summary: Finds or creates the dir_entry for the parent directory of a cache entry, recursively creating missing parent directories in dir_hash.

nodes.name: remove_dir_entry
nodes.summary: Drops a reference to the directory entries of a cache entry and removes from dir_hash and frees every directory whose count reaches zero.

nodes.name: hash_index_entry
nodes.summary: Inserts one cache entry into istate->name_hash (skipping sparse directories) and, on case-insensitive filesystems, registers its directories; marks the entry CE_HASHED.

nodes.name: cache_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: hashmap comparison callback for name_hash: pointer equality when removing an entry, always equal on hash match when searching (same_name decides later).

nodes.name: lookup_lazy_params
nodes.summary: Decides whether lazy name-hash initialization should use threads, depending on case sensitivity, CPU count and a minimum of 2000 entries per thread.

nodes.name: hash_dir_entry_with_parent_and_prefix
nodes.summary: Thread-safe variant that finds or creates a directory entry for a path prefix under a parent, locking the bucket mutex and bumping the parent count.

nodes.name: handle_range_dir
nodes.summary: Finds the end of the run of entries sharing a directory prefix (using binary search), creates the directory entry and recurses over that range.

nodes.name: handle_range_1
nodes.summary: Iterates a range of sorted index entries, recursing into subdirectories and recording each file's parent dir and name hash into the lazy_entries array without locking.

nodes.name: lazy_name_thread_proc
nodes.summary: Thread entry point of phase two: marks every entry hashed and adds all non-sparse entries to name_hash.

nodes.name: lazy_update_dir_ref_counts
nodes.summary: Increments the reference count of each entry's parent directory after the parallel phase, when no locking is needed.

nodes.name: threaded_lazy_init_name_hash
nodes.summary: Builds the hash tables with threads: spawns directory threads, joins them, then runs the name thread while the main thread updates directory counts.

nodes.name: lazy_init_name_hash
nodes.summary: Initializes name_hash and dir_hash on first use, choosing the threaded or sequential path and recording a trace2 region.

nodes.name: test_lazy_init_name_hash
nodes.summary: Test helper that forces lazy initialization with or without threads and returns how many threads were used.

nodes.name: add_name_hash
nodes.summary: Adds a new cache entry to the name hash if the hash has already been built.

nodes.name: remove_name_hash
nodes.summary: Removes a cache entry from name_hash and releases its directory references.

nodes.name: slow_same_name
nodes.summary: Compares two names case-insensitively for equal lengths with a byte loop using toupper.

nodes.name: same_name
nodes.summary: Compares a cache entry name with a lookup name: exact first, then case-insensitive if requested.

nodes.name: index_dir_find
nodes.summary: Finds a directory in the index by case-insensitive name, optionally returning the canonical spelling; expands the sparse index first.

nodes.name: adjust_dirname_case
nodes.summary: Rewrites each directory component of a path to the case recorded in the index.

nodes.name: index_file_exists
nodes.summary: Looks up a file by name in name_hash, matching exactly or case-insensitively with same_name, and returns the cache entry or NULL.

nodes.name: free_name_hash
nodes.summary: Frees name_hash and dir_hash and marks the hash as not initialized.

nodes.name: dir_entry
nodes.summary: Directory node stored in dir_hash: parent link, reference count, name length and flexible name.

nodes.name: lazy_entry
nodes.summary: Per-index-entry scratch record (directory pointer and two hashes) filled lock-free by phase one and consumed by phase two.

nodes.name: lazy_dir_thread_data
nodes.summary: Arguments for a "dir" worker thread: pthread, index, entry range and shared lazy_entries.

nodes.name: lazy_name_thread_data
nodes.summary: Arguments for the single "name" worker thread.

nodes.name: name-hash.h
nodes.summary: Declares the name-hash API of the index: lookup of files and directories by name with optional case folding, directory-name case adjustment, and add/remove/free hooks that keep the name and directory hashes in sync with index entries.

nodes.name: notes-merge.c
nodes.summary: Implements merging of two notes trees (git notes merge): it diffs base against both sides, merges per-object note changes using manual, ours, theirs, union or cat_sort_uniq strategies, writes conflicts into a NOTES_MERGE_WORKTREE directory, and later commits or aborts the resolution.

nodes.name: init_notes_merge_options
nodes.summary: Zero-initializes notes_merge_options and sets default verbosity and repository.

nodes.name: path_to_oid
nodes.summary: Converts a notes tree path (hex with fanout slashes) back into an object id.

nodes.name: verify_notes_filepair
nodes.summary: Checks that a diff pair is an add, delete or modify of a note and extracts the annotated object id from its path.

nodes.name: find_notes_merge_pair_pos
nodes.summary: Searches the sorted array of note merge pairs for an object id, caching the last index, and optionally opens a slot for insertion.

nodes.name: diff_tree_remote
nodes.summary: Diffs the base and remote notes trees and builds the array of notes_merge_pair entries with base and remote note oids.

nodes.name: diff_tree_local
nodes.summary: Diffs base against the local notes tree and fills in the local note oid of each existing pair, adding entries for local-only changes.

nodes.name: check_notes_merge_worktree
nodes.summary: Establishes NOTES_MERGE_WORKTREE, refusing to start a new merge if a previous unfinished merge left files there.

nodes.name: write_buf_to_worktree
nodes.summary: Writes a buffer to the notes merge worktree under the annotated object's hex name.

nodes.name: write_note_to_worktree
nodes.summary: Reads a note blob from the object database and writes it into the notes merge worktree.

nodes.name: ll_merge_in_worktree
nodes.summary: Three-way merges base, local and remote note contents with ll_merge and writes the result with conflict markers into the notes merge worktree.

nodes.name: merge_one_change_manual
nodes.summary: Handles a conflicting note under the manual strategy: appends to the commit message conflict list and writes the note (or conflict markers) to the notes merge worktree.

nodes.name: merge_one_change
nodes.summary: Resolves one conflicting note according to the strategy (manual, ours, theirs, union or cat_sort_uniq), updating the notes tree on success or returning 1 for an unresolved conflict.

nodes.name: merge_changes
nodes.summary: Iterates the note change pairs and applies them: skips unchanged, adopts remote-only changes and calls merge_one_change for conflicts, returning the conflict count.

nodes.name: merge_from_diffs
nodes.summary: Builds the change list via diff_tree_remote and diff_tree_local and merges it into the notes tree.

nodes.name: notes_merge
nodes.summary: Entry point of notes merge: resolves local and remote refs, finds the merge base, handles up-to-date and fast-forward cases, otherwise merges the diffs and creates a merge commit.

nodes.name: notes_merge_commit
nodes.summary: Finalizes a manual notes merge: adds each resolved file in NOTES_MERGE_WORKTREE as a note blob, and creates the notes commit with the original message and parents.

nodes.name: notes_merge_abort
nodes.summary: Aborts a notes merge by recursively removing the files inside NOTES_MERGE_WORKTREE but keeping the directory.

nodes.name: notes_merge_pair
nodes.summary: Record of one annotated object with its base, local and remote note oids, used to compare changes from both sides.

nodes.name: transaction.h
nodes.summary: Defines the object database transaction interface: a struct of backend callbacks (commit, finalize, write_object_stream, write_pack, env) plus begin/commit/finalize wrappers so that several object writes (loose objects or an ingested packfile) become visible atomically.
nodes.languageNotes: Each ODB source supplies its own transaction implementation through function pointers; only one transaction may be pending per object database at a time.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_write_pack_opts
nodes.summary: Options for ingesting a packfile into a transaction: fsck settings, shallow file, max size, thin-pack rejection, error fd and quiet flag.

nodes.name: odb_transaction
nodes.summary: Transaction handle with per-backend callbacks: commit, finalize, write_object_stream, write_pack and env.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_flags
nodes.summary: Flags configuring a transaction, such as ODB_TRANSACTION_RECEIVE for receive-pack.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_begin_or_die
nodes.summary: Starts a transaction and dies on failure.

nodes.name: odb_transaction_commit_and_finalize_or_die
nodes.summary: Commits and finalizes a transaction, dying if either step fails.

nodes.name: parallel-checkout.c
nodes.summary: Implements parallel working-tree checkout: eligible regular-file entries are queued, then split into batches for "checkout--worker" child processes that smudge and write files and send stat results back over pkt-line, or written sequentially below a threshold.

nodes.name: parallel_checkout_status
nodes.summary: Returns the current state (uninitialized, accepting entries, running) of the global parallel checkout queue.

nodes.name: get_parallel_checkout_configs
nodes.summary: Reads checkout.workers and checkout.thresholdForParallelism, with GIT_TEST_CHECKOUT_WORKERS as a test override, defaulting to one worker and a threshold of 100.

nodes.name: init_parallel_checkout
nodes.summary: Puts the queue into the accepting-entries state and refuses to run twice.

nodes.name: is_eligible_for_parallel_checkout
nodes.summary: Decides whether an entry can be written by a worker: regular files with in-core or streamable conversion and a small enough packet size; symlinks and external or process filters are excluded.

nodes.name: enqueue_checkout
nodes.summary: Queues an eligible cache entry with its conversion attributes for later parallel write, returning -1 when the entry should be checked out sequentially.

nodes.name: pc_queue_size
nodes.summary: Returns the number of queued entries.

nodes.name: handle_results
nodes.summary: After all items are written, updates index stat data for written entries and re-runs checkout_entry_ca for collided entries so collisions are reported consistently; returns an error for failed or pending items.

nodes.name: write_pc_item_to_fd
nodes.summary: Writes one entry to an open file: tries streaming through a stream filter, otherwise reads the blob, converts it to working tree format and writes it.

nodes.name: close_and_clear
nodes.summary: Closes a file descriptor if open and returns the close result.

nodes.name: write_pc_item
nodes.summary: Creates one working-tree file for a queue item: checks leading directories and O_EXCL creation to detect path collisions, writes content, fstats the output and sets the item status. Runs in the main process or in a worker.

nodes.name: send_one_item
nodes.summary: Serializes one queue item (fixed portion plus encoding and file name) and sends it to a worker as a pkt-line.

nodes.name: setup_workers
nodes.summary: Spawns the checkout--worker child processes and divides the queued items evenly among them, sending each its batch.

nodes.name: finish_workers
nodes.summary: Closes the pipes to every worker and waits for them, reporting workers killed by signals.

nodes.name: parse_and_save_result
nodes.summary: Validates one result packet from a worker and stores its status and stat data in the matching queue item.

nodes.name: gather_results_from_workers
nodes.summary: Polls all worker pipes, reading result packets and saving them until every worker has finished.

nodes.name: write_items_sequentially
nodes.summary: Writes all queued items in the current process when parallelism is not worthwhile.

nodes.name: run_parallel_checkout
nodes.summary: Runs the queue: below the threshold or with one worker writes sequentially, otherwise starts workers, gathers results and finishes them, then handles collisions and resets state.

nodes.name: pc_worker
nodes.summary: State for one worker process: child_process handle plus which item it should return next and how many remain.

nodes.name: parallel_checkout
nodes.summary: Global queue of items with status, counts and progress pointers for parallel checkout.

nodes.name: parallel-checkout.h
nodes.summary: Declares the parallel-checkout API used by checkout code (init, enqueue, run) and the structures shared with checkout--worker: queue item status, the fixed-size wire format for items, and the result record returned by workers.

nodes.name: pc_status
nodes.summary: State of the global parallel checkout queue: uninitialized, accepting entries, running.

nodes.name: pc_item_status
nodes.summary: Status of a queued item: pending, written, collided or failed.

nodes.name: parallel_checkout_item
nodes.summary: Queue item: cache entry, conversion attributes, id, counter, and the status and stat data returned by workers.

nodes.name: pc_item_fixed_portion
nodes.summary: Fixed-size header sent to workers for each item: id, oid, mode, CRLF action, ident and string lengths.

nodes.name: pc_item_result
nodes.summary: Result record returned by a worker: item id, status and stat data (omitted on error).

nodes.name: pathspec.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct pathspec and the pathspec magic flags (top, literal, glob, icase, exclude, attr) with parse, copy, clear and match functions used by nearly every path-limiting command, plus helpers for matching pathspecs against the index and sparse checkout.

nodes.name: pathspec
nodes.summary: Parsed set of pathspec items with magic flags, wildcard info, depth limit and per-item match, prefix and attribute requirements.

nodes.name: ps_skip_worktree_action
nodes.summary: Enum selecting whether matching honors or ignores the skip-worktree bit.

nodes.name: match_leading_pathspec
nodes.summary: Like match_pathspec but also matches a leading directory prefix.

nodes.name: preload-index.c
nodes.summary: Speeds up index refresh by running lstat() calls on index entries in up to 20 threads (preload_index), marking unchanged entries up-to-date before the main refresh; also provides repo_read_index_preload() which reads the index and then preloads it.

nodes.name: preload_thread
nodes.summary: Worker routine that lstat()s a slice of index entries, skipping unmerged, gitlink, up-to-date, skip-worktree, fsmonitor-valid and non-matching entries, and marks unchanged ones up-to-date.

nodes.name: preload_index
nodes.summary: Splits the index into up to 20 slices of at least 500 entries and runs preload_thread on each (with optional progress), controlled by core.preloadindex.

nodes.name: repo_read_index_preload
nodes.summary: Reads the repository index and then preloads it with preload_index.

nodes.name: progress_data
nodes.summary: Mutex-protected progress counter shared by preload threads.

nodes.name: thread_data
nodes.summary: Per-thread arguments: index, pathspec copy, slice offset and count, progress and lstat counter.

nodes.name: preload-index.h
nodes.summary: Declares preload_index() and repo_read_index_preload(), the entry points for multithreaded stat preloading of the index.

nodes.name: read-cache-ll.h
nodes.summary: Low-level index (directory cache) header: defines struct cache_entry, struct index_state, the CE_* flag bits, the on-disk cache_header, and the API to create, read, write, search, add, remove, stat-compare and refresh index entries.
nodes.languageNotes: CE_* flags are split into on-disk bits (stage, valid, extended flags) and in-memory-only bits (UPDATE, REMOVE, UPTODATE, HASHED, ...), guarded by a compile-time #error check.

nodes.name: cache_header
nodes.summary: On-disk header of the index file: signature "DIRC", version and entry count.

nodes.name: cache_entry
nodes.summary: One index entry: stat data, mode, flags, object id and path name.

nodes.name: sparse_index_mode
nodes.summary: Whether the index is expanded, collapsed into sparse directories or partially sparse.

nodes.name: index_state
nodes.summary: In-memory index: entry array, version, cache-tree, split-index, untracked cache, name and dir hashes and flags.

nodes.name: copy_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Copies stat data, oid and flags of a cache entry but keeps the name and hash state.

nodes.name: index_state_init
nodes.summary: Initializes an index_state for a repository.

nodes.name: make_transient_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Creates a cache entry not meant for an index, optionally in a memory pool.

nodes.name: dup_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Duplicates a cache entry using the index memory pool.

nodes.name: move_index_extensions
nodes.summary: Moves extension data such as cache-tree and untracked cache between indexes.

nodes.name: unmerged_index
nodes.summary: Returns whether the index has unmerged (staged 1-3) entries.

nodes.name: index_name_pos_sparse
nodes.summary: Like index_name_pos but does not expand sparse directories.

nodes.name: index_entry_exists
nodes.summary: Tells whether an exact entry exists without expanding a sparse index.

nodes.name: repo_refresh_and_write_index
nodes.summary: Refreshes the index and writes it to disk under a lock.

nodes.name: abspath.h
nodes.summary: Public header for absolute and canonical path helpers: realpath-style resolution into a strbuf, absolute_path, prefix_filename and an is_absolute_path inline. Implemented in abspath.c.

nodes.name: is_absolute_path
nodes.summary: Static inline test for an absolute path: a leading directory separator or a DOS drive prefix.

nodes.name: attr.c
nodes.summary: Implements the gitattributes engine: interns attribute names in a global hashmap, parses .gitattributes lines, builds a stack of attribute files (builtin, system, global, per-directory, info/attributes) and resolves attribute values for a path.

nodes.name: git_attr
nodes.summary: Opaque struct for an interned attribute: a unique attr_nr index plus the flexible-array attribute name.

nodes.name: all_attrs_item
nodes.summary: Per-attribute working slot used while collecting attributes for a path: the git_attr, its resolved value and, if it is a macro, the macro definition.

nodes.name: attr_stack
nodes.summary: Linked-list frame holding the parsed match_attr lines of one attribute source (builtin, system, global, a directory .gitattributes or info/attributes).

nodes.name: git_attr_name
nodes.summary: Returns the name string of an interned git_attr.

nodes.name: attr_hash_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback for the attribute dictionary: entries match when key length and bytes are equal.

nodes.name: attr_hashmap_get
nodes.summary: Looks up an interned attribute by name in the global attribute hashmap, returning NULL when absent.

nodes.name: attr_hashmap_add
nodes.summary: Allocates a hash entry and inserts a key/value pair into the attribute hashmap.

nodes.name: all_attrs_init
nodes.summary: Resizes and resets check->all_attrs from the global dictionary under the hashmap lock so every interned attribute starts with value UNKNOWN and no macro.

nodes.name: attr_name_valid
nodes.summary: Validates an attribute name: non-empty, not starting with "-", and only [-A-Za-z0-9_.] characters.

nodes.name: git_attr_internal
nodes.summary: Finds or creates the interned git_attr for a name under the global hashmap mutex, assigning the next attr_nr.

nodes.name: git_attr
nodes.summary: Public entry that interns an attribute by NUL-terminated name via git_attr_internal.

nodes.name: parse_attr
nodes.summary: Parses one attribute state ("attr", "-attr", "!attr" or "attr=value"); the first pass only validates, the second fills an attr_state and interns the name.

nodes.name: parse_attr_line
nodes.summary: Parses a full .gitattributes line into a match_attr: handles quoted patterns, [attr] macro definitions, the path pattern via parse_path_pattern, and the list of attribute states.

nodes.name: attr_stack_free
nodes.summary: Frees an attr_stack frame, its origin string and each match_attr including heap-allocated attribute values.

nodes.name: check_vector_add
nodes.summary: Appends an attr_check to the global check vector under its mutex so stacks can be dropped later.

nodes.name: check_vector_remove
nodes.summary: Removes an attr_check from the global check vector under its mutex (BUG if missing).

nodes.name: drop_all_attr_stacks
nodes.summary: Walks every registered attr_check and drops its attribute stack, used when the attribute read direction changes.

nodes.name: attr_check_alloc
nodes.summary: Allocates an empty attr_check and registers it in the global check vector.

nodes.name: attr_check_initl
nodes.summary: Builds an attr_check from a NULL-terminated variadic list of attribute names, interning each.

nodes.name: attr_check_dup
nodes.summary: Duplicates an attr_check and its item array into a new registered check.

nodes.name: attr_check_append
nodes.summary: Appends an attribute to a check, growing the item array, and returns the new item.

nodes.name: attr_check_reset
nodes.summary: Resets a check to zero requested items.

nodes.name: attr_check_clear
nodes.summary: Frees items and all_attrs of a check and drops its attribute stack.

nodes.name: attr_check_free
nodes.summary: Unregisters a check from the global vector, clears it and frees it.

nodes.name: handle_attr_line
nodes.summary: Parses one attribute line and, if valid, appends the resulting match_attr to an attr_stack.

nodes.name: read_attr_from_array
nodes.summary: Builds an attr_stack frame from an in-memory array of lines such as the builtin "[attr]binary" macro.

nodes.name: git_attr_set_direction
nodes.summary: Sets whether attributes are read from index, checkout or checkin sources, discarding cached stacks when it changes.

nodes.name: read_attr_from_file
nodes.summary: Reads a .gitattributes file from the working tree (optionally without following symlinks), enforcing a size limit and skipping a UTF-8 BOM.

nodes.name: read_attr_from_buf
nodes.summary: Parses a gitattributes buffer line by line into an attr_stack, rejecting oversized content.

nodes.name: read_attr_from_blob
nodes.summary: Reads a .gitattributes blob out of a tree object via get_tree_entry and odb_read_object and parses it.

nodes.name: read_attr_from_index
nodes.summary: Reads .gitattributes content from the index, including the sparse-directory case where it must come from the sparse tree object.

nodes.name: read_attr
nodes.summary: Chooses the attribute source by direction: tree blob, index, or working-tree file, always returning a (possibly empty) stack frame.

nodes.name: git_attr_system_file
nodes.summary: Returns the cached path of the system-wide gitattributes file.

nodes.name: git_attr_global_file
nodes.summary: Returns the global attributes file path from core.attributesFile or the XDG location.

nodes.name: git_attr_system_is_enabled
nodes.summary: Reports whether the system gitattributes file is enabled (GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM unset).

nodes.name: push_stack
nodes.summary: Pushes a stack frame on top of the attribute stack and records its origin directory.

nodes.name: bootstrap_attr_stack
nodes.summary: Seeds the attribute stack with the builtin, system, global, root .gitattributes and info/attributes frames.

nodes.name: prepare_attr_stack
nodes.summary: Adjusts the stack for a path by popping frames from other directories, reading each .gitattributes down to the path directory, and keeping info/attributes on top.

nodes.name: path_matches
nodes.summary: Tests whether a path matches an attribute pattern, handling directory-only patterns and basename or full-pathname glob matching.

nodes.name: fill_one
nodes.summary: Applies the states of one matched line to the output slots (earlier-found wins) and expands macro attributes via a work queue.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Scans the attribute stack from top to bottom, last line first, filling attribute values for a path until none remain unresolved.

nodes.name: determine_macros
nodes.summary: Marks which attributes are macros by scanning the stack, so expansion during fill needs no repeated search.

nodes.name: collect_some_attrs
nodes.summary: Collects attribute values for a path: computes directory and basename offsets, prepares the stack, initializes all_attrs, determines macros and fills.

nodes.name: set_git_attr_source
nodes.summary: Records the tree-ish given by --attr-source to read attributes from.

nodes.name: compute_default_attr_source
nodes.summary: Resolves the attribute source tree from --attr-source, GIT_ATTR_SOURCE or the bare-repo default, dying on a bad value unless it is the ignorable default.

nodes.name: default_attr_source
nodes.summary: Lazily computes and caches the default attribute-source tree object id.

nodes.name: interned_mode_string
nodes.summary: Returns an interned octal string for one of the supported file modes (tree, regular, executable, symlink, gitlink).

nodes.name: builtin_object_mode_attr
nodes.summary: Computes the builtin_objectmode attribute from the lstat mode (check-in) or from the index entry mode, including submodule detection.

nodes.name: compute_builtin_attr
nodes.summary: Returns values for reserved builtin_ attributes; currently only builtin_objectmode.

nodes.name: git_check_attr
nodes.summary: Looks up the requested attributes of a path and stores their values in the check items, computing builtin attributes for unknown ones.

nodes.name: git_all_attrs
nodes.summary: Collects every set attribute of a path into the check, skipping unset and unknown ones.

nodes.name: attr_start
nodes.summary: Initializes the mutexes of the global attribute hashmap and check vector.

nodes.name: bugreport.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git bugreport": writes a text template plus system info (git version, uname, compiler, libc, shell) and the list of enabled hooks to a timestamped file, optionally with a diagnostics zip, then opens an editor.

nodes.name: get_system_info
nodes.summary: Appends git version, uname, compiler, libc info and $SHELL to the report buffer.

nodes.name: get_populated_hooks
nodes.summary: Lists hook names from hook_name_list that exist in the repository, or notes that no repository is present.

nodes.name: get_bug_template
nodes.summary: Writes the translated bug-report questionnaire into the buffer.

nodes.name: get_header
nodes.summary: Appends a bracketed section title to the report.

nodes.name: cmd_bugreport
nodes.summary: Entry point of git bugreport: parses options, builds the report path with a strftime suffix, optionally creates a diagnostics zip, writes template, system info and hooks exclusively, then launches the editor.

nodes.name: bundle.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git bundle" with create, verify, list-heads and unbundle subcommands, delegating to the bundle API for packing refs and objects into a single file and reading them back.

nodes.name: parse_options_cmd_bundle
nodes.summary: Shared option parsing for bundle subcommands; requires a file argument and resolves it against the prefix.

nodes.name: cmd_bundle_create
nodes.summary: Implements "bundle create": requires a repository and calls create_bundle with the file, rev-list args, version and progress flag.

nodes.name: open_bundle
nodes.summary: Opens a bundle header from a path or from stdin when the path is "-".

nodes.name: cmd_bundle_verify
nodes.summary: Implements "bundle verify": reads the header and checks with verify_bundle that prerequisites exist in the repository.

nodes.name: cmd_bundle_list_heads
nodes.summary: Implements "bundle list-heads": prints the refs recorded in a bundle header.

nodes.name: cmd_bundle_unbundle
nodes.summary: Implements "bundle unbundle": feeds the packed objects to index-pack through unbundle and then lists the refs.

nodes.name: cmd_bundle
nodes.summary: Entry point of git bundle: dispatches the create, verify, list-heads and unbundle subcommands.

nodes.name: config.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git config": location options (system, global, local, worktree, file, blob), typed value formatting, get/set/unset/list/edit subcommands plus legacy action flags, color lookups and URL-matched config lookup.

nodes.name: config_location_options
nodes.summary: Holds which config scope or file to read or write (system, global, local, worktree, file, blob), include handling and the config source.

nodes.name: config_display_options
nodes.summary: Holds how values are displayed: type, key and origin/scope display, delimiters and default value.

nodes.name: option_parse_type
nodes.summary: Option callback that turns --type and legacy --bool/--int/--path style flags into one config value type, rejecting conflicts.

nodes.name: check_argc
nodes.summary: Dies with a usage error when the argument count is outside the allowed range.

nodes.name: die_missing_set_value
nodes.summary: Dies with an explanatory message when "config set" is given a key but no value.

nodes.name: show_config_origin
nodes.summary: Appends the origin of a config entry (file, blob, command line) to the output.

nodes.name: show_config_scope
nodes.summary: Appends the scope (system, global, local, ...) of a config entry to the output.

nodes.name: format_config_int64
nodes.summary: Formats a value as a 64-bit integer, parsing unit suffixes such as k, m, g.

nodes.name: format_config_bool
nodes.summary: Formats a value as "true" or "false".

nodes.name: format_config_bool_or_int
nodes.summary: Formats a value as a boolean or integer.

nodes.name: format_config_bool_or_str
nodes.summary: Formats a value as a boolean when it parses as one, otherwise as the raw string.

nodes.name: format_config_path
nodes.summary: Expands a path-valued config entry (~, ~user, %(prefix)) through git_config_pathname.

nodes.name: format_config_expiry_date
nodes.summary: Formats a value as an expiry timestamp using git_config_expiry_date.

nodes.name: format_config_color
nodes.summary: Formats a value as an ANSI color escape sequence.

nodes.name: format_config
nodes.summary: Central formatter: optionally prefixes scope, origin and key, converts the value according to the display type, and appends the terminator.

nodes.name: show_all_config
nodes.summary: Config callback used by "config list" that formats and prints every entry.

nodes.name: collect_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that filters entries by key, key regexp, value pattern or fixed value and collects formatted values.

nodes.name: get_value
nodes.summary: Implements the lookup behind "config get": compiles key and value patterns, scans the config sources, applies --default, and prints all or the last matching value.

nodes.name: normalize_value
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes a value to be written by "config set --type" (int, bool, color check) while keeping paths and dates verbatim.

nodes.name: git_get_color_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that parses a requested color slot value.

nodes.name: get_color
nodes.summary: Prints the ANSI color for a config slot, falling back to a default color.

nodes.name: git_get_colorbool_config
nodes.summary: Config callback gathering the slot, diff.color and color.ui settings for a colorbool query.

nodes.name: get_colorbool
nodes.summary: Decides whether color output is wanted from the slot setting, diff.color or color.ui and returns it as a bool or exit code.

nodes.name: check_write
nodes.summary: Aborts writes outside a repository, to stdin or to a blob source.

nodes.name: urlmatch_collect_fn
nodes.summary: URL-match collect callback storing the last value per variable with its key_value_info.

nodes.name: get_urlmatch
nodes.summary: Implements "config get --url": normalizes the URL, runs urlmatch_config_entry to find the best section for it, and prints matching values.

nodes.name: default_user_config
nodes.summary: Builds the commented template written when creating the global config file for editing.

nodes.name: location_options_init
nodes.summary: Resolves the config source from the scope flags, GIT_CONFIG, file or blob, validates exclusivity and repository requirements, and sets include handling.

nodes.name: display_options_init
nodes.summary: Sets NUL terminators when -z is requested.

nodes.name: display_options_init_list
nodes.summary: Initializes display options for list mode (keys shown, "=" delimiter or NUL separated).

nodes.name: cmd_config_list
nodes.summary: Implements "config list": prints every config entry from the chosen source through the pager.

nodes.name: cmd_config_get
nodes.summary: Implements "config get": validates flag combinations and dispatches to get_value, get_urlmatch or get_color.

nodes.name: cmd_config_set
nodes.summary: Implements "config set": normalizes the value and writes it with set_in_file or the multivar variant, honoring --all, --value, --append and --comment.

nodes.name: cmd_config_unset
nodes.summary: Implements "config unset": removes a variable or all matching values from the chosen file.

nodes.name: cmd_config_rename_section
nodes.summary: Implements "config rename-section" via repo_config_rename_section_in_file.

nodes.name: cmd_config_remove_section
nodes.summary: Implements "config remove-section" by renaming the section to NULL.

nodes.name: show_editor
nodes.summary: Opens the selected config file in the editor, creating a commented global file on first use.

nodes.name: cmd_config_edit
nodes.summary: Implements "config edit": checks write permissions and launches the editor on the config file.

nodes.name: cmd_config_actions
nodes.summary: Legacy dispatcher for "git config --get / --add / --unset / --list" style action flags that maps each to the same lookup and write helpers.

nodes.name: cmd_config
nodes.summary: Entry point of git config: tries subcommands first, otherwise falls back to the legacy action mode.

nodes.name: credential-cache--daemon.c
nodes.summary: Implements the long-running credential-cache daemon that listens on a Unix socket, stores credentials in memory with expiry times, and answers get, store, erase and exit requests from the credential-cache helper.

nodes.name: cache_credential
nodes.summary: Appends a credential to the in-memory cache, taking ownership of its pointers and stamping an expiration time.

nodes.name: lookup_credential
nodes.summary: Finds a cached entry matching the request using credential_match.

nodes.name: remove_credential
nodes.summary: Marks matching cached credentials as expired, optionally matching the password too.

nodes.name: check_expirations
nodes.summary: Evicts expired credentials and returns the seconds until the next expiry; returns 0 when the daemon has been idle past its 30 second grace period.

nodes.name: read_request
nodes.summary: Reads the action and timeout lines plus the credential attributes sent by a client.

nodes.name: serve_one_client
nodes.summary: Handles one client request: get replies with the cached credential, store caches it, erase removes it, exit terminates the daemon.

nodes.name: serve_cache_loop
nodes.summary: One iteration of the daemon loop: expire entries, poll the listening socket, accept a client and serve it.

nodes.name: serve_cache
nodes.summary: Binds the Unix stream socket, signals readiness, silences stderr unless debugging, and runs the serve loop.

nodes.name: init_socket_directory
nodes.summary: Ensures the socket directory exists with 0700 permissions (dying if too loose) and chdirs into it.

nodes.name: cmd_credential_cache_daemon
nodes.summary: Entry point of the daemon: validates the absolute socket path, registers a tempfile for cleanup, optionally ignores SIGHUP and serves the cache.

nodes.name: diagnose.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git diagnose": builds a timestamped zip archive of repository diagnostics (stats or all) via create_diagnostics_archive.

nodes.name: cmd_diagnose
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diagnose: builds the zip path from output directory and strftime suffix, creates leading directories and writes the diagnostics archive.

nodes.name: difftool.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git difftool": launches an external diff tool either per file (through GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF and git-difftool--helper) or in --dir-diff mode, which checks out left and right trees into temp directories and copies modified files back.

nodes.name: difftool_options
nodes.summary: Holds symlink availability, the symlinks flag and trust-exit-code setting for difftool.

nodes.name: difftool_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading difftool.trustExitCode and core.symlinks, deferring to the default config.

nodes.name: print_tool_help
nodes.summary: Runs "git mergetool --tool-help=diff" to list available diff tools.

nodes.name: parse_index_info
nodes.summary: Parses one raw diff line (modes, object ids, status) from "diff --raw -z" output.

nodes.name: add_path
nodes.summary: Truncates a strbuf to a base length and appends a relative path with a separator.

nodes.name: use_wt_file
nodes.summary: Decides whether the working-tree file can stand in for a blob by hashing it and comparing object ids.

nodes.name: working_tree_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison of working tree entries by path.

nodes.name: pair_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison of left/right pair entries by path.

nodes.name: add_left_or_right
nodes.summary: Records the left or right content of a submodule or symlink path in a hashmap of pair entries.

nodes.name: path_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison for modified-path entries.

nodes.name: changed_files
nodes.summary: Runs update-index and diff-files against a temporary index to collect paths modified under a directory.

nodes.name: ensure_leading_directories
nodes.summary: Creates missing parent directories of a path, returning an error on failure.

nodes.name: get_symlink
nodes.summary: Returns the link target text from the filesystem or the object database so a symlink can be diffed as plain text.

nodes.name: checkout_path
nodes.summary: Checks out one tree entry (mode, object id, path) into a temporary directory using a transient cache entry.

nodes.name: write_file_in_directory
nodes.summary: Writes a stand-in text file for a path inside the left or right temp directory.

nodes.name: write_standin_files
nodes.summary: Writes text stand-ins for submodule and symlink changes on both sides so external tools can diff them.

nodes.name: run_dir_diff
nodes.summary: Implements --dir-diff: runs "diff --raw", checks out left and right trees into temp directories, symlinks or copies working-tree files, runs the tool and copies edits back to the working tree.

nodes.name: run_file_diff
nodes.summary: Runs "git diff" with GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF pointing at git-difftool--helper for per-file diffs.

nodes.name: cmd_difftool
nodes.summary: Entry point of git difftool: parses options, sets tool environment variables and dispatches to run_dir_diff or run_file_diff.

nodes.name: gc.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git gc" and "git maintenance": garbage collection (repack, prune, reflog expire, rerere gc), the task table with auto-conditions, strategies, and background scheduling through cron, systemd timers, launchctl and schtasks.

nodes.name: gc_config
nodes.summary: Holds the gc settings: pack-refs and reflog pruning toggles, cruft pack options, aggressive window/depth, auto-detach and the expiry strings for prune, worktrees and gc.log.

nodes.name: maintenance_run_opts
nodes.summary: Options of one maintenance run: selected task list, auto flag, detach, quiet and schedule priority.

nodes.name: maintenance_task
nodes.summary: Descriptor of a maintenance task: name, foreground and background functions and an auto-condition that decides whether the task is needed.

nodes.name: maintenance_strategy
nodes.summary: Per-task table of which maintenance types (manual, scheduled) run a task and with what schedule frequency.

nodes.name: process_log_file
nodes.summary: At exit of a daemonized gc, commits gc.log if stderr output was recorded, otherwise removes any stale gc.log.

nodes.name: gc_config_is_timestamp_never
nodes.summary: Returns whether a gc.reflogExpire style setting parses to the expiry "never" (timestamp 0).

nodes.name: gc_config
nodes.summary: Loads gc.* configuration into a gc_config (packrefs, reflog expiry, aggressive window and depth, autodetach, cruftpacks, expiry dates) and then the default config.

nodes.name: parse_schedule
nodes.summary: Maps "hourly", "daily" or "weekly" to a schedule_priority value.

nodes.name: pack_refs_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for the pack-refs task: asks the ref store whether refs optimization is required.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_pack_refs
nodes.summary: Runs "git pack-refs --all --prune" (with --auto when requested) as a maintenance task.

nodes.name: count_reflog_entries
nodes.summary: Reflog iterator callback that counts entries that would expire and stops at a limit.

nodes.name: reflog_expire_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for reflog-expire: counts expirable HEAD reflog entries against maintenance.reflog-expire.auto (default 100).

nodes.name: maintenance_task_worktree_prune
nodes.summary: Runs "git worktree prune --expire <date>" as a maintenance task.

nodes.name: worktree_prune_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for worktree-prune: scans $GIT_DIR/worktrees and reports true once enough entries are prunable.

nodes.name: rerere_gc_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for rerere-gc: uses rerere_gc_needed with maintenance.rerere-gc.auto (default 512).

nodes.name: lock_repo_for_gc
nodes.summary: Takes the gc.pid lock; refuses if another live gc on this or another host holds it (younger than 12 hours) unless forced, and returns the other host name.

nodes.name: report_last_gc_error
nodes.summary: Checks gc.log for errors from a previous background gc and warns that automatic gc is blocked until it is removed.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_odb
nodes.summary: Runs odb_optimize with the incremental strategy built from gc config, honoring auto, quiet and aggressive flags.

nodes.name: cmd_gc
nodes.summary: Entry point of git gc: loads config, handles --auto checks and the pre-auto-gc hook, detaches to the background, takes the gc lock, runs foreground tasks, worktree prune, rerere gc, odb optimization, pack garbage cleanup and commit-graph writing.

nodes.name: maintenance_opt_schedule
nodes.summary: Option callback parsing --schedule=<frequency>.

nodes.name: dfs_on_ref
nodes.summary: Ref iterator callback that peels a ref to a commit and walks its ancestors depth-first counting commits missing from the commit-graph, stopping at a limit.

nodes.name: should_write_commit_graph
nodes.summary: Auto condition for commit-graph: true when more than maintenance.commit-graph.auto (default 100) reachable commits are outside the graph.

nodes.name: run_write_commit_graph
nodes.summary: Runs "git commit-graph write --split --reachable" with progress flags.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_commit_graph
nodes.summary: Maintenance task that writes a split commit-graph when core.commitGraph is enabled.

nodes.name: fetch_remote
nodes.summary: Runs a prefetch (--prefetch --prune --no-tags, no FETCH_HEAD) for one remote unless it opts out of default update.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_prefetch
nodes.summary: Maintenance task that prefetches every configured remote, so later fetches are fast.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_gc_background
nodes.summary: Maintenance task that spawns "git gc --no-detach --skip-foreground-tasks" for the long-running part of gc.

nodes.name: prune_packed
nodes.summary: Runs "git prune-packed" to delete loose objects already present in packs.

nodes.name: loose_object_auto_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for loose-objects: true when the loose object count reaches maintenance.loose-objects.auto (default 100).

nodes.name: write_loose_object_to_stdin
nodes.summary: Writes a loose object id to the pack-objects stdin pipe, stopping after the configured batch size.

nodes.name: pack_loose
nodes.summary: Packs loose objects by streaming their ids into "git pack-objects" up to maintenance.loose-objects.batchSize (default 50000).

nodes.name: incremental_repack_auto_condition
nodes.summary: Auto condition for incremental-repack: counts packs not covered by the multi-pack-index against maintenance.incremental-repack.auto (default 10).

nodes.name: multi_pack_index_write
nodes.summary: Runs "git multi-pack-index write" with progress flags.

nodes.name: multi_pack_index_expire
nodes.summary: Runs "git multi-pack-index expire" to drop packs fully covered by others.

nodes.name: get_auto_pack_size
nodes.summary: Computes the batch size for multi-pack-index repack as one more than the second largest pack, capped at 2 GiB.

nodes.name: multi_pack_index_repack
nodes.summary: Runs "git multi-pack-index repack" with the computed batch size.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_incremental_repack
nodes.summary: Incremental-repack task: multi-pack-index write, expire and repack in order, skipped when core.multiPackIndex is disabled.

nodes.name: maintenance_task_geometric_repack
nodes.summary: Geometric-repack task that calls odb_optimize with the geometric strategy.

nodes.name: maybe_run_task
nodes.summary: Runs one task in a phase, first checking its auto condition and the pre-auto-gc hook result when --auto is used, and wraps it in trace2 regions.

nodes.name: maintenance_run_tasks
nodes.summary: Takes the maintenance lock, runs the foreground phase of all selected tasks, optionally daemonizes, then runs the background phase.

nodes.name: parse_maintenance_strategy
nodes.summary: Returns the strategy table for "incremental", "gc" or "geometric", dying on unknown names.

nodes.name: initialize_task_config
nodes.summary: Chooses which tasks run: explicit --task list, or the strategy plus maintenance.<task>.enabled and .schedule config filtered by manual or scheduled type.

nodes.name: task_option_parse
nodes.summary: Option callback validating --task=<name> and rejecting duplicates.

nodes.name: maintenance_run
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance run": parses options, builds the task list and runs the tasks.

nodes.name: maintenance_register
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance register": disables foreground auto maintenance, sets the incremental strategy and records the repository path in maintenance.repo of the global config.

nodes.name: maintenance_unregister
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance unregister": removes this repository path from maintenance.repo, failing unless forced when it was not registered.

nodes.name: get_frequency
nodes.summary: Maps a schedule priority to the "hourly", "daily" or "weekly" string.

nodes.name: get_extra_config_parameters
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the "-c credential.interactive=false -c core.askPass=true" arguments added to scheduled git invocations.

nodes.name: get_extra_launchctl_strings
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the same extra -c options as plist XML string elements for launchctl.

nodes.name: get_schedule_cmd
nodes.summary: Resolves a scheduler command, honoring GIT_TEST_MAINT_SCHEDULER mocks for tests.

nodes.name: is_launchctl_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether launchctl can be used (macOS or a test mock).

nodes.name: launchctl_service_filename
nodes.summary: Builds the ~/Library/LaunchAgents plist path for a service name.

nodes.name: launchctl_boot_plist
nodes.summary: Runs launchctl bootstrap or bootout for a plist in the gui/<uid> domain.

nodes.name: launchctl_remove_plist
nodes.summary: Boots out and deletes the plist file for one schedule frequency.

nodes.name: launchctl_list_contains_plist
nodes.summary: Checks via "launchctl list" whether a service is already loaded.

nodes.name: launchctl_schedule_plist
nodes.summary: Writes the launchd plist for a frequency (running "git for-each-repo maintenance run --schedule=...") and bootstraps it.

nodes.name: is_schtasks_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether the Windows schtasks scheduler can be used.

nodes.name: schtasks_remove_task
nodes.summary: Deletes the "Git Maintenance (<frequency>)" scheduled task.

nodes.name: schtasks_schedule_task
nodes.summary: Generates the Windows task XML for a frequency and registers it with schtasks.

nodes.name: check_crontab_process
nodes.summary: Probes whether the crontab command runs by invoking it with -l.

nodes.name: is_crontab_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether crontab is usable (not on macOS, with test mock support).

nodes.name: crontab_update_schedule
nodes.summary: Rewrites the user crontab, replacing the marked git maintenance region with hourly, daily and weekly "for-each-repo maintenance run" lines.

nodes.name: real_is_systemd_timer_available
