nodes.summary: Probes "systemctl --user list-timers" to see whether systemd user timers work.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_delete_timer_file
nodes.summary: Deletes the user systemd timer unit file for one frequency.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_delete_service_template
nodes.summary: Deletes the shared systemd service template file.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_write_timer_file
nodes.summary: Writes a systemd timer unit with an OnCalendar pattern for hourly, daily or weekly runs at a random minute.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_write_service_template
nodes.summary: Writes the git-maintenance@.service template that invokes "git for-each-repo maintenance run".

nodes.name: systemd_timer_enable_unit
nodes.summary: Enables or disables a systemd timer unit via systemctl, writing the timer file first when enabling.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_delete_stale_timer_templates
nodes.summary: Removes obsolete systemd timer template files from older Git versions.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_delete_unit_files
nodes.summary: Deletes all timer files and the service template.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_delete_units
nodes.summary: Disables all timer units and then deletes their files.

nodes.name: systemd_timer_setup_units
nodes.summary: Writes the service template and enables hourly, daily and weekly timers, rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: parse_scheduler
nodes.summary: Parses a scheduler name (auto, cron, systemd, launchctl, schtasks) into the scheduler enum.

nodes.name: maintenance_opt_scheduler
nodes.summary: Option callback for --scheduler=<name>.

nodes.name: resolve_scheduler
nodes.summary: Resolves "auto" to the platform scheduler: launchctl, schtasks, or systemd then cron on Linux.

nodes.name: validate_scheduler
nodes.summary: Dies when the chosen scheduler is not available.

nodes.name: update_background_schedule
nodes.summary: Locks the schedule file, disables every other scheduler and enables the chosen one (or all off on stop).

nodes.name: maintenance_start
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance start": resolves and validates the scheduler, installs the background schedule and registers the repo.

nodes.name: maintenance_stop
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance stop": removes the background schedule from all schedulers.

nodes.name: maintenance_is_needed
nodes.summary: Subcommand "maintenance is-needed": exits 0 when any selected task has its auto condition true (or always without --auto).

nodes.name: cmd_maintenance
nodes.summary: Entry point of git maintenance: dispatches run, start, stop, register, unregister and is-needed.

nodes.name: init-db.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git init": parses options, resolves git dir, work tree, template, object format and ref format, guesses bare vs non-bare, then calls init_db to create the repository layout.

nodes.name: guess_repository_type
nodes.summary: Guesses bare or non-bare from the git dir: ".", cwd, or paths not ending in "/.git" count as bare.

nodes.name: cmd_init_db
nodes.summary: Entry point of git init: parses options, creates and enters the target directory, resolves object format, ref format, shared permissions, git dir and work tree, then calls init_db.

nodes.name: remote.c
nodes.summary: Implements "git remote": add, rename, remove, show, prune, update, set-head, set-branches, get-url and set-url, editing remote.<name>.* config and remote-tracking refs under refs/remotes.

nodes.name: branch_info
nodes.summary: Per-branch tracking config read from branch.<name>.remote, merge, rebase and pushRemote.

nodes.name: ref_states
nodes.summary: Remote ref classification for "remote show/prune": new, skipped, stale, tracked, remote heads and push info.

nodes.name: push_info
nodes.summary: Push destination, force flag and status (create, delete, up to date, fast-forward, out of date) for one local ref.

nodes.name: rename_info
nodes.summary: State carried while renaming a remote: old and new names, ref transaction and progress.

nodes.name: fetch_remote
nodes.summary: Runs "git fetch <name>" in a subprocess, optionally verbose.

nodes.name: add_branch
nodes.summary: Adds a +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<b> fetch refspec (or mirror form) to remote.<name>.fetch.

nodes.name: parse_mirror_opt
nodes.summary: Option callback for --mirror, --mirror=fetch and --mirror=push.

nodes.name: check_remote_collision
nodes.summary: Dies when a new remote name is a prefix or extension (before "/") of an existing remote name.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote add": validates the name, writes remote.<name>.url and fetch refspecs (or mirror/tagOpt settings), optionally fetches and sets the remote HEAD.

nodes.name: config_read_branches
nodes.summary: Config callback gathering branch.<name>.remote, merge, rebase and pushremote settings into branch_info.

nodes.name: get_ref_states
nodes.summary: Classifies remote refs through the fetch refspecs into new, skipped, tracked and stale (stale heads via get_stale_heads).

nodes.name: get_push_ref_states
nodes.summary: Computes push status for each matching local head by comparing old and new ids and fast-forward ancestry.

nodes.name: get_push_ref_states_noquery
nodes.summary: Fills push info from the configured push refspecs without contacting the remote.

nodes.name: get_head_names
nodes.summary: Determines which remote branches the remote HEAD may point to using guess_remote_head.

nodes.name: add_known_remote
nodes.summary: Collects every remote except the one being deleted.

nodes.name: add_branch_for_removal
nodes.summary: Ref callback selecting remote-tracking refs of the removed remote that no other remote tracks, and noting local branches to delete by hand.

nodes.name: rename_one_reflog_entry
nodes.summary: Reflog callback that re-queues one reflog entry under the renamed ref in the transaction.

nodes.name: rename_one_reflog
nodes.summary: Copies a ref reflog to the renamed ref and appends a "remote: renamed" entry.

nodes.name: rename_one_ref
nodes.summary: Ref callback queueing deletion of the old ref and creation of the renamed one (symrefs included) in the transaction.

nodes.name: migrate_file
nodes.summary: Migrates a remote defined in legacy .git/remotes or .git/branches files into config and removes the legacy file.

nodes.name: config_read_push_default
nodes.summary: Config callback recording where remote.pushDefault names the old remote.

nodes.name: handle_push_default
nodes.summary: Updates or warns about remote.pushDefault after a rename or removal depending on the config scope that sets it.

nodes.name: mv
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote rename": renames the config section, rewrites fetch refspecs, moves refs/remotes refs and reflogs in a transaction, and updates branch.*.remote.

nodes.name: rm
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote remove": unsets branch.*.remote and merge, deletes the remote-tracking refs not used by others and removes the remote config section.

nodes.name: append_ref_to_tracked_list
nodes.summary: Ref callback adding branches tracked by the remote to the tracked list (offline mode).

nodes.name: get_remote_ref_states
nodes.summary: Loads a remote and fills ref_states, either by querying it through a transport or from local refs.

nodes.name: show_remote_info_item
nodes.summary: Prints one remote branch line with its status (new, tracked, skipped, stale).

nodes.name: add_local_to_show_info
nodes.summary: Collects local branches configured to pull from this remote and tracks column width and rebase use.

nodes.name: show_local_info_item
nodes.summary: Prints how a local branch pulls from the remote (merge or rebase variants).

nodes.name: add_push_to_show_info
nodes.summary: Collects push entries for display and computes column widths.

nodes.name: show_push_info_item
nodes.summary: Prints one push entry with force marker and status.

nodes.name: get_one_entry
nodes.summary: Adds fetch and push URLs (plus partial clone filter) of one remote to the listing.

nodes.name: show_all
nodes.summary: Lists remote names, with URLs when verbose.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote show": prints URLs, HEAD branch, remote branches with status, pull configuration and push configuration for each remote.

nodes.name: report_set_head_auto
nodes.summary: Reports whether refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD was created, changed or left unchanged by set-head --auto.

nodes.name: set_head
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote set-head": sets, auto-detects or deletes refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD as a symref.

nodes.name: prune_remote
nodes.summary: Lists and deletes stale remote-tracking refs for one remote (or reports them on dry run) and warns about dangling symrefs.

nodes.name: prune
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote prune": prunes each named remote.

nodes.name: get_remote_default
nodes.summary: Config callback detecting a remotes.default setting.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote update": runs "git fetch --multiple" for the groups or all remotes.

nodes.name: add_branches
nodes.summary: Adds a fetch refspec for each named branch to a remote.

nodes.name: set_remote_branches
nodes.summary: Replaces or appends the remote.<name>.fetch refspecs with the given branches.

nodes.name: set_branches
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote set-branches" with an --add option.

nodes.name: get_url
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote get-url": prints the first or all fetch or push URLs.

nodes.name: set_url
nodes.summary: Subcommand "remote set-url": adds, replaces or deletes fetch or push URLs matched by a regular expression.

nodes.name: cmd_remote
nodes.summary: Entry point of git remote: dispatches the add, rename, remove, set-head, set-branches, get-url, set-url, show, prune and update subcommands.

nodes.name: ident.c
nodes.summary: Builds the "Name <email> date" identity strings that Git stamps into commit and tag objects. It resolves author and committer names from config, environment variables and the passwd/hostname fallback, parses ident lines back apart, and rewrites them through mailmap.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses file-scope static strbufs as lazily filled caches, and a two-slot static ring buffer in fmt_ident() so two results can be alive at once.

nodes.name: xgetpwuid_self
nodes.summary: Looks up the current user with getpwuid(getuid()); if there is no passwd entry it returns a static "unknown"/"Unknown" fallback and flags the identity as bogus.

nodes.name: copy_gecos
nodes.summary: Copies the real name from the passwd GECOS field up to the first comma, expanding "&" into the capitalised login name.

nodes.name: add_mailname_host
nodes.summary: Reads the first line of /etc/mailname and appends it to the buffer as the host part of a made-up email address; returns -1 if the file is unreadable.

nodes.name: canonical_name
nodes.summary: Resolves a host name to its canonical fully qualified name using getaddrinfo (or gethostbyname without IPv6) and accepts it only if it contains a dot.

nodes.name: add_domainname
nodes.summary: Appends the machine host name to the buffer, canonicalising it when it has no dot, and marks the result bogus with a "(none)" placeholder when it cannot be resolved.

nodes.name: copy_email
nodes.summary: Makes up a fake email "login@host[.domain]" from the passwd entry, preferring the host name from /etc/mailname over DNS lookup.

nodes.name: ident_default_name
nodes.summary: Returns the default user name, lazily deriving it from the GECOS field the first time unless user.name was configured.

nodes.name: ident_default_email
nodes.summary: Returns the default email, lazily taking it from the EMAIL environment variable, a platform query hook, or a synthesized login@host address, and records when the email counts as explicitly given.

nodes.name: reset_ident_date
nodes.summary: Clears the cached default ident timestamp so the next fmt_ident call samples the clock again.

nodes.name: crud
nodes.summary: Predicate that treats control characters, spaces and punctuation such as , : ; < > " \ ' as "crud" that must not start or end a name or email.

nodes.name: strbuf_addstr_without_crud
nodes.summary: Copies a string into a strbuf after trimming crud from both ends and dropping newline, "<" and ">" characters, which act as delimiters on an ident line.

nodes.name: split_ident_line
nodes.summary: Parses an ident line into name, email, date and timezone pointer ranges inside struct ident_split; returns -1 if there is no well-formed "<email>", and leaves the date and tz pointers NULL when only the person part is present.

nodes.name: rewrite_ident_line
nodes.summary: Splits one ident line, looks the name and email up in the mailmap via map_user, and splices the canonical "name <email>" back into the buffer, returning the length delta.

nodes.name: apply_mailmap_to_header
nodes.summary: Walks the header lines of a commit or tag buffer and replaces each requested header (such as author or committer) with its mailmap-canonical identity, stopping at the blank line.

nodes.name: ident_env_hint
nodes.summary: Prints the "Please tell me who you are" hint with the git config commands to set user.name and user.email, headed by an author or committer message.

nodes.name: fmt_ident
nodes.summary: Central ident formatter: picks name and email from arguments, author/committer config or defaults, dies in strict mode when they are missing or bogus, sanitises them, appends a date (parsed or the cached default) and returns a string from a two-slot static pool.

nodes.name: fmt_name
nodes.summary: Returns the strict, date-less ident for the author or committer by reading GIT_AUTHOR_* or GIT_COMMITTER_* environment variables and delegating to fmt_ident.

nodes.name: git_author_info
nodes.summary: Returns the formatted author ident from GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL and GIT_AUTHOR_DATE, noting which parts were explicitly supplied.

nodes.name: git_committer_info
nodes.summary: Returns the formatted committer ident from the GIT_COMMITTER_* environment variables, noting which parts were explicitly supplied.

nodes.name: ident_is_sufficient
nodes.summary: Decides whether an identity is explicitly given: email alone suffices on POSIX, while Windows requires both name and email.

nodes.name: committer_ident_sufficiently_given
nodes.summary: Reports whether the committer identity was explicitly configured, used to decide if a commit needs an identity warning.

nodes.name: author_ident_sufficiently_given
nodes.summary: Reports whether the author identity was explicitly configured.

nodes.name: set_ident
nodes.summary: Handles the author.*, committer.* and user.* name and email config keys by storing the value in the matching static strbuf and recording which identity parts were explicitly given.

nodes.name: git_ident_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads user.useConfigOnly and forwards the other identity keys to set_ident.

nodes.name: prepare_fallback_ident
nodes.summary: Sets GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* name and email environment variables to a fallback value unless the user already supplied them.

nodes.name: buf_cmp
nodes.summary: Three-way compares two byte ranges by memcmp over the common length and then by length.

nodes.name: ident_cmp
nodes.summary: Orders two split identities by email first and name second, ignoring any timestamp.

nodes.name: ident.h
nodes.summary: Public interface for building and parsing Git author/committer identity lines: the struct ident_split view of an ident string, the want_ident selector, and the fmt_ident, split_ident_line and mailmap helpers implemented in ident.c.

nodes.name: ident_split
nodes.summary: Holds begin/end pointers into an ident line for the name, email, date and timezone fields without copying; filled by split_ident_line.

nodes.name: want_ident
nodes.summary: Selects which identity to format: blank, author or committer, which decides the config and environment sources and the error hints.

nodes.name: iterator.h
nodes.summary: Defines the return codes shared by Git iterators (ITER_OK, ITER_DONE, ITER_ERROR) and the iterator_selection bit flags that merge-iterator selector callbacks return to choose which side to yield or skip.

nodes.name: iterator_selection
nodes.summary: Enum of values a merge-iterator selector returns: end or error codes, masks for the current side, and combined results such as ITER_SELECT_0_SKIP_1 that choose which iterator yields and which entry is discarded.

nodes.name: odb.c
nodes.summary: Implements the object database (odb) layer of a repository: it owns the list of object sources (the primary objects directory plus alternates and an in-memory source) and dispatches object lookups, existence checks, enumeration, writes, packing and fsck to those sources, with promisor fetch and hash-algorithm conversion on top.
nodes.languageNotes: Most operations are thin loops over a linked list of struct odb_source and call per-source vtable wrappers such as odb_source_read_object_info; hash algorithm conversion is delegated to object-file-convert.

nodes.name: odb_source_paths_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two object-source paths with strcmp or strcasecmp depending on a lazily read core.ignorecase value cached in the object_database.

nodes.name: odb_source_by_path_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback that matches odb_source entries by their path, used to deduplicate alternates.

nodes.name: odb_mkstemp
nodes.summary: Creates a read-only temporary file inside the repository objects directory from a pattern, creating missing leading directories and retrying when mkstemp fails.

nodes.name: odb_is_source_usable
nodes.summary: Checks that a candidate alternate path is an existing directory and is neither the primary object directory nor already registered, seeding the by-path hashmap with the primary source on first use.

nodes.name: parse_alternates
nodes.summary: Parses a separator-delimited alternates list (from the alternates file or environment), skipping comments and C-style quoted entries, resolving relative paths against a base and pushing normalized absolute paths into a strvec.

nodes.name: odb_add_alternate_recursively
nodes.summary: Registers an alternate object store as a new odb_source at the tail of the source list and hashmap, then recurses into the alternates it declares, refusing nesting deeper than five levels.

nodes.name: odb_add_to_alternates_file
nodes.summary: Appends a directory to the primary source alternates file and immediately adds it as a live alternate object store.

nodes.name: odb_set_temporary_primary_source
nodes.summary: Installs a new temporary primary object source in front of the old one (which becomes an alternate) and disables ref updates because the temporary objects may be rolled back.

nodes.name: odb_restore_primary_source
nodes.summary: Undoes the temporary primary source: verifies the expected path and linkage, re-enables ref updates, restores the original source and frees the temporary one.

nodes.name: compute_alternate_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a reference repository path to its objects directory (following .git files and .git subdirectories) and rejects linked checkouts, non-repositories, shallow repositories and grafted repositories with an error message.

nodes.name: odb_find_source
nodes.summary: Returns the object source whose real path equals the given object directory, or NULL when none matches.

nodes.name: odb_find_source_or_die
nodes.summary: Like odb_find_source but dies with a message when no source matches the directory.

nodes.name: fill_alternate_refs_command
nodes.summary: Prepares the child process that lists refs of an alternate: either the user-configured core.alternateRefsCommand via shell, or "git for-each-ref --format=%(objectname)" with optional core.alternateRefsPrefixes.

nodes.name: read_alternate_refs
nodes.summary: Runs the alternate-refs command, parses each output line as a hex object ID, and calls the callback for every ref tip of the alternate repository.

nodes.name: refs_from_alternate_cb
nodes.summary: Per-alternate callback that derives the alternate repository path from its objects directory, checks it has a refs directory, and reads its ref tips.

nodes.name: odb_for_each_alternate_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over the ref tips of every alternate object store and passes each object ID to the callback.

nodes.name: odb_for_each_alternate
nodes.summary: Calls a callback for each alternate source (everything after the primary) and stops at the first non-zero return.

nodes.name: odb_prepare_alternates
nodes.summary: Reads alternates from the given environment-style string and from the primary source alternates file, and adds each as an alternate source.

nodes.name: odb_has_alternates
nodes.summary: Returns whether the object database has any source besides the primary one.

nodes.name: enable_obj_read_lock
nodes.summary: Turns on the global recursive mutex that serializes object reads in multi-threaded code.

nodes.name: disable_obj_read_lock
nodes.summary: Turns off the global object-read lock and destroys the mutex.

nodes.name: do_oid_object_info_extended
nodes.summary: Core object lookup: applies replace refs, checks the in-memory source, then tries every source (and a second read that lets sources refresh caches), lazily fetches from a promisor remote if missing, and dies or returns an error for corrupt objects.

nodes.name: oid_object_info_convert
nodes.summary: Handles lookups by an object ID of a different hash algorithm: maps it to the repository algorithm, reads the object, then converts the content and delta base ID back to the caller algorithm.

nodes.name: odb_read_object_info_extended
nodes.summary: Public entry for looking up an object and filling struct object_info, converting between hash algorithms when needed and holding the object read lock.

nodes.name: odb_read_object_info
nodes.summary: Returns the type of an object (and optionally its size) with replace-object lookup, or -1 when the object cannot be read.

nodes.name: odb_pretend_object
nodes.summary: Hashes a buffer and, if the object does not already exist, stores it only in the in-memory source so it appears to exist without being written to disk.

nodes.name: odb_read_object
nodes.summary: Reads the full content, type and size of an object into a newly allocated buffer, dying on corruption and returning NULL if absent.

nodes.name: odb_read_object_peeled
nodes.summary: Reads an object and peels it until it reaches the required type, following a tag to its target object and a commit to its tree by parsing the header line.

nodes.name: odb_has_object
nodes.summary: Tests whether an object exists, using the quick lookup and skipping lazy fetch unless the flags ask for repacked or promisor checks.

nodes.name: odb_freshen_object
nodes.summary: Asks each source to refresh the timestamp of an existing object so garbage collection treats it as recent.

nodes.name: odb_for_each_object_ext
nodes.summary: Enumerates objects across all sources (optionally only local ones) by calling each source iterator with the request and options.

nodes.name: odb_for_each_object
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper over odb_for_each_object_ext that builds the options struct from a flags value.

nodes.name: odb_count_objects
nodes.summary: Sums the object counts reported by every source and caches the total together with the flags it was computed with.

nodes.name: msb
nodes.summary: Returns the index of the most significant set bit of an unsigned long by shifting.

nodes.name: odb_find_abbrev_len
nodes.summary: Computes the unique hex prefix length for an object ID: derives a default from the approximate object count, then lets each source lengthen it until the prefix is unambiguous.

nodes.name: odb_assert_oid_type
nodes.summary: Dies unless the object exists and has the expected type.

nodes.name: odb_write_object_ext
nodes.summary: Writes an object: hashes it, skips the write and only freshens it when it already exists, computes the compatibility-hash ID when a second algorithm is enabled, and delegates the write to the primary source.

nodes.name: odb_write_object_stream
nodes.summary: Writes an object from a stream through the primary source.

nodes.name: odb_optimize
nodes.summary: Optimizes the primary object source (for example repacking) with the given options.

nodes.name: odb_optimize_required
nodes.summary: Asks the primary source whether optimization is currently needed.

nodes.name: odb_generate_pack_options_release
nodes.summary: Frees the wants, haves and shallows object ID arrays of pack generation options.

nodes.name: odb_generate_pack
nodes.summary: Starts generating a packfile from the primary source, returning an error if that source cannot do so.

nodes.name: odb_pack_generator_finish
nodes.summary: Finishes a pack generator by calling its finish method.

nodes.name: odb_new
nodes.summary: Allocates an object_database for a repository, creates the primary source from GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY or the common dir, adds the in-memory source, and loads alternates from GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES.

nodes.name: odb_close
nodes.summary: Closes every object source and the commit graph.

nodes.name: odb_free_sources
nodes.summary: Frees every source in the list, the in-memory source and the by-path hashmap.

nodes.name: odb_free
nodes.summary: Destroys the object database: clears the replace map, closes and frees sources, then frees the structure.

nodes.name: odb_prepare
nodes.summary: Lets every source load its state and, when flushing caches, rereads the alternates file and invalidates the cached object count.

nodes.name: odb_reprepare
nodes.summary: Re-prepares the object database with cache flushing, picking up objects and alternates added by other processes.

nodes.name: odb_fsck
nodes.summary: Runs fsck on each object source and ORs the results.

nodes.name: alternate_refs_data
nodes.summary: Bundles the user callback and its payload so they can be passed through the alternate-source iterator.

nodes.name: path.c
nodes.summary: Utilities for building and manipulating the paths Git uses: printf-style helpers for the git dir, common dir, working tree and submodule git dirs (with worktree-aware redirection through a trie of shared entries), shared-repository permission handling, race-safe directory creation, textual path normalization, relative paths, NTFS .git alias detection and XDG locations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a small compressed trie (struct trie) to classify git-dir entries as shared or per-worktree, and REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC macros to generate memoized accessors for files such as MERGE_HEAD.

nodes.name: get_pathname
nodes.summary: Returns the next of four static strbufs in a round-robin ring, reset and ready to build a path; the reason results of mkpath() stay valid across a few calls.

nodes.name: replace_dir
nodes.summary: Replaces the first len bytes of a path buffer with another directory, inserting a separator when neither side provides one.

nodes.name: make_trie_node
nodes.summary: Allocates a compressed trie node holding a copy of the key fragment and a value.

nodes.name: add_to_trie
nodes.summary: Inserts a key and value into a compressed trie, splitting an existing node when the key diverges inside its compressed prefix, and returns the previous value for the key if any.

nodes.name: trie_find
nodes.summary: Finds the longest slash-terminated prefix of a key that has a value in the trie and invokes a match callback, falling back to shorter parent prefixes when the callback returns negative; skips doubled slashes.

nodes.name: init_common_trie
nodes.summary: Lazily builds the trie of paths from common_list that decides which git-dir entries are shared across worktrees.

nodes.name: check_common
nodes.summary: Trie match callback that says whether a git-dir path belongs to the shared common directory, treating directory entries and file entries differently.

nodes.name: update_common_dir
nodes.summary: Rewrites a path under a linked worktree git dir to the common dir when its prefix is listed as common, preserving a trailing ".lock" suffix.

nodes.name: report_linked_checkout_garbage
nodes.summary: For a linked worktree, reports files in its private git dir that belong in the common dir (not marked ignorable) as garbage entries.

nodes.name: adjust_git_path
nodes.summary: Applies the special-case redirections to a git-dir path: grafts file, index file override, objects directory, hooks path from config, and common-dir sharing for linked worktrees.

nodes.name: strbuf_worktree_gitdir
nodes.summary: Appends the git directory for a worktree (the repository git dir, the common dir for the main worktree, or worktrees/<id> for a linked one).

nodes.name: repo_git_pathv
nodes.summary: Core builder for repo_git_path: starts from the worktree git dir, formats the suffix, applies path adjustments (for the current worktree) and cleans the result.

nodes.name: repo_git_path
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated path inside the repository git directory built from a printf-style format.

nodes.name: repo_git_path_append
nodes.summary: Appends a git-dir path to a strbuf and returns its buffer.

nodes.name: repo_git_path_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces the strbuf contents with a git-dir path built from a format and returns its buffer.

nodes.name: mkpathdup
nodes.summary: Formats a path with printf semantics, strips a leading "./", and returns it as an allocated string.

nodes.name: mkpath
nodes.summary: Formats a path into one of four rotating static buffers and returns it with a leading "./" removed.

nodes.name: worktree_git_path
nodes.summary: Builds a path inside the git directory of a specific worktree; it is a bug to pass NULL.

nodes.name: do_worktree_path
nodes.summary: Builds a path under the repository working tree from a format, adding a separator and cleaning the result.

nodes.name: repo_worktree_path
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated path in the repository working tree.

nodes.name: repo_worktree_path_append
nodes.summary: Appends a working-tree path to a strbuf, returning NULL for a repository without a working tree.

nodes.name: repo_worktree_path_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces the strbuf with a working-tree path, returning NULL when there is no working tree.

nodes.name: do_submodule_path
nodes.summary: Resolves the git directory of a submodule from its path, appends a formatted suffix and redirects shared entries to the submodule common dir.

nodes.name: repo_submodule_path
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated path inside a submodule git directory, or NULL if the submodule cannot be found.

nodes.name: repo_submodule_path_append
nodes.summary: Appends a submodule git-dir path to a strbuf, returning NULL on failure.

nodes.name: repo_submodule_path_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces a strbuf with a submodule git-dir path, returning NULL on failure.

nodes.name: repo_common_pathv
nodes.summary: Builds a path under the common git directory shared by all worktrees from a format and cleans it.

nodes.name: repo_common_path
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated path in the common git directory.

nodes.name: repo_common_path_append
nodes.summary: Appends a common-dir path to a strbuf.

nodes.name: repo_common_path_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces a strbuf with a common-dir path.

nodes.name: interpolate_path
nodes.summary: Expands "~", "~user" and a leading "%(prefix)/" in a configured path, using HOME or getpwnam and the Git install prefix, and returns an allocated string or NULL on failure.

nodes.name: calc_shared_perm
nodes.summary: Computes the file mode to use under core.sharedRepository, merging group or umask-style permission bits into the given mode.

nodes.name: adjust_shared_perm
nodes.summary: Applies the shared-repository permissions to an existing path with chmod when they differ, adding execute and setgid bits for directories.

nodes.name: safe_create_dir
nodes.summary: Makes a directory (tolerating EEXIST), exiting on other errors, and optionally applies shared permissions.

nodes.name: safe_create_dir_in_gitdir
nodes.summary: Creates a directory in the git dir, following an absolute symlink target for symlinked worktrees whose origin repository does not have the directory yet, then adjusts shared permissions.

nodes.name: safe_create_leading_directories_1
nodes.summary: Walks the components of a path creating missing parent directories while tolerating races, and reports SCLD_EXISTS, SCLD_VANISHED, SCLD_FAILED or SCLD_PERMS.

nodes.name: safe_create_leading_directories
nodes.summary: Creates parent directories of a mutable path, honouring core.sharedRepository.

nodes.name: safe_create_leading_directories_no_share
nodes.summary: Creates parent directories without applying shared-repository permissions, for working tree files.

nodes.name: safe_create_leading_directories_const
nodes.summary: Const-path variant that duplicates the path, creates its leading directories and preserves errno.

nodes.name: safe_create_file_with_leading_directories
nodes.summary: Opens a new file exclusively, creating the parent directories and retrying if the first open fails.

nodes.name: relative_path
nodes.summary: Expresses a path relative to a prefix, emitting "../" components when the prefix is not an ancestor and returning "./" for identical paths; may return the input pointer unchanged.

nodes.name: remove_leading_path
nodes.summary: Strips a leading directory prefix from a path (a simpler relative_path) and returns "." when nothing remains.

nodes.name: normalize_path_copy_len
nodes.summary: Purely textual path normalizer that squashes slashes, removes "." and resolves ".." components without touching the filesystem, failing when ".." climbs above the root; optionally shrinks a protected prefix length.

nodes.name: normalize_path_copy
nodes.summary: Normalizes a path into a destination buffer without a prefix length.

nodes.name: strbuf_normalize_path
nodes.summary: Normalizes the path stored in a strbuf in place, leaving it untouched and returning -1 on error.

nodes.name: longest_ancestor_length
nodes.summary: Returns the length of the longest listed prefix directory that is a proper ancestor of a canonical path, used for ceiling directories in repository discovery.

nodes.name: stripped_path_suffix_offset
nodes.summary: Checks that a path ends with a suffix made of whole path components and returns the offset where the suffix begins, or -1.

nodes.name: ends_with_path_components
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path ends with the given complete path components.

nodes.name: strip_path_suffix
nodes.summary: Returns the part of a path before a matching suffix of whole components, or NULL if it does not end with that suffix.

nodes.name: daemon_avoid_alias
nodes.summary: Rejects git-daemon style paths containing "//", "/./", "/../" or trailing dot components so they cannot alias another path; returns 0 when the path is acceptable.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dotgit
nodes.summary: Detects names that NTFS treats as ".git", including "git~1" short names, trailing spaces and dots, and alternate data stream suffixes, so such entries are never tracked.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dot_generic
nodes.summary: Generic NTFS alias matcher for dot-files such as .gitmodules: accepts the literal name, the 6-character "~N" short name, and the fallback 8.3 short name built from a hash prefix, followed only by spaces, dots or a stream suffix.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dotgitmodules
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name is an NTFS alias of .gitmodules.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dotgitignore
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name is an NTFS alias of .gitignore.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dotgitattributes
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name is an NTFS alias of .gitattributes.

nodes.name: is_ntfs_dotmailmap
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name is an NTFS alias of .mailmap.

nodes.name: looks_like_command_line_option
nodes.summary: Returns true when a string starts with "-" and so could be mistaken for an option by a sub-program such as ssh.

nodes.name: xdg_config_home_for
nodes.summary: Builds "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<subdir>/<file>" or the "$HOME/.config" fallback as an allocated string.

nodes.name: xdg_config_home
nodes.summary: Builds the path of a file in the user git config XDG directory.

nodes.name: xdg_cache_home
nodes.summary: Builds "$XDG_CACHE_HOME/git/<file>" or the "$HOME/.cache/git" fallback.

nodes.name: format_path
nodes.summary: Writes a path into a strbuf in one of four formats: unmodified, relative to a prefix (default current directory), relative only if sharing a root, or canonical absolute.

nodes.name: dir_prefix
nodes.summary: Returns true when a path equals a directory name or begins with that name followed by a separator.

nodes.name: git_path_squash_msg
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the SQUASH_MSG file (merge-squash message) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_merge_msg
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the MERGE_MSG file (merge commit message) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_merge_rr
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the MERGE_RR file (rerere merge record) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_merge_mode
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the MERGE_MODE file (merge mode marker) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_merge_head
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the MERGE_HEAD file (merge head list) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_fetch_head
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the FETCH_HEAD file (fetch result list) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: git_path_shallow
nodes.summary: Macro-generated (REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC) accessor returning the memoized path of the shallow file (shallow boundary file) in the repository git directory.

nodes.name: common_dir
nodes.summary: Describes one git-dir entry: whether it is a directory, belongs to the common dir shared by linked worktrees, and whether it is ignored when reporting garbage.

nodes.name: trie
nodes.summary: Compressed trie node with 256 child pointers, a shared key fragment and an optional value, used for fast longest-prefix path classification.

nodes.name: path.h
nodes.summary: Declares the path-building API (mkpath, repo_git_path, repo_common_path, repo_worktree_path, repo_submodule_path families), the REPO_GIT_PATH_FUNC memoization macro, directory-creation and shared-permission helpers, NTFS dotfile checks, path normalization, and the path_format and scld_error enums.

nodes.name: scld_error
nodes.summary: Result codes of safe_create_leading_directories: success, generic failure, permission failure, a non-directory in the way, or an ancestor that vanished mid-call (retryable).

nodes.name: path_format
nodes.summary: Selects how format_path renders a path: unmodified, relative, relative only when sharing a root, or canonical absolute.

nodes.name: pathspec.c
nodes.summary: Parses command-line pathspecs into struct pathspec: it recognises magic prefixes (":(top)", ":(glob)", ":(attr:...)", ":!" and so on), global pathspec environment switches, prefix handling relative to the working directory, and wildcard metadata, and provides copy, clear, attribute-matching and sparse-index expansion helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: The pathspec magic table maps mnemonics and long names to bit flags; global GIT_*_PATHSPECS environment variables are read once into function-static caches.

nodes.name: add_pathspec_matches_against_index
nodes.summary: Walks the index entries and records in a seen[] array the closest match each pathspec achieves, optionally skipping skip-worktree and out-of-cone entries, and returns early if every pathspec is already matched.

nodes.name: find_pathspecs_matching_against_index
nodes.summary: One-shot wrapper that allocates a seen[] array and fills it by matching all pathspecs against the index.

nodes.name: find_pathspecs_matching_skip_worktree
nodes.summary: Returns a seen[] array for pathspecs that match index entries that are marked skip-worktree or lie outside the sparse checkout.

nodes.name: prefix_magic
nodes.summary: Writes the ":(...,prefix:N)" magic header for an element, converting shorthand magic to long names or copying longhand magic and appending the prefix length.

nodes.name: strcspn_escaped
nodes.summary: Like strcspn but treats a backslash as escaping the next character, so escaped stop characters do not end the scan.

nodes.name: attr_value_unescape
nodes.summary: Unescapes an attribute value of an attr: pathspec, dying on a trailing backslash or characters other than alphanumerics, comma, dash and underscore.

nodes.name: parse_pathspec_attr_match
nodes.summary: Parses the body of "attr:" magic (a space-separated list such as "text -diff eol=lf") into an attr_check and per-attribute match modes (set, unset, unspecified, value).

nodes.name: get_global_magic
nodes.summary: Combines the literal, glob, noglob and icase pathspec environment switches into a magic bitmask, rejecting incompatible combinations.

nodes.name: parse_long_magic
nodes.summary: Parses the longhand ":(name,name,prefix:N,attr:...)" syntax, setting magic bits, the prefix length and attribute matchers, and dying on unknown magic or a missing closing parenthesis.

nodes.name: parse_short_magic
nodes.summary: Parses shorthand magic characters after a colon (such as "/" and "!", with "^" as an alias for "!") into magic bits and returns the position after them.

nodes.name: parse_element_magic
nodes.summary: Dispatches a pathspec element to the longhand or shorthand magic parser, or returns it untouched when it has no leading colon or literal mode is global.

nodes.name: init_pathspec_item
nodes.summary: Builds one pathspec_item from an element: parses magic, merges global magic, makes the match string relative to the prefix (dying if outside the repository), sets the original string, nowildcard length and the ONESTAR flag.

nodes.name: pathspec_item_cmp
nodes.summary: qsort comparator ordering pathspec items by their match string.

nodes.name: pathspec_magic_names
nodes.summary: Appends human-readable names (and mnemonics) of the magic bits that are set to a strbuf.

nodes.name: unsupported_magic
nodes.summary: Dies with a message listing pathspec magic that the calling command does not support.

nodes.name: parse_pathspec
nodes.summary: Main entry point: turns argv into a struct pathspec, validating flags, initialising each item, rejecting unsupported magic and paths beyond symlinks, adding an implicit match-all item when all items are excludes, and sorting when a max depth is used.

nodes.name: parse_pathspec_file
nodes.summary: Reads pathspecs from a file or stdin (newline or NUL separated, C-style unquoting quoted lines) and feeds them to parse_pathspec.

nodes.name: copy_pathspec
nodes.summary: Deep-copies a pathspec including item strings, attribute match values and attribute check structures.

nodes.name: clear_pathspec
nodes.summary: Frees all strings, attribute matches and attr checks of a pathspec and resets it to empty.

nodes.name: match_pathspec_attrs
nodes.summary: Checks the gitattributes of a path against an item "attr:" requirements (set, unset, unspecified, or equal to a value) and returns 1 only if all match.

nodes.name: pathspec_needs_expanded_index
nodes.summary: Decides whether a sparse index must be expanded to evaluate a pathspec, based on magic, wildcards that may match inside sparse directories, and whether literal paths lie in the sparse cone.

nodes.name: pathspec_magic
nodes.summary: Table entry mapping a pathspec magic bit to its single-character mnemonic and its long name (top, literal, glob, icase, exclude, attr).

nodes.name: quote.c
nodes.summary: Implements the string quoting and unquoting routines Git uses for shell-safe single-quote quoting (sq_quote), C-style double-quoted path names (as in diff and ls-files output), and string-literal escaping for Perl, Python, Tcl and basic regular expressions.

nodes.name: sq_quote_buf
nodes.summary: Appends a string wrapped in single quotes, rewriting each embedded single quote or exclamation mark as an escaped sequence, and handles the source aliasing the destination buffer.

nodes.name: sq_quote_buf_pretty
nodes.summary: Like sq_quote_buf but leaves strings made only of alphanumerics and a few safe punctuation characters unquoted, and emits "" for an empty string.

nodes.name: sq_quotef
nodes.summary: Formats a printf-style string and appends it single-quoted as one shell word.

nodes.name: sq_quote_argv
nodes.summary: Appends every argv entry single-quoted, each preceded by a space.

nodes.name: sq_quote_argv_pretty
nodes.summary: Legacy variant of the pretty argv quoter that emits a leading space before the first argument.

nodes.name: sq_append_quote_argv_pretty
nodes.summary: Appends argv entries separated by spaces, quoting only those that need it.

nodes.name: sq_dequote_step
nodes.summary: Unwraps one single-quoted item in place, accepting backslash-escaped quote or exclamation mark between quoted sections, and reports where the next item starts.

nodes.name: sq_dequote
nodes.summary: Dequotes a string that must be exactly one sq_quote result, or returns NULL.

nodes.name: sq_dequote_to_strvec
nodes.summary: Dequotes a whitespace-separated list of single-quoted items in place and pushes each result into a strvec, returning -1 on malformed input.

nodes.name: cq_must_quote
nodes.summary: Consults the 256-entry cq_lookup table, together with core.quotePath, to tell whether a byte needs C-style escaping.

nodes.name: next_quote_pos
nodes.summary: Returns the length of the leading run of bytes that need no quoting, up to an optional maximum length.

nodes.name: quote_c_style_counted
nodes.summary: Core C-style quoter: counts or emits (to a strbuf and/or FILE) the double-quoted form of a name, using named escapes such as \n and three-digit octal escapes, and returns 0 if no quoting was needed.

nodes.name: quote_c_style
nodes.summary: C-style quotes a NUL-terminated name to a strbuf or file.

nodes.name: quote_two_c_style
nodes.summary: Quotes a prefix and path as one name, wrapping them in a single pair of double quotes only if either needs quoting.

nodes.name: write_name_quoted
nodes.summary: Writes a name to a file followed by a terminator, C-style quoting it unless the terminator is NUL.

nodes.name: write_name_quoted_relative
nodes.summary: Writes a name relative to a prefix, quoted when needed.

nodes.name: quote_path
nodes.summary: Produces a possibly quoted path relative to a prefix, optionally forcing double quotes when the path contains spaces.

nodes.name: unquote_c_style
nodes.summary: Parses a double-quoted C-style string (named escapes and octal escapes) into a strbuf, optionally reporting where it ended, and restores the buffer on error.

nodes.name: perl_quote_buf
nodes.summary: Appends a string as a single-quoted Perl literal, escaping quotes and backslashes.

nodes.name: perl_quote_buf_with_len
nodes.summary: Perl single-quote escaping for a length-delimited buffer that may contain NULs.

nodes.name: python_quote_buf
nodes.summary: Appends a string as a single-quoted Python literal, escaping quotes, backslashes and newlines.

nodes.name: tcl_quote_buf
nodes.summary: Appends a double-quoted Tcl string, escaping brackets, braces, dollar, quotes, backslashes and control whitespace.

nodes.name: basic_regex_quote_buf
nodes.summary: Escapes a string for a POSIX basic regular expression, quoting only a leading "^", a trailing "$" and the characters [ . \ *.

nodes.name: quote.h
nodes.summary: Declares the quoting API: shell single-quote quoting and dequoting (sq_quote_*, sq_dequote_*), C-style path quoting and unquoting, relative-path quoting, and escaping helpers for Perl, Python, Tcl and basic regex literals, plus the CQUOTE_NODQ and QUOTE_PATH_QUOTE_SP flags.

nodes.name: refs.c
nodes.summary: Backend-independent part of the reference module: it validates refnames, resolves refs and symbolic refs, expands short names with the rev-parse rules, iterates refs and reflogs, and implements atomic ref transactions (queue, prepare, hook, commit) and ref storage migration by dispatching to the files or reftable backend vtable.
nodes.languageNotes: Backends are plugged in through struct ref_storage_be function tables, and most ref_store functions are thin dispatchers such as refs->be->read_raw_ref.

nodes.name: find_ref_storage_backend
nodes.summary: Looks up the ref storage backend vtable (files or reftable) for a storage format enum value, returning NULL if unknown.

nodes.name: ref_storage_format_by_name
nodes.summary: Maps a backend name such as "files" or "reftable" to its ref_storage_format enum value, or UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: ref_storage_format_to_name
nodes.summary: Returns the name of a ref storage format, or "unknown".

nodes.name: update_ref_namespace
nodes.summary: Overrides the prefix of a ref namespace (for example the replace or notes refs) and frees the previous string if it was itself overridden.

nodes.name: check_refname_component
nodes.summary: Validates or sanitizes one refname component using a per-character disposition table: rejects "..", "@{", control and special characters, a leading ".", a trailing ".lock" and unexpected "*" unless refspec patterns are allowed.

nodes.name: check_or_sanitize_refname
nodes.summary: Checks every slash-separated component of a refname (or rewrites it into a valid one when a sanitized buffer is supplied), rejecting "@", a trailing dot and single-level names unless allowed.

nodes.name: check_refname_format
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if a refname is not well-formed according to git check-ref-format rules.

nodes.name: refs_fsck_ref
nodes.summary: fsck check for a regular ref that reports a null object ID as bad.

nodes.name: refs_fsck_symref
nodes.summary: fsck check for a symbolic ref: HEAD must point to a branch, and the target must be a valid refname that lies in refs/ or worktrees/ unless it is a root ref.

nodes.name: refs_fsck
nodes.summary: Runs the ref backend consistency check for a worktree via the backend fsck callback.

nodes.name: sanitize_refname_component
nodes.summary: Rewrites an arbitrary string into a refname-safe form in a strbuf, treating failure as a bug.

nodes.name: refname_is_safe
nodes.summary: Checks that a refname cannot escape refs/ (by normalizing the path) or, for non-refs/ names, consists only of uppercase letters and underscores like HEAD.

nodes.name: ref_resolves_to_object
nodes.summary: Returns true when a ref is not broken and its object ID exists in the object database, warning otherwise.

nodes.name: refs_resolve_refdup
nodes.summary: Resolves a ref through symrefs and returns the final name as a newly allocated string.

nodes.name: refs_read_ref_full
nodes.summary: Reads the object ID a ref resolves to, with resolve flags, returning 0 on success and -1 if it cannot be resolved.

nodes.name: refs_read_ref
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that reads a ref value in reading mode.

nodes.name: refs_ref_exists
nodes.summary: Returns whether a ref exists, by trying to resolve it for reading.

nodes.name: for_each_filter_refs
nodes.summary: Iteration callback that passes only refs whose name matches a wildmatch pattern to a user callback, optionally trimming a prefix from the name.

nodes.name: warn_if_dangling_symref
nodes.summary: Callback that prints a warning for a symref whose target is one of the refs being deleted.

nodes.name: refs_warn_dangling_symrefs
nodes.summary: Iterates all refs (including broken ones) and warns about symbolic refs that point at the given deleted ref names.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_tag_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over refs/tags/ with the prefix trimmed from each name.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_branch_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over refs/heads/ with the prefix trimmed from each name.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_remote_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over refs/remotes/ with the prefix trimmed from each name.

nodes.name: refs_head_ref_namespaced
nodes.summary: Reads HEAD within the current ref namespace (GIT_NAMESPACE) and passes it to a callback if it exists.

nodes.name: normalize_glob_ref
nodes.summary: Normalizes a ref glob pattern by adding a prefix (refs/ by default), stripping a trailing slash and recording whether it has glob special characters.

nodes.name: prettify_refname
nodes.summary: Strips the refs/heads/, refs/tags/ or refs/remotes/ prefix from a refname for display.

nodes.name: refname_match
nodes.summary: Tests whether an abbreviated name can mean a given full ref name using the rev-parse rules, returning a precedence value for disambiguation.

nodes.name: expand_ref_prefix
nodes.summary: Expands a user-supplied prefix through the rev-parse rules into the list of full ref prefixes to search.

nodes.name: repo_default_branch_name
nodes.summary: Returns the name for the initial branch from the test environment variable or init.defaultBranch (falling back to master or main, with advice), and validates it as a branch refname.

nodes.name: substitute_branch_name
nodes.summary: Expands magic branch shorthands like "@{-1}" or "@{upstream}" into a real name, returning the allocated replacement or NULL.

nodes.name: copy_branchname
nodes.summary: Copies a branch name into a strbuf after expanding any allowed magic shorthand at its start.

nodes.name: check_branch_ref
nodes.summary: Builds the full refs/heads/ name for a branch (expanding shorthands) and validates it, rejecting names that start with "-" or equal HEAD.

nodes.name: check_tag_ref
nodes.summary: Builds refs/tags/<name> and validates it, rejecting names that start with "-" or equal HEAD.

nodes.name: repo_dwim_ref
nodes.summary: Resolves a short name to a full ref (and object ID) by expanding branch shorthands and trying the rev-parse rules.

nodes.name: expand_ref
nodes.summary: Tries each rev-parse rule (name, refs/, refs/tags/, refs/heads/, refs/remotes/...) to resolve an abbreviated ref, counting matches and warning about dangling or broken ones.

nodes.name: repo_dwim_log
nodes.summary: Finds which ref names expanded from a short name have a reflog, returning the first and counting ambiguity.

nodes.name: is_per_worktree_ref
nodes.summary: Returns true for refs stored per worktree (refs/worktree/, refs/bisect/, refs/rewritten/).

nodes.name: is_pseudo_ref
nodes.summary: Returns true for the pseudo refs FETCH_HEAD and MERGE_HEAD, which hold extra data and are not regular refs.

nodes.name: is_root_ref_syntax
nodes.summary: Checks that a name consists only of uppercase letters, dashes and underscores, as root refs such as HEAD do.

nodes.name: is_root_ref
nodes.summary: Returns true for root refs: names ending in _HEAD or in a fixed list of irregular names (HEAD, AUTO_MERGE, BISECT_EXPECTED_REV, ...), excluding pseudo refs.

nodes.name: parse_worktree_ref
nodes.summary: Splits a possibly worktree-qualified ref ("worktrees/<name>/..." or "main-worktree/...") into the worktree name and bare refname and classifies it as current, main, other or shared.

nodes.name: get_files_ref_lock_timeout_ms
nodes.summary: Returns the lock timeout for files-backend ref updates from core.filesRefLockTimeout, defaulting to 100 ms and cached after the first call.

nodes.name: refs_delete_ref
nodes.summary: Deletes a single ref by running a one-update transaction (optionally checking the old value), printing an error and returning 1 on failure.

nodes.name: copy_reflog_msg
nodes.summary: Copies a reflog message collapsing runs of whitespace into single spaces and trimming the end.

nodes.name: normalize_reflog_message
nodes.summary: Returns a normalized copy of a reflog message (or an empty string).

nodes.name: refs_parse_log_all_ref_updates_config
nodes.summary: Parses core.logAllRefUpdates as always, normal (true) or none.

nodes.name: should_autocreate_reflog
nodes.summary: Decides whether a reflog should be created automatically for a ref under the logAllRefUpdates policy (branches, remotes, notes and HEAD in normal mode).

nodes.name: is_branch
nodes.summary: Returns true for HEAD and anything under refs/heads/.

nodes.name: set_read_ref_cutoffs
nodes.summary: Stores the message, timestamp, timezone and entry count of the reflog record where the search stopped into the caller output parameters.

nodes.name: read_ref_at_ent
nodes.summary: Reverse reflog callback for ref@{time} or ref@{n}: finds the entry at or before the requested time or count, warning about gaps or an unexpectedly ended log.

nodes.name: read_ref_at_ent_oldest
nodes.summary: Forward reflog callback that takes the oldest entry as the fallback result for a time earlier than the log.

nodes.name: read_ref_at
nodes.summary: Resolves ref@{time} or ref@{n} from the reflog by scanning entries newest-first, falling back to the oldest entry, and dying (or exiting quietly) for an empty log.

nodes.name: ref_store_transaction_begin
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes a ref_transaction for a ref store, with optional rejection tracking when partial failure is allowed.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_free
nodes.summary: Frees a ref transaction with all its queued updates and rejection records, rejecting a transaction that is still in the prepared state.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_maybe_set_rejected
nodes.summary: Marks one queued update as rejected (for transactions that allow failures), removes its name from the availability list, and records the error and details; returns 1 when the update was rejected.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_add_update
nodes.summary: Appends a new ref_update to an open transaction with the old and new values or symref targets, reflog message and committer info, and registers the refname for duplicate detection.

nodes.name: transaction_refname_valid
nodes.summary: Validates a refname for a transaction update, refusing pseudo refs and badly formed names, with different messages for reflog-only updates.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_update
nodes.summary: Queues an update of a ref to a new object ID or symref target, validating flags and refname, checking that the new object exists and that branches only point to commits, and peeling tags.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_update_reflog
nodes.summary: Queues a reflog-only update with explicit old and new object IDs, committer info and index, tracking the maximum index on the transaction.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_create
nodes.summary: Queues creation of a ref by updating it with a null old value (it must not exist), requiring a valid object ID or symref target.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_delete
nodes.summary: Queues deletion of a ref by updating it to the null object ID, optionally checking the old value or symref target.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_verify
nodes.summary: Queues a check that a ref still has the expected value or target when the transaction commits, without changing it.

nodes.name: refs_update_ref
nodes.summary: Convenience helper that updates one ref in a single-update transaction and reports failure by message, die or silently according to an action_on_err mode.

nodes.name: match_parse_rule
nodes.summary: Checks whether a full refname fits a "prefix%.*ssuffix" rev-parse rule and returns the part matched by the placeholder with its length.

nodes.name: refs_shorten_unambiguous_ref
nodes.summary: Finds the shortest name for a full ref that still resolves unambiguously by testing earlier rev-parse rules (and all other rules in strict mode) against the existing refs.

nodes.name: parse_hide_refs_config
nodes.summary: Parses transfer.hideRefs (and section-specific hideRefs) config values into a strvec, stripping trailing slashes.

nodes.name: ref_is_hidden
nodes.summary: Evaluates the hidden-refs rules from last to first (supporting "!" negation and "^" for full name matching) to decide whether a ref is hidden from advertisement.

nodes.name: hidden_refs_to_excludes
nodes.summary: Returns the hidden-ref patterns as iterator exclude patterns, or NULL when any rule uses "!" or "^" that cannot be expressed that way.

nodes.name: get_namespaced_exclude_patterns
nodes.summary: Prefixes exclude patterns with the ref namespace when one is active.

nodes.name: find_descendant_ref
nodes.summary: Looks in a sorted list of ref names for one that lives under a directory name, which signals a directory/file conflict, ignoring names in a skip list.

nodes.name: refs_head_ref
nodes.summary: Calls a callback with HEAD and the object ID it resolves to, if HEAD resolves.

nodes.name: refs_ref_iterator_begin
nodes.summary: Creates a ref iterator from the backend for a prefix, normalizing exclude patterns, turning on broken and dangling-symref handling unless GIT_REF_PARANOIA is disabled, and trimming a prefix if asked.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_ref_ext
nodes.summary: General ref iteration entry point: validates the options, builds the effective prefix, glob pattern filter and namespaced exclude patterns, creates a backend ref iterator and drives the callback over it.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over every ref with default options.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_replace_ref
nodes.summary: Iterates over refs under the replace-ref namespace (refs/replace/ unless overridden), including broken ones, with the prefix trimmed.

nodes.name: qsort_strcmp
nodes.summary: qsort comparator for an array of C strings.

nodes.name: find_longest_prefixes_1
nodes.summary: Recursively groups sorted patterns by common characters to compute the longest literal prefixes before any glob special character.

nodes.name: find_longest_prefixes
nodes.summary: Sorts patterns and returns the list of longest literal prefixes using find_longest_prefixes_1.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_ref_in_prefixes
nodes.summary: Iterates refs for several patterns by walking only the longest literal prefixes, stopping early if a callback returns non-zero.

nodes.name: refs_read_special_head
nodes.summary: Reads a pseudo ref such as FETCH_HEAD or MERGE_HEAD directly from a file in the git dir and parses it like a loose ref.

nodes.name: refs_read_raw_ref
nodes.summary: Reads the raw content of a ref (object ID or symref target and type flags) from the backend, handling pseudo refs specially.

nodes.name: refs_read_symbolic_ref
nodes.summary: Reads the target of a symbolic ref through the backend.

nodes.name: refs_resolve_ref_unsafe
nodes.summary: Core ref resolver: validates the name, reads the raw ref and follows symbolic refs up to SYMREF_MAXDEPTH, setting REF_ISSYMREF, REF_ISBROKEN and bad-name flags and returning a static string with the final refname.

nodes.name: refs_create_refdir_stubs
nodes.summary: Writes placeholder HEAD, refs and refs/heads files in a git dir so legacy Git recognises a repository whose refs live in another backend.

nodes.name: ref_store_create_on_disk
nodes.summary: Creates the on-disk structure of a ref store via the backend and adds the stub files when the repository uses a non-files or alternate refs storage.

nodes.name: ref_store_remove_on_disk
nodes.summary: Removes a ref store from disk through its backend and deletes the stub HEAD, refs/heads and refs entries that non-files backends leave behind.

nodes.name: repo_resolve_gitlink_ref
nodes.summary: Resolves a ref inside a submodule repository to an object ID, returning -1 if the submodule or ref cannot be found.

nodes.name: lookup_ref_store_map
nodes.summary: Looks up a registered ref store by name in a string map, returning NULL when absent.

nodes.name: ref_store_init
nodes.summary: Instantiates a ref store for a git dir by finding the backend for a storage format and calling its init callback.

nodes.name: ref_store_release
nodes.summary: Releases a ref store through its backend and frees its git dir string.

nodes.name: get_main_ref_store
nodes.summary: Returns the repository main ref store, creating it on first use (guarding against recursion) and optionally wrapping it for debugging.

nodes.name: register_ref_store_map
nodes.summary: Records a ref store under a name in a string map, treating a duplicate registration as a bug.

nodes.name: repo_get_submodule_ref_store
nodes.summary: Returns a cached read-only ref store for a submodule, locating its git dir and initializing a subrepository when needed.

nodes.name: get_worktree_ref_store
nodes.summary: Returns the ref store for a worktree: the main store for the current one, otherwise a cached store rooted in worktrees/<id> or the common dir.

nodes.name: base_ref_store_init
nodes.summary: Fills the common fields (backend, repository, git dir) of a ref store, called by backend init functions.

nodes.name: refs_optimize
nodes.summary: Optimizes ref storage (for example packing loose refs or compacting reftable) through the backend.

nodes.name: refs_optimize_required
nodes.summary: Asks the backend whether optimizing ref storage is currently required.

nodes.name: reference_get_peeled_oid
nodes.summary: Returns the peeled object ID of a ref, using a precomputed value when the backend provides one or peeling the object otherwise.

nodes.name: refs_update_symref
nodes.summary: Points a symbolic ref at a new target in a transaction.

nodes.name: refs_update_symref_extended
nodes.summary: Creates or updates a symbolic ref through a transaction, optionally in create-only mode and reporting the previous referent or object ID.

nodes.name: ref_update_reject_duplicates
nodes.summary: Errors out if the sorted list of refnames in a transaction contains the same name twice.

nodes.name: transaction_hook_feed_stdin
nodes.summary: Feeds one queued ref update per call to the reference-transaction hook stdin as "<old> <new> <refname>" lines, using zero IDs and "ref:" targets as appropriate.

nodes.name: transaction_feed_cb_data_alloc
nodes.summary: Allocates the per-task state used to stream updates to the hook.

nodes.name: transaction_feed_cb_data_free
nodes.summary: Frees the per-task hook feed state.

nodes.name: run_transaction_hook
nodes.summary: Runs the reference-transaction hook for a given phase, passing the transaction updates on stdin.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_prepare
nodes.summary: Prepares a transaction: checks state and quarantine restrictions, sorts and rejects duplicate refnames, runs the "preparing" hook, lets the backend lock refs and verify old values, then runs the "prepared" hook.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_abort
nodes.summary: Aborts a transaction: asks the backend to release locks if it was prepared, runs the "aborted" reference-transaction hook, and frees the transaction.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_commit
nodes.summary: Commits a transaction: prepares it if still open, lets the backend write all updates atomically, then runs the "committed" hook unless it was an initial transaction.

nodes.name: refs_verify_refnames_available
nodes.summary: Verifies that none of a set of refnames conflicts with an existing ref or other update: a leading directory exists as a ref, or a descendant ref exists under the name, recording rejections per update when allowed.

nodes.name: refs_verify_refname_available
nodes.summary: Single-refname variant of refs_verify_refnames_available.

nodes.name: do_for_each_reflog_helper
nodes.summary: Adapter that passes the name of an iterated reflog ref to a reflog callback.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_reflog
nodes.summary: Iterates over all refs that have a reflog using the backend reflog iterator.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_reflog_ent_reverse
nodes.summary: Calls a callback for each reflog entry of a ref from newest to oldest.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_reflog_ent
nodes.summary: Calls a callback for each reflog entry of a ref from oldest to newest.

nodes.name: refs_reflog_exists
nodes.summary: Returns whether a ref has a reflog.

nodes.name: refs_create_reflog
nodes.summary: Creates an empty reflog for a ref through the backend.

nodes.name: refs_delete_reflog
nodes.summary: Deletes the reflog of a ref.

nodes.name: refs_reflog_expire
nodes.summary: Expires reflog entries of a ref using prepare, should-prune and cleanup callbacks supplied by the caller.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_for_each_queued_update
nodes.summary: Calls a callback for each queued update with its refname and old and new object IDs.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_for_each_rejected_update
nodes.summary: Calls a callback for each rejected update with its refname, old and new values or targets, the error code and details.

nodes.name: refs_delete_refs
nodes.summary: Deletes many refs in a single transaction, warning about queue failures and reporting a commit error.

nodes.name: refs_rename_ref
nodes.summary: Renames a ref (with its reflog) through the backend after normalizing the log message.

nodes.name: refs_copy_existing_ref
nodes.summary: Copies an existing ref to a new name through the backend.

nodes.name: ref_update_original_update_refname
nodes.summary: Follows the parent chain of an update (created by split symref updates) and returns the refname of the original update.

nodes.name: ref_update_has_null_new_value
nodes.summary: Returns true when an update would delete the ref (null new object ID and no new target).

nodes.name: ref_update_check_old_target
nodes.summary: Checks that the current symref target matches the expected old target of an update and returns a nonexistent-ref or incorrect-old-value error with a message otherwise.

nodes.name: migrate_one_ref
nodes.summary: Migration callback that copies one ref (regular or symbolic) from the old ref store into a transaction on the new ref store, skipping reflog creation and OID verification.

nodes.name: migrate_one_reflog_entry
nodes.summary: Re-creates one reflog entry in the new ref store, rebuilding the committer ident string from the parsed name, email and date.

nodes.name: migrate_one_reflog
nodes.summary: Migrates every entry of one ref reflog by iterating it with migrate_one_reflog_entry.

nodes.name: move_files
nodes.summary: Moves every file from one directory into another with rename, recording the error text on failure.

nodes.name: has_worktrees
nodes.summary: Returns true if the repository has linked worktrees besides the main one.

nodes.name: repo_migrate_ref_storage_format
nodes.summary: Converts a repository between ref storage formats: builds the new ref store in a temporary directory, copies refs and reflogs in one initial transaction, then (unless dry-run) removes the old store, moves the new files into place and updates the repository format.

nodes.name: ref_update_expects_existing_old_ref
nodes.summary: Returns true when an update requires the ref to exist with a specific old value or symref target.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_error_msg
nodes.summary: Maps a ref_transaction_error code to a short human-readable description.

nodes.name: refs_compute_filesystem_location
nodes.summary: Works out where a ref backend keeps its data: the common dir, whether the git dir is a linked worktree, and the ref directory (honouring an alternate refs payload path).

nodes.name: for_each_ref_filter
nodes.summary: State for for_each_filter_refs: the glob pattern, prefix length to trim and the wrapped callback with its data.

nodes.name: warn_if_dangling_data
nodes.summary: State passed to warn_if_dangling_symref: ref store, output stream, names being deleted, indent and dry-run flag.

nodes.name: read_ref_at_cb
nodes.summary: State shared by the reflog callbacks that implement ref@{time} lookup: target time or count, result OID, previous and next IDs and cutoff outputs.

nodes.name: transaction_feed_cb_data
nodes.summary: Per-hook-invocation state holding the next update index and a reusable line buffer.

nodes.name: do_for_each_reflog_help
nodes.summary: Pairs a reflog callback with its payload for the ref-iterator adapter.

nodes.name: migration_data
nodes.summary: State shared by the ref migration callbacks: the old ref store, the target transaction, error buffer, scratch buffers and a reflog entry index.

nodes.name: strbuf.c
nodes.summary: Implements the strbuf growable NUL-terminated byte buffer that Git uses for nearly all string building: allocation and growth, trimming, splice and insert, printf-style append, reading files, fds and lines, URL and XML quoting, human-readable sizes, strftime wrapping and stripspace cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: The empty strbuf points at a shared one-byte slop buffer (strbuf_slopbuf) so buf is never NULL and always NUL terminated; alloc == 0 means the buffer is not heap owned. strbuf_getwholeline has two implementations selected by HAVE_GETDELIM.

nodes.name: starts_with
nodes.summary: Returns true when str begins with prefix by comparing byte by byte until the prefix ends.

nodes.name: istarts_with
nodes.summary: Case-insensitive variant of starts_with that compares with tolower.

nodes.name: starts_with_mem
nodes.summary: Prefix test for a possibly non-NUL-terminated memory block of known length.

nodes.name: skip_to_optional_arg_default
nodes.summary: Matches an option prefix and returns its optional "=value" argument, or a default when the prefix stands alone; used by command line option parsing.

nodes.name: strbuf_init
nodes.summary: Resets a strbuf to the blank STRBUF_INIT state and optionally pre-grows it to a hinted size.

nodes.name: strbuf_release
nodes.summary: Frees the heap buffer if the strbuf owns one and reinitializes it to the blank state.

nodes.name: strbuf_detach
nodes.summary: Hands the buffer to the caller as a malloc()ed string, optionally reporting its length, and leaves the strbuf blank.

nodes.name: strbuf_attach
nodes.summary: Makes a strbuf adopt an existing malloc()ed buffer with a given length and allocation size, releasing any previous content.

nodes.name: strbuf_grow
nodes.summary: Ensures at least the requested extra bytes (plus the NUL) are available, using ALLOC_GROW and overflow-checked arithmetic.

nodes.name: strbuf_trim
nodes.summary: Removes whitespace from both ends of the buffer by calling strbuf_rtrim then strbuf_ltrim.

nodes.name: strbuf_rtrim
nodes.summary: Removes trailing whitespace from the buffer by shrinking len and re-terminating.

nodes.name: strbuf_trim_trailing_dir_sep
nodes.summary: Strips trailing directory separators from a path held in the strbuf.

nodes.name: strbuf_trim_trailing_newline
nodes.summary: Removes one trailing LF and a CR before it if present, as done for lines read from text.

nodes.name: strbuf_ltrim
nodes.summary: Removes leading whitespace by advancing a pointer and memmove()ing the remainder to the front.

nodes.name: strbuf_reencode
nodes.summary: Converts the buffer between character encodings via reencode_string_len, replacing the contents on success.

nodes.name: strbuf_tolower
nodes.summary: Lower-cases every byte of the buffer in place.

nodes.name: strbuf_split_buf
nodes.summary: Splits a memory block at a terminator character into a NULL-terminated array of newly allocated strbufs, with an optional maximum count.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_separated_string_list
nodes.summary: Appends the items of a string_list to a strbuf joined with a separator string.

nodes.name: strbuf_list_free
nodes.summary: Releases every strbuf in a NULL-terminated array produced by strbuf_split and frees the array itself.

nodes.name: strbuf_cmp
nodes.summary: Three-way comparison of two strbufs using memcmp on the common length and then comparing lengths.

nodes.name: strbuf_splice
nodes.summary: Replaces len bytes at pos with new data, after bounds and overflow checks, using memmove to shift the tail; base of insert and remove.

nodes.name: strbuf_insert
nodes.summary: Inserts data at a position by splicing with a zero-length removal.

nodes.name: strbuf_vinsertf
nodes.summary: Formats a printf-style message with a va_list and inserts it at a position, measuring first with vsnprintf and then writing in place.

nodes.name: strbuf_insertf
nodes.summary: Variadic wrapper around strbuf_vinsertf.

nodes.name: strbuf_remove
nodes.summary: Deletes a range from the buffer by splicing in an empty replacement.

nodes.name: strbuf_add
nodes.summary: Appends len bytes of data to the buffer, growing as needed and keeping the NUL terminator.

nodes.name: strbuf_addstrings
nodes.summary: Appends a string n times, reserving the space with an overflow-checked multiplication.

nodes.name: strbuf_addbuf
nodes.summary: Appends the contents of another strbuf.

nodes.name: strbuf_join_argv
nodes.summary: Appends argv strings separated by a delimiter character and returns the buffer contents.

nodes.name: strbuf_addchars
nodes.summary: Appends a single character n times with memset.

nodes.name: strbuf_addf
nodes.summary: printf-style append that forwards to strbuf_vaddf.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_uint
nodes.summary: Appends the decimal representation of an unsigned integer using a stack buffer, without calling printf.

nodes.name: add_lines
nodes.summary: Static helper that copies a text block line by line, prefixing every line (with an optional space) and completing the final newline.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_commented_lines
nodes.summary: Appends text with each line prefixed by a comment prefix, as used for commit message templates and editor hints.

nodes.name: strbuf_commented_addf
nodes.summary: Formats a message and appends it as comment lines, dropping the trailing newline when the buffer ended on an incomplete line.

nodes.name: strbuf_vaddf
nodes.summary: Core printf appender: tries vsnprintf into the available space and regrows and retries once if the output did not fit.

nodes.name: strbuf_expand_step
nodes.summary: Copies the text up to the next percent sign of a format string into the buffer and tells whether a placeholder follows; building block of format expanders.

nodes.name: strbuf_expand_literal
nodes.summary: Expands the literal placeholders %n and %xNN (hex byte) shared by pretty-format style expanders.

nodes.name: strbuf_expand_bad_format
nodes.summary: Dies with a translated message describing a malformed "%(...)" element for a named command.

nodes.name: strbuf_addbuf_percentquote
nodes.summary: Appends a buffer while doubling every percent sign so it survives later format expansion.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_percentencode
nodes.summary: Percent-encodes bytes that are control characters or URL-unsafe, with flags to also encode slashes or to apply host-and-port rules.

nodes.name: strbuf_fread
nodes.summary: Reads up to size bytes from a FILE into the buffer and releases it again if nothing was read from an unallocated buffer.

nodes.name: strbuf_read
nodes.summary: Reads an entire file descriptor into the buffer with read_in_full, growing in chunks and restoring the old length on error.

nodes.name: strbuf_read_once
nodes.summary: Performs a single xread of up to the hinted size into the buffer, for pipes and sockets where only available data is wanted.

nodes.name: strbuf_write
nodes.summary: Writes the buffer contents to a FILE with fwrite.

nodes.name: strbuf_readlink
nodes.summary: Reads a symbolic link target into the buffer, doubling the buffer until readlink fits.

nodes.name: strbuf_getcwd
nodes.summary: Fills the buffer with the current working directory, growing until getcwd succeeds and handling EACCES and ERANGE.

nodes.name: strbuf_getwholeline
nodes.summary: Reads one terminator-delimited line including its terminator, using getdelim when available or a getc_unlocked loop otherwise; returns EOF at end of input.

nodes.name: strbuf_appendwholeline
nodes.summary: Reads a whole line into a temporary strbuf and appends it to the target buffer, leaving the target untouched on EOF.

nodes.name: strbuf_getdelim_strip_crlf
