nodes.summary: Reads one line and strips the trailing LF and an optional CR when the terminator is newline.

nodes.name: strbuf_getline
nodes.summary: Reads a line terminated by LF with CRLF handling; the usual way Git reads text input.

nodes.name: strbuf_getline_lf
nodes.summary: Reads a line terminated by LF without CR stripping.

nodes.name: strbuf_getline_nul
nodes.summary: Reads a NUL-terminated record, as used with -z style output.

nodes.name: strbuf_getwholeline_fd
nodes.summary: Reads a line from a raw file descriptor one byte at a time with xread, avoiding stdio buffering.

nodes.name: strbuf_read_file
nodes.summary: Opens a path, reads the whole file into the buffer with strbuf_read and preserves errno on failure.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_lines
nodes.summary: Appends text with every line prefixed by a given string.

nodes.name: strbuf_addstr_xml_quoted
nodes.summary: Appends a string escaping the XML special characters quote, less-than, greater-than and ampersand.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_urlencode
nodes.summary: Static helper that percent-encodes each byte not accepted by a predicate, writing lower-case hex.

nodes.name: strbuf_addstr_urlencode
nodes.summary: URL-encodes a NUL-terminated string using a caller-supplied predicate for characters that may stay unencoded.

nodes.name: humanise_count
nodes.summary: Turns a count into a scaled decimal value and SI unit (k, M, G) as translated strings.

nodes.name: humanise_bytes
nodes.summary: Converts a byte size to a value and IEC unit (KiB, MiB, GiB), with flags for rate units and compact byte labels.

nodes.name: strbuf_humanise_bytes
nodes.summary: Appends a human-readable byte size such as "12.34 MiB" to the buffer.

nodes.name: strbuf_humanise_rate
nodes.summary: Appends a human-readable transfer rate such as "1.20 MiB/s", used by progress output.

nodes.name: printf_ln
nodes.summary: printf that also writes a newline and returns the total byte count or -1 on error.

nodes.name: fprintf_ln
nodes.summary: fprintf to a given stream that appends a newline and returns the total byte count or -1.

nodes.name: xstrdup_tolower
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated lower-cased copy of a string.

nodes.name: xstrdup_toupper
nodes.summary: Returns a newly allocated upper-cased copy of a string.

nodes.name: xstrvfmt
nodes.summary: Formats with a va_list into a strbuf and detaches it as a malloc()ed string.

nodes.name: xstrfmt
nodes.summary: Variadic sprintf that returns a newly allocated string; heavily used across Git.

nodes.name: strbuf_addftime
nodes.summary: strftime into a strbuf that handles %z, %Z and %s itself (no portable way to pass a timezone) and retries with a bigger buffer.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Static helper returning a line length without trailing whitespace.

nodes.name: strbuf_stripspace
nodes.summary: Implements git stripspace: removes leading and trailing blank lines, trailing spaces per line, collapses blank-line runs and skips comment-prefixed lines.

nodes.name: strbuf_strip_file_from_path
nodes.summary: Cuts a path down to its directory part, keeping the trailing separator.

nodes.name: strbuf.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct strbuf and the whole strbuf API (init, grow, append, trim, splice, printf-style, read and line input, URL encoding, humanising, stripspace) plus inline helpers such as strbuf_addch and strbuf_setlen that most of Git builds strings with.
nodes.languageNotes: Documented in API-doc style comments; STRBUF_INIT points buf at the shared slop buffer so an unused strbuf needs no allocation and no free.

nodes.name: strbuf_swap
nodes.summary: Inline helper that swaps the contents of two strbufs with SWAP.

nodes.name: strbuf_avail
nodes.summary: Inline helper returning the allocated but unused bytes after len.

nodes.name: strbuf_setlen
nodes.summary: Inline helper that sets len, checks it against the allocation (BUG if beyond) and writes the NUL terminator.

nodes.name: strbuf_addch
nodes.summary: Inline helper that appends one character, growing by one when no space is left.

nodes.name: strbuf_addstr
nodes.summary: Inline helper that appends a NUL-terminated string through strbuf_add.

nodes.name: strbuf_complete
nodes.summary: Inline helper that appends a terminator character unless the buffer is empty or already ends with it.

nodes.name: strbuf
nodes.summary: The growable string buffer: alloc (bytes allocated), len (current length) and buf (always NUL terminated, possibly the shared slop buffer).

nodes.name: humanise_flags
nodes.summary: Flags (HUMANISE_RATE, HUMANISE_COMPACT) controlling whether humanised values use rate units or compact "B" labels.

nodes.name: string-list.c
nodes.summary: Implements string_list, an array of (string, util pointer) items that can be kept sorted for binary-search lookup or used unsorted: insert, lookup, remove, dedupe, filter, sort, clear and delimiter splitting. Used throughout Git for ref names, paths and config values.

nodes.name: string_list_init_nodup
nodes.summary: Resets a string_list to the empty state that does not own its strings.

nodes.name: string_list_init_dup
nodes.summary: Resets a string_list to the empty state that duplicates every string it stores.

nodes.name: get_entry_index
nodes.summary: Binary search over the sorted items with the list comparator; returns the match or the insertion point and sets exact_match.

nodes.name: add_entry
nodes.summary: Inserts a string at its sorted position (shifting later items with MOVE_ARRAY) unless it already exists, duplicating it when the list owns strings.

nodes.name: string_list_insert
nodes.summary: Public sorted insert returning the item for the string, reusing an existing entry.

nodes.name: string_list_remove
nodes.summary: Removes a string from a sorted list, freeing the string and optionally util, and closing the gap.

nodes.name: string_list_has_string
nodes.summary: Reports whether a sorted list contains the string via binary search.

nodes.name: string_list_find_insert_index
nodes.summary: Exposes the binary-search result: the index of the string or where it would be inserted.

nodes.name: string_list_lookup
nodes.summary: Binary-search lookup returning the item for a string or NULL.

nodes.name: string_list_remove_duplicates
nodes.summary: Compacts a sorted list in place by dropping adjacent equal entries and freeing their strings.

nodes.name: for_each_string_list
nodes.summary: Calls a callback on every item and stops on the first non-zero return.

nodes.name: filter_string_list
nodes.summary: Keeps only items accepted by a predicate callback, compacting the array and freeing rejected strings.

nodes.name: item_is_not_empty
nodes.summary: Predicate used to drop items whose string is empty.

nodes.name: string_list_remove_empty_items
nodes.summary: Removes items with empty strings through filter_string_list.

nodes.name: string_list_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the items array, the owned strings and optionally the util pointers, and resets the list.

nodes.name: string_list_clear_func
nodes.summary: Like string_list_clear but passes each util pointer and string to a custom clear callback first.

nodes.name: string_list_setlen
nodes.summary: Truncates a non-owning list to a shorter length, with BUG checks against misuse.

nodes.name: string_list_append_nodup
nodes.summary: Appends a string pointer without copying it, growing the array with ALLOC_GROW.

nodes.name: string_list_append
nodes.summary: Appends a string at the end, duplicating it when the list owns its strings; keeps the list unsorted.

nodes.name: cmp_items
nodes.summary: qsort_s comparator that unwraps the list comparison function from a context struct.

nodes.name: string_list_sort
nodes.summary: Sorts the items with the list comparator (strcmp by default) using QSORT_S.

nodes.name: string_list_sort_u
nodes.summary: Sorts the list and removes duplicates to produce a sorted set.

nodes.name: unsorted_string_list_lookup
nodes.summary: Linear search for a string in an unsorted list.

nodes.name: unsorted_string_list_has_string
nodes.summary: Tells whether an unsorted list contains a string.

nodes.name: unsorted_string_list_delete_item
nodes.summary: Deletes item i from an unsorted list by moving the last item into its slot.

nodes.name: unsorted_string_list_remove
nodes.summary: Finds a string in an unsorted list and removes it.

nodes.name: append_one
nodes.summary: Static helper that appends one split substring, with optional right trim, skipping empty pieces and in-place NUL-termination.

nodes.name: split_string
nodes.summary: Core splitter that walks a string on any delimiter character, honoring a maximum split count and TRIM and NONEMPTY flags.

nodes.name: string_list_split
nodes.summary: Splits a string on delimiters into a list that duplicates the pieces.

nodes.name: string_list_split_in_place
nodes.summary: Splits a writable string in place by overwriting delimiters with NUL, so the list points into the original buffer.

nodes.name: string_list_split_f
nodes.summary: Duplicating split with flags such as trimming and dropping empty items.

nodes.name: string_list_split_in_place_f
nodes.summary: In-place split with trim and non-empty flags.

nodes.name: string_list_sort_ctx
nodes.summary: Small context struct carrying the comparison function through qsort_s.

nodes.name: strvec.c
nodes.summary: Implements strvec, a NULL-terminated array of owned strings used to build argv and environment lists for child processes: push, printf-style push, splice, replace, remove, split on whitespace, clear and detach.

nodes.name: strvec_init
nodes.summary: Resets a strvec to the empty state that points at the shared empty_strvec array.

nodes.name: strvec_push_nodup
nodes.summary: Appends a pointer the strvec takes ownership of, growing the array and keeping the NULL terminator.

nodes.name: strvec_push
nodes.summary: Appends a duplicate of a string and returns the stored copy.

nodes.name: strvec_pushf
nodes.summary: Appends a printf-formatted string built with strbuf_vaddf.

nodes.name: strvec_pushl
nodes.summary: Appends a NULL-terminated variadic list of strings.

nodes.name: strvec_pushv
nodes.summary: Appends every string of a NULL-terminated array.

nodes.name: strvec_splice
nodes.summary: Replaces a range of entries by copies of a replacement array, freeing the old strings and shifting the tail.

nodes.name: strvec_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces one entry by a copy of a new string and frees the old one.

nodes.name: strvec_remove
nodes.summary: Removes and frees an entry, closing the gap including the NULL sentinel.

nodes.name: strvec_pop
nodes.summary: Removes and frees the last entry.

nodes.name: strvec_split
nodes.summary: Splits a string on whitespace and appends every word as a new entry.

nodes.name: strvec_clear
nodes.summary: Frees all strings and the array and returns the strvec to the empty state.

nodes.name: strvec_detach
nodes.summary: Returns the underlying array to the caller (a fresh empty one if unused) and resets the strvec.

nodes.name: symlinks.c
nodes.summary: Caches lstat() results for the leading directory components of a path so Git can cheaply tell whether any component is a symlink, missing or not a directory (used by checkout, apply and index operations), and tracks directories scheduled for removal once they become empty.
nodes.languageNotes: The cache remembers only the last checked path and a few flags (directory, missing, symlink); an unrelated lookup resets it, so callers that change the tree must call invalidate_lstat_cache.

nodes.name: longest_path_match
nodes.summary: Computes the length of the longest common prefix of two paths on a path-component (slash) basis and reports the previous slash position.

nodes.name: reset_lstat_cache
nodes.summary: Clears the cached path and flags of an lstat cache.

nodes.name: lstat_cache_matchlen
nodes.summary: Core of the cache: reuses the cached prefix when the new path shares it, then stat()s or lstat()s the remaining components one at a time to classify them as directory, missing, symlink or error, and updates the cache.

nodes.name: lstat_cache
nodes.summary: Wrapper around lstat_cache_matchlen that returns only the resulting flags.

nodes.name: threaded_has_symlink_leading_path
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if some leading component of the path is a symlink, using a caller-supplied cache so threads do not share state.

nodes.name: has_symlink_leading_path
nodes.summary: Symlink-in-leading-path check using the process-wide default cache.

nodes.name: check_leading_path
nodes.summary: Checks the leading path with the default cache and optionally warns when lstat failed for another reason than a missing file.

nodes.name: threaded_check_leading_path
nodes.summary: Returns 0 if a leading component is missing, -1 if all leading components are directories, or the offending component length if it is not a directory, emitting an lstat warning when asked.

nodes.name: has_dirs_only_path
nodes.summary: Tells whether every component of the path exists as a directory, using the default cache.

nodes.name: threaded_has_dirs_only_path
nodes.summary: Directory-only path check against a given cache, optionally following symlinks inside a prefix via stat().

nodes.name: do_remove_scheduled_dirs
nodes.summary: Walks the queued removal path upward, rmdir()ing directories that are now empty and never removing the original working directory.

nodes.name: schedule_dir_for_removal
nodes.summary: Records a directory path whose last file was removed, first flushing deeper queued directories that are no longer on the path, so empty parent directories can be deleted later.

nodes.name: remove_scheduled_dirs
nodes.summary: Removes all queued directories that are empty by calling do_remove_scheduled_dirs down to the root.

nodes.name: invalidate_lstat_cache
nodes.summary: Resets the default lstat cache after the working tree has been modified.

nodes.name: lstat_cache_aware_rmdir
nodes.summary: rmdir that invalidates the default lstat cache when the directory was removed.

nodes.name: thread-utils.c
nodes.summary: Portable thread helpers: online_cpus detects the number of usable processors across Windows, HP-UX, BSD sysctl and sysconf for sizing worker pools, init_recursive_mutex initializes a recursive pthread mutex, and dummy pthread stubs are provided for builds without threads.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of #ifdef to select the platform API; with NO_PTHREADS the pthread functions become stubs that return ENOSYS.

nodes.name: online_cpus
nodes.summary: Returns the number of online processors using the best API of the platform (GetSystemInfo, pstat, sysctl, sysconf), falling back to 1.

nodes.name: init_recursive_mutex
nodes.summary: Initializes a pthread mutex with the recursive attribute, or does nothing when threads are disabled.

nodes.name: dummy_pthread_create
nodes.summary: Stub for pthread_create in NO_PTHREADS builds that always returns ENOSYS.

nodes.name: dummy_pthread_init
nodes.summary: Stub init function for NO_PTHREADS builds that returns ENOSYS to keep compilers from warning about unused variables.

nodes.name: dummy_pthread_join
nodes.summary: Stub for pthread_join in NO_PTHREADS builds that returns ENOSYS.

nodes.name: sub-process.h
nodes.summary: Declares the long-running subprocess helper used by filters and similar protocols: a hashmap of started child processes keyed by command, a handshake that negotiates protocol version and capabilities, and status reading in pkt-line format.

nodes.name: subprocess_get_child_process
nodes.summary: Inline accessor returning the child_process of an entry.

nodes.name: subprocess_entry
nodes.summary: Hashmap entry for one long-running child: the command string and its struct child_process.

nodes.name: subprocess_capability
nodes.summary: Name and bit flag of an optional capability that can be negotiated in the handshake.

nodes.name: tar.h
nodes.summary: Defines the POSIX ustar header layout (struct ustar_header with name, mode, size, mtime, checksum, magic and prefix fields) and typeflag constants used by git archive when writing tar files.

nodes.name: ustar_header
nodes.summary: The 512-byte-block ustar header record with fixed-width character fields for name, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime, checksum, typeflag, linkname, magic and prefix.

nodes.name: unix-socket.c
nodes.summary: Creates and connects Unix domain stream sockets, working around the short sun_path limit by temporarily chdir()ing into the socket directory and restoring the original working directory afterwards.

nodes.name: chdir_len
nodes.summary: Static helper that chdir()s into the first len bytes of a path string.

nodes.name: unix_sockaddr_cleanup
nodes.summary: Restores the original working directory saved by unix_sockaddr_init, dying if that fails because the process cwd would be left wrong.

nodes.name: unix_sockaddr_init
nodes.summary: Fills a sockaddr_un for a path; when the path exceeds sun_path it changes into the directory and uses only the basename, remembering the old cwd.

nodes.name: unix_stream_connect
nodes.summary: Opens a socket and connects it to a Unix domain stream socket path, preserving errno on failure.

nodes.name: unix_stream_listen
nodes.summary: Unlinks any stale socket file, binds and listens on a Unix domain stream socket with a configurable backlog.

nodes.name: unix_sockaddr_context
nodes.summary: Context remembering the original working directory to restore after a chdir used for a long socket path.

nodes.name: unix-socket.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Unix domain stream socket client and server helpers and the options struct that sets the listen backlog and whether chdir may be used.

nodes.name: unix_stream_listen_opts
nodes.summary: Options for unix_stream_listen: listen backlog size and a flag forbidding the chdir workaround for long paths.

nodes.name: unix-stream-server.c
nodes.summary: Creates a Unix domain socket server safely: takes a .lock file, refuses to start if another server already answers on the path, binds the socket, and can later detect that the socket file was replaced ("stolen") by another process.

nodes.name: is_another_server_alive
nodes.summary: Pokes a socket path by connecting and immediately hanging up to learn whether a live server is listening.

nodes.name: unix_ss_create
nodes.summary: Acquires a lock for the path, fails with EADDRINUSE if a server is alive, otherwise listens on the socket and records its stat data for later steal detection.

nodes.name: unix_ss_free
nodes.summary: Closes the server socket, unlinks the socket file unless it was stolen, and frees the structure.

nodes.name: unix_ss_was_stolen
nodes.summary: Compares the current lstat of the socket path with the saved inode and device to detect that another process replaced the socket.

nodes.name: unix-stream-server.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct unix_ss_socket and the create, free and was-stolen functions of the lock-protected Unix domain socket server helper.

nodes.name: unix_ss_socket
nodes.summary: Server socket record holding the socket path, the lstat data captured at creation and the listening file descriptor.

nodes.name: url.c
nodes.summary: Small URL helpers: RFC 3986 character classes, URL scheme detection, percent-decoding (including query parameters), appending a trailing slash, telling local paths from scp-style SSH remotes and mapping a scheme name to the url_scheme enum.

nodes.name: is_rfc3986_unreserved
nodes.summary: Predicate for the RFC 3986 unreserved characters: alphanumerics and -, _, ., ~.

nodes.name: is_casefolding_rfc3986_unreserved
nodes.summary: Like is_rfc3986_unreserved but only for lower-case letters, digits and the punctuation, used for case-folding comparisons.

nodes.name: is_urlschemechar
nodes.summary: Tells whether a character may appear in a URL scheme (looser rule for the first character).

nodes.name: is_url
nodes.summary: Returns true when a string looks like "scheme://", checking the scheme characters and the colon-slash-slash.

nodes.name: url_decode_internal
nodes.summary: Static percent-decoder that reads up to len bytes, stops at given delimiters and optionally turns + into space, returning the detached strbuf.

nodes.name: url_decode
nodes.summary: Percent-decodes an entire NUL-terminated URL, leaving the scheme part untouched.

nodes.name: url_decode_mem
nodes.summary: Percent-decodes a URL of known length while copying the protocol part before the first colon verbatim.

nodes.name: url_percent_decode
nodes.summary: Percent-decodes a string without any protocol special-casing.

nodes.name: url_decode_parameter_name
nodes.summary: Decodes a query-string parameter name up to the next = or &, mapping + to space and advancing the cursor.

nodes.name: url_decode_parameter_value
nodes.summary: Decodes a query-string parameter value up to the next &, mapping + to space and advancing the cursor.

nodes.name: end_url_with_slash
nodes.summary: Appends a URL to a strbuf and makes sure it ends with a slash.

nodes.name: str_end_url_with_slash
nodes.summary: Replaces a heap string pointer by a copy of the URL that ends with a slash.

nodes.name: url_is_local_not_ssh
nodes.summary: Distinguishes local paths (including DOS drive paths) from scp-style user@host:path remotes using the position of the first colon and slash.

nodes.name: url_get_scheme
nodes.summary: Maps the scheme name (ssh, git, file, and the deprecated git+ssh and ssh+git) to the url_scheme enum.

nodes.name: urlmatch.c
nodes.summary: Normalizes and parses URLs per RFC 3986 (lower-casing, percent-escape normalization, default-port removal, dot-segment resolution, scp-style SSH conversion) and implements the config matching used for http.<url>.* settings, picking the most specific matching URL pattern for a variable.

nodes.name: append_normalized_escapes
nodes.summary: Copies text into a strbuf while unescaping characters that need no escaping and escaping those that do, upper-casing hex digits and rejecting malformed %XX sequences.

nodes.name: end_of_token
nodes.summary: Static helper that returns the position of the next occurrence of a character in a block or the end of the block.

nodes.name: match_host
nodes.summary: Compares a URL host to a pattern host label by label (dot separated), allowing a single "*" label as a wildcard.

nodes.name: url_normalize_1
nodes.summary: Parses and normalizes a full URL into scheme, user, password, host, port and path parts, validating each, removing default ports and . and .. segments, and filling a url_info with offsets.

nodes.name: url_normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes a URL without allowing wildcard host characters.

nodes.name: url_normalize_pattern
nodes.summary: Normalizes a URL pattern from configuration, allowing "*" in the host.

nodes.name: url_parse
nodes.summary: Parses any Git remote URL (including scp-style host:path and bracketed IPv6 forms) by rewriting it to ssh:// form, normalizing it and adjusting the path for ~user.

nodes.name: url_match_prefix
nodes.summary: Checks that a URL prefix matches a URL on a path-component boundary and returns the match length.

nodes.name: match_urls
nodes.summary: Decides whether a pattern URL matches a URL by comparing scheme, user, host, port and path, and records how specific the match is.

nodes.name: cmp_matches
nodes.summary: Orders two matches by host match length, then path match length, then whether the user matched.

nodes.name: urlmatch_config_entry
nodes.summary: Config callback for http.<url>.var style keys: matches the key URL against the target, keeps the most specific value per variable and forwards winning entries to the collect callback.

nodes.name: urlmatch_config_release
nodes.summary: Frees the string_list of collected variables of a urlmatch_config.

nodes.name: usage.c
nodes.summary: Git's central error and diagnostics reporting: die(), error(), warning(), usage(), BUG() and their errno variants write prefixed messages to stderr and exit with the right code, through replaceable routine pointers, with trace2 logging and recursion protection.
nodes.languageNotes: The behavior of die, error, warn, usage and die_message is held in static function pointers that libgit users can replace with set_die_routine and friends; the built-in defaults are the *_builtin functions.

nodes.name: vfreportf
nodes.summary: Formats a prefixed message into a 4 KiB buffer, replaces control characters with ?, and writes it with a single write_in_full so concurrent messages do not interleave.

nodes.name: vreportf
nodes.summary: Writes a prefixed message to stderr via vfreportf.

nodes.name: usage_builtin
nodes.summary: Default usage handler: prints the usage text, labels the trace2 command name "_usage_" and exits with status 129.

nodes.name: die_message_builtin
nodes.summary: Default handler that logs the message to trace2 and prints it with a "fatal: " prefix without exiting.

nodes.name: die_builtin
nodes.summary: Default die handler: prints the message through the die message routine and exits with status 128.

nodes.name: error_builtin
nodes.summary: Default error handler that logs to trace2 and prints an "error: " message.

nodes.name: warn_builtin
nodes.summary: Default warning handler that logs to trace2 and prints a "warning: " message.

nodes.name: die_is_recursing_builtin
nodes.summary: Counts nested die() calls and reports recursion beyond a limit, warning on the second call, to stop infinite die loops.

nodes.name: set_die_routine
nodes.summary: Installs a custom die handler, used by embedders and tests.

nodes.name: get_die_message_routine
nodes.summary: Returns the current die message handler.

nodes.name: set_error_routine
nodes.summary: Installs a custom error handler.

nodes.name: get_error_routine
nodes.summary: Returns the current error handler.

nodes.name: set_warn_routine
nodes.summary: Installs a custom warning handler.

nodes.name: get_warn_routine
nodes.summary: Returns the current warning handler.

nodes.name: set_die_is_recursing_routine
nodes.summary: Replaces the die recursion detector, for example with a thread-aware one.

nodes.name: usagef
nodes.summary: Reports a printf-style usage error through the usage routine and does not return.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Reports a fixed usage string through usagef.

nodes.name: show_usage_if_asked_helper
nodes.summary: Prints usage text to stdout and exits successfully, used for -h.

nodes.name: show_usage_if_asked
nodes.summary: Shows the usage and exits when the only argument is -h or --help-all.

nodes.name: die
nodes.summary: Prints a fatal error message through the die routine and exits with status 128, guarding against recursion; the standard way Git aborts.

nodes.name: fmt_with_err
nodes.summary: Appends strerror(errno) to a format string, doubling percent signs of the error text so it can be used as a printf format.

nodes.name: die_errno
nodes.summary: Like die but appends the errno description to the message.

nodes.name: die_message
nodes.summary: Prints a fatal-style message without exiting and returns 128 so callers can return it as an exit code.

nodes.name: die_message_errno
nodes.summary: die_message variant that appends the errno description.

nodes.name: error_errno
nodes.summary: Prints an error with the errno description and returns -1.

nodes.name: error
nodes.summary: Prints an "error: " message and returns -1 so it can be used in return statements.

nodes.name: warning_errno
nodes.summary: Prints a warning that includes the errno description.

nodes.name: warning
nodes.summary: Prints a "warning: " message.

nodes.name: BUG_vfl_common
nodes.summary: Formats the "BUG: file:line:" prefix and reports the message, shared by BUG and bug.

nodes.name: BUG_vfl
nodes.summary: Reports an internal bug, logs it to trace2 and aborts (or exits with BUG_exit_code in tests), preventing recursion.

nodes.name: BUG_fl
nodes.summary: Entry point behind the BUG() macro: records file and line and aborts with an internal error message.

nodes.name: bug_fl
nodes.summary: Entry point behind the bug() macro: reports the problem but defers the abort until a later BUG_if_bug call.

nodes.name: you_still_use_that
nodes.summary: Announces that a deprecated command will be removed, prints pointers to the breaking-changes document and the mailing list, then dies unless the user opted in.

nodes.name: userdiff.c
nodes.summary: Holds the table of built-in diff drivers (per-language hunk-header funcname regexes and word-diff regexes for Ada, C, Python, Rust, etc.), reads custom diff.<driver>.* configuration, and resolves which driver, textconv and external command apply to a path through the "diff" gitattribute.
nodes.languageNotes: The bulk of the file is the static builtin_drivers[] array built with the PATTERNS and IPATTERN macros; each entry pairs a funcname regex (for the @@ hunk header) with a word-diff regex.

nodes.name: userdiff_find_by_namelen_cb
nodes.summary: Callback for for_each_userdiff_driver that stops when a driver name matches a name of a given length.

nodes.name: regexec_supports_multi_byte_chars
nodes.summary: Probes once whether the C library regexec treats a UTF-8 multibyte character as one non-space unit, to pick the best word regex.

nodes.name: userdiff_find_by_namelen
nodes.summary: Looks up a driver (custom first, then built-in) by name and length via for_each_userdiff_driver.

nodes.name: parse_funcname
nodes.summary: Reads a funcname pattern from config into a driver, owning the string and setting regex flags.

nodes.name: parse_tristate
nodes.summary: Parses a config value that may be a boolean or "auto" (stored as -1).

nodes.name: parse_bool
nodes.summary: Parses a boolean config value into a driver field.

nodes.name: userdiff_config
nodes.summary: Handles a diff.<driver>.<key> config entry: creates a custom driver if needed and sets funcname, xfuncname, binary, command, textconv, wordregex, algorithm or cache flags.

nodes.name: userdiff_find_by_name
nodes.summary: Returns the driver of a given name and activates the multibyte word regex when the platform supports it.

nodes.name: userdiff_find_by_path
nodes.summary: Checks the "diff" attribute of a path: returns the built-in true or false drivers or the named driver, or NULL when unset.

nodes.name: userdiff_get_textconv
nodes.summary: Returns the driver if it has a textconv command and sets up a notes cache for textconv results when caching is enabled.

nodes.name: for_each_userdiff_driver_list
nodes.summary: Helper that runs a callback over an array of drivers and stops on a non-zero result.

nodes.name: for_each_userdiff_driver
nodes.summary: Iterates the custom drivers and then the built-in drivers with a callback that can stop early.

nodes.name: find_by_namelen_data
nodes.summary: Callback state for finding a driver by name and length.

nodes.name: userdiff.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct userdiff_driver (funcname regex, word regex, external diff command, textconv and its cache, algorithm) and the functions that look drivers up by name or by path attribute.

nodes.name: userdiff_funcname
nodes.summary: Regex pattern (and its compile flags) that identifies the function-name line for diff hunk headers.

nodes.name: external_diff
nodes.summary: External diff command and whether its exit code is trusted.

nodes.name: userdiff_driver
nodes.summary: One diff driver: name, external command, algorithm, binary flag, funcname and word regexes, textconv command and notes cache.

nodes.name: userdiff_driver_type
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing built-in drivers from custom drivers defined in configuration.

nodes.name: utf8.c
nodes.summary: UTF-8 and character-encoding support: validating and decoding UTF-8, computing display width (wide and zero-width characters, ANSI escapes), word wrapping and alignment of text, iconv-based re-encoding with BOM handling, and HFS+ ignorable-character handling for detecting .git-like names.
nodes.languageNotes: git_wcwidth uses the generated unicode-width.h interval tables with a binary search; is_hfs_dotgit and friends emulate how HFS+ ignores some Unicode code points, which matters for the CVE-fixing .git name checks.

nodes.name: display_mode_esc_sequence_len
nodes.summary: Returns the length of an ANSI SGR escape sequence (ESC [ digits ; m) at the start of a string or 0, so it can be skipped when measuring width.

nodes.name: bisearch
nodes.summary: Binary search of a code point in a sorted table of intervals.

nodes.name: git_wcwidth
nodes.summary: Returns the terminal column width of a code point: -1 for control characters, 0 for combining or zero-width, 2 for wide East Asian characters, otherwise 1.

nodes.name: pick_one_utf8_char
nodes.summary: Decodes one UTF-8 character, rejecting overlong forms, surrogates and non-characters, and advances the pointer or sets it to NULL on invalid input.

nodes.name: utf8_width
nodes.summary: Returns the display width of the next UTF-8 character and advances the cursor, or NULL start on invalid UTF-8.

nodes.name: utf8_strnwidth
nodes.summary: Computes the display width of a string of given length, optionally skipping ANSI escapes and falling back to byte length on invalid UTF-8.

nodes.name: utf8_strwidth
nodes.summary: Display width of a NUL-terminated string.

nodes.name: is_utf8
nodes.summary: Checks that a text is valid UTF-8 (allowing newline, tab and CR).

nodes.name: strbuf_add_indented_text
nodes.summary: Appends text with an indent on the first line and another on following lines, without wrapping.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_wrapped_text
nodes.summary: Appends text wrapped at a display width with first-line and continuation indents, aware of UTF-8 width and ANSI escapes, retrying as bytes if the text is not valid UTF-8.

nodes.name: strbuf_add_wrapped_bytes
nodes.summary: Wrapping variant for a non-NUL-terminated byte range.

nodes.name: strbuf_utf8_replace
nodes.summary: Replaces the characters occupying a column range of the buffer by a substitute string, keeping ANSI escapes intact.

nodes.name: same_utf_encoding
nodes.summary: Compares two encoding names as UTF variants ignoring case and the dash after "utf".

nodes.name: is_encoding_utf8
nodes.summary: Tells whether an encoding name (NULL means UTF-8) denotes UTF-8.

nodes.name: same_encoding
nodes.summary: Compares two encoding names, treating NULL as UTF-8 and UTF-8 spelling variants as equal.

nodes.name: utf8_fprintf
nodes.summary: fprintf that returns the number of display columns printed instead of bytes.

nodes.name: reencode_string_iconv
nodes.summary: Runs iconv over a buffer, growing the output on E2BIG and leaving room for a BOM prefix.

nodes.name: fallback_encoding
nodes.summary: Maps unusual encoding names (UTF-8 spellings, latin-1) to names iconv understands.

nodes.name: reencode_string_len
nodes.summary: Converts a string between encodings with iconv, adding a UTF-16 BOM where required, with a fallback encoding name retry.

nodes.name: has_bom_prefix
nodes.summary: Tells whether data starts with a given BOM byte sequence.

nodes.name: has_prohibited_utf_bom
nodes.summary: Detects a BOM in data declared as UTF-16BE/LE or UTF-32BE/LE, where a BOM is not allowed.

nodes.name: is_missing_required_utf_bom
nodes.summary: Detects absence of the BOM required by the UTF-16 or UTF-32 encodings.

nodes.name: mbs_chrlen
nodes.summary: Returns the byte length of the next character in a given encoding, treating invalid UTF-8 as one raw byte.

nodes.name: next_hfs_char
nodes.summary: Reads the next UTF-8 code point skipping the ignorable Unicode characters that HFS+ ignores in file names.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dot_generic
nodes.summary: Checks whether a path component equals ".<name>" under HFS+ semantics (ignorable code points, case-insensitive).

nodes.name: is_hfs_dot_str
nodes.summary: Helper that tests a path against ".<needle>" with HFS+ rules.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dotgit
nodes.summary: True if the path component is .git as seen by HFS+; used to refuse malicious tree entries.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dotgitmodules
nodes.summary: True if the component is .gitmodules under HFS+ rules.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dotgitignore
nodes.summary: True if the component is .gitignore under HFS+ rules.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dotgitattributes
nodes.summary: True if the component is .gitattributes under HFS+ rules.

nodes.name: is_hfs_dotmailmap
nodes.summary: True if the component is .mailmap under HFS+ rules.

nodes.name: skip_utf8_bom
nodes.summary: Skips a leading UTF-8 byte order mark and reports whether one was present.

nodes.name: strbuf_utf8_align
nodes.summary: Appends a string padded to a display width with left, middle or right alignment, compensating for multibyte characters.

nodes.name: interval
nodes.summary: First and last code point of a range used by the width tables.

nodes.name: varint.c
nodes.summary: Encodes and decodes the variable-length offset integers used in Git pack and index formats (7 bits per byte, with an added-one bias so every value has a unique shortest encoding).

nodes.name: decode_varint
nodes.summary: Reads an offset-style varint from a buffer, advancing the pointer and returning 0 on overflow.

nodes.name: encode_varint
nodes.summary: Encodes a value as an offset-style varint into a buffer (or just measures it when buf is NULL) and returns the byte length.

nodes.name: version.c
nodes.summary: Provides the Git version strings and the HTTP user agent: git_user_agent, a sanitized variant that appends sanitized OS information (uname), and get_uname_info that formats the sysname (or full uname) into a strbuf.

nodes.name: redact_non_printables
nodes.summary: Trims a buffer and replaces unprintable characters and spaces by dots so the text can sit inside a header.

nodes.name: git_user_agent
nodes.summary: Returns the user agent string, honoring the GIT_USER_AGENT environment variable and caching the result.

nodes.name: os_info
nodes.summary: Gets and caches sanitized uname information for the user agent.

nodes.name: git_user_agent_sanitized
nodes.summary: Builds and caches a sanitized user agent that includes OS info unless the user overrode it.

nodes.name: get_uname_info
nodes.summary: Appends the system name, or the full release, version and machine string, from uname() to a strbuf; reports failure text.

nodes.name: versioncmp.c
nodes.summary: Implements versioncmp, the "natural" version-number string comparison behind tag version sorting (for example git tag --sort=version:refname), with leading-zero rules and configurable prerelease suffixes from versionsort.suffix.
nodes.languageNotes: A small finite-state machine (next_state and result_type tables, adapted from glibc strverscmp) decides how digit runs and leading zeros compare.

nodes.name: find_better_matching_suffix
nodes.summary: Searches a tag name for a configured prerelease suffix and records the best (earliest, longest) match with its config position.

nodes.name: swap_prereleases
nodes.summary: Orders two tag names by the position of their prerelease suffix in the config so that, e.g., v1.0-rc1 sorts before v1.0.

nodes.name: versioncmp
nodes.summary: Compares two version strings digit-run aware, applying the prerelease suffix rules read lazily from config.

nodes.name: suffix_match
nodes.summary: Tracks the best match of a prerelease suffix in a tag name: config position, start offset and length.

nodes.name: versioncmp.h
nodes.summary: Declares versioncmp, the version-aware string comparison function.

nodes.name: wildmatch.c
nodes.summary: Implements Git's glob matcher used by .gitignore, pathspecs and gitattributes: recursive dowild handles ?, *, ** (with WM_PATHNAME slash rules), bracket classes including POSIX [:alpha:] names, backslash escapes and optional case folding.
nodes.languageNotes: dowild returns WM_ABORT_ALL or WM_ABORT_TO_STARSTAR to stop pointless backtracking in * and ** loops; adapted from rsync wildmatch.

nodes.name: dowild
nodes.summary: Recursive glob matcher: walks pattern and text together, handling literals, ?, single and double star with pathname flags, bracket expressions with ranges, negation and POSIX classes, and prunes backtracking with abort codes.

nodes.name: wildmatch
nodes.summary: Public entry that runs dowild and reduces the result to WM_MATCH or WM_NOMATCH.

nodes.name: wrapper.c
nodes.summary: Safe wrappers around libc: xmalloc, xrealloc, xcalloc, xstrdup that die on failure (with an optional GIT_ALLOC_LIMIT), restartable xread and xwrite with *_in_full loops, open and fopen wrappers that report errors, temp-file creation, fsync strategies, random bytes and mmap helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Many functions are the "x" family: they never return on failure and instead call die(), so callers do not check for NULL. I/O wrappers cap each call at MAX_IO_SIZE and retry on EINTR and EAGAIN.

nodes.name: memory_limit_check
nodes.summary: Enforces the optional GIT_ALLOC_LIMIT environment limit on a requested allocation size, dying or returning -1 when over it.

nodes.name: xstrdup
nodes.summary: strdup that dies when memory runs out.

nodes.name: do_xmalloc
nodes.summary: Shared malloc implementation honoring the memory limit and the gentle mode, with a 1-byte fallback for zero sizes.

nodes.name: xmalloc
nodes.summary: malloc that dies on failure; the standard allocator used across Git.

nodes.name: do_xmallocz
nodes.summary: Allocates size+1 bytes with an overflow check and NUL-terminates the block.

nodes.name: xmallocz
nodes.summary: Allocates a NUL-terminated block of the given size, dying on failure.

nodes.name: xmallocz_gently
nodes.summary: Like xmallocz but returns NULL with an error message instead of dying.

nodes.name: xmemdupz
nodes.summary: Duplicates len bytes of memory and appends a NUL terminator.

nodes.name: xstrndup
nodes.summary: strndup replacement that copies up to len bytes or the first NUL.

nodes.name: xstrncmpz
nodes.summary: Compares a counted string with a NUL-terminated one, requiring the latter to end exactly at len.

nodes.name: xrealloc
nodes.summary: realloc that dies on failure and honors the allocation limit.

nodes.name: xcalloc
nodes.summary: calloc with multiplication overflow detection that dies on failure.

nodes.name: xsetenv
nodes.summary: setenv that dies with errno information on failure.

nodes.name: xopen
nodes.summary: open() that retries on EINTR and dies with a descriptive message depending on the mode flags.

nodes.name: handle_nonblock
nodes.summary: Polls a non-blocking descriptor until it is ready after EAGAIN, so xread and xwrite can retry.

nodes.name: xread
nodes.summary: read() restarted on EINTR and EAGAIN with the size capped at MAX_IO_SIZE.

nodes.name: xwrite
nodes.summary: write() restarted on EINTR and EAGAIN with the size capped at MAX_IO_SIZE.

nodes.name: xpread
nodes.summary: pread() restarted on EAGAIN and EINTR with a capped size.

nodes.name: read_in_full
nodes.summary: Loops xread until the requested count is read or EOF, returning the total bytes read.

nodes.name: write_in_full
nodes.summary: Loops xwrite until all data is written, turning a zero write into ENOSPC.

nodes.name: xwritev
nodes.summary: writev() restarted on EINTR and EAGAIN that limits the total size to MAX_IO_SIZE.

nodes.name: writev_in_full
nodes.summary: Loops xwritev, advancing through the iovec array to cope with partial writes.

nodes.name: pread_in_full
nodes.summary: Loops xpread to read a count from an offset, stopping at EOF.

nodes.name: xdup
nodes.summary: dup() that dies on failure.

nodes.name: xfopen
nodes.summary: fopen that retries on EINTR and dies with a mode-specific message.

nodes.name: xfdopen
nodes.summary: fdopen that dies on failure.

nodes.name: fopen_for_writing
nodes.summary: Opens a file for writing, unlinking and retrying once when EPERM occurs (for read-only files).

nodes.name: warn_on_inaccessible
nodes.summary: Static helper emitting a warning that a path could not be accessed.

nodes.name: warn_on_fopen_errors
nodes.summary: Warns about fopen errors other than ENOENT and ENOTDIR and returns -1 for them.

nodes.name: fopen_or_warn
nodes.summary: fopen that warns on unexpected errors and returns NULL.

nodes.name: xmkstemp
nodes.summary: Creates a unique temporary file from a template with mode 0600, dying on failure.

nodes.name: git_mkdstemps_mode
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary file or directory by replacing XXXXXX with random characters from csprng_bytes, retrying on EEXIST.

nodes.name: git_mkstemps_mode
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary file from a pattern with a suffix and given mode.

nodes.name: git_mkdtemp
nodes.summary: Creates a unique temporary directory from an XXXXXX template.

nodes.name: git_mkstemp_mode
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary file from a template with a given mode.

nodes.name: xmkstemp_mode
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary file from a template with a chosen mode, dying with the absolute path of the template when creation fails.

nodes.name: fsync_loop
nodes.summary: Calls fsync repeatedly while it fails with EINTR.

nodes.name: git_fsync
nodes.summary: Flushes a file descriptor either as writeout only (sync_file_range or similar) or with a full hardware flush, per platform, counting trace2 counters.

nodes.name: warn_if_unremovable
nodes.summary: Static helper that warns about a failed removal (naming the operation and file) unless the error was ENOENT, preserving errno.

nodes.name: unlink_or_msg
nodes.summary: Removes a file, putting an error message in a strbuf on failure and treating ENOENT as success.

nodes.name: unlink_or_warn
nodes.summary: Removes a file and warns on failure.

nodes.name: rmdir_or_warn
nodes.summary: Removes a directory and warns on failure.

nodes.name: access_error_is_ok
nodes.summary: Decides whether an access() error (a missing-file error, or EACCES when ACCESS_EACCES_OK is set) may be ignored.

nodes.name: access_or_warn
nodes.summary: access() that warns about unexpected errors.

nodes.name: access_or_die
nodes.summary: access() that dies about unexpected errors.

nodes.name: xgetcwd
nodes.summary: Returns the current working directory as a malloc()ed string using strbuf_getcwd, dying on failure.

nodes.name: xsnprintf
nodes.summary: snprintf that BUGs when the output is truncated, for buffers known to be large enough.

nodes.name: write_file_buf
nodes.summary: Writes a buffer to a file, dying on any error.

nodes.name: write_file
nodes.summary: Writes a printf-formatted line (adding a newline) to a file, dying on error.

nodes.name: sleep_millisec
nodes.summary: Sleeps for a number of milliseconds by calling poll with no descriptors.

nodes.name: xgethostname
nodes.summary: gethostname that guarantees NUL termination.

nodes.name: is_missing_file
nodes.summary: Returns true if stat fails with ENOENT, and dies on any other stat error.

nodes.name: is_empty_or_missing_file
nodes.summary: Returns true when a file does not exist or has zero size, dying on other stat errors.

nodes.name: open_nofollow
nodes.summary: Opens a path refusing to follow a final symlink (O_NOFOLLOW, or an lstat check where unavailable), setting ELOOP when the path is a link.

nodes.name: csprng_bytes
nodes.summary: Fills a buffer with cryptographically secure random bytes using arc4random, getrandom, getentropy, RtlGenRandom, OpenSSL or /dev/urandom depending on the platform.

nodes.name: git_rand
nodes.summary: Returns a random 32-bit value from csprng_bytes, dying if it fails.

nodes.name: xmmap_gently
nodes.summary: mmap wrapper that enforces the GIT_MMAP_LIMIT limit (dying when exceeded) and returns NULL for a zero-length mapping.

nodes.name: mmap_os_err
nodes.summary: Returns an extra hint for failed mmap messages (on Linux ENOMEM it mentions vm.max_map_count and RLIMIT_DATA), otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: xmmap
nodes.summary: mmap that dies on failure; used to map pack and index files.

nodes.name: wrapper.h
nodes.summary: Declares the x* safe wrappers (allocation, open, read, write, fopen, mkstemp), the *_in_full I/O loops, write_file helpers, fsync actions, unlink and access helpers, random byte generation and the log2u inline.

nodes.name: write_str_in_full
nodes.summary: Inline helper that writes a NUL-terminated string with write_in_full.

nodes.name: log2u
nodes.summary: Inline integer base-2 logarithm (floor) of an unsigned value, returning 0 for zero.

nodes.name: fsync_action
nodes.summary: Enum selecting writeout-only or hardware-flush behavior for git_fsync.

nodes.name: ws.c
nodes.summary: Implements whitespace-error rules for git diff --check, git apply and the whitespace gitattribute: parsing rule lists like "trailing-space,-indent-with-non-tab,tabwidth=4", checking and highlighting whitespace errors in a line, and rewriting a line to fix them.

nodes.name: parse_whitespace_rule
nodes.summary: Parses a comma-separated whitespace rule string (with "-" negation and tabwidth=N) into a bitmask starting from the default rule.

nodes.name: whitespace_rule
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective whitespace rule for a path from the "whitespace" attribute (true, false, unset or a rule string) and the core.whitespace default.

nodes.name: whitespace_error_string
nodes.summary: Builds a human-readable, comma-separated description of the whitespace errors in a result bitmask.

nodes.name: ws_check_emit_1
nodes.summary: Scans one line for whitespace errors under a rule, returning the error bits and optionally printing the line with the offending parts wrapped in color codes.

nodes.name: ws_check_emit
nodes.summary: Prints a line highlighting its whitespace errors, discarding the result bits.

nodes.name: ws_check
nodes.summary: Returns the whitespace error bits of a line without printing.

nodes.name: ws_blank_line
nodes.summary: Tells whether a line consists only of whitespace.

nodes.name: ws_fix_copy
nodes.summary: Copies a line to a strbuf while repairing whitespace errors (trailing blanks, space-before-tab, indentation with non-tab, CR at EOL), counting fixes; used by git apply --whitespace=fix.

nodes.name: whitespace_rule
nodes.summary: Table entry naming a whitespace rule and its bit, with flags for rules that loosen errors or are excluded from the default.

nodes.name: ws.h
nodes.summary: Declares the whitespace error flags (WS_BLANK_AT_EOL, WS_SPACE_BEFORE_TAB, WS_INDENT_WITH_NON_TAB, WS_CR_AT_EOL, WS_TAB_IN_INDENT and others), the default rule and the functions that parse, check and fix whitespace.

nodes.name: xdiff-interface.c
nodes.summary: Git-side glue for the xdiff library: wraps xdl_diff with size limits and common-tail trimming, turns xdiff output into per-line and per-hunk callbacks, reads files and blobs into mmfile_t, detects binary data, sets up hunk-header function-name regexes, and parses merge conflict style config.

nodes.name: xdiff_out_hunk
nodes.summary: xdiff hunk callback that forwards hunk header numbers and funcname to the user hunk function, BUGging if a line was left incomplete.

nodes.name: consume_one
nodes.summary: Splits a buffer into lines and passes each to the line callback, stopping if it returns non-zero.

nodes.name: xdiff_outf
nodes.summary: xdiff output callback that reassembles lines split across buffers using a remainder strbuf and then feeds whole lines to the user callback.

nodes.name: trim_common_tail
nodes.summary: Trims identical trailing 1 KiB blocks of two buffers (at a line boundary) before diffing, an optimization when no context is wanted.

nodes.name: xdi_diff
nodes.summary: Runs xdl_diff on two buffers after rejecting files over the size limit and trimming the common tail.

nodes.name: xdi_diff_outf
nodes.summary: Diffs two buffers and delivers results through line and hunk callbacks.

nodes.name: read_mmfile
nodes.summary: Reads a file into an mmfile_t, reporting errors.

nodes.name: read_mmblob
nodes.summary: Reads a blob object from the object database into an mmfile_t, with an empty buffer for the null oid, dying if the object is not a blob.

nodes.name: buffer_is_binary
nodes.summary: Treats a buffer as binary if a NUL byte appears within the first 8000 bytes.

nodes.name: ff_regexp
nodes.summary: xdiff find-function callback that matches a line against a list of regexes (with negations) to extract the hunk-header function name.

nodes.name: xdiff_set_find_func
nodes.summary: Compiles a newline-separated list of funcname regexes (with ! negation) and installs ff_regexp as the find-function hook.

nodes.name: xdiff_clear_find_func
nodes.summary: Frees the compiled funcname regexes and clears the find-function hook.

nodes.name: xdiff_hash_string
nodes.summary: Hashes a string with xdiff record hashing under the whitespace flags.

nodes.name: xdiff_compare_lines
nodes.summary: Compares two lines for equality under xdiff whitespace-ignoring flags.

nodes.name: parse_conflict_style_name
nodes.summary: Maps merge.conflictstyle names (merge, diff3, zdiff3) to xdiff merge flags or -1.

nodes.name: conflict_style_name
nodes.summary: Returns the name of a conflict style for a flag value.

nodes.name: git_xmerge_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that parses merge.conflictstyle into git_xmerge_style and defers other keys to git_default_config.

nodes.name: xdiff_emit_state
nodes.summary: State of the xdiff output adapter: hunk and line callbacks, user data and a remainder buffer for partial lines.

nodes.name: ff_regs
nodes.summary: Array of compiled funcname regexes with a negate flag per entry.

nodes.name: xdiffi.h
nodes.summary: Internal header of the xdiff diff engine declaring the Myers recursion (xdl_recs_cmp), diff setup, change compaction, edit script building and emission, and the patience and histogram algorithms.

nodes.name: xdalgoenv_t
nodes.summary: Tuning parameters of the Myers algorithm: maximum cost, snake count threshold and heuristic minimum.

nodes.name: xdchange_t
nodes.summary: One node of the edit script: a changed hunk with line positions and counts in both files.

nodes.name: xtypes.h
nodes.summary: Internal type definitions of the xdiff library: character-pool nodes, a record (line) with pointer, size and hash, a per-file record table with change flags, and the two-file diff environment.

nodes.name: chanode_t
nodes.summary: Node of the chunked allocator list used by xdiff.

nodes.name: chastore_t
nodes.summary: Chunked memory pool used to allocate xdiff records.

nodes.name: xrecord_t
nodes.summary: One line of a file for diffing: pointer, size and minimal perfect hash.

nodes.name: xdfile_t
nodes.summary: All lines of one file for diffing with change marks and the index of lines to compare.

nodes.name: xdfenv_t
nodes.summary: The pair of prepared files compared by a diff run.

nodes.name: xutils.h
nodes.summary: Internal utility declarations of xdiff: record hashing with whitespace-insensitive variants, line comparison under whitespace flags, chunk allocator, hunk header emission, line guessing and a growable array helper.

nodes.name: xdl_hash_record
nodes.summary: Inline dispatcher choosing between the verbatim and whitespace-aware record hash.

nodes.name: prompt.h
nodes.summary: Declares git_prompt() and git_read_line_interactively(), the helpers used to ask the user for a line of input (credentials, confirmations) via askpass or the terminal.

nodes.name: range-diff.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git range-diff`: reads two commit ranges via `git log -p`, normalizes each commit into a comparable patch text, pairs commits with exact matching and then a linear assignment over diff-of-diff costs, and prints the pairing with nested diffs.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a minimum-cost assignment (linear-assignment.h) over an n x n cost matrix built from the diff sizes of unmatched patches.

nodes.name: patch_util
nodes.summary: Per-commit record used by range-diff: hash map entry for exact matching, the normalized patch and diff text, its index, the diff size, and the index of the matching commit in the other range.

nodes.name: read_patches
nodes.summary: Runs `git log -p --reverse` on a range as a child process and rewrites the output into one normalized string per commit (metadata, commit message, file headers, hunk headers), with the commit object id stored in a patch_util on each string_list item.

nodes.name: patch_util_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback that compares two patch_util entries by their normalized diff text.

nodes.name: find_exact_matches
nodes.summary: Hashes the diff text of every patch of the left range and then removes identical diffs found in the right range, recording matching indices for commits whose patches are byte-for-byte equal.

nodes.name: diffsize
nodes.summary: Computes the cost of two patch texts as the number of lines in the diff between them, using xdiff with 3 lines of context; returns COST_MAX on failure.

nodes.name: get_correspondences
nodes.summary: Builds an n x n cost matrix (diff size between unmatched patches, creation/deletion cost scaled by creation_factor, COST_MAX for already matched pairs), enforces a memory cap, and solves the assignment to pair commits of the two ranges.

nodes.name: output_pair_header
nodes.summary: Prints one line of the range-diff table: left and right commit numbers and abbreviated object ids, a status symbol (=, !, <, >), colors, and the one-line commit subject.

nodes.name: get_filespec
nodes.summary: Creates a diff_filespec backed by an in-memory string and assigns the section_headers userdiff driver so hunk headers show the "## file ##" section names.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Walks both commit lists in the order of the newer range, printing unmatched left commits, unmatched right commits and matched pairs with a nested diff of the two patches via patch_diff.

nodes.name: show_range_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point of range-diff: reads patches for both ranges, finds exact matches, computes correspondences and prints the result.

nodes.name: is_range_diff_range
nodes.summary: Tells whether an argument looks like a revision range (has both positive and negative revisions) by running setup_revisions on it and counting UNINTERESTING pending objects.

nodes.name: range-diff.h
nodes.summary: Public interface for range-diff: the range_diff_options struct, default creation factor and memory limit macros, show_range_diff() and is_range_diff_range().

nodes.name: range_diff_options
nodes.summary: Options for show_range_diff: creation factor, dual color, left-only/right-only, include merges, memory limit, optional diff options and extra log arguments.

nodes.name: rebase-interactive.c
nodes.summary: Support code for `git rebase -i`: writes the todo list with its comment help, launches the sequence editor, re-parses the edited list and checks for accidentally dropped commits according to rebase.missingCommitsCheck.

nodes.name: get_missing_commit_check_level
nodes.summary: Reads the rebase.missingCommitsCheck config and maps ignore, warn or error to the internal check level, warning on unknown values.

nodes.name: append_todo_help
nodes.summary: Appends the commented help text (pick, reword, edit, squash, fixup, exec, label, merge, update-ref, ...) to the todo list buffer, with a header for the rebase range and a warning about removed lines.

nodes.name: edit_todo_list
nodes.summary: Writes the todo file and its backup, launches the sequence editor, parses the edited buffer into a todo_list and checks it for dropped commits against the backup, then filters the update-refs file.

nodes.name: todo_list_check
nodes.summary: Compares the old and new todo lists with a commit slab to find commits that disappeared, and warns or errors according to the check level.

nodes.name: todo_list_check_against_backup
nodes.summary: Parses the saved git-rebase-todo.backup file and runs todo_list_check against the current list.

nodes.name: rebase-interactive.h
nodes.summary: Declares the interactive rebase helpers: append_todo_help, edit_todo_list, todo_list_check and todo_list_check_against_backup.

nodes.name: ref-filter.c
nodes.summary: Core of for-each-ref, branch and tag listing: parses %(atom) format strings, filters refs by kind, pattern, contains/merged/points-at and ahead-behind, lazily reads the needed object data, sorts the ref_array and formats each item with a nestable if/then/else/align stack.
nodes.languageNotes: Atoms are table driven: valid_atom[] maps each name to a parser, and per-ref values are filled lazily by populate_value() only for atoms that were used in the format or sort keys.

nodes.name: setup_ref_filter_porcelain_msg
nodes.summary: Replaces the untranslated plumbing strings for "gone", "ahead %d", "behind %d" with translated porcelain messages used by the upstream:track atom.

nodes.name: expand_data
nodes.summary: Scratch record holding the object id, type, size, disk size, delta base and content of the object being inspected, together with the object_info request filled in as atoms are parsed.

nodes.name: if_then_else
nodes.summary: State of an %(if)...%(then)...%(else) block: the comparison mode and string, which branches were seen and whether the condition was satisfied.

nodes.name: used_atom
nodes.summary: Descriptor of an atom used in the format or sort keys: its type, name, comparison type, object source, and a union of parsed per-atom options (color, align, contents, remote ref, signature, describe, ...).

nodes.name: ref_formatting_stack
nodes.summary: One level of the output stack used while formatting: its own output strbuf, the at_end callback run on %(end) and its data.

nodes.name: ref_formatting_state
nodes.summary: Formatting state holding the quote style and the top of the ref_formatting_stack.

nodes.name: atom_value
nodes.summary: Value produced for one atom of one ref: the string, its size, a handler that appends it to the output stack, and a numeric value for sorting.

nodes.name: ref_sorting
nodes.summary: Node of the linked list of sort keys: the index of the atom in used_atom and sort flags (reverse, ignore case, version sort).

nodes.name: match_atom_arg_value
nodes.summary: Parses one "name[=value]" item of a comma separated atom argument list and returns the value span and the remaining string.

nodes.name: remote_ref_atom_parser
nodes.summary: Parses the argument of %(upstream) and %(push) (track, trackshort, nobracket, remotename, remoteref, or a refname strip option) into the remote_ref union.

nodes.name: trailers_atom_parser
nodes.summary: Parses %(trailers:...) options into a heap allocated ref_trailer_buf and trailer options so pointers survive reallocation of the used_atom array.

nodes.name: contents_atom_parser
nodes.summary: Parses %(contents:...) arguments (body, size, signature, subject, trailers, lines=N) into the contents option of the atom.

nodes.name: describe_atom_option_parser
nodes.summary: Parses one option of %(describe:...) (tags, abbrev, match, exclude) and turns it into the corresponding `git describe` command line argument.

nodes.name: align_atom_parser
nodes.summary: Parses %(align:width,position) arguments into a width and a left, middle or right alignment, rejecting unknown or missing values.

nodes.name: parse_ref_filter_atom
nodes.summary: Looks a format or sort atom up in valid_atom[], reuses an already registered used_atom, otherwise appends a new one, runs its parser and sets flags (object content needed, deref, symref).

nodes.name: quote_formatting
nodes.summary: Appends a string to a strbuf with shell, Perl, Python or Tcl quoting depending on the quote style.

nodes.name: if_then_else_handler
nodes.summary: End-of-block handler for %(if): drops the unused then/else branch from the output stack depending on whether the condition was satisfied.

nodes.name: then_atom_handler
nodes.summary: Handles %(then): checks the %(if) state and evaluates the condition (equals, notequals, or non-empty output) on the text collected so far.

nodes.name: end_atom_handler
nodes.summary: Handles %(end): runs the at_end callback of the top stack element (align or if), applies quoting for top level blocks and pops the element.

nodes.name: verify_ref_format
nodes.summary: Scans the format string for %(...) atoms, parses each through parse_ref_filter_atom and rejects invalid combinations such as raw with a quoting style.

nodes.name: grab_common_values
nodes.summary: Fills the atoms common to every object type: objecttype, objectsize, deltabase and the dereferenced objectname.

nodes.name: grab_commit_values
nodes.summary: Parses the object as a commit and fills the tree, parent and numparent atoms.

nodes.name: grab_date
nodes.summary: Extracts the timestamp and timezone from an ident line and formats the date atom according to the requested date mode.

nodes.name: grab_person
nodes.summary: Fills name, email and date atoms of author, committer or tagger from the object header, optionally applying the mailmap, and fills the creator atoms.

nodes.name: grab_signature
nodes.summary: Verifies the GPG or SSH signature of a commit once and fills the %(signature:...) atoms (grade, signer, key, fingerprint, trustlevel).

nodes.name: find_subpos
nodes.summary: Locates the subject, body and signature in a commit or tag message buffer.

nodes.name: grab_sub_body_contents
nodes.summary: Fills the raw, subject, body, contents, signature, lines and trailers atoms from the object content.

nodes.name: grab_values
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the object type (tag, commit, tree, blob) and calls the matching grab_* helpers to fill the atom values of one object.

nodes.name: fill_remote_ref_details
nodes.summary: Computes the string for upstream/push atoms: the short ref, ahead/behind tracking text, trackshort symbol, remote name or remote ref of a branch.

nodes.name: get_head_description
nodes.summary: Builds the "(HEAD detached at ...)" or "(no branch, rebasing ...)" description of the current HEAD from wt_status state.

nodes.name: get_object
nodes.summary: Reads the object info of a ref target through the object database and, when content is needed, calls grab_values and grab_common_values.

nodes.name: populate_value
nodes.summary: Computes all atom values of one ref: handles ref based atoms (refname, upstream, push, HEAD, worktreepath, flag, align, if/then/else, ahead-behind), then reads the object and its peeled tag target.

nodes.name: get_ref_atom_value
nodes.summary: Lazily populates the values of a ref on first access and returns the value of one atom.

nodes.name: match_pattern
nodes.summary: Matches a refname against literal prefix or wildcard patterns, ignoring the refs/tags, refs/heads and refs/remotes prefixes.

nodes.name: match_name_as_path
nodes.summary: Matches a refname against patterns as path prefixes or wildmatch globs (used with match_as_path).

nodes.name: ref_filter_forked_add
nodes.summary: Registers a --forked pattern on the filter, resolving a ref argument to its full name or keeping a glob.

nodes.name: apply_ref_filter
nodes.summary: Applies kind, pattern, exclude, points-at, forked and contains filters to one ref and returns a new ref_array_item or NULL.

nodes.name: ref_array_push
nodes.summary: Allocates a ref_array_item for a refname and object id and appends it to a ref_array.

nodes.name: ref_kind_from_refname
nodes.summary: Classifies a refname as branch, remote, tag, detached HEAD, pseudo ref, root ref or other.

nodes.name: filter_and_format_one
nodes.summary: Per-ref callback that filters, formats and prints one ref immediately and stops at max_count.

nodes.name: ref_array_clear
nodes.summary: Frees every ref_array_item, the used_atom table and its per-atom allocations, and the worktree map.

nodes.name: reach_filter
nodes.summary: Keeps or drops refs by reachability from the --merged/--no-merged commits using tips_reachable_from_bases and clears the marks.

nodes.name: filter_ahead_behind
nodes.summary: Computes ahead and behind counts of every ref against the bases named by %(ahead-behind:) atoms.

nodes.name: filter_is_base
nodes.summary: Finds, for each %(is-base:) atom, which ref tip is the base of the given commit and records its name.

nodes.name: do_filter_refs
nodes.summary: Chooses the ref iteration strategy by kind (branches, remotes, tags, patterns, all) and calls a callback per ref, then adds HEAD when requested.

nodes.name: filter_refs
nodes.summary: Public filtering entry: iterates refs with filter_one into a ref_array and applies the merged/no-merged reachability filters.

nodes.name: filter_and_format_refs
nodes.summary: Either formats refs during iteration when sorting and filtering allow it, or builds a ref_array, computes ahead-behind and is-base, sorts and prints it.

nodes.name: ref_sorting_set_sort_flags_all
nodes.summary: Sets or clears sort flags on every node of a ref_sorting list.

nodes.name: ref_array_sort
nodes.summary: Sorts the items of a ref_array with compare_refs using the ref_sorting list.

nodes.name: format_ref_array_item
nodes.summary: Formats one ref according to the format string, walking its %(atoms), pushing handlers on the output stack and writing the result to a strbuf.

nodes.name: print_formatted_ref_array
nodes.summary: Formats and prints up to max_count items of a ref_array, honoring omit_empty.

nodes.name: pretty_print_ref
nodes.summary: Formats and prints a single ref given by name and object id outside of a filter.

nodes.name: ref_sorting_options
nodes.summary: Converts the list of --sort strings into a linked ref_sorting list.

nodes.name: ref_sorting_release
nodes.summary: Frees every node of a ref_sorting list.

nodes.name: parse_opt_merge_filter
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --merged and --no-merged: resolves the commit and adds it to the reachable_from or unreachable_from list.

nodes.name: ref_filter_init
nodes.summary: Resets a ref_filter to the REF_FILTER_INIT state.

nodes.name: ref_filter_clear
nodes.summary: Releases the vectors, oid array and commit lists held by a ref_filter and re-initializes it.

nodes.name: ref-filter.h
nodes.summary: Public API of the ref-filter engine: ref_array, ref_filter, ref_format and sorting types, quoting and filter-kind constants, and functions to filter, sort and format refs.

nodes.name: ref_array_item
nodes.summary: One ref that passed the filter: object id, peeled id, flags, kind, symref target, cached commit and per-atom values, counts and refname.

nodes.name: ref_array
nodes.summary: Growable array of ref_array_item pointers plus the rev_info and ahead-behind counts.

nodes.name: ref_filter
nodes.summary: Filter criteria: name patterns, excludes, forked, points-at, contains, no-contains, merged, no-merged, kind, and internal contains caches.

nodes.name: ref_format
nodes.summary: Output format settings: format string, rest, quote style, color use, and max_count/omit_empty options.

nodes.name: ref_sorting_order
nodes.summary: Enum of sort flags: reverse, ignore case, version sort and detached HEAD first.

nodes.name: reflog-walk.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git log -g` style reflog walking: reads the complete reflog of a ref, keeps a cursor per commit_reflog, merges several reflogs by timestamp and renders the reflog selector, message and ident for each visited entry.

nodes.name: complete_reflogs
nodes.summary: All entries of one reflog loaded in memory (old and new object ids, ident email, timestamp, timezone, message) with the full and short ref name.

nodes.name: read_one_reflog
nodes.summary: refs_for_each_reflog_ent callback that appends one reflog entry to a complete_reflogs array.

nodes.name: free_complete_reflog
nodes.summary: Frees a complete_reflogs and the strings held by its entries.

nodes.name: read_complete_reflog
nodes.summary: Loads the full reflog of a ref, trying the name as given, the symref it resolves to, refs/<name> and refs/heads/<name>.

nodes.name: commit_reflog
nodes.summary: Cursor into a complete_reflogs: current entry number and whether the user selected by index, by date or not at all.

nodes.name: reflog_walk_info
nodes.summary: State of a reflog walk: list of commit_reflog cursors, cache of loaded reflogs and the last visited entry.

nodes.name: init_reflog_walk
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes a reflog_walk_info.

nodes.name: reflog_walk_info_release
nodes.summary: Releases the cursors, cached reflogs and the reflog_walk_info itself.

nodes.name: add_reflog_for_walk
nodes.summary: Parses a ref@{N} or ref@{date} selector, loads the reflog (using dwim_log if needed) and registers a cursor so the commit can be walked through its reflog.

nodes.name: get_reflog_selector
nodes.summary: Builds the display selector (ref@{N} or ref@{date}) of the last visited reflog entry, optionally shortening the ref name.

nodes.name: get_reflog_message
nodes.summary: Appends the message of the last visited reflog entry without the trailing newline.

nodes.name: get_reflog_ident
nodes.summary: Returns the ident (email field) of the last visited reflog entry.

nodes.name: get_reflog_timestamp
nodes.summary: Returns the timestamp of the last visited reflog entry.

nodes.name: show_reflog_message
nodes.summary: Prints the "Reflog: ..." header lines (or oneline form) for the current reflog entry in log output.

nodes.name: reflog_walk_empty
nodes.summary: Tells whether a reflog walk has no registered reflog cursors.

nodes.name: next_reflog_commit
nodes.summary: Moves a cursor backwards until it finds an entry whose new object is a commit and returns it.

nodes.name: next_reflog_entry
nodes.summary: Picks, across all cursors, the commit whose reflog entry has the latest timestamp and advances that cursor.

nodes.name: reflog-walk.h
nodes.summary: Declares the reflog walking API used by the revision machinery: initialization, add_reflog_for_walk, iteration with next_reflog_entry and accessors for selector, message, ident and timestamp.

nodes.name: reflog.c
nodes.summary: Reflog expiry policy: parses gc.reflogExpire config, decides per entry whether it is expired or unreachable (marking reachable commits from the ref tips), checks object completeness for stale-fix, and implements deletion of single reflog entries.

nodes.name: find_cfg_ent
nodes.summary: Finds or creates the per-pattern reflog expiry entry in the options list.

nodes.name: reflog_expire_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for gc.reflogExpire and gc.reflogExpireUnreachable, with optional ref pattern subsections; falls back to git_default_config.

nodes.name: reflog_clear_expire_config
nodes.summary: Frees the list of per-pattern expiry entries.

nodes.name: reflog_expire_options_set_refname
nodes.summary: Chooses the expiry times for a specific ref from its matching pattern, the refs/stash exception or the defaults, unless given explicitly.

nodes.name: tree_is_complete
nodes.summary: Recursively checks that a tree and everything it references exists in the object database, marking trees SEEN or INCOMPLETE.

nodes.name: commit_is_complete
nodes.summary: Walks the ancestry of a commit until SEEN commits and verifies that all trees are complete, setting SEEN or INCOMPLETE flags.

nodes.name: keep_entry
nodes.summary: Returns whether a reflog entry object is the null id or a complete commit that can be kept (used by stalefix).

nodes.name: mark_reachable
nodes.summary: Marks as REACHABLE the commits reachable from the mark list, stopping at commits older than a limit and queueing them for a later deeper pass.

nodes.name: is_unreachable
nodes.summary: Decides whether a reflog commit is unreachable from the ref tip(s), extending the reachability marking to the root when needed.

nodes.name: should_expire_reflog_ent
nodes.summary: Expiry predicate for one reflog entry: too old, incomplete (stalefix), older than the unreachable limit and unreachable, or selected by recno.

nodes.name: should_expire_reflog_ent_verbose
nodes.summary: Wraps should_expire_reflog_ent and prints "keep", "would prune" or "prune" for each entry.

nodes.name: push_tip_to_list
nodes.summary: Callback of refs_for_each_ref that adds the commit of every non-symbolic ref to a commit list.

nodes.name: is_head
nodes.summary: Tells whether a (possibly worktree-prefixed) refname is HEAD.

nodes.name: reflog_expiry_prepare
nodes.summary: Prepares the expiry policy for a ref: chooses the unreachable-expire kind, collects tips and runs the first reachability marking.

nodes.name: reflog_expiry_cleanup
nodes.summary: Clears the REACHABLE marks and frees the tip and mark lists after a ref was processed.

nodes.name: count_reflog_ent
nodes.summary: Callback that counts reflog entries newer than the expiry time to turn ref@{N} into a recno.

nodes.name: reflog_delete
nodes.summary: Deletes the reflog entry named by ref@{N} or ref@{date} by counting entries and running refs_reflog_expire with a recno based policy.

nodes.name: reflog.h
nodes.summary: Declares the reflog expiry types (expire options and policy callback data) and the callbacks used with refs_reflog_expire: should_expire_reflog_ent, prepare, cleanup, count and reflog_delete.

nodes.name: reflog_expire_entry_option
nodes.summary: Per-pattern reflog expiry times, linked in a list with a flexible pattern string.

nodes.name: reflog_expire_options
nodes.summary: Expiry options: per-pattern entries, stalefix, explicit flags, default and effective expire times and recno.

nodes.name: expire_reflog_policy_cb
nodes.summary: Callback data of the expiry policy: unreachable kind, mark list and limit, options, tip commits and dry-run flag.

nodes.name: refs.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the reference subsystem: resolving and reading refs, iterating refs and reflogs, atomic ref transactions, ref name validation, worktree-aware ref parsing, reflog expiry hooks, ref namespaces and the low-level ref iterator API that the files, packed and reftable backends implement.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents the contract of ref_transaction_* (queue updates, prepare, commit or abort) that gives atomic multi-ref updates across backends.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_error
nodes.summary: Error codes returned by transaction operations: generic, name conflict, create exists, nonexistent ref, incorrect old value, invalid new value, expected symref and case conflict.

nodes.name: log_refs_config
nodes.summary: Values of core.logAllRefUpdates controlling whether reflogs are created automatically.

nodes.name: reference_status
nodes.summary: Bit flags describing a ref in iteration callbacks: symbolic, packed, broken, bad name.

nodes.name: reference
nodes.summary: A reference passed to for_each_ref callbacks: name, symref target, object id, optional peeled id and status flags.

nodes.name: refs_for_each_flag
nodes.summary: Flags that change which refs a refs_for_each_* iteration includes (broken refs, root refs, per-worktree refs and so on).

nodes.name: refs_for_each_ref_options
nodes.summary: Options of a ref iteration: prefix, glob pattern, namespace, exclude patterns, prefix trimming and flags.

nodes.name: refs_optimize_opts
nodes.summary: Options of refs_optimize (pack and prune refs, auto mode).

nodes.name: ref_transaction_flag
nodes.summary: Flags of a ref transaction: initial creation of an empty ref store and allow partial failure.

nodes.name: ref_worktree_type
nodes.summary: Classifies a refname relative to worktrees: current, main, other or shared.

nodes.name: expire_reflog_flags
nodes.summary: Flags for reflog expiry: dry run, update the ref, rewrite the reflog.

nodes.name: ref_namespace_info
nodes.summary: Describes one special ref namespace (ref prefix or exact name, decoration type, and whether it was replaced).

nodes.name: ref_namespace
nodes.summary: Enum of the well-known ref namespaces: HEAD, branches, tags, remote refs, stash, replace, notes, prefetch, rewritten.

nodes.name: peel_iterated_oid
nodes.summary: Peels a ref object id to a non-tag object, using the peeled value stored by the backend when possible.

nodes.name: replay.c
