nodes.summary: Prints the line(s) for a ref, iterating over detailed server reports when present.

nodes.name: transport_summary_width
nodes.summary: Computes the column width for abbreviated old..new object ids.

nodes.name: transport_print_push_status
nodes.summary: Prints the full push report (up to date, ok, then rejected refs) and collects reject reason flags used for advice.

nodes.name: git_transport_push
nodes.summary: Vtable push_refs for the smart transport: translates flags to send_pack_args and calls send_pack (v0/v1 only), then closes the connection.

nodes.name: connect_git
nodes.summary: Vtable connect: opens the connection for the requested service and returns its fds.

nodes.name: disconnect_git
nodes.summary: Vtable disconnect: flushes, closes the connection and frees smart transport data.

nodes.name: transport_take_over
nodes.summary: Switches a helper-based transport to the builtin smart transport using the helper's process pipes.

nodes.name: protocol_allow_list
nodes.summary: Parses GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL once into a sorted list of allowed protocols.

nodes.name: parse_protocol_config
nodes.summary: Maps always, never and user config values to the allow enum.

nodes.name: get_protocol_config
nodes.summary: Finds the effective protocol.<type>.allow setting with built-in defaults (http, https, git, ssh always; ext never; others user-only).

nodes.name: is_transport_allowed
nodes.summary: Tells whether a protocol is allowed, honoring GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, config and whether the user typed the URL.

nodes.name: parse_transport_option
nodes.summary: Config helper that appends a value to a transport option list, or clears it on an empty value.

nodes.name: transport_check_allowed
nodes.summary: Dies if the protocol type is not allowed.

nodes.name: transport_get
nodes.summary: Creates a transport for a remote and URL: remote helper (foreign vcs, 'name::' or unknown scheme), bundle file, or builtin smart transport; sets default upload-pack and receive-pack and applies sideband URL config.

nodes.name: transport_get_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Returns the hash algorithm negotiated for the transport.

nodes.name: transport_set_option
nodes.summary: Applies an option to both the builtin options and the transport-specific set_option, combining their result codes.

nodes.name: transport_set_verbosity
nodes.summary: Sets verbosity and whether progress is shown.

nodes.name: die_with_unpushed_submodules
nodes.summary: Prints the list of submodule paths with unpushed changes and dies.

nodes.name: pre_push_hook_feed_stdin
nodes.summary: Feeds one 'local-ref local-oid remote-ref remote-oid' line per ref to the pre-push hook stdin, skipping refs that will not be pushed.

nodes.name: run_pre_push_hook
nodes.summary: Runs the pre-push hook with remote name and URL arguments and the ref lines on stdin.

nodes.name: transport_push
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a push: lists remote refs, matches local to remote refs, applies force-with-lease, runs pre-push hook and submodule checks, calls push_refs, prints status, sets upstream and updates tracking refs.

nodes.name: transport_get_remote_refs
nodes.summary: Lists remote refs once through the vtable and caches them on the transport.

nodes.name: transport_ls_refs_options_release
nodes.summary: Frees the ref prefixes and unborn head target of ls-refs options.

nodes.name: transport_fetch_refs
nodes.summary: Selects the refs that differ from local ones and passes them to the transport's fetch_refs.

nodes.name: transport_get_remote_bundle_uri
nodes.summary: Asks the server for bundle URIs once when transfer.bundleURI is enabled.

nodes.name: transport_unlock_pack
nodes.summary: Removes pack lock files created during fetch, in a way that is also safe in a signal handler.

nodes.name: transport_connect
nodes.summary: Opens a raw service connection through the transport's connect callback.

nodes.name: transport_disconnect
nodes.summary: Calls the transport's disconnect, frees cached refs and bundle list and frees the transport.

nodes.name: transport_anonymize_url
nodes.summary: Strips the user name and password from a URL, leaving local paths and ambiguous forms unchanged.

nodes.name: git_transport_data
nodes.summary: Per-transport state for the builtin smart transport: options, connection, fds, protocol version, extra haves and shallow list.

nodes.name: git_transport_options
nodes.summary: Options of the smart transport: thin pack, depth, deepen-since/not, filter options, negotiation tips, receivepack and uploadpack paths and result flags.

nodes.name: transport_family
nodes.summary: Selects any, IPv4 or IPv6 for connections.

nodes.name: transport
nodes.summary: A connection to a remote: remote, URL, vtable, data pointer, cached refs, verbosity, progress, bundle list and pack lock files.

nodes.name: transport_ls_refs_options
nodes.summary: Options for listing remote refs: ref prefixes and unborn HEAD handling.

nodes.name: upload_pack_data
nodes.summary: Per-request state: wants, haves, shallow and deepen settings, sideband and multi_ack mode, filter options, hidden refs and v0/v2 flags.

nodes.name: output_state
nodes.summary: Buffer and flags used while relaying pack-objects output to the client.

nodes.name: upload_pack_data_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the request state with empty collections and defaults.

nodes.name: upload_pack_data_clear
nodes.summary: Releases every collection held by the request state.

nodes.name: send_client_data
nodes.summary: Sends data either through side-band or directly to stdout or stderr.

nodes.name: relay_pack_data
nodes.summary: Reads pack-objects output, handles packfile-uris preamble lines, and forwards buffered pack data, keeping one byte back so a failure can corrupt the stream.

nodes.name: create_pack_file
nodes.summary: Starts the pack generator for the wants and haves (with shallow, filter and thin options) and polls its output and progress, relaying to the client with keepalives and aborting on failure.

nodes.name: do_got_oid
nodes.summary: Records a 'have' object: tracks the oldest commit date, flags parents as THEY_HAVE and adds the object to the common list.

nodes.name: got_oid
nodes.summary: Parses a 'have' hex id and records it if the object exists locally, else returns -1.

nodes.name: ok_to_give_up
nodes.summary: Returns whether all wants are reachable from the common commits (so the server may stop negotiating).

nodes.name: get_common_commits
nodes.summary: v0/v1 negotiation loop: reads 'have' lines, answers ACK common/continue/ready or NAK, and returns when the client says done.

nodes.name: allow_hidden_refs
nodes.summary: Returns whether hidden refs need to be visited given allow-tip, allow-reachable and allow-any settings.

nodes.name: for_each_namespaced_ref_1
nodes.summary: Iterates refs within the git namespace, excluding hidden refs unless they must be marked.

nodes.name: is_our_ref
nodes.summary: Tells whether an object counts as an advertised (our) ref under the current policy.

nodes.name: do_reachable_revlist
nodes.summary: Starts 'git rev-list --stdin' with our refs as negative and the requested objects as positive to see what is reachable.

nodes.name: has_unreachable
nodes.summary: Returns true if any wanted object is not reachable from advertised refs, based on rev-list output.

nodes.name: check_non_tip
nodes.summary: Validates wants that are not ref tips (allowed with allowReachableSHA1InWant or stateless RPC) and dies with 'not our ref' otherwise.

nodes.name: send_shallow
nodes.summary: Sends 'shallow <oid>' for new border commits and registers them locally.

nodes.name: send_unshallow
nodes.summary: Sends 'unshallow' for client shallow commits that are now deepened, adding their parents to the wants.

nodes.name: deepen
nodes.summary: Handles a --depth request: computes shallow commits and sends shallow and unshallow lines.

nodes.name: deepen_by_rev_list
nodes.summary: Handles deepen-since and deepen-not requests through a rev-list based shallow computation.

nodes.name: send_shallow_list
nodes.summary: Dispatches on depth or rev-list style deepening, registers the client's shallows otherwise, and returns whether shallow info was sent.

nodes.name: process_shallow
nodes.summary: Parses a client 'shallow <oid>' line into the shallow object list.

nodes.name: process_deepen
nodes.summary: Parses 'deepen <n>' with validation.

nodes.name: process_deepen_since
nodes.summary: Parses 'deepen-since <time>' and switches to rev-list deepening.

nodes.name: process_deepen_not
nodes.summary: Resolves 'deepen-not <ref>' to an object id, rejecting ambiguous or missing refs.

nodes.name: send_err_and_die
nodes.summary: Sends an ERR packet to the client with the message and dies with it.

nodes.name: check_one_filter
nodes.summary: Checks one list-objects filter against uploadpackfilter.<name>.allow and tree max depth settings.

nodes.name: check_filter_recurse
nodes.summary: Checks a filter and recursively each sub-filter of a combine filter.

nodes.name: receive_needs
nodes.summary: Reads 'want' lines of the v0/v1 request along with client capabilities (side-band, no-progress, filter, session-id) and shallow/deepen lines.

nodes.name: mark_our_ref
nodes.summary: Marks an advertised ref's object as OUR_REF or HIDDEN_REF.

nodes.name: write_v0_ref
nodes.summary: Writes one advertised ref in v0 format; the first line carries capabilities, followed by the peeled tag line when applicable.

nodes.name: find_symref
nodes.summary: Collects symbolic refs for the symref capability.

nodes.name: parse_object_filter_config
nodes.summary: Parses uploadpackfilter.* config into allowed filters and tree depth limit.

nodes.name: upload_pack_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for uploadpack.* settings (allowTipSHA1InWant, allowFilter, keepalive, allowRefInWant...).

nodes.name: upload_pack_protected_config
nodes.summary: Reads uploadpack.packObjectsHook from protected config only.

nodes.name: get_upload_pack_config
nodes.summary: Loads regular and protected upload-pack configuration into the request state.

nodes.name: upload_pack
nodes.summary: v0/v1 entry point: advertises refs, reads wants, negotiates common commits and creates the pack.

nodes.name: parse_want
nodes.summary: Parses a v2 'want <oid>' line.

nodes.name: parse_want_ref
nodes.summary: Parses a v2 'want-ref <name>', resolving the ref and recording it in wanted-refs.

nodes.name: parse_have
nodes.summary: Parses a v2 'have <oid>' line.

nodes.name: trace2_fetch_info
nodes.summary: Emits a fetch-info trace2 event summarizing haves, wants, depth and filter.

nodes.name: process_args
nodes.summary: Parses the argument section of a v2 fetch request: wants, haves, thin-pack, ofs-delta, shallow, deepen, filter, sideband-all and packfile-uris.

nodes.name: send_acks
nodes.summary: Writes the acknowledgments section with ACK lines or NAK, and 'ready' when enough is known.

nodes.name: process_haves_and_send_acks
nodes.summary: Chooses between sending a pack or continuing negotiation based on done and ready.

nodes.name: send_wanted_ref_info
nodes.summary: Sends the wanted-refs section for resolved want-ref requests.

nodes.name: send_shallow_info
nodes.summary: Sends the shallow-info section.

nodes.name: upload_pack_v2
nodes.summary: Protocol v2 fetch command: a state machine of process arguments, send acknowledgments and send pack.

nodes.name: upload_pack_advertise
nodes.summary: Builds the fetch capability value (shallow, wait-for-done, filter, ref-in-want, sideband-all, packfile-uris) from config.

nodes.name: url_scheme
nodes.summary: Known URL schemes: unknown, local, file, ssh and git.

nodes.name: urlmatch.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct url_info and the URL normalization and matching API used for per-URL config such as http.<url>.* and sideband.<url>.*.

nodes.name: version.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Git version strings, the user-agent string builders and a uname-based system information helper.

nodes.name: walker.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct walker, the abstraction used by dumb-protocol fetchers (http walker) to prefetch and fetch objects and refs.

nodes.name: write-or-die.c
nodes.summary: Small wrappers around write, fwrite, fflush and fsync that die with a clear message on failure, plus fsync policy handling via core.fsync components and GIT_TEST_FSYNC.

nodes.name: write-or-die.h
nodes.summary: Declares the write-or-die helpers and the fsync_component and fsync_method enums with the default component masks used for durability settings.

nodes.name: maybe_flush_or_die
nodes.summary: Flushes a stream unless it is stdout redirected to a regular file, dying on error.

nodes.name: fprintf_or_die
nodes.summary: vfprintf that dies on error.

nodes.name: maybe_fsync
nodes.summary: Performs fsync unless disabled, using writeout-only when configured and otherwise a hardware flush.

nodes.name: fsync_or_die
nodes.summary: fsyncs a descriptor and dies on error.

nodes.name: fsync_component
nodes.summary: Syncs a file only if its component is enabled in core.fsync.

nodes.name: fsync_component_or_die
nodes.summary: fsync_component that dies on failure.

nodes.name: write_or_die
nodes.summary: Writes the full buffer to a descriptor, dying on error and treating a broken pipe quietly.

nodes.name: writev_or_die
nodes.summary: Gathered write that dies on failure.

nodes.name: fwrite_or_die
nodes.summary: fwrite that dies on a short write.

nodes.name: fflush_or_die
nodes.summary: fflush that dies on error.

nodes.name: fsync_component
nodes.summary: Bit flags naming what can be fsynced: loose objects, packs, pack metadata, commit-graph, index, refs, object map.

nodes.name: fsync_method
nodes.summary: Fsync strategies: plain fsync, writeout-only, or batch.

nodes.name: url_info
nodes.summary: A normalized URL with offsets and lengths of its scheme, user, password, host, port and path.

nodes.name: urlmatch_config
nodes.summary: State for matching config sections like http.<url>.* with callbacks to select the best match.

nodes.name: walker
nodes.summary: Dumb-protocol fetch driver with callbacks for fetching refs, prefetching and fetching objects.

nodes.name: base85.c
nodes.summary: Implements Git base85 coding used by binary patches: decode_85 turns base85 text back into bytes and chunk_and_encode85 splits data into 52-byte chunks, each emitted as one length-prefixed text line through a callback.

nodes.name: decode_85
nodes.summary: Decodes base85 text into raw bytes five characters per four bytes, using a lazily built reverse alphabet table, and rejects characters outside the alphabet or groups that overflow 32 bits.

nodes.name: encode_85
nodes.summary: Encodes up to 52 bytes of data into base85 groups of five characters by repeated division by 85 and NUL-terminates the output.

nodes.name: chunk_and_encode85
nodes.summary: Splits data into chunks of at most 52 bytes, encodes each with a one-letter length prefix (A-Z, a-z) and a trailing newline, and hands every line to the output callback.

nodes.name: base85.h
nodes.summary: Declares the base85 codec API: BASE85_CHUNK_SIZE, the each_encoded_line_fn callback type, decode_85 and chunk_and_encode85, used by diff (emit) and apply (parse) for binary patches.

nodes.name: diff.c
nodes.summary: Core of the diff machinery: holds the diff_options setup and option parsing, the queue of diff_filepair entries, the filespec loader, and every output format (patch, raw, stat, numstat, dirstat, word diff, color-moved, binary, check, patch-id), plus the diffcore pipeline driver diffcore_std and diff_flush.

nodes.name: diff_tempfile
nodes.summary: Describes a file handed to an external diff or textconv program: name (or /dev/null), hex id, mode and the tempfile object that controls its lifetime.

nodes.name: emit_callback
nodes.summary: State shared by the xdiff output callbacks: color and whitespace flags, line numbers, labels, word-diff data and the pending header.

nodes.name: line_range_callback
nodes.summary: State of the -L line-range filter that wraps xdiff output, tracking pre and post image line numbers and buffering range hunks and pending removals.

nodes.name: emitted_diff_symbol
nodes.summary: One buffered output line with its symbol kind, flags, indentation data and interned id, kept so moved-line coloring can run after the whole diff is produced.

nodes.name: moved_entry
nodes.summary: Node of the moved-code detection lists linking an emitted symbol to the next line in its block and the next identical line elsewhere.

nodes.name: diff_words_data
nodes.summary: State of --word-diff: the buffered removed and added text, current positions, word regex and output style.

nodes.name: parse_dirstat_params
nodes.summary: Parses the comma separated --dirstat argument (changes, lines, files, cumulative, percentage) into diff flags and the permille threshold, reporting errors in a buffer.

nodes.name: git_config_rename
nodes.summary: Maps a rename config value to DIFF_DETECT_RENAME, DIFF_DETECT_COPY or off.

nodes.name: parse_algorithm_value
nodes.summary: Translates myers, minimal, patience or histogram into the xdiff algorithm flag, or -1 for an unknown name.

nodes.name: parse_color_moved
nodes.summary: Parses a color-moved mode (no, plain, blocks, zebra, dimmed-zebra or a boolean) into its constant.

nodes.name: git_diff_ui_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for porcelain diff output: reads diff.color, colorMoved, context, interHunkContext, algorithm, wordRegex and other UI settings, then defers to the color and basic config handlers.

nodes.name: git_diff_basic_config
nodes.summary: Config callback shared by plumbing and porcelain: diff.renameLimit, userdiff driver settings and diff.color slot values.

nodes.name: emit_line_0
nodes.summary: Writes one output line with the line prefix, sign, color set and reset, handling a trailing CR and newline so color codes never end up after the newline.

nodes.name: append_emitted_diff_symbol
nodes.summary: Copies an emitted symbol (with a duplicate of its text) into the buffer used for deferred output.

nodes.name: add_lines_to_move_detection
nodes.summary: Interns each added or removed line in a hashmap (with optional whitespace-insensitive hashing) and builds per-line add and delete lists plus next-line links for moved-block detection.

nodes.name: pmb_advance_or_null
nodes.summary: Advances each potential moved block to the next line of its candidate and drops blocks whose next line no longer matches the current line.

nodes.name: fill_potential_moved_blocks
nodes.summary: Seeds the set of candidate moved blocks from every earlier identical line when a new block starts, computing the whitespace delta where indentation changes are allowed.

nodes.name: adjust_last_block
nodes.summary: Rejects a moved block that has too few alphanumeric characters and clears its moved flags.

nodes.name: mark_color_as_moved
nodes.summary: Scans buffered plus and minus lines and marks runs that appear as the same contiguous block on the opposite side as moved, alternating zebra colors.

nodes.name: dim_moved_lines
nodes.summary: Marks moved lines at the edges of blocks as interesting and the interior as uninteresting for the dimmed color-moved modes.

nodes.name: emit_line_ws_markup
nodes.summary: Emits a diff line with whitespace error highlighting, deciding between plain and ws-checked output for the given sign and rule.

nodes.name: emit_diff_symbol_from_struct
nodes.summary: Central printer that renders one diff symbol (header, hunk marker, context, plus, minus, stat line, submodule note, binary body and more) with the proper colors and prefixes.

nodes.name: emit_diff_symbol
nodes.summary: Either buffers a symbol for later color-moved processing or prints it immediately.

nodes.name: diff_emit_submodule_header
nodes.summary: Emits a submodule summary header line through the symbol printer.

nodes.name: emit_hunk_header
nodes.summary: Reformats an xdiff hunk header, coloring the @@ ranges and the function context and keeping the line prefix.

nodes.name: emit_rewrite_lines
nodes.summary: Emits whole-file removed or added lines with a prefix for a complete rewrite, buffering data for the line-by-line output.

nodes.name: emit_rewrite_diff
nodes.summary: Produces the patch for a complete rewrite (break -B) as a full removal of the old content and addition of the new content under a single hunk.

nodes.name: fn_out_diff_words_write_helper
nodes.summary: Writes a run of words with the style prefix, color and suffix, re-emitting the line prefix after each newline.

nodes.name: fn_out_diff_words_aux
nodes.summary: Callback of the word-level xdiff that prints common words, then removed and added word ranges using the chosen word-diff style.

nodes.name: find_word_boundaries
nodes.summary: Uses the word regex to find the next word in a buffer and returns its begin and end, skipping newlines.

nodes.name: diff_words_fill
nodes.summary: Splits a buffer into words (by regex or whitespace) and writes them one per line into a new buffer, recording original offsets.

nodes.name: diff_words_show
nodes.summary: Runs a word-level xdiff between the accumulated removed and added text and prints the result in the chosen style.

nodes.name: diff_words_flush
nodes.summary: Flushes pending word-diff buffers when a hunk ends and forwards any buffered symbols to the original output.

nodes.name: init_diff_words_data
nodes.summary: Copies the diff options for word diff, loads the word regex from options or userdiff driver and sets up the style colors.

nodes.name: diff_get_color
nodes.summary: Returns the ANSI color string for a diff color slot when color is enabled, otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: diff_line_prefix
nodes.summary: Returns the per-line output prefix produced by the options callback (used by graph output) or an empty string.

nodes.name: fn_out_consume
nodes.summary: Main xdiff line callback: emits the pending file header and ---/+++ labels, handles hunk headers, word-diff buffering and plus, minus, context and incomplete-line markers.

nodes.name: flush_rhunk
nodes.summary: Emits the accumulated range hunk of a -L filter with a synthetic @@ header, including pending removals that proved to be in range.

nodes.name: line_range_hunk_fn
nodes.summary: Hunk callback of the line-range wrapper that records the hunk start positions and function name.

nodes.name: line_range_line_fn
nodes.summary: Line callback of the line-range wrapper that tracks post-image positions, buffers removals and forwards only lines inside the requested ranges.

nodes.name: pprint_rename
nodes.summary: Formats a rename pair for diffstat as prefix, braced differing middle and common suffix, quoting names when needed.

nodes.name: diffstat_add
nodes.summary: Allocates and appends a diffstat_file entry for a changed path pair.

nodes.name: show_stats
nodes.summary: Computes name, number and graph column widths from the terminal width and prints the --stat table with scaled plus and minus bars and the summary line.

nodes.name: show_shortstats
nodes.summary: Prints the one-line summary of files changed, insertions and deletions.

nodes.name: show_numstat
nodes.summary: Prints machine readable per-file added and deleted counts (dashes for binary files).

nodes.name: gather_dirstat
nodes.summary: Recursively sums changes of sorted file entries per directory and prints directories above the permille threshold.

nodes.name: show_dirstat
nodes.summary: Computes per-file change amounts (by file, line or byte damage) for the queued pairs and prints a directory distribution of the changes.

nodes.name: show_dirstat_by_line
nodes.summary: Prints dirstat from line-based diffstat data when dirstat-by-line is selected.

nodes.name: checkdiff_consume
nodes.summary: xdiff callback for --check that flags added lines with whitespace errors and leftover conflict markers.

nodes.name: deflate_it
nodes.summary: Compresses a buffer with zlib using the configured compression level and returns the allocated result.

nodes.name: emit_binary_diff_body
nodes.summary: Chooses the smaller of a deflated literal or deflated delta for a binary diff and emits it as base85 lines via chunk_and_encode85.

nodes.name: diff_filespec_is_binary
nodes.summary: Decides whether a file is binary from the userdiff driver setting or by loading content and scanning it, caching the result.

nodes.name: diff_set_mnemonic_prefix
nodes.summary: Sets default a/ and b/ style prefixes if the user has not set them.

nodes.name: builtin_diff
nodes.summary: Generates the textual patch for one file pair: header lines (new, deleted, mode), submodule summary, binary handling, textconv, whitespace options and the call into xdiff with all output callbacks.

nodes.name: get_compact_summary
nodes.summary: Returns the short mode and type change annotation used by --compact-summary.

nodes.name: builtin_diffstat
nodes.summary: Computes insertion and deletion counts for one file pair by running xdiff with a counting callback, recording binary files and rewrites.

nodes.name: builtin_checkdiff
nodes.summary: Runs xdiff on one pair with checkdiff_consume to report whitespace errors and conflict markers.

nodes.name: alloc_filespec
nodes.summary: Allocates a reference-counted diff_filespec for a path with unknown mode and object id.

nodes.name: free_filespec
nodes.summary: Drops a reference and frees the filespec and its data when the count reaches zero.

nodes.name: fill_filespec
nodes.summary: Fills a filespec with canonical mode and object id when a mode is given.

nodes.name: reuse_worktree_file
nodes.summary: Decides whether a work tree file can stand in for the blob with a given object id by checking the index entry and stat data, avoiding a read of the object database.

nodes.name: diff_populate_gitlink
nodes.summary: Fills a filespec for a submodule entry with a "Subproject commit" line.

nodes.name: diff_populate_filespec
nodes.summary: Loads the content or size of a filespec from the work tree (applying clean filters and conversions) or from the object database, with optional binary check and promisor prefetch hook.

nodes.name: diff_free_filespec_blob
nodes.summary: Releases the loaded blob data, either freeing or unmapping it.

nodes.name: diff_free_filespec_data
nodes.summary: Releases loaded data and the cached change-count data of a filespec.

nodes.name: prep_temp_blob
nodes.summary: Writes blob contents (after conversion) into a temporary file whose name keeps the original base name, for external programs.

nodes.name: prepare_temp_file
nodes.summary: Chooses what an external diff will read for a side: /dev/null, the work tree file, a symlink target text or a temp blob, and fills hex id and mode.

nodes.name: run_external_diff
nodes.summary: Runs the configured external diff program with the old and new files and metadata as arguments and handles its exit status.

nodes.name: diff_abbrev_oid
nodes.summary: Abbreviates an object id to the requested length, working out the shortest unique form when needed.

nodes.name: fill_metainfo
nodes.summary: Builds the extended header lines (similarity, rename or copy from and to, dissimilarity, index and mode lines) for a file pair.

nodes.name: run_diff_cmd
nodes.summary: Chooses between a userdiff external driver, a global external diff or the builtin diff for a pair and runs it after building header text.

nodes.name: run_diff
nodes.summary: Per-pair patch driver: normalizes the names and prefix, handles unmerged and unchanged pairs and calls run_diff_cmd.

nodes.name: run_diffstat
nodes.summary: Per-pair diffstat driver that calls builtin_diffstat for a pair.

nodes.name: run_checkdiff
nodes.summary: Per-pair check driver that calls builtin_checkdiff for a pair.

nodes.name: repo_diff_setup
nodes.summary: Initializes diff_options from defaults and config (colors, rename detection, algorithm, prefixes, color-moved) for a repository.

nodes.name: diff_check_follow_pathspec
nodes.summary: Validates that --follow is used with exactly one literal pathspec.

nodes.name: diff_setup_done
nodes.summary: Finalizes options after parsing: checks for incompatible option combinations, derives implicit flags and settings, and prepares output.

nodes.name: parse_long_opt
nodes.summary: Matches a --name=value or --name value argument and returns the value.

nodes.name: diff_opt_stat
nodes.summary: Option callback for --stat and its width, name-width, graph-width and count variants.

nodes.name: diff_opt_diff_filter
nodes.summary: Option callback for --diff-filter that turns status letters, upper or lower case, into include and exclude bit masks.

nodes.name: add_diff_options
nodes.summary: Builds the parse-options table of all diff output, rename, whitespace, algorithm and pickaxe options bound to a diff_options struct.

nodes.name: diff_opt_parse
nodes.summary: Parses one diff option from argv for callers that handle their own option loops.

nodes.name: parse_rename_score
nodes.summary: Parses a similarity percentage such as 50 or 50% or .5 into the internal MAX_SCORE based value.

nodes.name: diff_q
nodes.summary: Appends a filepair to a diff queue, growing the array.

nodes.name: diff_queue
nodes.summary: Allocates a filepair for two filespecs and optionally queues it.

nodes.name: diff_free_filepair
nodes.summary: Releases both filespecs and the filepair.

nodes.name: diff_queue_init
nodes.summary: Resets a diff queue to the empty state.

nodes.name: diff_queue_clear
nodes.summary: Frees every queued filepair and the queue array.

nodes.name: diff_aligned_abbrev
nodes.summary: Returns an abbreviated object id padded or ellipsized to a fixed width for raw output.

nodes.name: diff_flush_raw
nodes.summary: Prints one pair in raw format (modes, abbreviated ids, status letter, score and path or paths).

nodes.name: diff_unmodified_pair
nodes.summary: Returns whether a pair has identical mode, type and object id so it carries no change.

nodes.name: diff_flush_patch
nodes.summary: Emits the patch for one pair unless it is unmodified, handling pairs that exist only to carry conflict headers.

nodes.name: diff_queue_is_empty
nodes.summary: Returns whether the queue has no real changes, treating header-only entries and filters correctly.

nodes.name: diff_debug_queue
nodes.summary: Dumps the whole diff queue to stderr for debugging.

nodes.name: diff_resolve_rename_copy
nodes.summary: Assigns the final status letter (added, deleted, modified, renamed, copied, type changed) to each queued pair and resolves which rename destinations are renames or copies.

nodes.name: flush_one_pair
nodes.summary: Dispatches a pair to the raw, name, name-status or check output depending on output format.

nodes.name: diff_summary
nodes.summary: Prints the --summary line for a pair: create, delete, rename, copy and mode change lines.

nodes.name: flush_one_hunk
nodes.summary: Finishes the current hunk hash and adds it into the running patch-id sum with carry.

nodes.name: patch_id_consume
nodes.summary: xdiff callback that hashes each diff line after whitespace removal for patch-id.

nodes.name: diff_get_patch_id
nodes.summary: Computes a stable patch id by hashing the whitespace-stripped diff of each file pair and summing hunk hashes.

nodes.name: diff_flush_patch_id
nodes.summary: Computes the patch id of the queued diff and then clears the queue.

nodes.name: diff_warn_rename_limit
nodes.summary: Prints the warning that rename detection was skipped or degraded and the rename limit that would be needed.

nodes.name: create_filepairs_for_header_only_notifications
nodes.summary: Adds placeholder pairs for paths that have extra headers (such as remerge conflicts) but no diff entry so the header is still printed.

nodes.name: diff_flush_patch_all_file_pairs
nodes.summary: Prints patches for all queued pairs, buffering output first when color-moved is on and then marking moved blocks before the final print.

nodes.name: diff_free
nodes.summary: Releases the resources owned by diff_options: object set, order file, anchors, output file, ignore regexes and pathspec.

nodes.name: diff_flush
nodes.summary: Final output stage: prints the queue in the selected formats in order (raw or name, stat, summary, patch), then frees the queue.

nodes.name: diffcore_apply_filter
nodes.summary: Applies --diff-filter status letters to the queue, keeping or removing pairs and handling the all-or-none mode.

nodes.name: diff_filespec_check_stat_unmatch
nodes.summary: Decides whether a pair differs by comparing sizes and, if needed, contents, to implement skip-stat-unmatch.

nodes.name: diffcore_skip_stat_unmatch
nodes.summary: Removes pairs whose content is identical despite differing stat data from the queue.

nodes.name: diff_add_if_missing
nodes.summary: Appends the blob id of a filespec to a list when the object is not available locally (partial clone).

nodes.name: diff_queued_diff_prefetch
nodes.summary: Collects missing blobs of all queued pairs and fetches them in one batch from the promisor remote.

nodes.name: diffcore_std
nodes.summary: Runs the standard diffcore pipeline on the queue: skip-stat-unmatch, break, rename and copy detection, merge broken, pickaxe, ordering, rotate, status resolution and filter.

nodes.name: diff_result_code
nodes.summary: Computes the process exit status (--exit-code, --check) and warns about rename limits.

nodes.name: diff_can_quit_early
nodes.summary: Tells whether quick mode can stop after the first change.

nodes.name: compute_diffstat
nodes.summary: Builds a diffstat for all queued pairs without printing.

nodes.name: diff_queue_addremove
nodes.summary: Queues an addition or removal filepair for a path, handling reverse diff, prefix filtering and submodule ignore rules.

nodes.name: diff_queue_change
nodes.summary: Queues a modification filepair with old and new mode and object id, honouring reverse diff and prefix filters.

nodes.name: diff_addremove
nodes.summary: Adds an addition or removal to the global diff queue.

nodes.name: diff_change
nodes.summary: Adds a change to the global diff queue.

nodes.name: diff_same
nodes.summary: Adds an unchanged entry so copy detection can use it as a source.

nodes.name: diff_unmerge
nodes.summary: Queues an unmerged pair for a path.

nodes.name: run_textconv
nodes.summary: Runs a textconv program on a temp file of the blob and returns its output as the text to diff.

nodes.name: fill_textconv
nodes.summary: Returns the contents to diff for a filespec, running the textconv driver (with a notes-based cache) when one applies, otherwise the raw blob.

nodes.name: textconv_object
nodes.summary: Applies the textconv driver for a path to an object id and returns the converted text, used by blame and cat-file.

nodes.name: setup_diff_pager
nodes.summary: Starts the pager for diff output unless exit-status or quiet mode is requested.

nodes.name: init_diff_ui_defaults
nodes.summary: Sets the default rename detection mode of the diff UI.

nodes.name: git_diff_heuristic_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads diff.indentHeuristic.

nodes.name: diff_set_noprefix
nodes.summary: Clears source and destination prefixes for --no-prefix.

nodes.name: diff_set_default_prefix
nodes.summary: Sets the standard a/ and b/ prefixes.

nodes.name: get_textconv
nodes.summary: Returns the textconv driver for a filespec via its userdiff driver, or NULL for invalid files.

nodes.name: diff_filter_bit
nodes.summary: Returns the filter bit for a status letter.

nodes.name: print_stat_summary
nodes.summary: Prints the "N files changed, M insertions, K deletions" summary for given totals.

nodes.name: free_diffstat_info
nodes.summary: Frees all diffstat file entries and the array.

nodes.name: init_diffstat_widths
nodes.summary: Initializes stat width options to use terminal width and configured widths.

nodes.name: diffcore_fix_diff_index
nodes.summary: Sorts the queue by name so diff-index output order is stable.

nodes.name: diff_emit_submodule_add
nodes.summary: Emits a submodule addition line through the symbol printer.

nodes.name: diff_emit_submodule_del
nodes.summary: Emits a submodule deletion line through the symbol printer.

nodes.name: diff_debug_filepair
nodes.summary: Dumps one filepair for debugging.

nodes.name: diff_debug_filespec
nodes.summary: Dumps one filespec for debugging.

nodes.name: diffcore-rename.c
nodes.summary: Implements rename and copy detection for the diffcore pipeline: exact matching by blob hash, basename and directory-rename heuristics, then an inexact similarity matrix scored with delta-based change counting.

nodes.name: diff_rename_dst
nodes.summary: Table entry for a rename or copy destination: the filepair, the filespec to free later and an is_rename flag set once a source has been matched.

nodes.name: diff_rename_src
nodes.summary: Table entry for a possible rename source: the filepair and the break score remembered from break detection.

nodes.name: diff_score
nodes.summary: One cell of the similarity matrix: source index, destination index, content similarity score and a basename-match score used to break ties.

nodes.name: file_similarity
nodes.summary: Hashmap entry linking a filespec and its index so identical blobs can be found by object-id hash during exact rename detection.

nodes.name: dir_rename_info
nodes.summary: Bookkeeping for directory-rename heuristics: mapping from file name to destination index, per-directory counts of where files went, and the best guess destination directory.

nodes.name: register_rename_src
nodes.summary: Appends a filepair to the rename source table and, for a broken pair, records its path in break_idx so the matching destination can be located later.

nodes.name: basename_same
nodes.summary: Walks both paths backwards and returns whether they end in the same file name component after the last slash.

nodes.name: inexact_prefetch
nodes.summary: Missing-object callback that collects blobs needed by the inexact matrix and prefetches them in one batch from the promisor remote (partial clone).

nodes.name: estimate_similarity
nodes.summary: Scores how similar a source and destination blob are on a 0 to MAX_SCORE scale: skips non-regular files, rejects pairs whose sizes differ too much, then uses diffcore_count_changes to count copied bytes.

nodes.name: record_rename_pair
nodes.summary: Records a match by pointing the destination filepair at the source filespec, marks it renamed, bumps the source use count and stores the score.

nodes.name: score_compare
nodes.summary: qsort comparator that orders similarity matrix entries by descending score, using the basename score to break ties and sinking unused entries to the end.

nodes.name: hash_filespec
nodes.summary: Returns a hash for a filespec, computing the blob object id from its contents first when it is not yet known.

nodes.name: find_identical_files
nodes.summary: For one destination finds the best source with the same object id from a hashmap, preferring unused sources and same basenames, and records it as a 100 percent rename.

nodes.name: insert_file_table
nodes.summary: Allocates a file_similarity entry from the mem_pool and inserts it into the hash table keyed by the blob hash.

nodes.name: find_exact_renames
nodes.summary: First rename pass: hashes all sources into a table (in reverse order) and matches each destination against identical blobs.

nodes.name: get_highest_rename_path
nodes.summary: Iterates a strintmap of destination directories and returns the one with the highest count.

nodes.name: dir_rename_already_determinable
nodes.summary: Returns true when the leading destination directory count exceeds the runner-up plus the unknown count, so more renames cannot change the majority result.

nodes.name: increment_count
nodes.summary: Increments the count of files moved from old_dir to new_dir in the nested strmap of strintmaps, creating the inner map on demand.

nodes.name: update_dir_rename_counts
nodes.summary: For one detected file rename walks up the parent directories while trailing components match and increments old-dir to new-dir counters, restricted to relevant directories.

nodes.name: initialize_dir_rename_info
nodes.summary: Builds dir_rename_info: maps unrenamed destination files to indices, counts directory pairs from known renames and cached pairs, then collapses counts into a best-guess destination per directory.

nodes.name: partial_clear_dir_rename_count
nodes.summary: Clears the inner count maps and entries of a dir_rename_count strmap while keeping the outer map for reuse.

nodes.name: cleanup_dir_rename_info
nodes.summary: Frees the idx_map, guesses and, unless the caller wants to keep them, the count maps, and prunes irrelevant source directories from dirs_removed.

nodes.name: idx_possible_rename
nodes.summary: Uses the guessed destination directory of a removed directory to look up the destination file with the same basename, for filenames that are not unique among sources or destinations.

nodes.name: basename_prefetch
nodes.summary: Mirrors the basename matching loop to collect the blobs it will compare and prefetch them from the promisor remote in one request.

nodes.name: find_basename_matches
nodes.summary: Second rename pass: pairs sources and destinations that share a unique basename (or a directory-rename guess), scores them and records matches above a raised minimum score before the full matrix runs.

nodes.name: record_if_better
nodes.summary: Keeps the best NUM_CANDIDATE_PER_DST candidates for a destination by replacing the worst entry when a new score ranks higher.

nodes.name: too_many_rename_candidates
nodes.summary: Checks the destinations times sources matrix against rename_limit squared and says whether to skip inexact detection or to degrade -C -C to -C.

nodes.name: find_renames
nodes.summary: Walks the sorted similarity matrix from best score down and records each pair above the minimum score whose destination (and, for renames, source) is still unused.

nodes.name: remove_unneeded_paths_from_src
nodes.summary: Compacts the rename source table by dropping sources already used by a rename or not in the set of interesting paths, shrinking the inner loop of the matrix.

nodes.name: handle_early_known_dir_renames
nodes.summary: Counts potential renames per removed directory and drops sources whose directory rename is already decided by majority, so fewer file pairs are compared.

nodes.name: pool_free_filespec
nodes.summary: Frees a filespec either fully or, if it came from a mem_pool, only its data.

nodes.name: pool_diff_free_filepair
nodes.summary: Frees a filepair directly or, when allocated from a pool, only the data of both of its filespecs.

nodes.name: diffcore_rename_extended
nodes.summary: Orchestrates rename and copy detection: collects sources and destinations from the diff queue, runs exact, basename and inexact passes with culling, then rewrites the queue with renamed pairs and frees temporary tables.

nodes.name: diffcore_rename
nodes.summary: Public entry that runs rename detection with no pool, relevant-source or directory-rename arguments.

nodes.name: hashmap.c
nodes.summary: Generic chained hash table with automatic grow and shrink (load factor 80 percent), FNV-1 string and memory hash functions with case-insensitive variants, and the memintern string pool built on top of it.

nodes.name: strhash
nodes.summary: FNV-1 32-bit hash of a NUL-terminated string.

nodes.name: strihash
nodes.summary: Case-insensitive FNV-1 hash of a string, upper-casing ASCII letters first.

nodes.name: memhash
nodes.summary: FNV-1 32-bit hash of a memory buffer.

nodes.name: memihash
nodes.summary: Case-insensitive FNV-1 hash of a memory buffer.

nodes.name: memihash_cont
nodes.summary: Continues a case-insensitive hash from a seed so data can be hashed in several chunks.

nodes.name: alloc_table
nodes.summary: Allocates the bucket array and computes the grow and shrink thresholds from the 80 percent load factor.

nodes.name: rehash
nodes.summary: Reallocates the table at a new size and relinks every chain entry into its new bucket.

nodes.name: find_entry_ptr
nodes.summary: Returns a pointer to the link that points at the matching entry in a bucket chain (or to the terminating NULL), used by get and remove.

nodes.name: hashmap_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a hashmap with a comparison callback, callback data and an optional expected size used to pick the initial table size.

nodes.name: free_individual_entries
nodes.summary: Frees every entry by iterating the map and subtracting the caller-supplied member offset from each entry pointer.

nodes.name: hashmap_partial_clear_
nodes.summary: Optionally frees entries and zeroes the bucket array but keeps the table allocated for reuse.

nodes.name: hashmap_clear_
nodes.summary: Optionally frees entries then releases the table itself and resets size counters.

nodes.name: hashmap_get
nodes.summary: Looks up the first entry equal to a key (hash plus cmp callback) and returns NULL if the table is empty or nothing matches.

nodes.name: hashmap_get_next
nodes.summary: Returns the next entry in the same chain that equals the given entry, to walk duplicates.

nodes.name: hashmap_add
nodes.summary: Pushes an entry at the head of its bucket chain and grows the table when the load factor threshold is exceeded.

nodes.name: hashmap_remove
nodes.summary: Unlinks and returns the entry matching a key, shrinking the table when the count falls under the shrink threshold.

nodes.name: hashmap_put
nodes.summary: Replaces an existing equal entry (returned to the caller) or inserts the new one.

nodes.name: hashmap_iter_init
nodes.summary: Resets an iterator to the start of a map.

nodes.name: hashmap_iter_next
nodes.summary: Advances the iterator through each bucket chain and returns the next entry or NULL at the end.

nodes.name: pool_entry
nodes.summary: Entry type of the interned string pool: a hashmap_entry, a length and the flexible data bytes.

nodes.name: pool_entry_cmp
nodes.summary: Comparison callback of the string pool that compares length and bytes of an entry against key data.

nodes.name: memintern
nodes.summary: Returns a unique pointer for a byte sequence from a static hashmap-based pool, creating the entry on first sight so equal data can be compared by pointer.

nodes.name: hashmap.h
nodes.summary: Public API and intrusive-entry design of the hashmap: struct hashmap_entry embedded in user structs, container_of-based macros for get, put, remove and iteration, and the hash function declarations.

nodes.name: hashmap_entry
nodes.summary: Intrusive entry embedded at the start of user structs: a next pointer for collision chaining and the cached hash code.

nodes.name: hashmap
nodes.summary: The hash table: bucket array, comparison function and data, item count, table size, and grow and shrink thresholds.

nodes.name: hashmap_iter
nodes.summary: Iterator state: the map, the current bucket position and the next entry in the chain.

nodes.name: mem-pool.c
nodes.summary: Arena-style memory pool: allocates large blocks and hands out aligned slices, supports strdup and printf-style formatting into the pool, merging pools, ownership checks and freeing everything at once.

nodes.name: mem_pool_alloc_block
nodes.summary: Allocates a new mp_block and links it at the head of the pool or after a given block, adding its size to the pool total.

nodes.name: mem_pool_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes a pool, sets the default block growth size (about 1 MiB) and optionally allocates a first block of the requested size.

nodes.name: mem_pool_discard
nodes.summary: Frees every block of the pool, optionally overwriting contents with 0xDD to catch use after free.

nodes.name: mem_pool_alloc
nodes.summary: Rounds a request up to maximum alignment, serves it from the current block when it fits, otherwise adds a dedicated block for large requests or a new standard block.

nodes.name: mem_pool_strvfmt
nodes.summary: Formats a string with vsnprintf directly into the pool free space when possible and otherwise allocates the exact size and formats again.

nodes.name: mem_pool_strfmt
nodes.summary: printf-style wrapper that formats a string into pool memory.

nodes.name: mem_pool_calloc
nodes.summary: Allocates count times size bytes from the pool with an overflow check and zero fills them.

nodes.name: mem_pool_strdup
nodes.summary: Copies a NUL-terminated string into pool memory.

nodes.name: mem_pool_strndup
nodes.summary: Copies at most len bytes of a string into the pool, stopping at an embedded NUL and terminating the copy.

nodes.name: mem_pool_contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether an address lies inside any block owned by the pool.

nodes.name: mem_pool_combine
nodes.summary: Moves all blocks of a source pool to the end of a destination pool and empties the source, so lifetimes can be merged.

nodes.name: mem-pool.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct mp_block and struct mem_pool and the pool API (init, discard, alloc, calloc, strdup, strfmt, combine, contains) used by diff, merge and rename code that wants cheap bulk allocation.

nodes.name: mp_block
nodes.summary: One block of pool memory: next block link, next free and end pointers and the flexible data area.

nodes.name: mem_pool
nodes.summary: Pool descriptor: head of the block list, bytes to grow by and total bytes allocated.

nodes.name: strmap.c
nodes.summary: String-keyed map, int map and string set built on the hashmap, optionally allocating entries from a mem_pool and optionally duplicating keys; used by rename detection and merge-ort.

nodes.name: cmp_strmap_entry
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback that compares two strmap entries by their key strings with strcmp.

nodes.name: find_strmap_entry
nodes.summary: Builds a key entry on the stack with the string hash and looks it up in the underlying hashmap.

nodes.name: strmap_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a strmap from the STRMAP_INIT blank value.

nodes.name: strmap_init_with_options
nodes.summary: Initializes a strmap with an optional mem_pool for entries and a flag controlling whether keys are duplicated.

nodes.name: strmap_free_entries_
nodes.summary: Iterates the map to free values and, when no pool owns the memory, the entries, since hashmap cannot free them itself.

nodes.name: strmap_clear
nodes.summary: Frees entries (and optionally values) and the underlying hashmap table.

nodes.name: strmap_partial_clear
nodes.summary: Frees entries and optionally values but keeps the table allocated for reuse.

nodes.name: create_entry
nodes.summary: Allocates an entry from the heap or the pool, copying the key into the entry tail when keys are duplicated, and sets hash, key and value.

nodes.name: strmap_put
nodes.summary: Inserts a key with data or replaces the value of an existing key and returns the old value.

nodes.name: strmap_get_entry
nodes.summary: Returns the entry for a key, or NULL, so a stored NULL value can be told from a missing key.

nodes.name: strmap_get
nodes.summary: Returns the value stored for a key or NULL.

nodes.name: strmap_contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether a key is present in the map.

nodes.name: strmap_remove
nodes.summary: Removes a key from the hashmap and frees the value and the entry when the map owns them.

nodes.name: strintmap_incr
nodes.summary: Adds an amount to an integer stored in the value slot, creating the entry from the default value plus the amount if the key is new.

nodes.name: strset_add
nodes.summary: Adds a string to a set and returns 1 if it was new, 0 if it was already present.

nodes.name: strmap.h
nodes.summary: Declares strmap, strintmap and strset types, their iteration macros and inline wrappers around the hashmap, including default-value handling for strintmap.

nodes.name: strmap
nodes.summary: String-to-pointer map: a hashmap, an optional mem_pool and a flag to duplicate keys.

nodes.name: strmap_entry
nodes.summary: Entry of a strmap: embedded hashmap_entry, key string and value pointer.

nodes.name: strintmap
nodes.summary: String-to-integer map layered on strmap that stores the integer in the value slot and a default value for missing keys.

nodes.name: strset
nodes.summary: String set layered on strmap with unused values.

nodes.name: xdiffi.c
nodes.summary: Core of xdiff's line diff engine: implements Myers' O(ND) divide-and-conquer algorithm (xdl_split/xdl_recs_cmp), dispatches to patience or histogram when requested, then compacts change groups with the indent heuristic, builds the edit script and drives hunk emission through xdl_diff.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses goto-based cleanup and caller-allocated K vectors indexed by diagonal, with negative diagonal offsets handled by shifting the base pointer.

nodes.name: xemit.c
nodes.summary: Turns an edit script into unified-diff output: groups changes into hunks with xdl_get_hunk, computes pre/post context (optionally extended to whole functions), finds function-name headers and emits the hunk header and +/-/space lines through the emit callback.

nodes.name: xhistogram.c
nodes.summary: Histogram diff algorithm: indexes occurrences of lines of the first file in a bounded-chain hash table, finds the longest common substring whose lines are rarest, and recurses on both sides, falling back to the classic Myers diff when lines repeat too often.

nodes.name: get_hash
nodes.summary: Returns the minimal perfect hash (classified line id) of the record at a given position of the reduced reference index; used by the Myers loops to compare lines by integer equality.

nodes.name: xdpsplit_t
nodes.summary: Result of a box split in the Myers algorithm: the split point (i1, i2) and flags telling whether the two sub-boxes must be searched for a minimal edit script.

nodes.name: xdl_split
nodes.summary: Heart of Myers' algorithm: scans forward diagonals from the box start and backward diagonals from the box end until they overlap, returning the split point, with heuristics that cut off expensive searches and return a good-enough suboptimal split.

nodes.name: xdl_recs_cmp
nodes.summary: Recursively diffs a box of the two files: trims matching diagonals at both ends, marks all records changed when one side is empty, otherwise splits with xdl_split and recurses on both halves, setting the per-record changed flags.

nodes.name: xdl_do_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point of the diff computation: prepares both files with xdl_prepare_env, dispatches to the patience or histogram algorithm when selected, else allocates the K vectors and runs the Myers search to set each record's changed flag.

nodes.name: xdl_add_change
nodes.summary: Allocates a new edit-script node holding the start and length of a changed region in both files and pushes it on the front of the singly linked script.

nodes.name: recs_match
nodes.summary: Compares two records by their minimal perfect hash, so that equal lines (after whitespace normalisation) compare equal in constant time.

nodes.name: get_indent
nodes.summary: Computes the indentation width of a line (tab counts to the next multiple of 8, capped at 200), returning -1 for whitespace-only lines; input to the indent heuristic.

nodes.name: split_measurement
nodes.summary: Struct describing a hypothetical split position in a file: whether it is at end of file, and indentation and blank-line counts of the line after the split and of the nearest non-blank lines before and after.

nodes.name: split_score
nodes.summary: Accumulator for a split's badness: a penalty sum and an effective indent total, compared across candidate positions when sliding a hunk.

nodes.name: measure_split
nodes.summary: Fills a split_measurement for a candidate split position by scanning outward for the nearest non-blank lines and counting blank lines (bounded by MAX_BLANKS) before and after.

nodes.name: score_add_split
nodes.summary: Adds to a score the penalties of one split: file-edge penalties, blank-line bonuses, and indent-relative penalties that favour splitting before a block start and after a block end, using empirically tuned weights.

nodes.name: score_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two split scores, ranking first by the sign of effective-indent difference weighted by INDENT_WEIGHT and then by accumulated penalty; used to pick the best slide position.

nodes.name: xdlgroup
nodes.summary: Struct representing a maximal run of consecutive changed records (start and end) in a file, the unit that xdl_change_compact slides up and down.

nodes.name: group_init
nodes.summary: Initialises a change group at the first run of changed records in a file, positioning start and end around it.

nodes.name: group_next
nodes.summary: Advances a change group to the next run of changed records, returning -1 at end of file.

nodes.name: group_previous
nodes.summary: Moves a change group back to the previous run of changed records, returning -1 at the start of the file.

nodes.name: group_slide_down
nodes.summary: Slides a change group one line down if the line just after it equals the first line of the group (so the hunk keeps the same meaning), merging with an adjacent group when it bumps into one.

nodes.name: group_slide_up
nodes.summary: Slides a change group one line up when the preceding line equals the last line of the group, merging with a previous group if the move touches it.

nodes.name: xdl_change_compact
nodes.summary: Post-processes the changed flags: shifts each change group up and down as far as possible, merges groups that collide, aligns shifts with changes in the other file, applies the indent heuristic to choose the most readable position, and re-diffs merged groups for histogram diff.

nodes.name: xdl_build_script
nodes.summary: Walks the changed flags from the end of both files backward and builds the edit script as a linked list of xdchange_t nodes (start and length of each changed run in both files).

nodes.name: xdl_free_script
nodes.summary: Frees every node of an edit script linked list.

nodes.name: xdl_call_hunk_func
nodes.summary: Hunk-emit mode used when a hunk callback is configured: groups changes into hunks with xdl_get_hunk and calls the callback with each hunk's line ranges instead of emitting diff text.

nodes.name: xdl_mark_ignorable_lines
nodes.summary: Sets the ignore flag on each change whose lines on both sides are all blank, implementing --ignore-blank-lines.

nodes.name: record_matches_regex
nodes.summary: Tests a record against every configured ignore regular expression and returns 1 on the first match.

nodes.name: xdl_mark_ignorable_regex
nodes.summary: Marks a change as ignorable when every line of it on both sides matches an ignore regex (-I), without overriding changes already ignored as blank.

nodes.name: xdl_diff
nodes.summary: Public entry of the diff library: runs xdl_do_diff, compacts both sides, builds the edit script, marks ignorable changes, then emits via the hunk callback or xdl_emit_diff, freeing the environment and script.

nodes.name: xdl_emit_record
nodes.summary: Emits one record (line) with a prefix character (' ', '-' or '+') by delegating to xdl_emit_diffrec.

nodes.name: saturating_add
nodes.summary: Adds two longs, clamping to LONG_MAX on overflow, used when computing the maximum common-line distance between hunks.

nodes.name: xdl_get_hunk
nodes.summary: Starting at an edit-script node, finds the last node that belongs to the same hunk given the context length and inter-hunk context, skipping ignorable changes that are too far from real ones and advancing the script start when leading changes are discarded.

nodes.name: def_ff
nodes.summary: Default function-name matcher: a line is a function header if it begins with a letter, underscore or dollar sign; copies it (trimmed of trailing whitespace) into the buffer.

nodes.name: match_func_rec
nodes.summary: Matches a record against the function-header pattern, using the configured find_func callback (e.g. a userdiff driver) or def_ff as default.

nodes.name: is_func_rec
nodes.summary: Returns whether a record is a function-header line, via match_func_rec with a one-byte dummy buffer.

nodes.name: func_line
nodes.summary: Struct holding the text and length of the function-name line that is shown after the @@ in a hunk header.

nodes.name: get_func_line
nodes.summary: Scans records from start toward limit (either direction) for the nearest function-header line, optionally copying it into a func_line, returning its index or -1.

nodes.name: is_empty_rec
nodes.summary: Returns true if a record consists only of whitespace.

nodes.name: xdl_emit_diff
nodes.summary: Emits a unified diff from an edit script: for each hunk computes start/end context (extending to whole functions for --function-context), writes the @@ header with function name, then the pre-context, the -/+ lines of each change, and the post-context.

nodes.name: histindex
nodes.summary: Struct holding the histogram index: hash table of line occurrence chains (records), line-to-record map, next-occurrence pointers, chain length limit and the running minimal occurrence count of the best match.

nodes.name: region
nodes.summary: Struct for a matched region: begin and end line numbers in the first and second file, used to carry the longest common substring.

nodes.name: cmp_recs
nodes.summary: Compares two records by minimal perfect hash for histogram lookup.

nodes.name: scanA
nodes.summary: Builds the histogram index over the first file's line range from the last line back: equal lines are chained and counted, a new chain is created for each distinct line, and it aborts if a hash bucket chain grows to the cap.

nodes.name: try_lcs
nodes.summary: Given a line of the second file, tries every indexed occurrence of that line in the first file, extends each match forwards and backwards, and keeps the longest region (preferring those with the lowest occurrence count); returns the next B position to try.

nodes.name: fall_back_to_classic_diff
nodes.summary: Runs the standard Myers diff on a sub-range by clearing the algorithm flags and calling xdl_fall_back_diff, used when the histogram index is unusable.

nodes.name: free_index
nodes.summary: Frees the hash table, line map, next-pointer array and the chunk allocator of a histindex.

nodes.name: find_lcs
nodes.summary: Allocates the histogram index, scans the first range with scanA, then iterates over the second range with try_lcs to find the longest low-frequency common region; reports whether to fall back to classic diff.

nodes.name: histogram_diff
nodes.summary: Recursive core of the histogram diff: handles empty ranges, finds the longest common region, then recurses on the part before it and iterates on the part after it (manual tail recursion), marking unmatched lines as changed.

nodes.name: xdl_do_histogram_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point for histogram diff: runs histogram_diff over the unchanged-trimmed range of both prepared files.

nodes.name: xinclude.h
nodes.summary: Umbrella header for the xdiff library that pulls in git-compat-util.h and every internal xdiff header (types, utils, prepare, diffi, emit); every xdiff .c file includes only this.

nodes.name: xmerge.c
nodes.summary: Three-way file merge built on xdiff: diffs the common ancestor against both sides, walks the two edit scripts to classify each region as taken-from-one-side or conflicting, optionally refines and simplifies conflicts, and renders the merged text with conflict markers in merge, diff3 or zdiff3 style.

nodes.name: xpatience.c
nodes.summary: Patience diff algorithm: hashes lines of the range, keeps lines that are unique in both files, finds their longest increasing common subsequence as anchors, and recursively diffs the gaps, falling back to the classic algorithm when no unique line matches.

nodes.name: xdmerge_t
nodes.summary: Linked-list node describing one merged region: a mode (0 conflict, 1 take first, 2 take second, 3 both) and line positions and counts in side 1, side 2 and the common ancestor.

nodes.name: xdl_append_merge
nodes.summary: Appends a merge region to the list, or coalesces it with the previous one when they overlap or touch, downgrading the mode to conflict if the two sides disagree.

nodes.name: xdl_cleanup_merge
nodes.summary: Frees the whole merge region list and returns the number of conflict regions (mode 0).

nodes.name: xdl_merge_cmp_lines
nodes.summary: Compares a range of post-image lines from the two sides using xdl_recmatch with the whitespace flags; used to detect identical changes on both sides.

nodes.name: xdl_recs_copy_0
nodes.summary: Copies or measures a run of lines from either the ancestor or a post-image into the output buffer, optionally adding a missing final newline in CRLF or LF style; with a null dest it only counts size.

nodes.name: xdl_recs_copy
nodes.summary: Copies post-image lines of a side into the merge output via xdl_recs_copy_0.

nodes.name: xdl_orig_copy
nodes.summary: Copies ancestor (pre-image) lines into the merge output via xdl_recs_copy_0, used for the diff3 base section.

nodes.name: is_eol_crlf
nodes.summary: Determines whether a line ends with CRLF, falling back to the preceding line when the last line lacks an end-of-line, or -1 when it cannot be known.

nodes.name: is_cr_needed
nodes.summary: Decides whether conflict markers and inserted newlines need a CR by examining the line endings near the region in both post-images and the pre-image.

nodes.name: fill_conflict_hunk
nodes.summary: Writes (or measures) one conflict block: the preceding unchanged lines, '<<<<<<<' marker with side name, side 1 lines, optional '|||||||' ancestor section for diff3, '=======', side 2 lines and '>>>>>>>' marker.

nodes.name: xdl_fill_merge_buffer
nodes.summary: Walks the merge region list and builds the result text: conflicts via fill_conflict_hunk, resolved regions by copying the chosen side(s), honouring the favor option; called once with null dest to size and once to fill.

nodes.name: recmatch
nodes.summary: Compares two records with xdl_recmatch under the whitespace flags.

nodes.name: xdl_refine_zdiff3_conflicts
nodes.summary: For zdiff3 style, trims identical lines from the beginning and end of each conflict so only the differing middle is shown between markers.

nodes.name: xdl_refine_conflicts
nodes.summary: For each conflict, runs a nested diff between the two sides' conflicting text and splits it into smaller conflicts (or marks it resolved if the sides are identical), so only truly differing lines remain in conflict.

nodes.name: line_contains_alnum
nodes.summary: Returns 1 if a byte string contains at least one alphanumeric character.

nodes.name: lines_contain_alnum
nodes.summary: Checks whether any of a range of lines contains an alphanumeric character.

nodes.name: xdl_merge_two_conflicts
nodes.summary: Merges two adjacent conflict regions into one, absorbing the lines between them into the conflict.

nodes.name: xdl_simplify_non_conflicts
nodes.summary: Folds short runs (3 lines or fewer, optionally only without alphanumerics) of non-conflicting lines between two conflicts into the conflict, producing fewer and more compact conflict blocks.

nodes.name: xdl_do_merge
nodes.summary: Core three-way merge: walks the two edit scripts (ancestor to side 1, ancestor to side 2), emits regions as taken-from-one-side or conflicting, applies refinement and simplification per level and style, then renders the result buffer and returns the conflict count.

nodes.name: xdl_merge
nodes.summary: Public three-way merge entry: diffs ancestor against each side, compacts and builds both edit scripts, short-circuits when one side is unchanged, otherwise calls xdl_do_merge; cleans up and returns status or conflict count.

nodes.name: hashmap
nodes.summary: Struct mapping line hashes to their line numbers in the first and second file (with a NON_UNIQUE marker), plus links to chain entries into the longest common sequence.

nodes.name: is_anchor
nodes.summary: Returns whether a line starts with one of the user-supplied anchor strings (--anchored).

nodes.name: insert_record
nodes.summary: Inserts a line into the open-addressing hash map: records first-file occurrences, and for the second file sets line2 or marks the entry NON_UNIQUE if seen again; tracks whether any common lines exist.

nodes.name: fill_hashmap
nodes.summary: Allocates the entries array (twice the first range size) and inserts every record of the first then second line range.

nodes.name: binary_search
nodes.summary: Binary search over the current best subsequence tails to find the longest sequence whose last line2 is smaller than the new entry's.

nodes.name: find_longest_common_sequence
nodes.summary: Computes the longest increasing common subsequence of unique lines, treating anchors as immovable, and links the result entries into a chain from first to last.

nodes.name: match
nodes.summary: Compares line numbers of the two files by their minimal perfect hash.

nodes.name: walk_common_sequence
nodes.summary: Walks the unique-line common sequence, grows each matched range outward over equal neighbouring lines, and recursively runs patience_diff on the gaps between the matches.

nodes.name: fall_back_to_classic_diff
nodes.summary: Diffs a range with the classic Myers algorithm by clearing the algorithm flags and calling xdl_fall_back_diff, when no unique common lines exist.

nodes.name: patience_diff
nodes.summary: Recursive patience diff on a line range: handles empty sides, builds the hash map, marks all lines changed if nothing matches, else finds the common unique sequence and walks it, or falls back to the classic diff.

nodes.name: xdl_do_patience_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point for patience diff over the whole of both prepared files.

nodes.name: xprepare.c
nodes.summary: Prepares two files for diffing: splits them into records (lines) and hashes them, classifies equal lines onto small integer ids, trims common prefix and suffix, and discards lines with no counterpart (or in noisy runs) so the diff core works on a reduced problem.

nodes.name: xutils.c
nodes.summary: Shared xdiff helpers: line hashing (verbatim and whitespace-insensitive), whitespace-aware line comparison, a chunked allocator, line-count estimation, hunk header formatting, record emission with the no-newline marker, and a fallback that diffs a sub-range with the classic algorithm.

nodes.name: xdlclass_t
nodes.summary: Struct for one equivalence class of lines: its hash, text pointer, class index and how many times it occurs in each file.

nodes.name: xdlclassifier_t
nodes.summary: Struct for the line classifier: hash table of classes, chunk allocator, array mapping class index to class, and diff flags.

nodes.name: xdl_init_classifier
nodes.summary: Initialises the classifier: sizes the hash table from the line-count estimate, sets up the chunk allocator and the class array.

nodes.name: xdl_free_classifier
nodes.summary: Releases the classifier's class array, hash table and chunk allocator.

nodes.name: xdl_classify_record
nodes.summary: Looks up a record's hash and text in the classifier (using whitespace-aware equality), creating a new class if unseen, counts it for the given file and stores the class index as the record's minimal perfect hash.

nodes.name: xdl_free_ctx
nodes.summary: Frees one file context's reference index, changed array and record array.

nodes.name: xdl_prepare_ctx
nodes.summary: Splits a file into line records by hashing each line, classifies them, and allocates the changed flag array with sentinels and the initial diff window.

nodes.name: xdl_free_env
nodes.summary: Frees both file contexts of a diff environment.

nodes.name: xdl_clean_mmatch
nodes.summary: Decides whether a line with many matches should be discarded by scanning a bounded window around it: discards it only if it sits in a run containing enough unmatched lines.

nodes.name: xdl_cleanup_records
nodes.summary: Reduces the diff problem: marks lines absent from the other file as changed, keeps lines with a moderate number of matches, investigates frequent ones, and builds the reference index of surviving records used by Myers' algorithm.

nodes.name: xdl_trim_ends
nodes.summary: Finds the common prefix and suffix of equal records of the two files and sets dstart and dend so the middle only is diffed.

nodes.name: xdl_optimize_ctxs
nodes.summary: Runs xdl_trim_ends and then xdl_cleanup_records on the two contexts.

nodes.name: xdl_prepare_env
nodes.summary: Builds the diff environment for two files: estimates line counts, creates the classifier, prepares both file contexts, and for the Myers algorithm also optimises them (patience and histogram skip this step).

nodes.name: xdl_bogosqrt
nodes.summary: Cheap integer approximation of a square root using shifts, used to size cost limits and equality limits.

nodes.name: xdl_emit_diffrec
nodes.summary: Emits a record through the output callback as prefix plus line, appending the '\ No newline at end of file' marker when the line lacks a trailing newline.

nodes.name: xdl_mmfile_first
nodes.summary: Returns the pointer and size of the in-memory file's data.

nodes.name: xdl_mmfile_size
nodes.summary: Returns the size of an in-memory file.

nodes.name: xdl_cha_init
nodes.summary: Initialises a chunked allocator that hands out fixed-size items from large blocks.

nodes.name: xdl_cha_free
nodes.summary: Frees all blocks of a chunked allocator.

nodes.name: xdl_cha_alloc
nodes.summary: Returns the next fixed-size item from the current block of a chunked allocator, allocating and linking a new block when the current one is full.

nodes.name: xdl_guess_lines
nodes.summary: Estimates the number of lines in a file by sampling the average line length of the first lines, so arrays can be sized up front.

nodes.name: xdl_blankline
nodes.summary: Returns whether a line is blank, treating whitespace-only lines as blank when whitespace-ignoring flags are set.

nodes.name: ends_with_optional_cr
nodes.summary: Checks that the remainder of a line after position i is nothing but an optional CR before the newline, for --ignore-cr-at-eol.

nodes.name: xdl_recmatch
nodes.summary: Compares two lines for equality under the active whitespace mode (-w, -b, --ignore-space-at-eol, --ignore-cr-at-eol), skipping or collapsing whitespace as each mode requires.

nodes.name: xdl_hash_record_with_whitespace
nodes.summary: Hashes a line while ignoring or collapsing whitespace according to the flags, producing equal hashes for lines that xdl_recmatch treats as equal.

nodes.name: xdl_hash_record_verbatim
nodes.summary: Hashes a line verbatim with an unrolled two-bytes-per-iteration djb2-style loop, using reassociation fences to shorten the dependency chain, and advances past the newline.

nodes.name: xdl_hashbits
nodes.summary: Returns the number of bits needed for a hash table able to hold the given number of entries.

nodes.name: xdl_num_out
nodes.summary: Formats a long as decimal text into a buffer without printf and returns its length.

nodes.name: xdl_format_hunk_hdr
nodes.summary: Formats the '@@ -s,c +s,c @@ funcname' hunk header text (omitting count 1, adjusting start for empty ranges, truncating long function names) and sends it through the output callback.

nodes.name: xdl_emit_hunk_hdr
nodes.summary: Emits a hunk header either as numbers through the out_hunk callback or, when none is set, as formatted text.

nodes.name: xdl_fall_back_diff
nodes.summary: Diffs a sub-range of lines of two prepared files with the classic algorithm by building temporary mmfiles over the range and copying the resulting changed flags back; used by patience, histogram and change compaction.

nodes.name: xdl_alloc_grow_helper
nodes.summary: Growth helper behind XDL_ALLOC_GROW: computes a new capacity (2n+16, overflow-checked), reallocs the array and frees it on failure.

nodes.name: banned.h
nodes.summary: Turns a list of unsafe C library functions (strcpy, strcat, strncpy, strncat, strtok, sprintf, vsprintf, gmtime, localtime, ctime, asctime and their _r variants, mktemp) into compile-time errors by redefining them as macros that expand to a nonexistent "sorry_<func>_is_a_banned_function" identifier.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure preprocessor trick: #undef then #define each function name so that any call fails to compile with a readable undefined-identifier message.

nodes.name: commit-slab-decl.h
nodes.summary: Declaration half of the commit-slab facility: macros that declare a slab struct type and its function prototypes (init, clear, deep_clear, _at, _peek), plus the static initializer COMMIT_SLAB_INIT. A commit slab is a chunked array indexed by commit->index that lets code attach per-commit data without growing struct commit.
nodes.languageNotes: Generics by macro: declare_commit_slab(name, type) generates a typed struct, standing in for C++ templates.

nodes.name: declare_commit_slab
nodes.summary: Macro that defines "struct <slabname>" with slab_size, stride, slab_count and a pointer to an array of element-type chunks.

nodes.name: COMMIT_SLAB_INIT
nodes.summary: Static initializer macro for a commit slab with a given stride, computing slab_size from COMMIT_SLAB_SIZE (about 512 KiB per chunk).

nodes.name: declare_commit_slab_prototypes
nodes.summary: Macro that emits prototypes of init_<name>, init_<name>_with_stride, clear_<name>, deep_clear_<name>, <name>_at, <name>_at_peek and <name>_peek for a slab type.

nodes.name: define_shared_commit_slab
nodes.summary: Macro that declares a slab struct together with its prototypes so the slab can be shared across translation units.

nodes.name: commit-slab-impl.h
nodes.summary: Implementation half of the commit-slab facility: implement_commit_slab (and its static and shared wrappers) generates the init, clear, deep_clear, _at, _at_peek and _peek functions. Elements are looked up by splitting commit->index into a slab number and a slot, allocating zeroed chunks lazily.
nodes.languageNotes: The macro ends with a redundant "struct slabname" so that instantiations can be terminated with a semicolon and look like declarations.

nodes.name: implement_commit_slab
nodes.summary: Macro that expands to the full slab implementation: stride-aware initialisation, freeing slabs (with an optional per-element free callback) and the lazy indexing function slabname_at_peek that grows the slab array and calloc's a chunk on first write.

nodes.name: implement_static_commit_slab
nodes.summary: Wrapper macro that instantiates a slab implementation with static (file-local) linkage.

nodes.name: implement_shared_commit_slab
nodes.summary: Wrapper macro that instantiates a slab implementation with external linkage, for slabs declared with define_shared_commit_slab.

nodes.name: reftable-block.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of a single block of a reftable file (the binary ref storage format): struct reftable_block with header offset, restart point data and optional zlib state for log blocks, plus functions to initialise it from a block source, create a record iterator, query its type and decode its first key.

nodes.name: reftable_block
nodes.summary: In-memory view of one reftable block: raw block data, hash size, uncompressed log data and zstream, restart point count and offset, on-disk size and block type.

nodes.name: reftable-constants.h
nodes.summary: Defines the single-character block type tags of the reftable format: 'g' for log, 'i' for index, 'r' for ref, 'o' for object-id blocks, and 0 meaning any type.

nodes.name: reftable-system.h
nodes.summary: Platform glue for the reftable library: pulls in Git's POSIX and zlib compatibility headers, declares reftable_fsync and redirects fsync() to it, so the library can be built standalone by other projects that replace this header.

nodes.name: reftable-writer.h
