nodes.summary: Public API for writing a single reftable: option and statistics structs (block size, restart interval, index/log settings, auto-compaction factor, lock timeout) and the writer functions to create a writer, set update-index limits, add ref and log records in sorted order, close and free it.

nodes.name: reftable_write_options
nodes.summary: Options for writing a reftable: unpadded blocks, block size, whether to skip the object-id index, restart interval, default file permissions, exact log messages, auto-compaction switches and factor, and the lock timeout for tables.list.

nodes.name: reftable_block_stats
nodes.summary: Statistics for one block type: number of entries, restarts, blocks, index blocks, index depth and the offsets of the first and top-level index blocks.

nodes.name: reftable_stats
nodes.summary: Overall statistics for a finished reftable: total blocks, per-type stats for refs, object-id map, index and log blocks, and the abbreviated object id length.

nodes.name: sane-ctype.h
nodes.summary: Replaces the locale-dependent <ctype.h> classification macros (isspace, isdigit, isalpha, isalnum, isxdigit, tolower, toupper, ...) with locale-independent versions driven by a 256-entry sane_ctype table and hexval_table, adding Git-specific classes (glob, regex, pathspec magic).
nodes.languageNotes: Includes <ctype.h> first and then #undefs and redefines its macros, so the header must be included before any other header that pulls in <ctype.h>.

nodes.name: sane_case
nodes.summary: Static inline helper that sets or clears the 0x20 bit of an ASCII letter to change its case, leaving non-letters unchanged; backs tolower and toupper.

nodes.name: sane_iscase
nodes.summary: Static inline helper that tests whether an ASCII letter is lower or upper case using its 0x20 bit; backs islower and isupper.

nodes.name: unicode-width.h
nodes.summary: Data tables for terminal column width of Unicode code points: zero_width (combining marks, format characters, variation selectors, tag characters) and double_width (East Asian wide characters and emoji) as sorted ranges of struct interval, textually #included inside the body of git_wcwidth in utf8.c, which binary-searches them.
nodes.languageNotes: Two static const arrays of { first, last } code point pairs, intended for binary search; it is not a self-contained header: it has no include guard and is meant to be included at function scope.

nodes.name: xemit.h
nodes.summary: Declares the output stage of the xdiff library: the emit_func_t callback type, xdl_get_hunk (group changes into a hunk using the context size) and xdl_emit_diff (format the diff via the callbacks).

nodes.name: xprepare.h
nodes.summary: Declares the preparation stage of the xdiff library: xdl_prepare_env builds the per-file records, hashes and classification for two input files (the xdfenv_t), and xdl_free_env releases it.

nodes.name: grep.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git grep`: searches file contents in the working tree, the index, untracked files, or tree-ish objects (including submodules) using a bounded work queue with worker threads that preserves output order, plus a prefetch step for blobs of a partial clone.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fixed-size ring buffer (todo[TODO_SIZE]) guarded by a pthread mutex and three condition variables so worker threads can grep in parallel while results are still written to stdout in submission order.

nodes.name: add_work
nodes.summary: Queues a grep_source into the ring-buffer work list for worker threads, blocking while the buffer is full.

nodes.name: work_done
nodes.summary: Marks a work item finished and flushes completed items to stdout strictly in submission order, so threaded output stays deterministic.

nodes.name: free_repos
nodes.summary: Frees the submodule repository structs opened during the grep.

nodes.name: start_threads
nodes.summary: Initializes the mutex and condition variables and spawns the grep worker threads that consume the work queue.

nodes.name: wait_all
nodes.summary: Signals that all work has been added, waits for workers to drain the queue, joins the threads and merges their hit status.

nodes.name: grep_cmd_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads grep.* variables (line number, column, extended regexp, threads, fallback to no-index) and color settings.

nodes.name: grep_source_name
nodes.summary: Builds the display name of a grep match source (working tree path, tree-ish:path, or index path) with the submodule prefix applied.

nodes.name: grep_oid
nodes.summary: Greps a blob given by object id, either queuing it for a worker thread or running it directly.

nodes.name: grep_file
nodes.summary: Greps a working tree file by path, queuing it for threads or running it inline.

nodes.name: run_pager
nodes.summary: Collects matched file names and launches the pager (or editor) with them, implementing the open-files-in-pager option.

nodes.name: grep_submodule
nodes.summary: Opens an active submodule as a separate repository and greps its index or a tree-ish within it, honoring the superproject prefix.

nodes.name: grep_cache
nodes.summary: Walks the index entries (expanding sparse directories by reading their trees) and greps each tracked blob or working tree file that matches the pathspec.

nodes.name: grep_tree
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a tree object, matching entries against the pathspec and grepping each blob, descending into subtrees and submodules.

nodes.name: collect_blob_oids_for_tree
nodes.summary: Recursively collects the blob ids reachable in a tree that match the pathspec into an oidset.

nodes.name: collect_blob_oids_for_treeish
nodes.summary: Resolves a tree-ish and collects all pathspec-matching blob ids beneath it.

nodes.name: prefetch_grep_blobs
nodes.summary: In a partial clone, gathers blob ids from the requested trees and prefetches the missing ones from the promisor remote in one batch before grepping.

nodes.name: grep_object
nodes.summary: Greps one object from the command line: a blob directly, or a tree or tag after peeling to a tree.

nodes.name: grep_objects
nodes.summary: Runs grep_object over every revision given on the command line, first prefetching blobs when needed.

nodes.name: grep_directory
nodes.summary: Greps untracked working tree files found by fill_directory, honoring the exclude rules.

nodes.name: context_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for the -A/-B/-C/-NUM context line options.

nodes.name: file_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for -f <file>: reads one pattern per line from a file or stdin and adds each as a grep pattern.

nodes.name: cmd_grep
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git grep`: parses options, resolves revisions and paths, chooses between working tree, index, untracked and tree-ish modes, sets up threads and runs the search.

nodes.name: ls-files.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git ls-files`: lists entries of the index (cached, staged, deleted, modified, unmerged with stages) and working-tree files (others, ignored, killed), with format strings, pathspec filtering, resolve-undo info and sparse-index awareness.

nodes.name: write_name_to_buf
nodes.summary: Formats a path (relative to the prefix, quoted as needed) into a strbuf for format-string output.

nodes.name: show_killed_files
nodes.summary: Detects working tree files or directories that would be killed (overwritten) by checking out the index, and prints them.

nodes.name: show_submodule
nodes.summary: Reports whether a gitlink entry's directory is a real, populated submodule so it can be treated as a directory when listing.

nodes.name: expand_objectsize
nodes.summary: Expands the %(objectsize) placeholder for an index entry, reading the object size from the object database.

nodes.name: show_ce_fmt
nodes.summary: Prints one index entry according to a --format string (mode, object name, stage, path, eol info and so on).

nodes.name: show_ce
nodes.summary: Prints one index entry in the default or --stage layout, optionally with a status tag and eol information.

nodes.name: show_ru_info
nodes.summary: Prints the resolve-undo information recorded for previously resolved conflicts (--resolve-undo).

nodes.name: show_files
nodes.summary: Core listing routine: lists untracked/ignored/killed files from the directory scan, then iterates the index to show cached, staged, deleted, modified and unmerged entries.

nodes.name: prune_index
nodes.summary: Binary-searches the sorted index and trims it down to the entries that share a directory prefix, to speed up listing in a subdirectory.

nodes.name: get_common_prefix_len
nodes.summary: Computes the longest leading directory common to all pathspecs so the walk can be limited.

nodes.name: option_parse_exclude
nodes.summary: Option callback that adds a pattern given with -x to the exclude list.

nodes.name: option_parse_exclude_from
nodes.summary: Option callback that loads exclude patterns from a file given with -X.

nodes.name: option_parse_exclude_standard
nodes.summary: Option callback that sets up the standard exclude sources (.gitignore files, info/exclude, core.excludesFile).

nodes.name: cmd_ls_files
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git ls-files`: parses options, loads the index, applies pathspec, sparse-index expansion and exclude setup, then calls show_files and checks that every pathspec matched.

nodes.name: merge-index.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command `git merge-index`: for each unmerged path in the index, gathers the stage 1/2/3 blob ids and modes and runs an external merge program on them.

nodes.name: merge_entry
nodes.summary: Collects the stage 1, 2 and 3 object ids and modes of one unmerged path from the index and runs the external merge program on them.

nodes.name: merge_one_path
nodes.summary: Merges a single named path unless it is already at stage 0 in the index.

nodes.name: merge_all
nodes.summary: Iterates all index entries and merges every unmerged path.

nodes.name: cmd_merge_index
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git merge-index`: parses -o and -q, then merges the named paths or all unmerged paths with the given merge program.

nodes.name: mv.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git mv`: validates sources and destinations (files, directories, symlinks, submodules, sparse entries), renames them in the working tree, and rewrites the index entries and .gitmodules paths under the index lock.

nodes.name: internal_prefix_pathspec
nodes.summary: Builds the destination pathspec for a directory move by prefixing source paths with the destination directory.

nodes.name: index_range_of_same_dir
nodes.summary: Finds the contiguous range of sorted index entries that live under a source directory.

nodes.name: empty_dir_has_sparse_contents
nodes.summary: Checks whether a source directory that looks empty on disk still has index entries outside the sparse checkout.

nodes.name: remove_empty_src_dirs
nodes.summary: After a move, removes source directories that have become empty in the working tree.

nodes.name: pathmap_cmp
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison function for the table of moved directories.

nodes.name: cmd_mv
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git mv`: validates each source/destination pair, renames files in the working tree, rewrites index entries (sorted, under the index lock) and updates .gitmodules for submodules.

nodes.name: read-tree.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command `git read-tree`: reads one to three tree objects into the index, driving unpack_trees with the selected merge function (one-way, two-way, three-way, reset, prefix, sparse checkout).

nodes.name: list_tree
nodes.summary: Resolves an object name to a tree and appends it to the list of trees to be unpacked, up to MAX_UNPACK_TREES.

nodes.name: exclude_per_directory_cb
nodes.summary: Option callback for --exclude-per-directory: sets up the per-directory exclude file used while unpacking.

nodes.name: debug_stage
nodes.summary: Prints one stage of a merge (missing, conflict, or mode, stage, path and abbreviated object id) for --debug-unpack.

nodes.name: debug_merge
nodes.summary: Merge function that prints every stage of an N-way merge instead of merging, for debugging unpack_trees.

nodes.name: cmd_read_tree
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git read-tree`: parses options, chooses the unpack_trees merge function (one-way, two-way, three-way, reset, prefix) for the given trees, runs it and writes the new index under the lock.

nodes.name: reset.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git reset`: moves HEAD (and the current branch ref) to another commit, resets the index (and optionally the working tree) with soft, mixed, hard, merge or keep modes, or resets selected paths in the index from a tree.

nodes.name: reset_index
nodes.summary: Resets the index (and with hard/merge/keep, the working tree) to a given tree by running unpack_trees with one-way or two-way merge options, then primes the cache tree.

nodes.name: print_new_head_line
nodes.summary: Prints the HEAD-is-now-at message with the abbreviated commit id and subject after a reset.

nodes.name: update_index_from_diff
nodes.summary: Diff callback that updates index entries for a path-limited reset: removes entries absent in the tree or re-adds the tree's version, honoring intent-to-add.

nodes.name: read_from_tree
nodes.summary: Resets selected paths in the index to their state in a tree by running a tree-to-index diff and applying update_index_from_diff.

nodes.name: set_reflog_message
nodes.summary: Builds the reflog message used when reset updates refs.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Disambiguates `git reset` arguments into a revision and a pathspec, deciding whether the first argument is a commit/tree or a filename.

nodes.name: reset_refs
nodes.summary: Saves the old HEAD as ORIG_HEAD and updates HEAD (and the branch it points to) to the new commit with a reflog message.

nodes.name: cmd_reset
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git reset`: parses mode and arguments, performs a path-limited reset or a commit reset (index, working tree, refs, cleanup of merge state).

nodes.name: rm.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git rm`: removes paths from the index and working tree, first checking that no local or staged modifications would be lost, handling submodules and sparse entries, and updating .gitmodules.

nodes.name: print_error_files
nodes.summary: Prints the list of files that block removal with a header message and an advice hint.

nodes.name: submodules_absorb_gitdir_if_needed
nodes.summary: Absorbs the git directory of each submodule being removed into the superproject so no history is lost.

nodes.name: check_local_mod
nodes.summary: Checks every path to be removed for staged or working tree changes relative to HEAD and the index, and reports those that would lose data unless forced.

nodes.name: cmd_rm
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git rm`: builds the pathspec, matches index entries, runs the safety checks, removes files from the working tree and index, and updates .gitmodules.

nodes.name: sparse-checkout.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git sparse-checkout` and its subcommands (list, init, set, add, reapply, disable, clean, check-rules): maintains the sparse-checkout pattern file and config in cone or non-cone mode and updates the working tree and index to match.

nodes.name: write_patterns_to_file
nodes.summary: Writes a pattern list to the sparse-checkout file in non-cone (gitignore-style) form.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_list
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout list`: prints the current patterns, or the cone directories in cone mode.

nodes.name: clean_tracked_sparse_directories
nodes.summary: Removes tracked directories outside the sparse cone that are left empty or contain only ignored files, using the sparse index to find them.

nodes.name: update_working_directory
nodes.summary: Applies a new pattern list to the index and working tree through unpack_trees with sparsity updates, rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: write_cone_to_file
nodes.summary: Writes the cone-mode sparse-checkout file from a set of recursive and parent directories.

nodes.name: write_patterns_and_update
nodes.summary: Writes the sparse-checkout file, updates the working directory, and cleans up leftover tracked directories.

nodes.name: set_config
nodes.summary: Enables or disables core.sparseCheckout and core.sparseCheckoutCone in the worktree config.

nodes.name: update_modes
nodes.summary: Updates cone mode and sparse-index config as requested by the command-line options.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_init
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout init`: turns on sparse checkout, writes the default patterns and updates the working tree.

nodes.name: insert_recursive_pattern
nodes.summary: Inserts a directory into the cone-mode pattern table, marking it recursive and registering its parents.

nodes.name: strbuf_to_cone_pattern
nodes.summary: Normalizes an input line into a cone-mode directory pattern.

nodes.name: add_patterns_from_input
nodes.summary: Reads patterns or directories from stdin or the argument list and applies them in cone or non-cone mode.

nodes.name: add_patterns_cone_mode
nodes.summary: Adds directories to the cone-mode pattern list after expanding the existing cone.

nodes.name: modify_pattern_list
nodes.summary: Replaces or extends the current pattern list based on the set/add subcommand and the active mode.

nodes.name: sanitize_paths
nodes.summary: Validates and prefixes user-supplied paths, rejecting files, wildcards and out-of-tree paths in cone mode.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_add
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout add`: adds directories or patterns to the existing sparse set.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_set
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout set`: replaces the sparse set with the given directories or patterns.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_reapply
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout reapply`: re-applies the existing patterns to the working tree.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_clean
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout clean`: in cone mode only, removes leftover directories outside the cone (supports dry-run, force and verbose).

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_disable
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout disable`: restores all files to the working tree and turns the feature off.

nodes.name: check_rules
nodes.summary: Reads paths from stdin and prints those that are inside the sparse checkout according to a pattern list.

nodes.name: sparse_checkout_check_rules
nodes.summary: Implements `sparse-checkout check-rules`: loads patterns (cone or non-cone) from the repo or a given file and runs check_rules.

nodes.name: cmd_sparse_checkout
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git sparse-checkout`: dispatches to the subcommand handlers via parse_options.

nodes.name: stash.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git stash` (push, save, apply, pop, drop, clear, list, show, branch, create, store, export, import): records working tree and index state as merge-shaped commits referenced by refs/stash and its reflog, and re-applies them with a three-way merge.
nodes.languageNotes: A stash entry is a commit with 2 or 3 parents (HEAD, index tree commit, optional untracked-files commit) whose own tree is the working tree; check_stash_topology validates that shape.

nodes.name: check_stash_topology
nodes.summary: Validates that a commit has the shape of a stash (two or three parents, with the index commit's parent equal to HEAD and the untracked commit parentless).

nodes.name: get_stash_info
nodes.summary: Resolves a stash revision (stash@{n} or a commit) into its component commits and trees (working tree, base, index, untracked) and its reflog position.

nodes.name: clear_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash clear`: deletes refs/stash and its reflog.

nodes.name: reset_tree
nodes.summary: Updates the index (and optionally working tree) to a given tree via unpack_trees one-way merge.

nodes.name: create_index_from_tree
nodes.summary: Builds a temporary index file populated from a tree, used to compute the index tree of a stash.

nodes.name: diff_tree_binary
nodes.summary: Generates a binary diff between a stash commit's parent and itself into a buffer for later `apply --cached`.

nodes.name: apply_cached
nodes.summary: Runs `git apply --cached` on a patch buffer to restore staged changes.

nodes.name: add_diff_to_buf
nodes.summary: Diff callback that appends the formatted patch of each changed file to a buffer.

nodes.name: restore_untracked
nodes.summary: Restores the files saved in a stash's untracked commit into the working tree.

nodes.name: unstage_changes_unless_new
nodes.summary: After a clean stash merge, unstages the staged results except for newly added files, and clears skip-worktree bits for paths the stash touches.

nodes.name: do_apply_stash
nodes.summary: Core of `stash apply`/`pop`: three-way merges the stash's working tree commit into the current tree with merge-ort using the stash base, optionally restoring the index and untracked files, then reports status.

nodes.name: apply_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash apply`: parses options, resolves the stash and calls do_apply_stash.

nodes.name: do_drop_stash
nodes.summary: Deletes a stash reflog entry, rewriting refs/stash to the next entry or removing it when empty.

nodes.name: drop_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash drop`: resolves the stash and drops it.

nodes.name: pop_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash pop`: applies a stash and drops it only if the apply succeeded.

nodes.name: branch_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash branch`: creates a branch at the stash's base commit, checks it out, applies the stash and drops it.

nodes.name: list_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash list`: runs `git log -g --first-parent` over the refs/stash reflog to print each entry.

nodes.name: git_stash_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for stash.showStat, stash.showPatch, stash.showIncludeUntracked and stash.index.

nodes.name: diff_include_untracked
nodes.summary: Builds a diff that includes the stash's untracked files by diffing against the empty tree.

nodes.name: show_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash show`: sets up a revision walk and diff options and prints stat or patch of the stash against its base.

nodes.name: do_store_stash
nodes.summary: Stores a given commit as the newest stash entry by updating refs/stash and its reflog.

nodes.name: store_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash store`: validates the commit and records it as a stash.

nodes.name: get_untracked_files
nodes.summary: Collects untracked (and optionally ignored) files that match the pathspec into a buffer.

nodes.name: check_changes_tracked_files
nodes.summary: Checks whether any tracked file differs from HEAD or the index to decide if there is anything to stash.

nodes.name: check_changes
nodes.summary: Reports whether there are stashable changes among tracked and untracked files.

nodes.name: save_untracked_files
nodes.summary: Writes the untracked files into a temporary index and tree, then creates the untracked commit stored as the third parent.

nodes.name: stash_staged
nodes.summary: For `push --staged`, writes the index as a tree and runs `diff-tree -p --binary` against HEAD to capture only the staged changes as a patch.

nodes.name: stash_patch
nodes.summary: For `push --patch`, runs the interactive hunk selection and produces a patch of the selected changes.

nodes.name: stash_working_tree
nodes.summary: Builds the stash's working tree commit tree by diffing and updating a temporary index from the working tree.

nodes.name: do_create_stash
nodes.summary: Builds the stash commits: an index commit, an optional untracked-files commit, and the final working-tree commit with the proper parents and message, without touching refs/stash.

nodes.name: create_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash create`: builds a stash commit and prints its object id.

nodes.name: do_push_stash
nodes.summary: Core of `stash push`: validates option combinations, creates the stash commit, stores it, then resets the working tree and index (respecting --keep-index and pathspecs).

nodes.name: push_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash push`: parses its options and calls do_push_stash.

nodes.name: save_stash
nodes.summary: Implements the legacy `stash save [message]` form on top of do_push_stash.

nodes.name: write_commit_with_parents
nodes.summary: Copies a stash commit's tree, author and committer into a new commit with a replacement parent list.

nodes.name: do_import_stash
nodes.summary: Imports a chain of stash commits (from an exported ref) into refs/stash by walking the first-parent chain and storing each entry.

nodes.name: import_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash import`: validates the revision and imports its stash chain.

nodes.name: collect_stash_entries
nodes.summary: Reflog callback that collects each stash commit, checking its topology.

nodes.name: do_export_stash
nodes.summary: Builds a chain of commits that records all stash entries (or the given ones) reproducibly with a fixed date, so they can be pushed as a single ref.

nodes.name: export_stash
nodes.summary: Implements `stash export`: requires exactly one of --print or --to-ref, then calls do_export_stash to print the object id or write it to a ref.

nodes.name: cmd_stash
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git stash`: dispatches to the subcommand handler (push by default).

nodes.name: submodule--helper.c
nodes.summary: Implements the internal `git submodule--helper` builtin that backs `git submodule`: one subcommand per operation (add, init, update, status, sync, deinit, summary, foreach, absorbgitdirs, set-url, set-branch, clone and more). It reads gitlink entries from the index and .gitmodules via submodule-config, clones submodule repositories into the superproject gitdir, and runs fetch/checkout/merge/rebase inside them, in parallel for update.
nodes.languageNotes: Typical Git builtin style: static helpers plus one `cmd_*` entry point, argument parsing through parse-options (OPT_SUBCOMMAND dispatch), and work delegated to child processes (`struct child_process`) that re-invoke git inside each submodule with a sanitized environment.

nodes.name: get_default_remote
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the default remote name of the current repository using repo_default_remote.

nodes.name: resolve_relative_url
nodes.summary: Resolves a submodule URL written relative to the superproject (./ or ../) against the superproject default remote URL, or against the current directory with a warning when no remote URL is configured.

nodes.name: get_default_remote_submodule
nodes.summary: Finds the remote name to use inside a submodule: it looks the submodule URL from .gitmodules up among the submodule remotes and falls back to its default remote.

nodes.name: module_get_default_remote
nodes.summary: Subcommand `get-default-remote`: resolves the path argument and prints the default remote name of that submodule.

nodes.name: get_submodule_displaypath
nodes.summary: Computes the path shown to the user for a submodule, made relative to the current prefix or prepended with the super-prefix when recursing.

nodes.name: compute_rev_name
nodes.summary: Runs `git describe` in a submodule with increasingly permissive options (none, --tags, --contains, --all --always) and returns the first name found for an object id.

nodes.name: module_list_compute
nodes.summary: Builds a module_list of gitlink (submodule) entries from the index that match the given pathspec, skipping duplicate stages and reporting unmatched paths.

nodes.name: module_list_active
nodes.summary: Filters a module_list in place, keeping only submodules that is_submodule_active reports as active.

nodes.name: get_up_path
nodes.summary: Builds the "../" prefix that leads from a submodule path back up to the superproject root.

nodes.name: runcommand_in_submodule_cb
nodes.summary: Callback of `foreach`: validates the path, skips unpopulated submodules, and runs the user command through a shell inside the submodule, exposing name, sm_path, displaypath, sha1 and toplevel as variables for single-argument commands.

nodes.name: module_foreach
nodes.summary: Subcommand `foreach`: lists submodule entries from the index and runs a shell command in each populated submodule.

nodes.name: validate_and_set_submodule_gitdir
nodes.summary: Checks that a candidate git directory is safe for a submodule name and stores it in `submodule.<name>.gitdir` unless already configured.

nodes.name: create_default_gitdir_config
nodes.summary: Chooses a gitdir under .git/modules for a new submodule by trying the plain name, URI-encoded and case-folding-safe names, numbered variants and finally a hash of the name, and records it in config.

nodes.name: init_submodule
nodes.summary: Registers one submodule in the superproject config: sets submodule.<name>.url (resolving relative URLs), the update strategy and the active flag from .gitmodules data.

nodes.name: module_init
nodes.summary: Subcommand `init`: computes the module list for the pathspec and runs init_submodule on each entry.

nodes.name: print_status
nodes.summary: Prints a single `git submodule status` line with the state character, object id, display path and a `git describe` name.

nodes.name: status_submodule
nodes.summary: Computes the status of one submodule (uninitialized, merge conflict, modified, up to date) by running diff-files in the superproject and reading the submodule HEAD, recursing when asked.

nodes.name: module_status
nodes.summary: Subcommand `status`: lists submodule gitlinks and prints the status of each through status_submodule.

nodes.name: module_cb_list_release
nodes.summary: Frees all entries of a module_cb_list used while summarising submodule changes.

nodes.name: print_submodule_summary
nodes.summary: Formats and prints one entry of `git submodule summary`: the arrow range, commit count and the subjects of the commits in the submodule.

nodes.name: generate_submodule_summary
nodes.summary: Prepares the data for a summary line: finds source and destination commit ids, abbreviates them, counts commits with `rev-list --first-parent --count` inside the submodule and warns on missing commits.

nodes.name: prepare_submodule_summary
nodes.summary: Walks the changed-module list and generates a summary for each, honouring the submodule.<name>.ignore setting when the summary is for `git status`.

nodes.name: submodule_summary_callback
nodes.summary: diff-index callback that collects changed gitlink entries (source/destination mode and object id) into a module_cb_list.

nodes.name: verify_submodule_committish
nodes.summary: Uses `rev-parse --short` inside a submodule to check that a commit-ish exists and returns its abbreviated id.

nodes.name: get_diff_cmd
nodes.summary: Maps the diff mode enum to the diff command name (diff-index, diff-files).

nodes.name: compute_summary_module_list
nodes.summary: Runs diff-index or diff-files on the superproject through the revision machinery and gathers the list of changed submodules for the summary.

nodes.name: module_summary
nodes.summary: Subcommand `summary`: parses options, resolves the commit to compare with, collects changed submodules with compute_summary_module_list and prints their summaries.

nodes.name: module_gitdir
nodes.summary: Subcommand `gitdir`: prints the path of the git directory that stores a submodule given its name.

nodes.name: module_migrate
nodes.summary: Subcommand `migrate-gitdir-configs`: scans .git/modules and writes `submodule.<name>.gitdir` config for existing git directories, then enables the submodulePathConfig repository extension.

nodes.name: sync_submodule
nodes.summary: Synchronises one submodule URL: writes the resolved URL from .gitmodules into the superproject config and the submodule remote config, recursing into nested submodules.

nodes.name: module_sync
nodes.summary: Subcommand `sync`: runs sync_submodule for each active submodule in the module list.

nodes.name: deinit_submodule
nodes.summary: Deinitialises one submodule: absorbs a nested .git directory, removes the work tree (via `git rm -n` safety check or force), recreates the empty directory and removes its submodule.<name> config section.

nodes.name: module_deinit
nodes.summary: Subcommand `deinit`: validates arguments (--all or paths) and calls deinit_submodule for each matching submodule.

nodes.name: add_possible_reference_from_superproject
nodes.summary: Alternate-odb callback that locates the matching submodule object directory inside a superproject alternate so it can be passed as --reference to a clone.

nodes.name: prepare_possible_alternates
nodes.summary: Reads submodule.alternateLocation and alternateErrorStrategy and, for "superproject", builds --reference arguments from the superproject alternates.

nodes.name: clone_submodule_sm_gitdir
nodes.summary: Returns the gitdir path (under .git/modules) that a submodule of a given name will use.

nodes.name: dir_contains_only_dotgit
nodes.summary: Checks that a directory contains nothing except a .git entry, used to verify a fresh clone target.

nodes.name: clone_submodule
nodes.summary: Clones a submodule into the superproject gitdir with `git clone --no-checkout --separate-git-dir`, honouring depth, reference, filter and ref-format, then connects work tree and gitdir and copies alternate settings.

nodes.name: module_clone
nodes.summary: Subcommand `clone`: parses the clone options and calls clone_submodule to set up the submodule repository.

nodes.name: determine_submodule_update_strategy
nodes.summary: Decides which update strategy (checkout, merge, rebase, none, command) applies to a submodule from the command line, config or .gitmodules.

nodes.name: next_submodule_warn_missing
nodes.summary: Prints a skip message for a submodule that is not initialised or has no .gitmodules entry during update.

nodes.name: prepare_to_clone_next_submodule
nodes.summary: Decides whether a submodule needs cloning during `update` and, if so, fills a child_process that runs `submodule--helper clone` with the proper URL, depth, reference and filter options.

nodes.name: update_clone_get_next_task
nodes.summary: Task source for run_processes_parallel: yields the next submodule clone to start, then retries failed clones once.

nodes.name: update_clone_task_finished
nodes.summary: Callback when a parallel clone ends: schedules a retry on the first failure or stops everything after a second failure.

nodes.name: git_update_clone_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads submodule.fetchjobs to set the number of parallel jobs for update.

nodes.name: is_tip_reachable
nodes.summary: Runs `rev-list -n 1 <oid> --not --all` in the submodule to test whether an object id is already reachable from a ref.

nodes.name: fetch_in_submodule
nodes.summary: Runs `git fetch` inside a submodule, optionally shallow and optionally for one object id from the default remote.

nodes.name: run_update_command
nodes.summary: Runs the chosen update (`checkout`, `rebase`, `merge` or a custom command) with the target object id inside the submodule and reports the outcome.

nodes.name: run_update_procedure
nodes.summary: Fetches the wanted commit into the submodule if it is not reachable (falling back to a direct object fetch) and then applies run_update_command.

nodes.name: remote_submodule_branch
nodes.summary: Determines the branch to follow for `update --remote` from submodule.<name>.branch, .gitmodules, or the superproject current branch when set to ".".

nodes.name: ensure_core_worktree
nodes.summary: Rewrites core.worktree in the submodule config as a relative path so the work tree link stays valid after a move.

nodes.name: update_data_to_args
nodes.summary: Serialises an update_data back into command-line arguments so the update can recurse into nested submodules by a child process.

nodes.name: update_submodule
nodes.summary: Updates one submodule: decides the strategy, resolves the current and wanted commit (from the index or the remote branch), runs the update procedure if they differ and recurses into nested submodules.

nodes.name: update_submodules
nodes.summary: Runs the update across all submodules: first clones missing ones in parallel with run_processes_parallel, then updates each one in order.

nodes.name: module_update
nodes.summary: Subcommand `update`: parses the many update options, optionally initialises submodules, builds the module list and runs update_submodules.

nodes.name: push_check
nodes.summary: Subcommand `push-check`: before a recursive push, checks that the submodule remote is configured and that each push refspec source names a single local ref (or HEAD on the same branch as the superproject).

nodes.name: absorb_git_dirs
nodes.summary: Subcommand `absorbgitdirs`: moves nested .git directories of submodules into the superproject .git/modules via absorb_git_dir_into_superproject.

nodes.name: module_set_url
nodes.summary: Subcommand `set-url`: writes a new URL for a submodule into .gitmodules, reloads it and runs sync_submodule so the repository and submodule config follow.

nodes.name: module_set_branch
nodes.summary: Subcommand `set-branch`: records the tracked branch of a submodule (-b) or the default (-d) in .gitmodules.

nodes.name: module_create_branch
nodes.summary: Subcommand `create-branch`: creates a branch in a submodule from a start point, with tracking, reflog and dry-run options.

nodes.name: append_fetch_remotes
nodes.summary: Appends the list of fetch remotes of an existing git directory to a message, used when `add` finds a leftover submodule gitdir.

nodes.name: add_submodule
nodes.summary: Adds a submodule repository: reuses an existing repository at the path or clones it with clone_submodule and checks out the requested branch.

nodes.name: config_submodule_in_gitmodules
nodes.summary: Writes one `submodule.<name>.<key>` value into the .gitmodules file after checking it can be written.

nodes.name: configure_added_submodule
nodes.summary: Finishes `submodule add`: sets submodule.<name>.url, stages the path and .gitmodules with `git add`, records path/url/branch in .gitmodules and sets the active flag.

nodes.name: die_on_index_match
nodes.summary: Dies if the path to add already exists in the index (unless forced for an existing gitlink).

nodes.name: die_on_repo_without_commits
nodes.summary: Dies if the submodule path is a repository with no commit checked out.

nodes.name: module_add
nodes.summary: Subcommand `add`: validates path, name and URL, resolves relative URLs, picks the submodule gitdir and calls add_submodule then configure_added_submodule.

nodes.name: cmd_submodule__helper
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git submodule--helper`; dispatches to one of seventeen subcommands with OPT_SUBCOMMAND.

nodes.name: module_clone_data
nodes.summary: Parameter block of the clone subcommand (name, path, url, depth, reference, filter, ref format, flags).

nodes.name: submodule_update_clone
nodes.summary: State of the parallel clone phase of `submodule update`: the list of clones, current position, failures to retry and quickstop flag.

nodes.name: update_data
nodes.summary: Aggregates all options and per-submodule state of `submodule update` (strategy, oid, suboid, force, recursive, jobs, filter, remote).

nodes.name: add_data
nodes.summary: Parameter block of `submodule add` (prefix, path, name, repo URL, branch, depth, force).

nodes.name: summary_cb
nodes.summary: State of `submodule summary` (prefix, cached, files, summary limit, argv).

nodes.name: update-index.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command `git update-index`, the low-level editor of the index (staging area). It adds, removes and refreshes cache entries from the working tree, injects entries by mode/object id (--cacheinfo, --index-info), sets assume-unchanged, skip-worktree and fsmonitor bits, restores resolve-undo data, and toggles split index, untracked cache and fsmonitor.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a table of parse-options entries with callbacks (cacheinfo_callback, chmod_callback, ...) that run while the command line is being parsed, so options act in the order they appear. Index changes are made in memory on `the_repository->index` and written once through a lock file at the end of cmd_update_index.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: printf-style helper that prints an action message only when --verbose is set.

nodes.name: test_if_untracked_cache_is_supported
nodes.summary: Probes the file system by creating and removing files and directories to check that mtime of directories behaves well enough for the untracked cache.

nodes.name: mark_ce_flags
nodes.summary: Sets or clears a flag (CE_VALID or CE_SKIP_WORKTREE) on an index entry, invalidating the fsmonitor bit and the cache-tree path.

nodes.name: add_one_path
nodes.summary: Adds or refreshes one file in the index: creates a cache entry from lstat data, writes the blob to the object database (unless info_only) and inserts it with add_index_entry.

nodes.name: process_directory
nodes.summary: Handles a path that is a directory: keeps or updates an existing gitlink, removes a file entry, or adds a nested repository as a gitlink.

nodes.name: process_path
nodes.summary: Decides what to do for one path (skip-worktree, lstat error, directory, regular file) and dispatches to the matching handler.

nodes.name: add_cacheinfo
nodes.summary: Adds an index entry with a given mode, object id and stage without touching the working tree (--cacheinfo).

nodes.name: chmod_path
nodes.summary: Flips the executable bit of an index entry (--chmod=+x|-x).

nodes.name: update_one
nodes.summary: Applies the current command-line mode to one path: marks flags, force-removes it, or stats the path and calls process_path.

nodes.name: read_index_info
nodes.summary: Reads entries in `git ls-files --stage`, `ls-tree` or `apply --index-info` format from stdin and adds, removes or stages them in the index.

nodes.name: read_one_ent
nodes.summary: Looks up a path in a tree and returns an index entry built from its mode and object id.

nodes.name: unresolve_one
nodes.summary: Restores unmerged stages of one path from the resolve-undo record.

nodes.name: do_unresolve
nodes.summary: Runs unresolve_one for every path argument (--unresolve).

nodes.name: do_reupdate
nodes.summary: Implements `--again` (-g): for every merged index entry that differs from HEAD (or all entries when there is no HEAD), re-runs update_one on the path, expanding a sparse index first when a sparse directory entry changed.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Reads the index and runs refresh_index to update cached stat data, marking the index changed when racy timestamps remain.

nodes.name: chmod_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --chmod that validates the (+|-)x argument and stores the sign for later use by chmod_path.

nodes.name: parse_new_style_cacheinfo
nodes.summary: Parses the `mode,object,path` form of --cacheinfo.

nodes.name: cacheinfo_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --cacheinfo (old and new style); adds the entry with add_cacheinfo.

nodes.name: stdin_cacheinfo_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --index-info (and -z variant): requires it to be the last argument, turns on add, replace and remove, and reads the entries from stdin through read_index_info.

nodes.name: stdin_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --stdin: requires it to be the last argument and sets the flag that makes cmd_update_index read path names from standard input.

nodes.name: unresolve_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --unresolve: consumes the remaining arguments, restores their merge stages through do_unresolve and drops index changes if it failed.

nodes.name: reupdate_callback
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for --again: runs do_reupdate for the remaining path arguments.

nodes.name: cmd_update_index
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git update-index`: parses options step by step, takes the index lock, applies updates inside an object-database transaction, toggles split index, untracked cache and fsmonitor, and writes the index once.

nodes.name: cache-tree.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the cache-tree, the index extension that remembers the tree object id of every directory so that write-tree and commit can reuse unchanged subtrees. Declares struct cache_tree and cache_tree_sub, update/invalidate/verify/read/write functions, write_index_as_tree and the WRITE_TREE_* flags and error codes.

nodes.name: checkout.h
nodes.summary: Tiny header declaring unique_tracking_name, which finds the one remote-tracking branch matching a name so that `git checkout <name>` and `git switch` can DWIM-create a local tracking branch.

nodes.name: cache_tree
nodes.summary: Directory node of the cache-tree: remembers the tree object id of a directory (entry_count negative means invalid) and owns an array of subtree entries.

nodes.name: cache_tree_sub
nodes.summary: Named child link of a cache_tree node, holding the subtree and its name with a flexible array member.

nodes.name: diff-lib.c
nodes.summary: Library behind `git diff-files` and `git diff-index`: compares the index against the working tree (run_diff_files) or a tree against the index/working tree (run_diff_index via unpack_trees one-way merge), handling unmerged stages, submodules, sparse directories and intent-to-add entries. Results are queued as diff filepairs and flushed through diffcore_std and diff_flush; also exposes index_differs_from, diff_get_merge_base and show_interdiff.

nodes.name: check_removed
nodes.summary: Checks whether the working-tree entry for an index entry has been removed, taking fsmonitor, symlinked leading paths and submodule directories into account.

nodes.name: match_stat_with_submodule
nodes.summary: Compares an index entry with lstat data and, for gitlinks, also asks whether the submodule is modified or dirty according to the diff options.

nodes.name: run_diff_files
nodes.summary: Core of `git diff-files`: walks the index, compares each entry with the working tree (including unmerged stages and combined diffs), queues changes with diff_change/diff_addremove and flushes via diffcore_std and diff_flush.

nodes.name: diff_index_show_file
nodes.summary: Queues the addition or removal of a file for diff-index by calling diff_addremove.

nodes.name: get_stat_data
nodes.summary: Returns the object id and mode of an index entry, or of the working-tree file when the entry is stale and not cached-only.

nodes.name: show_new_file
nodes.summary: Handles a path present only in the index while diffing against a tree, treating sparse directories as tree diffs.

nodes.name: show_modified
nodes.summary: Handles a path present in both tree and index: compares stat data, builds combined-diff paths for merges and queues a diff_change.

nodes.name: do_oneway_diff
nodes.summary: Per-path logic for diff-index: decides cached or working-tree comparison, handles unmerged entries, additions, removals and modifications.

nodes.name: oneway_diff
nodes.summary: unpack_trees callback that adapts the merge-style (index, tree) pair to a diff and applies pathspec filtering.

nodes.name: diff_cache
nodes.summary: Runs a one-way unpack_trees of a tree against the index with oneway_diff as the callback, which produces the diff-index result.

nodes.name: diff_get_merge_base
nodes.summary: Computes the single merge base of the given commits (or of one commit and HEAD) for the --merge-base option, failing on ranges or multiple bases.

nodes.name: run_diff_index
nodes.summary: Core of `git diff-index`: diffs a tree (or its merge base) against the index or working tree, then runs diffcore_std and diff_flush.

nodes.name: do_diff_cache
nodes.summary: Queues the differences between a tree and the index into the given diff options without flushing, for callers like commit and status.

nodes.name: index_differs_from
nodes.summary: Reports whether the index differs from HEAD or another revision, by running a quiet diff-index.

nodes.name: show_interdiff
nodes.summary: Shows the diff between two trees as an indented patch, used for the interdiff in format-patch.

nodes.name: idiff_prefix_cb
nodes.summary: Output-prefix callback that returns the indent string for show_interdiff.

nodes.name: diffcore-pickaxe.c
nodes.summary: Diffcore transformer for the pickaxe options `-S`, `-G` and `--find-object`: filters the queued diff filepairs, keeping those where the count of a string or regex changes (-S), where an added or removed line matches a regex (-G), or where a given object id appears. With --pickaxe-all it keeps or drops the whole changeset.

nodes.name: diffgrep_consume
nodes.summary: xdiff line callback for -G that tests added and removed lines against the regex and records the first hit.

nodes.name: diff_grep
nodes.summary: Implements -G for a filepair: runs a textual xdiff between both sides and checks whether the regex matches an added or removed line.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Counts occurrences of a regex or fixed string (kwset) in a buffer, stopping at an optional limit.

nodes.name: has_changes
nodes.summary: Implements -S: returns whether the number of occurrences of the needle differs between the two sides.

nodes.name: pickaxe_match
nodes.summary: Decides whether one filepair matches: handles --find-object, textconv filters, unmodified pairs and binary files, then calls the match function on both blobs.

nodes.name: pickaxe
nodes.summary: Filters the diff queue, keeping matching filepairs or, with --pickaxe-all, the whole changeset if any pair matches.

nodes.name: regcomp_or_die
nodes.summary: Compiles a regular expression and dies with the regerror message on failure.

nodes.name: diffcore_pickaxe
nodes.summary: Diffcore entry point for -S, -G and --find-object: prepares the regex or kwset matcher from the diff options and filters diff_queued_diff.

nodes.name: diffcore.h
nodes.summary: Internal header shared between diff.c and its transformers (rename, break, pickaxe, order, rotate). Defines the core diff data model: diff_filespec (one side of a file), diff_filepair (preimage/postimage pair), diff_queue_struct and the global diff_queued_diff, plus score constants and the diffcore_* entry points.

nodes.name: range_set
nodes.summary: Sorted set of disjoint line ranges used for `-L` line-range tracking in diff filepairs.

nodes.name: diff_filespec
nodes.summary: One side of a diff: blob object id, path, mode, loaded data and flags (binary, dirty submodule, should_free). The internal representation of a file fed to the diff queue.

nodes.name: diff_filepair
nodes.summary: Pair of diff_filespec (`one` is the preimage, `two` the postimage) with score and status; rename and copy detection rewires these pairs.

nodes.name: diff_queue_struct
nodes.summary: Growable array of diff_filepair pointers; the global diff_queued_diff is the queue that every diffcore transformer rewrites in turn.

nodes.name: obj_order
nodes.summary: Low-level record used by order_objects to sort objects according to an orderfile.

nodes.name: dir.c
nodes.summary: Implements the directory listing API: walks the work tree to find untracked and ignored paths, parses and matches .gitignore and sparse-checkout patterns, matches pathspecs, and persists the untracked cache index extension. Also holds helpers for removing directories, case-aware path comparison and wiring a work tree to its git directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Large C file built around the struct dir_struct traversal state; static helper functions are paired with prototypes near the top, and on-disk untracked-cache data is encoded with varints and EWAH bitmaps.

nodes.name: dir.h
nodes.summary: Public header of the directory listing API: struct dir_struct and its DIR_* flags, pattern_list/path_pattern types for ignore rules, the untracked cache structures, and prototypes for fill_directory, pattern matching, path comparison and worktree/git-dir connection helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Calling sequence is documented in the header comment: dir_init, add patterns, fill_directory, read dir.entries[], dir_clear.

nodes.name: entry.c
nodes.summary: Writes index entries out to the working tree during checkout: creates leading directories, converts blobs to working-tree format, writes files, symlinks and submodule directories, and handles delayed (async filter) checkout, name collisions on clone, and removal of entries.

nodes.name: entry.h
nodes.summary: Header for checkout of index entries: defines struct checkout (options such as force, quiet, clone, refresh_cache) and declares checkout_entry_ca, delayed checkout, unlink_entry and blob reading helpers.

nodes.name: fsmonitor-ll.h
nodes.summary: Low-level header for the fsmonitor index extension: declares reading, writing, adding and removing the extension, refreshing the CE_FSMONITOR_VALID state through the configured integration, and the trivial-response check.

nodes.name: cached_dir
nodes.summary: Iteration state for one directory read: either a live opendir/readdir handle or the cached entries of an untracked_cache_dir, so traversal can use the untracked cache transparently.

nodes.name: ondisk_untracked_cache
nodes.summary: On-disk header layout of the untracked cache index extension: stat data of info/exclude and the excludes file plus the dir_flags it was built with.

nodes.name: paths_collide
nodes.summary: Reports whether two paths collide on the file system, either by differing only in case or by one lying under a symlink at the other path.

nodes.name: git_fnmatch
nodes.summary: Matches a string against a pathspec pattern with fnmatch semantics, honouring a literal prefix, case folding and the glob/literal pathspec magic.

nodes.name: match_pathspec_item
nodes.summary: Decides whether a single pathspec item matches a path, trying exact, prefix, recursive-leading and wildcard matches and returning the strength of the match.

nodes.name: do_match_pathspec
nodes.summary: Runs every item of a pathspec against a path, records which items matched in the seen[] array, and keeps the most specific match, handling exclude magic.

nodes.name: match_pathspec
nodes.summary: Public entry that evaluates a pathspec (positive and negative items) against a path and reports whether it is selected.

nodes.name: report_path_error
nodes.summary: After a command has matched its pathspec, reports the pathspec items that never matched any path as an error message.

nodes.name: add_pattern_to_hashsets
nodes.summary: For cone-mode sparse-checkout, stores parsed patterns in the recursive and parent hashmaps so path lookups avoid a linear scan of the pattern list.

nodes.name: add_pattern
nodes.summary: Parses one gitignore-style line into a path_pattern with its flags (negative, must-be-dir, ends-with, no-dir) and appends it to a pattern_list.

nodes.name: add_patterns
nodes.summary: Reads an ignore or sparse-checkout file (or the index blob when the worktree file is skip-worktree), parses its lines into a pattern_list, and records the file stat and object ID for untracked-cache validation.

nodes.name: path_matches_pattern_list
nodes.summary: Scans an ordered pattern_list for a path (via cone-mode hashmaps or the linear list) and returns matched, not matched or undecided, last match winning.

nodes.name: prep_exclude
nodes.summary: Maintains the stack of per-directory exclude lists while walking: pops lists for directories left, pushes and loads .gitignore for each new directory, and stops early if a parent directory is excluded.

nodes.name: last_matching_pattern
nodes.summary: Loads the exclude lists for the directory of a path via prep_exclude, then returns the last pattern across command-line, per-directory and fallback lists that matches it.

nodes.name: is_excluded
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path is ignored, by taking the last matching pattern and treating a negative pattern as not excluded.

nodes.name: treat_directory
nodes.summary: Decides how the traversal treats a directory that is not tracked: ignore it, show it as a single directory, treat it as a gitlink, or recurse into it, based on the index and DIR_* flags.

nodes.name: get_dtype
nodes.summary: Returns the d_type of a dirent, falling back to lstat or index lookup when the file system reports DT_UNKNOWN, optionally following one symlink.

nodes.name: treat_path
nodes.summary: Classifies one directory entry during traversal (skip .git, index-tracked, excluded, untracked, or recurse) using exclude rules, the index and the pathspec.

nodes.name: valid_cached_dir
nodes.summary: Checks whether an untracked_cache_dir is still valid by comparing directory stat data and the .gitignore object ID, invalidating it otherwise.

nodes.name: read_directory_recursive
nodes.summary: Core recursive walk of the work tree: opens a directory (from cache or readdir), asks treat_path about each entry, recurses when told to, and files results into entries[] or ignored[].

nodes.name: read_directory
nodes.summary: Top-level traversal entry: validates the untracked cache, handles leading path components, runs read_directory_recursive, sorts the results and emits trace2 statistics.

nodes.name: fill_directory
nodes.summary: Public API that computes the pathspec common prefix and calls read_directory, filling dir->entries[] (and ignored[]) for the work tree.

nodes.name: remove_dir_recurse
nodes.summary: Recursively deletes a directory tree honoring REMOVE_DIR_* flags such as keep-toplevel, keep-nested-git and empty-only.

nodes.name: setup_standard_excludes
nodes.summary: Sets up the standard exclude sources: per-directory .gitignore, core.excludesfile and the repository info/exclude file.

nodes.name: write_untracked_extension
nodes.summary: Serializes the untracked cache into the index extension buffer: header with stat data and exclude hashes, then the directory tree with EWAH bitmaps for valid, check-only and sha1-valid flags.

nodes.name: read_untracked_extension
nodes.summary: Parses the untracked cache index extension from raw bytes back into struct untracked_cache, returning NULL if the data is malformed or not fully consumed.

nodes.name: untracked_cache_invalidate_path
nodes.summary: Invalidates the untracked cache entries for the directories along a path when a file is added, removed or changed in the index.

nodes.name: connect_work_tree_and_git_dir
nodes.summary: Links a work tree to its git directory by writing a .git file containing gitdir and setting core.worktree in the git directory config, optionally recursing into nested submodules.

nodes.name: create_directories
nodes.summary: Creates every missing leading directory for a checkout path, replacing a conflicting file or symlink with a directory when force is set.

nodes.name: remove_subtree
nodes.summary: Recursively removes a directory and everything in it, dying on any error; used when a directory blocks a file being checked out.

nodes.name: read_blob_entry
nodes.summary: Reads the blob for a cache entry from the object database and returns its bytes, or NULL if the object is missing or not a blob.

nodes.name: streaming_write_entry
nodes.summary: Writes a regular file by streaming the blob from the object database through a stream filter directly into the output file descriptor.

nodes.name: finish_delayed_checkout
nodes.summary: Completes delayed checkout: repeatedly asks external filter processes which blobs are ready, then checks those entries out, reporting any path never filtered.

nodes.name: update_ce_after_write
nodes.summary: After a file is written, refreshes the cache entry stat data, flags it for update and invalidates its fsmonitor state when the checkout refreshes the index.

nodes.name: write_entry
nodes.summary: Writes one cache entry to disk by mode: regular files (converted to working-tree format, possibly delayed), symlinks, or submodule directories, then updates the index stat info.

nodes.name: mark_colliding_entries
nodes.summary: On clone, marks index entries whose paths collide with an entry just written (same inode or case/symlink collision) so a warning can be shown.

nodes.name: checkout_entry_ca
nodes.summary: Main checkout routine: checks the existing path, handles submodules and force/overwrite rules, creates directories, then writes the entry directly or enqueues it for parallel checkout.

nodes.name: unlink_entry
nodes.summary: Removes the working-tree file of an index entry (moving submodule HEAD if needed) and schedules its leading directories for removal when they become empty.

nodes.name: fsmonitor.c
nodes.summary: Implements fsmonitor integration with the index: reads and writes the FSMN index extension (an EWAH bitmap of dirty entries plus a token), queries either the hook or the built-in IPC daemon for changed paths, and clears CE_FSMONITOR_VALID and untracked-cache state for those paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses NUL-separated query responses where a single "/" means a trivial response (treat everything as dirty); handles case-insensitive file systems through the name-hash and dir-name-hash.

nodes.name: fsmonitor.h
nodes.summary: Header that pulls in fsmonitor-ll.h, dir.h and fsmonitor settings and defines inline helpers to mark a cache entry fsmonitor-valid or invalid, plus a check that refresh_fsmonitor has run.

nodes.name: lockfile.h
nodes.summary: Documents and declares the lockfile API: create a .lock file with O_EXCL, write new contents, then atomically rename it into place or roll it back, with cleanup on exit or signals through the tempfile module. Provides inline wrappers for timeouts, modes and fd/FILE access.
nodes.languageNotes: Thin static-inline wrappers over a small set of exported functions; struct lock_file embeds a tempfile.

nodes.name: match-trees.h
nodes.summary: Declares shift_tree and shift_tree_by, which adjust a tree object to line up with another tree at a different path prefix (used by subtree merging).

nodes.name: read_fsmonitor_extension
nodes.summary: Parses the FSMN index extension (version 1 timestamp or version 2 token plus an EWAH bitmap of dirty entries) into the index_state.

nodes.name: write_fsmonitor_extension
nodes.summary: Serializes the FSMN index extension with the last-update token and the EWAH bitmap of entries that are not fsmonitor-valid.

nodes.name: query_fsmonitor_hook
nodes.summary: Runs the configured fsmonitor hook script with a protocol version and last-update token, capturing its output as the list of changed paths.

nodes.name: handle_using_name_hash_icase
nodes.summary: On case-insensitive file systems, finds the index entry for a path whose case differs by using the name hash, and invalidates its fsmonitor-valid bit.

nodes.name: fsmonitor_refresh_callback
nodes.summary: Handles one path reported by fsmonitor: invalidates the matching file or every index entry under a directory, with a case-insensitive fallback.

nodes.name: refresh_fsmonitor
nodes.summary: Queries fsmonitor (built-in IPC daemon or hook, v1 or v2) once per command, then marks reported paths dirty in the index and untracked cache, or invalidates everything on failure or a trivial response; finally saves the new token.

nodes.name: add_fsmonitor
nodes.summary: Turns fsmonitor on for an index: initializes the token, clears all valid bits, resets untracked-cache usage and performs a first refresh.

nodes.name: tweak_fsmonitor
nodes.summary: Reconciles the index with the current core.fsmonitor setting: restores valid bits from the saved bitmap when enabled, then adds or removes the extension.

nodes.name: am.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git am`: splits mailboxes (mbox, Maildir, StGit, Mercurial) into individual patches, applies each with the apply machinery, falls back to a 3-way merge when needed, and records each result as a commit on HEAD. Progress is kept in the .git/rebase-apply directory so the run can be resumed with --continue, --skip or --abort.
nodes.languageNotes: C state machine persisted as small files in the am state directory; uses die()/BUG() for error exits and goto next for the per-patch loop.

nodes.name: am_state
nodes.summary: In-memory form of an am session: the state directory path, current and last patch numbers, parsed author and message of the current patch, plus flags such as threeway, signoff, rebasing and the git-apply options. It mirrors the files stored under rebase-apply.

nodes.name: am_load
nodes.summary: Reads a saved am session back from the state directory (next and last counters, author script, commit message, original commit and flags like threeway, quiet, keep, scissors, apply options) so an interrupted git am can be resumed.

nodes.name: detect_patch_format
nodes.summary: Guesses the input patch format by inspecting the first lines of the first file: mbox (From lines), StGit series or single patch, or Mercurial changeset; stdin and directories default to mbox.

nodes.name: split_mail
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the patch format and splits the input into numbered one-patch files in the state directory, using mailsplit for mbox/mboxrd and converters for StGit and Hg input.

nodes.name: am_setup
nodes.summary: Creates the rebase-apply state directory, drops REBASE_HEAD, splits the mails, and writes the initial state files and ORIG_HEAD abort-safety data for a new am session.

nodes.name: am_next
nodes.summary: Advances to the next patch: clears author and message fields, removes per-patch files and REBASE_HEAD, records the current HEAD as abort-safety, and increments the next counter.

nodes.name: parse_mail
nodes.summary: Runs mailinfo on one split mail to extract author, date, subject and message body plus the patch text, applies keep-subject rules, and stores the results in the am state.

nodes.name: run_apply
nodes.summary: Invokes the apply machinery in-process on the current patch, either against the working tree and index or against a temporary index file, forwarding the user-supplied git-apply options.

nodes.name: fall_back_threeway
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a base tree from the blob ids on the patch index lines (a fake ancestor), applies the patch to it, and runs merge-ort between HEAD and the patched tree; calls rerere when the merge conflicts.

nodes.name: do_commit
nodes.summary: Runs the pre-applypatch hook, writes the index as a tree object, creates a commit with the patch author and message, advances HEAD with a reflog entry, records rewritten pairs when rebasing, then runs post-applypatch.

nodes.name: am_run
nodes.summary: Main loop over patches: verifies the index is clean, parses each mail, applies it (falling back to 3-way if allowed), commits it and advances, stopping with an error state on conflicts or when interactive mode asks to skip.

nodes.name: am_resolve
nodes.summary: Handles git am --continue: validates the resume state, checks that the index has changes and no unmerged paths (otherwise tells the user to git add or skip), runs rerere, commits the patch with do_commit, and moves on.

nodes.name: fast_forward_to
nodes.summary: Moves the working tree and index from one tree to another with a two-way unpack_trees merge under a locked index, used by --skip and --abort to restore state.

nodes.name: merge_tree
nodes.summary: Resets the index and working tree to match a tree object with a one-way unpack_trees merge under the index lock.

nodes.name: am_abort
nodes.summary: Handles `git am --abort`: checks it is safe, clears rerere state, restores the index and HEAD to ORIG_HEAD (or removes an unborn branch), and deletes the session state.

nodes.name: cmd_am
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git am`: parses options, decides between starting a new session and --continue/--skip/--abort/--show-current-patch, sets up the state, and calls am_run.

nodes.name: bisect.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git bisect` as a family of subcommands (start, good/bad or custom terms, skip, next, reset, log, replay, visualize, run, terms). It records marks as refs under refs/bisect/, writes BISECT_* state files, and calls the bisection computation to pick the next commit to test.
nodes.languageNotes: Subcommands are wired with OPT_SUBCOMMAND; bare `git bisect <term>` falls back to bisect_state after loading custom terms.

nodes.name: bisect_reset
nodes.summary: Implements `git bisect reset`: reads BISECT_START (or uses the given commit) and checks out the original branch unless BISECT_HEAD shows a no-checkout bisection.

nodes.name: bisect_write
nodes.summary: Records a good, bad or skip verdict for a revision by writing refs/bisect/<state> (with the rev suffix for good and skip) and appending the command to BISECT_LOG.

nodes.name: decide_next
nodes.summary: Decides whether bisection can proceed when the good or bad side is still missing, warning or prompting the user (for example bisecting with only a bad commit) or returning an error with usage guidance.

nodes.name: bisect_status
nodes.summary: Counts how many bad and good marks exist by looking up refs under refs/bisect/ with the configured term names.

nodes.name: bisect_print_status
nodes.summary: Prints and logs what the bisection is still waiting for (a good commit, a bad commit, or both) when it cannot start yet.

nodes.name: get_terms
nodes.summary: Loads the custom bisect terms from BISECT_TERMS (first line the bad term, second line the good term), optionally tolerating a missing file.

nodes.name: prepare_revs
nodes.summary: Sets up a revision walk whose positive tips are the bad ref and whose UNINTERESTING tips are all good refs, reading them from refs/bisect/.

nodes.name: bisect_skipped_commits
nodes.summary: When only skipped commits remain, walks the candidate range and appends each possible first-bad commit to BISECT_LOG as a comment.

nodes.name: bisect_successful
nodes.summary: After the first bad commit has been found, resolves the bad ref to a commit and appends a line naming it (hash and subject) to BISECT_LOG.

nodes.name: bisect_next
nodes.summary: Runs one bisection step: auto-starts if needed, checks that marks exist, calls bisect_next_all to compute and check out the midpoint, and reports a found commit or an only-skipped result.

nodes.name: bisect_auto_next
nodes.summary: Starts the next step if both a good and a bad mark exist; otherwise prints the waiting status and returns OK.

nodes.name: bisect_start
nodes.summary: Implements `git bisect start`: parses revisions and pathspecs, resets previous state, writes BISECT_START, BISECT_NAMES and BISECT_TERMS, marks given bad and good revisions, and triggers the first step.

nodes.name: bisect_autostart
nodes.summary: If BISECT_START is missing, tells the user to start first and, on an interactive terminal, offers to run bisect_start with no arguments for them.

nodes.name: bisect_state
nodes.summary: Handles git bisect good, bad, skip or a custom term: resolves each revision argument to a commit, writes the marks via bisect_write, drops BISECT_ANCESTORS_OK and BISECT_EXPECTED_REV when the verdict does not match the expected revision, and runs the next step.

nodes.name: bisect_log
nodes.summary: Prints the BISECT_LOG file to stdout, failing when no bisection is in progress.

nodes.name: process_replay_line
nodes.summary: Parses one line of a bisect log during replay, recognizing git bisect start, terms and good, bad or skip commands, and applies it through bisect_start, bisect_terms or bisect_write.

nodes.name: bisect_replay
nodes.summary: Implements `git bisect replay`: clears existing state, feeds each log line to process_replay_line, then continues to the next bisection step.

nodes.name: bisect_skip
nodes.summary: Implements git bisect skip: expands any A..B ranges into individual commits with a revision walk, then passes the commits to bisect_state as skip marks.

nodes.name: bisect_visualize
nodes.summary: Launches gitk (when a display is available) or `git log` restricted to --bisect over the saved paths, showing the remaining candidate range.

nodes.name: verify_good
nodes.summary: Checks out the first good revision, runs the user command on it, and restores the original revision, returning the command exit code, to confirm that exit codes 126 or 127 are not caused by a broken script.

nodes.name: bisect_run
nodes.summary: Implements git bisect run: repeatedly runs a command, maps its exit code to good (0), skip (125) or bad (other codes below 128), records the mark through bisect_state while capturing its output, and stops when the first bad commit is found or an error occurs.

nodes.name: cmd_bisect
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git bisect`: dispatches the subcommands, treats a bare term as a state command, and on success may reset the checkout according to the reset-when-found setting.

nodes.name: blame.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git blame` and `git annotate`: sets up a blame scoreboard for a file and line ranges, runs the blame algorithm over history (with copy, move, ignore-revs and mailmap support), and prints the result in default, porcelain, incremental or colored formats.
nodes.languageNotes: Output formatting lives here, while the scoreboard and attribution algorithm live in blame.c at the top level.

nodes.name: commit_info
nodes.summary: Holds author, committer, timestamp, time zone and summary strings of a commit shown next to a blamed line.

nodes.name: get_commit_info
nodes.summary: Re-encodes the commit message and extracts the author and committer lines (name, email, time, time zone) and the one-line subject into a commit_info.

nodes.name: emit_porcelain
nodes.summary: Writes the machine-readable porcelain block for a blame entry: hash with source and final line numbers and group size, commit details the first time it appears (or every line with --line-porcelain), and the tab-prefixed source lines.

nodes.name: emit_other
nodes.summary: Prints the human-readable blame lines of an entry: abbreviated hash, optional filename, author or email, date, line numbers and the source line, with color-by-line or color-by-age support.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Walks the final list of blame entries and prints each through emit_porcelain or emit_other depending on the selected output option.

nodes.name: find_alignment
nodes.summary: Scans all entries to compute the widest author, filename and line-number columns and an automatic hash abbreviation length, so the default output lines up.

nodes.name: git_blame_config
nodes.summary: Reads blame.* settings (showRoot, blankBoundary, showEmail, date, coloring, markIgnoredLines and similar) plus the shared color and diff config.

nodes.name: blame_copy_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for -C: each repetition widens copy detection (from removed files, to existing files in new files, to existing files everywhere), and an optional argument sets the copy score.

nodes.name: build_ignorelist
nodes.summary: Collects revisions to ignore from --ignore-rev and --ignore-revs-file into the scoreboard, resolving each to a commit id.

nodes.name: cmd_blame
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git blame`: parses options and arguments, builds the revision setup and scoreboard, initializes line ranges, runs assign_blame, then sorts, coalesces and prints the entries.

nodes.name: branch.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git branch`: lists, creates, renames, copies and deletes local and remote-tracking branches, edits descriptions and upstream settings, and deletes merged branches. All operations work on refs under refs/heads and refs/remotes through the ref store and ref-filter machinery.

nodes.name: stacked_branch_data
nodes.summary: Callback state for finding branches whose upstream is itself a branch that is about to be deleted, so those bases can be protected.

nodes.name: git_branch_config
nodes.summary: Reads branch.sort, column.*, color.branch and color.branch.<slot>, submodule.recurse and submodule.propagateBranches, then defers to the shared color and default config handlers.

nodes.name: branch_merged
nodes.summary: Decides whether a branch is fully merged by checking whether its tip is in the merge bases of its upstream or HEAD, and warns when the answer differs between upstream and HEAD.

nodes.name: check_branch_commit
nodes.summary: Resolves the commit of a branch to be deleted and refuses unless it is merged, honouring the force and skip-unmerged flags.

nodes.name: delete_branches
nodes.summary: Deletes the named local or remote-tracking branches: resolves each name, checks merge status with check_branch_commit, then removes all refs with refs_delete_refs (or only reports in dry-run) and deletes their branch config sections.

nodes.name: print_ref_list
nodes.summary: Filters refs matching the requested kind, builds or verifies the output format, computes ahead/behind when needed, sorts them, and prints them either directly or through the column layout.

nodes.name: copy_or_rename_branch
nodes.summary: Renames or copies a branch ref, checking worktrees that have it checked out, moving the reflog and branch.<name>.* config section, and updating symbolic HEADs.

nodes.name: collect_stacked_branch_base
nodes.summary: Ref iteration callback that marks a branch as protected when some surviving branch uses it as its upstream.

nodes.name: protect_stacked_branch_bases
nodes.summary: Iterates all local branches and removes from the deletable set any branch that is the upstream of a branch that will be kept.

nodes.name: clear_deleted_upstreams
nodes.summary: After merged branches are deleted, unsets branch.<name>.merge and branch.<name>.remote for retained branches whose upstream was among the deleted ones.

nodes.name: branch_pushes_to_upstream
nodes.summary: Applies the remote push and fetch refspecs to a branch to test whether pushing it would update its own upstream tracking ref.

nodes.name: delete_merged_branches
nodes.summary: Implements --delete-merged: filters branches forked from the given upstreams, keeps those that are merged and not checked out, protects stacked bases, then deletes the rest and clears dangling upstream config.

nodes.name: edit_branch_description
nodes.summary: Opens the editor on a temporary file seeded with the current branch description and stores the stripped result as branch.<name>.description in config.

nodes.name: die_if_upstream_looks_like_remote
nodes.summary: Gives a hint when a requested upstream does not exist but its name looks like a remote or remote-tracking branch, then dies.

nodes.name: cmd_branch
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git branch`: parses the many action flags and routes to list, delete, delete-merged, rename or copy, set or unset upstream, edit description, show current, or create a branch.

nodes.name: check-attr.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git check-attr`: for each given path (from arguments or stdin) it looks up gitattributes values and prints them, either for named attributes or all attributes with -a.

nodes.name: output_attr
nodes.summary: Prints each attribute of the check as "path: name: value", translating true, false and unset into set, unset and unspecified, with NUL-separated output when -z is used.

nodes.name: check_attr
nodes.summary: Resolves one path relative to the prefix, asks the attribute machinery for either the selected or all attributes, and prints them.

nodes.name: check_attr_stdin_paths
nodes.summary: Reads paths from stdin (line or NUL terminated, C-unquoting quoted lines when not NUL terminated) and runs check_attr on each, flushing stdout after each.

nodes.name: cmd_check_attr
nodes.summary: Entry point of git check-attr: reads the index, interprets the attribute names, -a, -- and --stdin combinations, validates them, builds the attr_check (optionally with a tree-ish source) and checks each path.

nodes.name: check-mailmap.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git check-mailmap`: reads the mailmap and prints the canonical name and email for each contact given on the command line or stdin.

nodes.name: check_mailmap
