nodes.summary: Splits a contact into name and email (or treats it as a bare address), maps it through the mailmap, and prints "Name <email>".

nodes.name: cmd_check_mailmap
nodes.summary: Entry point of git check-mailmap: loads the repository mailmap plus an optional blob or file, then maps each contact argument and, with --stdin, each stdin line.

nodes.name: clean.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git clean`: finds untracked (and optionally ignored) files and directories with the dir machinery and removes them, with a dry-run mode and an interactive menu for filtering, selecting or confirming deletions.

nodes.name: menu_opts
nodes.summary: Describes a menu prompt for the interactive mode: header text, prompt text and flags such as singleton selection.

nodes.name: menu_item
nodes.summary: One entry in the interactive command menu: a hotkey, a title, a selected flag and a handler function.

nodes.name: menu_stuff
nodes.summary: Generic list of choices for a menu, tagged as either a string list or an array of menu_item.

nodes.name: git_clean_config
nodes.summary: Reads column.*, color.interactive and its slot colors, and clean.requireForce, then defers to the shared color and default config handlers.

nodes.name: remove_dirs
nodes.summary: Recursively removes a directory: skips nested Git repositories unless forced, deletes files, recurses into subdirectories, then rmdirs, honouring dry-run and quiet and reporting whether the directory is gone.

nodes.name: pretty_print_dels
nodes.summary: Prints the paths queued for deletion, quoted and always in column layout, for the interactive menu.

nodes.name: print_highlight_menu_stuff
nodes.summary: Builds the numbered menu lines (marking already chosen entries with an asterisk and highlighting each item hotkey in color) and prints them in rows.

nodes.name: find_unique
nodes.summary: Finds the single menu item or string that matches a typed prefix or hotkey, returning 0 when the match is ambiguous or missing.

nodes.name: parse_choice
nodes.summary: Parses a user input line of numbers, ranges, names and "-" deselections into an array of chosen menu entries.

nodes.name: list_and_choose
nodes.summary: Shows a numbered menu and loops reading input until the user finishes, returning the chosen indexes.

nodes.name: filter_by_patterns_cmd
nodes.summary: Interactive command that asks for ignore patterns and drops matching paths from the deletion list using an exclude pattern list.

nodes.name: select_by_numbers_cmd
nodes.summary: Interactive command that lets the user pick entries by number to be cleaned and discards the others.

nodes.name: ask_each_cmd
nodes.summary: Interactive command that asks y/n for each path and removes the confirmed ones from the list.

nodes.name: interactive_main_loop
nodes.summary: Drives the main interactive menu (clean, filter by pattern, select by numbers, ask each, quit, help) until files are cleaned or the user quits.

nodes.name: correct_untracked_entries
nodes.summary: Rewrites the untracked entries list so that a directory containing ignored paths is dropped and entries nested inside a kept directory are not listed twice.

nodes.name: cmd_clean
nodes.summary: Entry point of git clean: parses options, enforces clean.requireForce, loads the index, scans the working tree for untracked or ignored paths with fill_directory, builds the deletion list, optionally runs the interactive menu, then deletes files and directories.

nodes.name: column.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git column`: reads lines from stdin and prints them in a column layout using the shared column library, with width, indent and padding options.

nodes.name: cmd_column
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git column`: reads config for the named command, parses layout options, reads stdin lines, and prints them as columns.

nodes.name: commit-graph.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git commit-graph` with the write and verify subcommands: builds or validates the commit-graph file (and split chains with Bloom filters) that accelerates commit walks in the object database.

nodes.name: opts_commit_graph
nodes.summary: Static option block shared by the subcommands: object directory, reachable, stdin-packs, stdin-commits, append, split, shallow, progress and changed-paths flags.

nodes.name: graph_verify
nodes.summary: Opens the commit-graph file or split chain of an object directory, loads it and calls verify_commit_graph, reporting incomplete chains.

nodes.name: write_option_parse_split
nodes.summary: Option callback for --split[=no-merge|replace] that turns on split mode and selects the merge-prohibited or replace strategy.

nodes.name: read_one_commit
nodes.summary: Parses one hex object id from stdin, peels tags with deref_tag, and inserts the resulting commit into an object-id set, reporting invalid input.

nodes.name: graph_write
nodes.summary: Implements `commit-graph write`: validates options, collects commits (from all refs, listed pack indexes, or stdin), and calls the writer with flags for append, split and Bloom filters.

nodes.name: cmd_commit_graph
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git commit-graph`: loads config, disables replace refs and commit buffer saving, and dispatches to graph_write or graph_verify.

nodes.name: commit-tree.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command `git commit-tree`: creates a commit object from a given tree, parents and a message (from -m, -F or stdin), optionally signed, and prints the new commit id.

nodes.name: new_parent
nodes.summary: Appends a parent commit to the parent list, ignoring and reporting a duplicate.

nodes.name: parse_parent_arg_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for -p that resolves the argument to a commit object id, asserts it is a commit in the object database, and adds it as a parent.

nodes.name: parse_file_arg_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback for -F that reads the commit message from a file or stdin into the shared buffer.

nodes.name: cmd_commit_tree
nodes.summary: Entry point of `git commit-tree`: parses options, resolves the tree, reads the message from stdin if none was given, calls commit_tree to write the commit object, and prints its id.

nodes.name: commit.c
nodes.summary: Implements git commit, git status and the shared index-selection logic behind them: it chooses which index to commit (as-is, normal with -a/-i, or a temporary index for partial commits with paths), runs the pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg and commit-msg hooks, builds the message in COMMIT_EDITMSG, writes the commit object with commit_tree_extended and moves HEAD with a reflog entry.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses file-scope static variables for every option and goes to a single exit label with explicit rollback of two lock_file objects (real index and temporary index). Commit parents are chosen by the origin of the commit (initial, amend, merge from MERGE_HEAD, cherry-pick/rebase, plain).

nodes.name: opt_parse_porcelain
nodes.summary: Option callback for --porcelain[=<version>] that maps v1 or v2 to the wt_status porcelain format and dies on an unknown version.

nodes.name: opt_parse_m
nodes.summary: Option callback for -m that appends each message to a strbuf, one paragraph per -m, and records that a message option was given.

nodes.name: opt_parse_rename_score
nodes.summary: Option callback for -M[<n>] on git status that stores the similarity argument, skipping a leading equals sign.

nodes.name: rollback_index_files
nodes.summary: Releases the index lock (and the temporary "false" index lock for partial commits) according to the commit style, undoing any prepared index state.

nodes.name: commit_index_files
nodes.summary: Finalizes the index after a successful commit: commits the real index lock and drops the temporary index used for partial commits.

nodes.name: list_paths
nodes.summary: Takes the union of paths in the index and an overlaid tree (normally HEAD) that match the pathspec, which defines the set of files affected by a partial commit.

nodes.name: add_remove_files
nodes.summary: Updates the in-memory index for each listed path, adding it from the working tree with add_to_index or removing it when the file no longer exists.

nodes.name: create_base_index
nodes.summary: Resets the index to the HEAD tree with a one-way unpack_trees merge (or empties it on an unborn branch), the base for the temporary index of a partial commit.

nodes.name: prepare_index
nodes.summary: Decides the commit style and returns the path of the index file to commit: an interactive-add temporary index, a normal index after add_files_to_cache for -a/-i, the real index as-is, or a temporary "next-index" for a partial commit with paths, taking locks and updating the cache tree as needed.

nodes.name: run_status
nodes.summary: Fills a wt_status with the current options, collects the index/working tree differences and prints them, returning whether anything is committable.

nodes.name: parse_force_date
nodes.summary: Converts the --date argument to the internal "@<epoch> <tz>" form, using parse_date and falling back to approxidate_careful.

nodes.name: determine_author_info
nodes.summary: Computes the author identity from GIT_AUTHOR_* environment variables, the reused commit (-C/-c), --author and --date, formats it with fmt_ident and re-exports the final values to the environment.

nodes.name: adjust_comment_line_char
nodes.summary: Chooses a comment character from a fixed candidate list that does not start any line of the message, used when core.commentChar=auto.

nodes.name: prepare_amend_commit
nodes.summary: Formats the body of the commit being amended for an amend! fixup, avoiding a duplicated subject when it is already an amend! commit.

nodes.name: prepare_to_commit
nodes.summary: Prepares everything before the commit object is written: runs pre-commit, builds COMMIT_EDITMSG from -m/-F/-C/--fixup/MERGE_MSG/SQUASH_MSG/template, appends the status and ident hints, decides whether the commit is empty, writes the cache tree, runs prepare-commit-msg, launches the editor and runs commit-msg.

nodes.name: handle_ignored_arg
nodes.summary: Maps the --ignored mode string (traditional, matching, no) to the wt_status ignored-files mode or dies.

nodes.name: parse_untracked_setting_name
nodes.summary: Parses the untracked-files setting (booleans, no, normal, all) into the untracked_status_type enum.

nodes.name: handle_untracked_files_arg
nodes.summary: Applies the -u/--untracked-files argument to the status settings and dies on an invalid mode.

nodes.name: read_commit_message
nodes.summary: Looks up a commit by name and returns its message re-encoded to the output encoding, used for -C, -c and the author of a cherry-pick.

nodes.name: finalize_deferred_config
nodes.summary: Resolves status format, branch display and ahead/behind settings by combining command-line options with config values deferred until the output format is known.

nodes.name: check_fixup_reword_options
nodes.summary: Rejects --fixup=reword combined with merge/cherry-pick state, pathspecs or content-selecting options.

nodes.name: parse_and_validate_options
nodes.summary: Parses git commit options and enforces their mutual compatibility, including amend, --fixup/--squash, -C/-c/-F/-m, --reset-author, -a/-i/-o/--interactive and merge or cherry-pick state, and loads the reused message and author.

nodes.name: dry_run_commit
nodes.summary: Implements --dry-run and the status output formats of git commit: prepares the index, prints the status and rolls the index back.

nodes.name: git_status_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for status.* and color.status.* keys, filling the wt_status and the deferred settings, and delegating the rest to the diff UI config.

nodes.name: cmd_status
nodes.summary: Entry point of git status: loads config, parses options, refreshes the index, collects the staged, unstaged, untracked and ignored differences with wt_status_collect and prints them in the chosen format.

nodes.name: git_commit_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for commit.template, commit.status, commit.cleanup, commit.gpgsign and commit.verbose, falling back to the status config.

nodes.name: cmd_commit
nodes.summary: Entry point of git commit: parses options, prepares the index and message, determines parents (initial, amend, merge, cherry-pick), writes the commit object, updates HEAD and the reflog, clears merge state, and runs post-commit, auto maintenance and post-rewrite.

nodes.name: status_deferred_config
nodes.summary: Holds status.short, status.branch and status.aheadBehind values read from config so they apply only when the output is not porcelain.

nodes.name: count-objects.c
nodes.summary: Implements git count-objects: walks the loose object directories to count objects and their on-disk size, and with -v also totals packfile objects and sizes, reports garbage in the pack directory, and lists alternates.

nodes.name: bits_to_msg
nodes.summary: Translates the set of pack file kinds seen for one basename (.pack, .idx, garbage) into a warning message, or NULL when a pack and its index are both present.

nodes.name: real_report_garbage
nodes.summary: Verbose-mode handler for stray files in the object directory: adds the file size to the garbage total and prints a warning with the reason.

nodes.name: count_loose
nodes.summary: Callback for each loose object file: counts it, adds its on-disk bytes and, in verbose mode, counts it as prune-packable when the object already exists in a pack.

nodes.name: count_cruft
nodes.summary: Callback for non-object files found among loose objects, reported as garbage.

nodes.name: print_alternate
nodes.summary: Callback that prints one alternate object directory path in C-quoted form.

nodes.name: cmd_count_objects
nodes.summary: Entry point of git count-objects: scans loose objects, and for -v scans local packs for object count and size, then prints the counts, garbage and alternates, optionally in human readable units.

nodes.name: credential.c
nodes.summary: Implements git credential: reads a credential description from stdin and runs fill, approve or reject through the credential subsystem (which drives the configured credential helpers), or announces supported capabilities.

nodes.name: cmd_credential
nodes.summary: Entry point of git credential: parses the subcommand (capability, fill, approve, reject), reads the credential from stdin and calls the matching credential_* function, writing the response for fill.

nodes.name: describe.c
nodes.summary: Implements git describe: finds the most recent reachable tag for a commit (or the commit that introduced a blob), by indexing refs by peeled commit in a hashmap and walking commit parents with a priority queue to compute depth, producing names like v2.1-14-gabcdef.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps a hashmap from peeled commit oid to commit_name (annotated tag priority 2, lightweight 1, other ref 0) and uses per-candidate bit flags on commit objects to track which candidate tags reach each commit.

nodes.name: commit_name_neq
nodes.summary: Hashmap comparison callback that compares commit_name entries by their peeled commit object id.

nodes.name: replace_name
nodes.summary: Decides whether a new ref should replace an existing name for the same commit, preferring annotated over lightweight tags and, among annotated tags, the newer tagger date.

nodes.name: add_to_known_names
nodes.summary: Inserts or replaces the commit_name for a peeled commit in the global hashmap of candidate refs.

nodes.name: get_name
nodes.summary: Ref iterator callback that filters refs by --all, --match and --exclude patterns, peels them to find annotated tags and registers them as candidate names.

nodes.name: compare_pt
nodes.summary: qsort comparator ordering candidate tags by depth and then by the order in which they were found.

nodes.name: finish_depth_computation
nodes.summary: Continues the commit walk after candidate collection to finish computing the depth of the best candidate, tracking commits not yet reached by it.

nodes.name: append_name
nodes.summary: Appends the tag or ref name to the output and warns when an annotated tag is known by a different name than its ref path.

nodes.name: append_suffix
nodes.summary: Appends the "-<depth>-g<abbrev>" suffix to the output name.

nodes.name: describe_commit
nodes.summary: Core algorithm of git describe: returns an exact tag match if present, otherwise walks parents by commit date, collects up to --candidates tags, selects the one with least depth, and formats the name with the distance suffix.

nodes.name: process_commit
nodes.summary: Callback for traverse_commit_list that records the commit currently being visited.

nodes.name: process_object
nodes.summary: Callback for traverse_commit_list that stops the walk when the blob being searched for is found and describes the commit that introduced it.

nodes.name: describe_blob
nodes.summary: Describes a blob by walking history from HEAD in commit order and reporting "<describe of commit>:<path>" for the first commit that contains it.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Resolves one argument to an object and describes it as a commit or blob, printing the result.

nodes.name: option_parse_exact_match
nodes.summary: Option callback for --exact-match that sets the candidate count to zero.

nodes.name: cmd_describe
nodes.summary: Entry point of git describe: parses options, handles --contains by running name-rev, builds the name table from refs, computes -dirty/-broken suffixes by running diff-index, and describes HEAD or each given commit-ish.

nodes.name: commit_name
nodes.summary: Hashmap entry associating a peeled commit oid with a ref path, optional tag object and priority (annotated, lightweight or head).

nodes.name: possible_tag
nodes.summary: Candidate tag during the search, recording its commit_name, depth, discovery order and the bit flag marking commits it can reach.

nodes.name: process_commit_data
nodes.summary: State shared by the traverse_commit_list callbacks when describing a blob.

nodes.name: diff-files.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command git diff-files: compares the index against the working tree through the diff machinery, defaulting to raw output and supporting --base/--ours/--theirs stages for unmerged paths.

nodes.name: cmd_diff_files
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diff-files: sets up revision/diff options, validates that no revisions were given, reads the index with preload and calls run_diff_files.

nodes.name: diff-index.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command git diff-index: compares a tree-ish with the index (--cached) or the working tree via run_diff_index, defaulting to raw output.

nodes.name: cmd_diff_index
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diff-index: parses --cached, --merge-base and -m, requires exactly one tree-ish, reads the index and calls run_diff_index.

nodes.name: diff-pairs.c
nodes.summary: Implements git diff-pairs: reads NUL-delimited raw diff records from stdin, rebuilds the diff queue of file pairs (added, deleted, modified, renamed, copied) and runs the diffcore pipeline and output on them.

nodes.name: parse_mode_or_die
nodes.summary: Parses an octal file mode from a raw diff line or dies.

nodes.name: parse_oid_or_die
nodes.summary: Parses a hex object id followed by a space from a raw diff line or dies.

nodes.name: cmd_diff_pairs
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diff-pairs: for each raw diff record on stdin, queues an add, delete, change or rename/copy filepair, flushes batches on empty lines, then runs diffcore_std and diff_flush.

nodes.name: diff-tree.c
nodes.summary: Implements the plumbing command git diff-tree: compares two trees or a commit with its parents via diff_tree_oid and log_tree_commit, and with --stdin reads commit or tree object ids from standard input.

nodes.name: diff_tree_commit_oid
nodes.summary: Looks up a commit by object id and shows its diff through log_tree_commit.

nodes.name: stdin_diff_commit
nodes.summary: Handles a "commit parent..." stdin line by grafting the given parents onto the commit locally and diffing it.

nodes.name: stdin_diff_trees
nodes.summary: Handles a stdin line naming two trees, printing their ids and diffing them.

nodes.name: diff_tree_stdin
nodes.summary: Parses one stdin line, loads the object and dispatches to commit or tree diffing based on its type.

nodes.name: diff_tree_tweak_rev
nodes.summary: Revision setup hook that selects raw output, or patch output when combined merges are dense.

nodes.name: cmd_diff_tree
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diff-tree: sets up revisions, handles --stdin and --merge-base, diffs one commit against parents or two trees directly, and loops over stdin objects.

nodes.name: diff.c
nodes.summary: Implements the porcelain git diff: classifies its arguments into trees, blobs and paths and dispatches to the right comparison (index vs working tree, tree vs index, tree vs tree, blob vs blob or file, combined merge diff, or --no-index), including A...B symmetric-difference handling.
nodes.languageNotes: The decision table of what is compared is documented in a comment in cmd_diff by the counts of trees (N), blobs (M) and pathspecs (P).

nodes.name: stuff_change
nodes.summary: Queues one filepair for two sides (honouring -R and path prefix) so a pair of blobs or a blob and a file can be diffed without a tree walk.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_b_f
nodes.summary: Diffs a blob against a file in the working tree, validating that the path is a regular file or symlink.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_blobs
nodes.summary: Diffs two blobs given on the command line using default regular-file modes.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_index
nodes.summary: Diffs one tree-ish against the index (--cached) or working tree through run_diff_index.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_tree
nodes.summary: Diffs two trees, applying --merge-base or swapping them when the second is marked uninteresting.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_combined
nodes.summary: Produces a combined diff for a merge against all its parents using diff_tree_combined.

nodes.name: refresh_index_quietly
nodes.summary: Refreshes the stat information in the index under a lock and writes it back if possible, used after a diff with stat-unmatched entries.

nodes.name: builtin_diff_files
nodes.summary: Diffs the index against the working tree, handling --base/--ours/--theirs stages, reading the index and calling run_diff_files.

nodes.name: symdiff_prepare
nodes.summary: Analyzes pending revisions for A...B symmetric difference, picks a merge base, marks revisions to skip and rejects invalid range combinations.

nodes.name: symdiff_release
nodes.summary: Frees the skip bitmap of a symdiff.

nodes.name: cmd_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point of git diff: detects --no-index (explicit or implicit), sets up revisions and defaults, resolves pending objects to trees and blobs, and dispatches to the matching builtin_diff_* function.

nodes.name: symdiff
nodes.summary: State for A...B handling: a bitmap of pending revision indices to skip, a multiple-merge-base warning flag and the names used in that warning.

nodes.name: name-rev.c
nodes.summary: Implements git name-rev and the experimental git format-rev. It names commits by walking parent links backwards from every ref tip (preferring tags, then fewer hops), and can rewrite 40-hex object IDs read from stdin as ref-based names or as pretty-formatted commit text.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses define_commit_slab to attach a rev_name record to every commit without a hash map.

nodes.name: set_commit_cutoff
nodes.summary: Lowers the global timestamp and commit-graph generation cutoffs to the given commit so the later walk never goes older than the oldest requested commit.

nodes.name: adjust_cutoff_timestamp_for_slop
nodes.summary: Subtracts one day of slop from the date cutoff (with underflow protection) to tolerate clock skew in commit timestamps.

nodes.name: is_better_name
nodes.summary: Decides whether a candidate name beats the stored one: nearer tag first, then a tag over a non-tag, then fewer effective hops, then older tagger date.

nodes.name: name_rev
nodes.summary: Propagates a ref name from a tip commit to its ancestors with an explicit stack, weighting merge-parent hops heavily, and stops at the date or generation cutoff.

nodes.name: subpath_matches
nodes.summary: Matches a wildmatch filter against a ref name and each of its slash-separated suffixes, returning the offset of the first match or -1.

nodes.name: add_to_tip_table
nodes.summary: Appends a ref tip (oid, shortened name, commit, tagger date, tag flags) to the global tip table, optionally shortening the refname unambiguously.

nodes.name: cmp_by_tag_and_age
nodes.summary: qsort comparator that orders tip table entries with tags first, then dereferenced tags, then older tagger date, so better names spread first.

nodes.name: name_ref
nodes.summary: For_each_ref callback that filters refs by --tags, --refs and --exclude patterns, peels annotated tags to commits and records the tip in the tip table.

nodes.name: name_tips
nodes.summary: Sorts the tip table by tag preference and age, then runs name_rev from each commit tip to name every reachable ancestor.

nodes.name: show_name
nodes.summary: Prints one name-rev result line, falling back to "undefined", an abbreviated object name with --always, or dying when no name exists.

nodes.name: name_rev_line
nodes.summary: Scans a line of text for full-length hex object IDs and replaces each with its ref-based name or its pretty-formatted commit, flushing the rest unchanged.

nodes.name: cmd_name_rev
nodes.summary: Entry point of git name-rev: parses options, collects requested objects, names all ref tips, then prints names for arguments, all commits, or annotates stdin.

nodes.name: format_nul_cb
nodes.summary: Option callback for -z that enables both NUL-terminated input and output for format-rev.

nodes.name: parse_stdin_mode
nodes.summary: Parses the --stdin-mode value into the text or revs enum, dying on an unknown mode.

nodes.name: cmd_format_rev
nodes.summary: Entry point of the experimental git format-rev: reads text or revision IDs on stdin and prints pretty-formatted commits using notes and NUL or newline terminators.

nodes.name: create_or_update_name
nodes.summary: Fetches the per-commit rev_name slab entry and overwrites it only when the new (taggerdate, generation, distance, from_tag) tuple is better.

nodes.name: get_parent_name
nodes.summary: Builds the textual name of a non-first parent as tip~N^k, stripping a trailing ^0 from the tip name, allocated from a memory pool.

nodes.name: get_exact_ref_match
nodes.summary: Binary-searches the sorted tip table for an object that is exactly a ref tip and returns that ref name.

nodes.name: get_rev_name
nodes.summary: Returns the display name for an object: an exact ref match for non-commits, otherwise tip~generation derived from the commit slab.

nodes.name: get_format_rev
nodes.summary: Formats a commit with the pretty-format machinery, optionally attaching display notes, and returns the buffer text.

nodes.name: notes.c
nodes.summary: Implements git notes, which attach extra text to objects via a notes tree stored under refs/notes/. Subcommands list, add, copy, append, edit, show, merge, remove, prune and get-ref are dispatched with OPT_SUBCOMMAND.

nodes.name: free_note_data
nodes.summary: Frees a note_data: unlinks the temporary edit file, releases the buffer and each collected -m/-F message.

nodes.name: copy_obj_to_fd
nodes.summary: Reads a blob object from the object database and writes its contents to a file descriptor, used to seed the editor with an existing note.

nodes.name: write_commented_object
nodes.summary: Writes the output of git show --stat for an object into the editor template as commented lines.

nodes.name: prepare_note_data
nodes.summary: Prepares note contents: when the editor is needed, writes NOTES_EDITMSG with a template and the commented object, launches the editor and strips whitespace.

nodes.name: write_note_data
nodes.summary: Writes the accumulated note buffer into the object database as a blob and returns its object ID, dying with a hint on failure.

nodes.name: append_separator
nodes.summary: Appends the configured --separator text to a note buffer, adding a newline when the separator does not already end with one.

nodes.name: concat_messages
nodes.summary: Joins the -m, -F and -C message pieces into one note buffer separated by blank lines.

nodes.name: parse_msg_arg
nodes.summary: Option callback for -m that stores each message as a new note_msg entry so that several -m options are joined later.

nodes.name: parse_file_arg
nodes.summary: Option callback for -F that reads a note body from a file or stdin into a note_data message slot.

nodes.name: parse_reuse_arg
nodes.summary: Option callback for -C and -c that resolves an object, reads its blob and reuses its content as a note message.

nodes.name: notes_copy_from_stdin
nodes.summary: Implements copy --stdin and the rewrite hook path: reads "from to" object pairs and copies notes for each, then commits the notes tree.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Implements notes list: prints every note, or the note blob ID of a single named object.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Implements notes add: resolves the target object, refuses to overwrite without -f, writes the note blob, updates the notes tree and commits it.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Implements notes copy: copies the note blob from one object to another, checking for an existing note unless forced, then commits the notes tree.

nodes.name: append_edit
nodes.summary: Implements notes append and edit: loads any existing note, appends or edits through the editor, writes a new blob and commits, removing the note if the result is empty.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Implements notes show: looks up the note blob for an object and runs git show on it.

nodes.name: merge_abort
nodes.summary: Aborts an in-progress notes merge by deleting NOTES_MERGE_PARTIAL and NOTES_MERGE_REF and removing the merge worktree.

nodes.name: merge_commit
nodes.summary: Finalizes a conflicted notes merge: reads NOTES_MERGE_PARTIAL, builds the result tree, updates the target notes ref and then aborts to clean up state.

nodes.name: git_config_get_notes_strategy
nodes.summary: Reads a notes merge strategy from a config key and parses it into the merge options.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Implements notes merge: parses strategy and mode, runs notes_merge between local and remote notes refs, and records partial state in NOTES_MERGE_PARTIAL when conflicts remain.

nodes.name: remove_one_note
nodes.summary: Resolves an object name and removes its note from the notes tree, reporting missing notes.

nodes.name: remove_cmd
nodes.summary: Implements notes remove: removes notes for the named objects or from stdin and commits the updated notes tree.

nodes.name: prune
nodes.summary: Implements notes prune: drops notes whose annotated objects no longer exist and commits the result unless in dry-run mode.

nodes.name: get_ref
nodes.summary: Implements notes get-ref: prints the resolved default notes ref.

nodes.name: cmd_notes
nodes.summary: Entry point of git notes: reads config, applies --ref via GIT_NOTES_REF and dispatches to the subcommand function, defaulting to list.

nodes.name: init_notes_check
nodes.summary: Initializes the default notes tree and refuses to operate on a notes ref outside refs/notes/.

nodes.name: pack-refs.c
nodes.summary: Thin builtin wrapper for git pack-refs that supplies the usage string and delegates all work to pack_refs_core, which is shared with git refs optimize.

nodes.name: cmd_pack_refs
nodes.summary: Entry point of git pack-refs; forwards to pack_refs_core with the pack-refs usage text.

nodes.name: patch-id.c
nodes.summary: Implements git patch-id, which hashes the content of a diff (ignoring line numbers and, unless verbatim, whitespace) to produce a stable patch ID for each patch read from stdin, such as the output of git log -p or format-patch.

nodes.name: remove_space
nodes.summary: Removes all whitespace characters from a line in place and returns the new length.

nodes.name: scan_hunk_header
nodes.summary: Parses an @@ -a,b +c,d @@ hunk header to extract the before and after line counts used to know when a hunk ends.

nodes.name: get_one_patchid
nodes.summary: Streams one patch from stdin through a hash context, skipping commit headers and hunk line numbers, optionally flushing per file in stable mode, and returns the patch length.

nodes.name: generate_id_list
nodes.summary: Loops over the patches on stdin and prints "patch-id commit-id" pairs.

nodes.name: git_patch_id_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading patchid.stable and patchid.verbatim before falling back to the default config handler.

nodes.name: cmd_patch_id
nodes.summary: Entry point of git patch-id: reads config, parses --stable/--unstable/--verbatim, ensures a hash algorithm is set and generates the ID list.

nodes.name: prune-packed.c
nodes.summary: Implements git prune-packed, which removes loose objects that are also present in a pack by calling prune_packed_objects with dry-run and verbose flags.

nodes.name: cmd_prune_packed
nodes.summary: Entry point of git prune-packed: parses -n and -q and calls prune_packed_objects.

nodes.name: pull.c
nodes.summary: Implements git pull as a driver: it spawns git fetch, reads the resulting FETCH_HEAD, decides between fast-forward, merge and rebase (using pull.rebase, pull.ff and branch config) and then spawns git merge or git rebase, plus submodule updates.

nodes.name: parse_config_rebase
nodes.summary: Parses a pull.rebase or branch.<name>.rebase value (true, false, merges, interactive) into a rebase_type enum.

nodes.name: parse_opt_rebase
nodes.summary: Option callback for --rebase and --no-rebase that stores the rebase_type.

nodes.name: argv_push_verbosity
nodes.summary: Pushes -v or -q arguments onto a child command line according to the pull verbosity level.

nodes.name: set_reflog_message
nodes.summary: Joins the command line into GIT_REFLOG_ACTION so that reflog entries written by pull and its children carry the invoked command.

nodes.name: config_get_rebase
nodes.summary: Resolves the default rebase mode from branch.<name>.rebase, then pull.rebase, defaulting to false.

nodes.name: git_pull_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading pull.* keys, merge.autostash and rebase.autostash before the default config handler.

nodes.name: get_merge_heads
nodes.summary: Reads FETCH_HEAD and collects the object IDs of lines not marked not-for-merge.

nodes.name: get_only_remote
nodes.summary: Remote iteration callback that records the single configured remote name and fails when there is more than one.

nodes.name: die_no_merge_candidates
nodes.summary: Dies with a context-specific explanation when git fetch left no merge candidate, such as no tracking info or a missing remote ref.

nodes.name: parse_repo_refspecs
nodes.summary: Splits positional arguments into an optional repository and the refspecs that follow it.

nodes.name: run_fetch
nodes.summary: Builds a git fetch command line from pull options and runs it as a child process.

nodes.name: pull_into_void
nodes.summary: Handles pulling into an unborn branch with a two-way fast-forward checkout against the empty tree and updates HEAD.

nodes.name: rebase_submodules
nodes.summary: Runs git submodule update --recursive --rebase after a rebase pull.

nodes.name: update_submodules
nodes.summary: Runs git submodule update --recursive --checkout after a merge pull.

nodes.name: run_merge
nodes.summary: Builds a git merge command line from pull options targeting FETCH_HEAD and runs it as a child process.

nodes.name: get_rebase_fork_point
nodes.summary: Runs git merge-base --fork-point against the upstream or tracking branch to find the fork point for a rebase pull.

nodes.name: get_octopus_merge_base
nodes.summary: Computes the reduced octopus merge base of the current head, merge head and optional fork point.

nodes.name: get_rebase_newbase_and_upstream
nodes.summary: Computes the <newbase> and <upstream> arguments for rebase --onto, dropping the fork point when it equals the octopus merge base.

nodes.name: run_rebase
nodes.summary: Builds a git rebase --onto command from pull options and runs it as a child process.

nodes.name: get_can_ff
nodes.summary: Returns whether HEAD can fast-forward to the single merge head, by testing ancestry with repo_is_descendant_of.

nodes.name: already_up_to_date
nodes.summary: Returns whether HEAD already contains every merge head by testing ancestry against each.

nodes.name: show_advice_pull_non_ff
nodes.summary: Prints advice on how to configure pull.rebase or pull.ff when branches have diverged.

nodes.name: cmd_pull
nodes.summary: Entry point of git pull: parses options, runs fetch, works out merge heads and fast-forward or divergence, then chooses run_merge, run_rebase or an unborn-branch update.

nodes.name: config_get_ff
nodes.summary: Translates the pull.ff config value into the matching --ff, --no-ff or --ff-only argument.

nodes.name: get_upstream_branch
nodes.summary: Returns the configured upstream branch of the current branch for the given remote, or NULL when it does not apply.

nodes.name: get_tracking_branch
nodes.summary: Derives the remote-tracking ref from a remote and fetch refspec using the default refs/heads to refs/remotes mapping.

nodes.name: range-diff.c
nodes.summary: Implements git range-diff, which compares two commit ranges (A..B C..D, A...B or base rev1 rev2) by resolving them to range strings and calling show_range_diff to pair up and diff the commits.

nodes.name: parse_max_memory
nodes.summary: Option callback parsing --max-memory as an unsigned size into range_diff_options.

nodes.name: cmd_range_diff
nodes.summary: Entry point of git range-diff: normalizes three argument forms into two ranges, sets diff and log options and calls show_range_diff.

nodes.name: rebase.c
nodes.summary: Implements git rebase with two backends: the merge backend (sequencer based, covering interactive, rebase-merges and update-refs) and the apply backend (git format-patch piped into git am). It manages the rebase state directory, fast-forward detection, autostash, hooks and the continue, skip, abort, quit and edit-todo actions.

nodes.name: rebase_options_release
nodes.summary: Frees every allocated field of rebase_options, including strvecs and string lists.

nodes.name: get_replay_opts
nodes.summary: Translates rebase_options into a sequencer replay_opts, mapping signoff, empty handling, strategy, gpg-sign and reflog action.

nodes.name: edit_todo_file
nodes.summary: Reads the rebase todo list, lets the user edit it via edit_todo_list and writes it back.

nodes.name: get_revision_ranges
nodes.summary: Builds the upstream...HEAD range strings and abbreviated variants used to generate and display the todo list.

nodes.name: init_basic_state
nodes.summary: Creates the merge state directory, removes the REBASE_HEAD reflog, marks the rebase interactive and writes the basic state files.

nodes.name: do_interactive_rebase
nodes.summary: Generates the todo list for the commit range, initializes state and hands over to complete_action, which edits and starts the sequencer run.

nodes.name: run_sequencer_rebase
nodes.summary: Dispatches the merge-backend actions: start, continue, skip, edit-todo and show-current-patch, using sequencer_continue for resuming.

nodes.name: imply_merge
nodes.summary: Checks that an option is compatible with the apply backend and otherwise switches the rebase to the merge backend.

nodes.name: read_basic_state
nodes.summary: Reads head-name, onto, orig-head and flag files from the apply-backend state directory to resume an interrupted rebase.

nodes.name: rebase_write_basic_state
nodes.summary: Writes head-name, onto, orig-head, quiet, verbose, gpg and signoff files to the apply-backend state directory.

nodes.name: cleanup_autostash
nodes.summary: Applies the saved autostash back to the working tree when a rebase ends.

nodes.name: finish_rebase
nodes.summary: Finishes a rebase by deleting REBASE_HEAD and AUTO_MERGE, applying autostash, running auto maintenance and removing state.

nodes.name: move_to_original_branch
nodes.summary: Moves the branch ref and HEAD back to the original branch after the apply backend completes, with reflog messages.

nodes.name: run_am
nodes.summary: Runs the apply backend: pipes git format-patch output into git am --rebasing, handling continue and restoring the original head on failure.

nodes.name: run_specific_rebase
nodes.summary: Selects the merge or apply backend, runs it and performs the common cleanup after the result.

nodes.name: rebase_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading rebase.* keys such as stat, autosquash, updateRefs, rebaseMerges and autostash.

nodes.name: checkout_up_to_date
nodes.summary: Updates HEAD and working tree to the original head when the branch is already up to date, running the post-checkout hook.

nodes.name: is_linear_history
nodes.summary: Walks parents from one commit to another and returns false if a merge commit is found.

nodes.name: can_fast_forward
nodes.summary: Decides whether the rebase can be skipped as a fast-forward by checking branch base, onto, merge bases and linear history.

nodes.name: fill_branch_base
nodes.summary: Computes the merge base of onto and the original head and stores it, or null if there are several merge bases.

nodes.name: parse_opt_am
nodes.summary: Option callback for --apply that selects the apply backend.

nodes.name: parse_opt_merge
nodes.summary: Option callback for --merge that selects the merge backend.

nodes.name: parse_opt_interactive
nodes.summary: Option callback for --interactive that selects the merge backend in interactive mode.

nodes.name: parse_empty_value
nodes.summary: Parses a drop, keep or stop value for --empty and rebase.empty.

nodes.name: parse_opt_keep_empty
nodes.summary: Option callback for --keep-empty and --no-keep-empty.

nodes.name: parse_opt_empty
nodes.summary: Option callback for --empty that stores the parsed empty-commit action.

nodes.name: parse_opt_rebase_merges
nodes.summary: Option callback for --rebase-merges that parses the rebase-cousins or no-rebase-cousins mode.

nodes.name: error_on_missing_default_upstream
nodes.summary: Prints guidance when no upstream is configured for the current branch and exits with status 1.

nodes.name: check_exec_cmd
nodes.summary: Validates an --exec command by rejecting empty commands and commands containing newlines.

nodes.name: cmd_rebase
nodes.summary: Entry point of git rebase: parses options, resolves onto and upstream, handles continue, abort and quit, detects fast-forward and runs the selected backend.

nodes.name: state_dir_path
nodes.summary: Returns the path of a named file inside the rebase state directory using a reusable static strbuf.

nodes.name: reflog.c
nodes.summary: Implements git reflog with subcommands show, list, exists, write, delete, drop and expire. Expiry prunes reflog entries by age and by reachability (optionally marking reachable objects first) across all worktrees through the ref store.

nodes.name: collect_reflog
nodes.summary: Callback that collects a reflog name for a worktree, skipping shared refs seen through non-current worktrees.

nodes.name: expire_unreachable_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback parsing --expire-unreachable into a timestamp and recording the explicit expiry.

nodes.name: expire_total_callback
nodes.summary: Option callback parsing --expire into a timestamp and recording the explicit expiry.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_show
nodes.summary: Subcommand that shows reflogs by delegating to the log machinery in reflog mode.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_list
nodes.summary: Subcommand that lists all refs that have a reflog.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_expire
nodes.summary: Subcommand that expires reflog entries by age and reachability for the given refs or all refs, optionally across worktrees and after marking reachable objects.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_delete
nodes.summary: Subcommand that deletes individual reflog entries such as ref@{n}.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_exists
nodes.summary: Subcommand that exits with success when the named ref has a reflog.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_drop
nodes.summary: Subcommand that deletes whole reflogs for given refs or for all refs.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog_write
nodes.summary: Subcommand that appends a reflog entry through a ref transaction after validating the ref name and old and new object IDs.

nodes.name: cmd_reflog
nodes.summary: Entry point of git reflog: dispatches subcommands, defaulting to show behaviour through the log machinery.

nodes.name: refs.c
nodes.summary: Implements the git refs plumbing command, with subcommands migrate (change ref storage format), verify, list, exists, optimize, and create, delete, update and rename that read and write references through the ref store API.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_migrate
nodes.summary: Subcommand that converts the repository between ref storage formats (files and reftable), with dry-run and reflog options.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_verify
nodes.summary: Subcommand that runs fsck-style consistency checks on the ref stores of every worktree.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_list
nodes.summary: Subcommand that lists refs by sharing the for-each-ref implementation.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_exists
nodes.summary: Subcommand that reports whether a reference exists by reading the raw ref, returning distinct exit codes for missing and failing.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_optimize
nodes.summary: Subcommand that optimizes ref storage by sharing the pack-refs implementation.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_create
nodes.summary: Subcommand that creates a ref pointing to an object, failing if the ref already exists.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_delete
nodes.summary: Subcommand that deletes a ref, optionally verifying its old object ID.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_update
nodes.summary: Subcommand that updates a ref to a new object ID, optionally checking the old value.

nodes.name: cmd_refs_rename
nodes.summary: Subcommand that renames a ref after validating both names and checking existence.

nodes.name: cmd_refs
nodes.summary: Entry point of git refs: registers the subcommands and dispatches to the chosen one.

nodes.name: replace.c
nodes.summary: Implements git replace, which manages replacement refs under refs/replace/ that make Git substitute one object for another when reading. It supports listing, deleting, creating by object, editing and grafting parents, and converting a legacy graft file.

nodes.name: show_reference
nodes.summary: Callback that prints a replace ref in short, medium or long format, the long format including object types.

nodes.name: list_replace_refs
nodes.summary: Lists replace refs matching a pattern in the chosen format.

nodes.name: for_each_replace_name
nodes.summary: Resolves each argument to an object, builds its refs/replace/ name and runs a callback on the matching replace ref.

nodes.name: check_ref_valid
nodes.summary: Builds the replace ref name for an object, validates the name and detects an existing ref unless forced.

nodes.name: replace_object_oid
nodes.summary: Creates or updates a replace ref via a ref transaction after checking that both objects have the same type unless forced.

nodes.name: replace_object
nodes.summary: Resolves two names to object IDs and creates the replacement mapping.

nodes.name: export_object
nodes.summary: Writes an object to a file by running git cat-file with replacements disabled, either raw or pretty printed.

nodes.name: import_object
nodes.summary: Reads an edited file back as an object, using git mktree for trees and writing blobs and commits into the object database.

nodes.name: edit_and_replace
nodes.summary: Exports an object, launches the editor, imports the result and registers it as a replacement for the original.

nodes.name: replace_parents
nodes.summary: Rewrites the parent lines of a raw commit buffer with the supplied commits.

nodes.name: check_one_mergetag
nodes.summary: Verifies that a mergetag header in the original commit still points at one of the new parents.

nodes.name: create_graft
nodes.summary: Creates a replacement commit with new parents from an existing commit, dropping signatures and checking mergetags.

nodes.name: convert_graft_file
nodes.summary: Converts each line of the legacy .git/info/grafts file into a replace ref and removes the file when done.

nodes.name: cmd_replace
nodes.summary: Entry point of git replace: parses the mode and dispatches to delete, replace, edit, graft, convert or list.

nodes.name: replay.c
nodes.summary: Implements git replay, which replays a range of commits onto a new base without touching the working tree or HEAD, using onto, advance or revert modes and then updating refs through a transaction or printing update commands.

nodes.name: get_ref_action_mode
nodes.summary: Resolves the ref action from the command line, then replay.refAction config, defaulting to update.

nodes.name: handle_ref_update
nodes.summary: Either queues a ref transaction update or prints an update command depending on the ref action mode.

nodes.name: cmd_replay
nodes.summary: Entry point of git replay: validates mode options, configures a topological oldest-first revision walk, calls replay_revisions and applies the resulting ref updates in one transaction.

nodes.name: rerere.c
nodes.summary: Implements git rerere (reuse recorded resolution), dispatching to record or replay conflict resolutions and to the forget, clear, gc, status, remaining and diff subcommands, with an xdiff based diff helper.

nodes.name: diff_two
nodes.summary: Reads two files into memory and prints a unified diff of them with xdiff.

nodes.name: cmd_rerere
nodes.summary: Entry point of git rerere: with no argument records resolutions, otherwise runs forget, clear, gc, status, remaining or diff.

nodes.name: rev-list.c
nodes.summary: Implements git rev-list, the plumbing front end to the revision walk. It lists commits and, with --objects, the objects reachable from them, and adds bisection, counting, bitmap fast paths, disk usage, partial-clone filters and missing-object reporting.

nodes.name: get_object_disk_usage
nodes.summary: Returns the on-disk size of an object via the object database info interface.

nodes.name: add_missing_object_entry
nodes.summary: Records a missing object with its path and type in an oidmap, once per object.

nodes.name: print_missing_object
nodes.summary: Prints a missing object in the selected format, optionally with path and type info.

nodes.name: finish_object__ma
nodes.summary: Applies the --missing policy for an absent object: die, ignore, print, or allow when promisor.

nodes.name: show_commit
nodes.summary: Traversal callback that prints one commit with parents, decorations, graph and pretty-formatted message, or only counts or measures it.

nodes.name: finish_object
nodes.summary: Checks that an object exists, reporting through the missing policy when it does not, and parses it when verifying objects.

nodes.name: show_object
nodes.summary: Traversal callback that prints a tree or blob ID and name, or counts it and tallies disk usage.

nodes.name: show_bisect_vars
nodes.summary: Selects the next bisection commit and prints shell variables like bisect_rev, bisect_nr and bisect_steps.

nodes.name: show_object_fast
nodes.summary: Bitmap traversal callback that prints just the object ID of each reachable object.

nodes.name: print_disk_usage
nodes.summary: Prints a total object disk usage either in bytes or in human-readable units.

nodes.name: parse_missing_action_value
nodes.summary: Parses the --missing option value into the missing_action enum and disables lazy fetch where appropriate.

nodes.name: try_bitmap_count
nodes.summary: Counts reachable commits and objects from the pack bitmap index instead of walking, if the options allow it.

nodes.name: try_bitmap_traversal
nodes.summary: Lists reachable objects directly from the bitmap index when no traversal limit or left-right mode is requested.

nodes.name: try_bitmap_disk_usage
nodes.summary: Computes the disk usage of reachable objects from the bitmap index.

nodes.name: prepare_maximal_independent
nodes.summary: Reduces the tips to maximal independent commits for --maximal-only when no other walk options apply.

nodes.name: cmd_rev_list
nodes.summary: Entry point of git rev-list: parses options, sets up the revision walk, picks a bitmap, bisect or normal traversal and prints commits, objects, counts or disk usage.

nodes.name: rev-parse.c
nodes.summary: Implements git rev-parse, which parses revision names, ranges and options and prints object IDs, paths and repository facts such as the git dir or work tree root. It also offers --parseopt and --sq-quote helpers for shell scripts.

nodes.name: is_rev_argument
nodes.summary: Returns whether an argument is one of the options that git rev-list understands and rev-parse should pass through as a revision flag.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Prints one argument either plainly or single-quoted for shell evaluation when --sq is active.

nodes.name: show_rev
nodes.summary: Prints a resolved revision as a full or abbreviated ID, or in symbolic or abbreviated ref form when requested.

nodes.name: show_flag
nodes.summary: Prints an option argument when the active filter allows flags, classifying it as a revision option or other option.

nodes.name: show_default
nodes.summary: Resolves the --default revision once and prints it, returning whether anything was shown.

nodes.name: show_datestring
nodes.summary: Converts a date string with approxidate and prints it as a --max-age= or --min-age= timestamp, only when both flag and revision output are enabled.

nodes.name: show_file
nodes.summary: Emits any pending --default revision, then prints a non-revision argument (optionally prefixed with the current directory) when the active filter allows non-flag, non-rev output.

nodes.name: try_difference
nodes.summary: Handles A..B and A...B arguments by resolving both ends and printing the range with merge bases excluded for the symmetric form.

nodes.name: try_parent_shorthands
nodes.summary: Handles rev^@, rev^! and rev^- parent shorthands by printing the revision and its parents.

nodes.name: parseopt_dump
nodes.summary: Option callback that records which options were parsed and quotes their values for shell output.

nodes.name: cmd_parseopt
nodes.summary: Implements rev-parse --parseopt: reads an option specification from stdin, builds option tables, parses arguments and prints shell-quoted results.

nodes.name: cmd_sq_quote
nodes.summary: Implements rev-parse --sq-quote by single-quoting each argument for safe shell use.

nodes.name: opt_with_value
nodes.summary: Parses an option written as opt or opt=value and returns the optional value.

nodes.name: handle_ref_opt
nodes.summary: Applies --branches, --tags or --remotes by iterating matching refs with prefix, pattern and exclusion rules.

nodes.name: print_path
nodes.summary: Prints a path in relative, canonical or unmodified form according to --path-format.

nodes.name: cmd_rev_parse
nodes.summary: Entry point of git rev-parse: loops over arguments, handling repository queries, ref glob options, revisions and ranges, then prints the results.

nodes.name: revert.c
nodes.summary: Implements git revert and git cherry-pick, which share one run_sequencer driver that parses options, sets up a revision list and delegates to the sequencer for picking, continuing, skipping, aborting or quitting a multi-commit sequence.

nodes.name: parse_opt_empty
nodes.summary: Option callback parsing --empty into stop, drop or keep.

nodes.name: option_parse_m
nodes.summary: Option callback for -m that parses the mainline parent number and rejects values that are not greater than zero.

nodes.name: verify_opt_compatible
nodes.summary: Variadic helper that dies when an option is combined with an incompatible option.

nodes.name: run_sequencer
nodes.summary: Shared driver for revert and cherry-pick: builds options, validates combinations, prepares the revision list and calls the matching sequencer function.

nodes.name: cmd_revert
nodes.summary: Entry point of git revert: sets the revert action and runs the sequencer driver.

nodes.name: cmd_cherry_pick
nodes.summary: Entry point of git cherry-pick: sets the pick action and runs the sequencer driver.

nodes.name: shortlog.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git shortlog`: it groups commits by author, committer, trailer value or a custom pretty format, applies the mailmap, and prints per-person commit counts or wrapped one-line subjects. It reads commits from a revision walk or parses `git log` output on stdin, and its init/add/output functions are shared with `git format-patch` through shortlog.h.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the string_list util pointer for two meanings (a sub-list of subjects, or an integer counter smuggled into the pointer slot when --summary is set) via the UTIL_TO_INT macro.

nodes.name: compare_by_list
nodes.summary: qsort comparator that orders shortlog entries by the number of subject lines in their util string_list, largest first; used for `-n` without `--summary`.

nodes.name: insert_one_record
nodes.summary: Adds one commit to the author bucket in log->list. In summary mode it only increments the integer counter stored in util; otherwise it strips leading whitespace and a "[PATCH" prefix from the subject, formats it with format_subject and appends it to the bucket string list.

nodes.name: parse_ident
nodes.summary: Splits an ident line ("Name <mail> date") with split_ident_line, maps name and email through the mailmap with map_user, and writes "Name" or "Name <email>" into the output strbuf.

nodes.name: read_from_stdin
nodes.summary: Reads `git log` text from stdin line by line, finds the "Author: "/"author " (or "Commit: "/"committer ") header line for the selected group, skips the remaining headers and blank lines, maps the identity and inserts a record per commit. It dies for trailer and format grouping, which need real commit objects.

nodes.name: shortlog_needs_dedup
nodes.summary: Returns true when records may be produced more than once for a commit (several --group kinds, several formats or trailer keys), so insertions must be deduplicated.

nodes.name: insert_records_from_trailers
nodes.summary: For each commit, re-encodes the log message, locates the body and iterates its trailers (Signed-off-by, Co-authored-by, ...). Trailers whose key is in log->trailers are normalised through parse_ident, deduplicated with a strset and inserted as records.

nodes.name: insert_records_from_format
nodes.summary: Expands each user-supplied or implied format (such as "%aN <%aE>") for a commit with repo_format_commit_message and inserts the result as a record, deduplicating through a strset when several groupings are active.

nodes.name: shortlog_add_commit
nodes.summary: Public entry point that records one commit: builds a pretty-print context, renders the one-line subject (unless in summary mode) and fans out to the trailer and format record inserters. Also called by `git format-patch` for its cover letter shortlog.

nodes.name: parse_uint
nodes.summary: Parses an unsigned decimal field from a comma separated width/indent argument, returning a default when the field is empty and -1 on overflow or a bad separator.

nodes.name: parse_wrap_args
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for `-w[<width>[,<indent1>[,<indent2>]]]`: fills log->wrap, in1 and in2 with defaults of 76/6/9 and rejects negative values or indents that are not smaller than the width.

nodes.name: parse_group_option
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for `--group`: accepts author, committer, trailer:<key> and format:<fmt> (or a bare string containing %), ORs the matching SHORTLOG_GROUP_* bit into log->groups and records trailer keys or format strings.

nodes.name: shortlog_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes a struct shortlog, loads the mailmap for the repository and sets defaults (wrap 76, indents 6 and 9, trailer keys compared case-insensitively). Shared with other builtins that print shortlogs.

nodes.name: shortlog_finish_setup
nodes.summary: Turns the author and committer group flags into pretty formats ("%aN <%aE>", "%cN") appended to log->format, and sorts the trailer key list so that lookups are stable.

nodes.name: cmd_shortlog
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point of `git shortlog`. It sets up the hash algorithm when run outside a repository, parses its own options and the revision options in one loop, sets up revisions, defaults to author grouping, then reads either stdin or a revision walk and prints the result.

nodes.name: shortlog_output
nodes.summary: Prints the collected buckets: optionally sorts them with STABLE_QSORT, then writes either "count<TAB>name" lines (summary) or "name (N):" followed by indented, optionally wrapped subjects, and finally releases the lists and mailmap.

nodes.name: get_from_rev
nodes.summary: Runs the revision walk (prepare_revision_walk, then get_revision in a loop) and feeds each commit to shortlog_add_commit.

nodes.name: show-branch.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git show-branch`: it takes up to 29 refs or revisions, walks their history with a date-ordered priority queue while tagging each commit with a bit per tip, and prints a matrix of which commits are reachable from which branch. It also provides the --merge-base, --independent and --reflog (-g) modes and names commits as head~N^M.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses commit->object.flags as a bit set (bit 0 UNINTERESTING, two bits reserved, then one bit per branch) and a commit-slab to attach naming info to commits.

nodes.name: commit_name
nodes.summary: Naming info stored per commit in a commit slab (commit_name_slab): the head it descends from and how many first-parent steps away it is, so a commit can be printed as head~N.

nodes.name: interesting
nodes.summary: Scans the priority queue and returns the first commit not flagged UNINTERESTING, or NULL when every queued commit is uninteresting; join_revs uses it to decide when to stop walking.

nodes.name: name_commit
nodes.summary: Records in the commit slab that a commit is the nth generation ancestor of head_name, allocating the commit_name on first use.

nodes.name: name_parent
nodes.summary: Gives a first parent the name "(n+1)th ancestor of the child's head" if it has no name yet or that name is a shorter route than the one it holds.

nodes.name: name_first_parent_chain
nodes.summary: Follows the first-parent chain from a named commit and names every unnamed ancestor along it; returns how many commits were newly named.

nodes.name: name_commits
nodes.summary: Three-pass naming of all commits shown: first the tips get their ref names, then first-parent chains, then the remaining unnamed parents get names like "head^2~3" built from their named child.

nodes.name: mark_seen
nodes.summary: Pushes a commit onto the seen list the first time it gets any flag, returning 1 when it was newly added and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: join_revs
nodes.summary: Core algorithm: pops commits from the date-ordered queue, propagates each commit's branch bits to its parents (parsing them as needed), marks commits reachable from all tips as UNINTERESTING merge points, then repeatedly poisons ancestors of uninteresting commits until no flags change.

nodes.name: show_one_commit
nodes.summary: Prints one commit as "[name~N^M] subject", using the one-line pretty format and the commit_name from the slab, or an abbreviated object id when no name exists.

nodes.name: find_digit_prefix
nodes.summary: Parses the leading run of decimal digits of a string into an int and returns a pointer to the first non-digit character; helper for version_cmp.

nodes.name: version_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two ref names the way a version sort would, treating digit runs as numbers so that v1.10 sorts after v1.9.

nodes.name: append_ref
nodes.summary: Adds a ref name to the ref_name array if its oid resolves to a commit, skipping duplicates unless allowed and refusing to exceed MAX_REVS (29) with a warning.

nodes.name: append_head_ref
nodes.summary: refs iterator callback for refs/heads/*: strips the prefix when the short name resolves to the same oid (avoids head/tag ambiguity) and appends the ref.

nodes.name: append_remote_ref
nodes.summary: refs iterator callback for refs/remotes/*: same disambiguation as append_head_ref but strips only "refs/", keeping "remotes/origin/..." names.

nodes.name: append_matching_ref
nodes.summary: Iterator callback for glob arguments: skips leading path components to align with the pattern, tests the tail with wildmatch and dispatches to the head, tag or generic append routine.

nodes.name: snarf_refs
nodes.summary: Collects all local and/or remote-tracking branches via refs_for_each_ref and sorts each newly appended range by version order.

nodes.name: rev_is_head
nodes.summary: Returns whether a ref name denotes the same branch as the resolved HEAD, ignoring refs/heads/ and heads/ prefixes.

nodes.name: show_merge_base
nodes.summary: Implements `--merge-base`: prints the oids of commits flagged as reachable from every tip but not yet UNINTERESTING, and returns the exit status 0 only if any was printed.

nodes.name: show_independent
nodes.summary: Implements `--independent`: prints each tip whose flags equal only its own bit (not reachable from any other tip) and marks it uninteresting.

nodes.name: append_one_rev
nodes.summary: Resolves a command-line argument to an oid and appends it, or, if it contains glob characters, expands it over all refs with append_matching_ref; dies on bad references.

nodes.name: git_show_branch_config
nodes.summary: Config callback handling showbranch.default (collected into default_args) and color.showbranch, delegating other keys to git_color_config and git_default_config.

nodes.name: omit_in_dense
nodes.summary: Decides whether a merge commit is skipped in dense output: tips are always kept, a merge reachable from exactly one tip is omitted.

nodes.name: parse_reflog_param
nodes.summary: parse-options callback for `-g[=<n>[,<base>]]` that sets the number of reflog entries (default 4) and an optional base given as count or date.

nodes.name: cmd_show_branch
nodes.summary: Builtin entry point of `git show-branch`. It parses options and config, builds the ref list (explicit revs, globs, all branches or reflog entries), flags each tip with a bit, runs join_revs, then lists, finds merge bases or independent refs, or prints the sorted commit matrix with names.

nodes.name: read-cache.c
nodes.summary: Core implementation of the Git index (the staging area, historically the read cache): reading and writing .git/index with its extensions, the sorted in-memory array of cache entries and its lookup, insertion and removal, stat-based change detection with racy-timestamp handling, path validation, refreshing against the working tree, and helpers that stage files or overlay a tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Large C file that mixes the on-disk index format (versions 2 to 4, extension blocks, multithreaded loading via the IEOT and EOIE extensions) with the in-memory index_state API used by almost every porcelain command.

nodes.name: replace_index_entry
nodes.summary: Swaps the cache entry at a given index slot for a new one: tells the split index about the replacement, drops the old entry from the name hash, installs the new entry, and flags it CE_UPDATE_IN_BASE and the index as changed.

nodes.name: rename_index_entry_at
nodes.summary: Renames the index entry at slot nr by building a copy under the new name, invalidating the old path in the cache tree and untracked cache, removing the old entry and re-adding the refreshed copy so the stat data reflects the rename.

nodes.name: fill_stat_cache_info
nodes.summary: Copies lstat() results into a cache entry's stat_data so later refreshes can detect changes without reading file contents.

nodes.name: ce_compare_data
nodes.summary: Hashes the working-tree file behind a cache entry with index_fd() and compares the resulting blob object id to the entry's oid; returns -1 if the file cannot be opened.

nodes.name: ce_match_stat_basic
nodes.summary: Compares a cache entry against an lstat() result by file type, executable bit, symlink-ness and recorded stat fields, returning a bitmask (TYPE_CHANGED, MODE_CHANGED, DATA_CHANGED) and treating a zero recorded size on a non-empty blob as a smudged (changed) entry.

nodes.name: is_racy_timestamp
nodes.summary: Reports whether an entry's mtime is not older than the index file timestamp, meaning the file could have changed within the same timestamp tick and must be verified by content (the racily-clean problem).

nodes.name: ie_match_stat
nodes.summary: Decides whether the working-tree file still matches its index entry: honours skip-worktree, assume-valid and fsmonitor flags, handles intent-to-add entries, calls ce_match_stat_basic and, for racily clean timestamps, falls back to comparing file contents.

nodes.name: ie_modified
nodes.summary: Stricter variant of ie_match_stat: when only the data appears changed, or stat data was never recorded (zero size after read-tree), it checks the real file contents so a touched but identical file is reported unchanged.

nodes.name: index_name_stage_pos
nodes.summary: Binary-searches the sorted cache array for (name, stage) and returns the slot or -insertion_pos-1; in EXPAND_SPARSE mode it expands a sparse-directory entry that is an ancestor of the path and searches again.

nodes.name: index_name_pos
nodes.summary: Public lookup of a stage-0 path in the index, expanding the sparse index when needed; returns the position or a negative insertion point.

nodes.name: remove_index_entry_at
nodes.summary: Removes the entry at pos from the cache array: records resolve-undo information for conflicted stages, removes it from the name hash, hands it to the split index (or frees it) and shifts the remaining entries down.

nodes.name: remove_marked_cache_entries
nodes.summary: Compacts the cache array by dropping every entry flagged CE_REMOVE, optionally invalidating the cache-tree and untracked-cache for each removed path.

nodes.name: remove_file_from_index
nodes.summary: Removes all stages of a path from the index and invalidates the cache-tree and untracked-cache entries for it.

nodes.name: add_to_index
nodes.summary: Stages a working-tree path: builds a cache entry from lstat data and mode rules, skips entries that did not change, hashes and writes the blob via index_path (or marks intent-to-add), handles case-folding aliases, then inserts the entry with add_index_entry.

nodes.name: add_file_to_index
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper that lstat()s a path and calls add_to_index to stage it.

nodes.name: make_empty_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Allocates a zeroed cache_entry with room for a name of the given length from the index's memory pool (or its split-index base pool).

nodes.name: verify_path
nodes.summary: Public predicate returning true when a path is acceptable as an index entry name, via verify_path_internal.

nodes.name: make_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Creates a cache entry for (mode, oid, path, stage) after validating the path, then refreshes it from the working tree; returns NULL with an error for an invalid path.

nodes.name: chmod_index_entry
nodes.summary: Flips the executable bit of a regular-file cache entry (+x or -x), invalidating its cache-tree path and marking the index changed.

nodes.name: verify_path_internal
nodes.summary: Walks a path component by component and rejects names that could escape or alias the repository: DOS drive prefixes, .git and .gitmodules variants (including HFS and NTFS spellings), empty or .. components and over-long names; a trailing slash is allowed only for sparse directory entries.

nodes.name: has_file_name
nodes.summary: Detects an existing index file whose path has the new entry's name as a directory prefix (file/directory conflict), removing those entries when replacing is allowed.

nodes.name: has_dir_name
nodes.summary: Checks whether any leading directory component of the new entry's path already exists in the index as a file, with a fast path when the entry sorts after the last index entry; removes the conflicting file when replacing is allowed.

nodes.name: check_file_directory_conflict
nodes.summary: Combines has_file_name and has_dir_name to prevent an index from containing both a path and a path below it, skipping the check for CE_REMOVE entries.

nodes.name: add_index_entry_with_check
nodes.summary: Finds the insert position for a new entry, replaces an equal entry, drops conflicting unmerged stages when adding a stage-0 entry, validates the path and checks file/directory conflicts; returns the position plus one.

nodes.name: add_index_entry
nodes.summary: Public way to insert a cache entry into the sorted index array (or append it with ADD_CACHE_JUST_APPEND), growing the array, shifting entries and updating the name hash.

nodes.name: refresh_cache_ent
nodes.summary: Refreshes one cache entry against the working tree: short-circuits for valid, skip-worktree or fsmonitor-valid entries, lstat()s the file, compares via ie_match_stat and ie_modified and returns either the same entry, an updated copy with new stat data, or NULL with an errno.

nodes.name: refresh_index
nodes.summary: Refreshes every index entry against the working tree (git update-index --refresh and friends): preloads stat data in threads, honours pathspecs and flags, reports unmerged, modified or deleted paths and replaces entries whose stat data changed.

nodes.name: refresh_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Public wrapper that refreshes a single cache entry via refresh_cache_ent.

nodes.name: verify_hdr
nodes.summary: Validates the mmap'd index file header: signature, supported version range, and the trailing hash over the whole file.

nodes.name: read_index_extension
nodes.summary: Dispatches one index extension block by its 4-byte signature (cache tree, resolve-undo, split-index link, untracked cache, fsmonitor, sparse directories) to the matching reader; unknown optional extensions are ignored, required ones are an error.

nodes.name: create_from_disk
nodes.summary: Decodes one on-disk cache entry (v2 to v4) into an in-memory cache_entry, including extended flags and the v4 prefix-compressed path name relative to the previous entry.

nodes.name: load_cache_entries_threaded
nodes.summary: Splits the entries of the index into IEOT blocks, spawns one thread per group to decode entries into per-thread memory pools, then joins the threads and combines the pools.

nodes.name: do_read_index
nodes.summary: Reads an index file: mmaps it, verifies the header and checksum, allocates the cache array, loads entries (optionally multithreaded using the EOIE and IEOT extensions), loads extensions, and finally fixes the sparsity of the in-core index.

nodes.name: read_index_from
nodes.summary: Reads the main index and, when it carries a split-index link, also reads the sharedindex.<oid> base file, checks its hash and merges the base entries into the in-core index.

nodes.name: release_index
nodes.summary: Frees everything an index_state owns: resolve-undo data, name hash, cache tree, fsmonitor data, entry array, split index, untracked cache, sparse patterns and the entry memory pool.

nodes.name: discard_index
nodes.summary: Releases an index and reinitializes it to an empty state.

nodes.name: repo_index_has_changes
nodes.summary: Reports whether the index differs from a tree (or HEAD) by running diff-cache, optionally collecting the changed paths into a strbuf; with no HEAD any index entry counts as a change.

nodes.name: ce_smudge_racily_clean_entry
nodes.summary: When writing the index, sets the recorded size to zero for an entry whose stat data matches but whose contents differ (racily clean), so the next run is forced to compare contents.

nodes.name: ce_write_entry
nodes.summary: Writes one cache entry to the index hashfile in the on-disk layout, using v4 prefix-compressed path names when a previous name is supplied.

nodes.name: do_write_index
nodes.summary: Serializes the whole index to a tempfile: header, every entry (smudging racy ones), an optional IEOT, then extensions (split-index link, cache tree, resolve-undo, untracked cache, fsmonitor, sparse directories, EOIE) and finally the trailing checksum.

nodes.name: do_write_locked_index
nodes.summary: Writes the index to the lock file after collapsing it to sparse form when allowed, commits or closes the lock, re-expands if needed, and runs the post-index-change hook.

nodes.name: write_split_index
nodes.summary: Writes the small split index (only changes against the shared base) between prepare_to_write_split_index and finish_writing_split_index.

nodes.name: write_shared_index
nodes.summary: Writes the shared base index into a tempfile, renames it to sharedindex.<oid>, records its oid in the split index and cleans up expired shared index files.

nodes.name: write_locked_index
nodes.summary: Public entry for writing the index under a lock: skips the write if unchanged, and chooses between a plain full write and a split-index write that may first emit a new shared index depending on config and how many entries are not shared.

nodes.name: repo_read_index_unmerged
nodes.summary: Reads the repository index and converts unmerged entries to stage-0 conflicted placeholders.

nodes.name: index_state_unmerged_to_stage0
nodes.summary: Replaces every conflicted (stage above 0) path with a single stage-0 entry flagged CE_CONFLICTED, returning whether any unmerged path existed.

nodes.name: discard_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Frees a cache entry unless it came from a memory pool.

nodes.name: prefetch_cache_entries
nodes.summary: Collects the object ids of index entries that are missing locally and that a predicate wants, and fetches them from the promisor remote in one batch.

nodes.name: read_eoie_extension
nodes.summary: Locates and validates the End-Of-Index-Entries extension at the end of the index file and returns the offset where extensions begin, so extensions can be loaded on a separate thread.

nodes.name: overlay_tree_on_index
nodes.summary: Reads a tree-ish into stage 1 of the index (used by the --with-tree option), moving unmerged stages aside, and marks stage-1 entries that already have a stage-0 twin with CE_UPDATE.

nodes.name: skip_submodule
nodes.summary: Decides whether git add should skip a submodule whose ignore setting is all, unless its path is named explicitly in the pathspec and force is given.

nodes.name: update_callback
nodes.summary: Diff queue callback used by add_files_to_cache: for each changed path it stages modified entries with add_file_to_index or removes deleted ones from the index.

nodes.name: add_files_to_cache
nodes.summary: Stages all worktree changes matching a pathspec by running diff-files with update_callback inside an object-database transaction.

nodes.name: ondisk_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Layout of one index entry as stored on disk: ctime, mtime, dev, ino, mode, uid, gid, size, object id and flags, followed by an optional extended flags field and the path name.

nodes.name: index_entry_offset_table
nodes.summary: In-memory form of the IEOT extension: a list of (offset, entry count) blocks that lets index entries be decoded by several threads.

nodes.name: read-cache.h
nodes.summary: Header with small inline helpers on cache entries: computing the stored mode from stat data, mapping an entry to a dirent type, and matching an entry against a pathspec; it pulls in read-cache-ll.h for the main index API.

nodes.name: ce_mode_from_stat
