nodes.summary: Stores a duplicate of a string config value, reporting an error for a valueless key.

nodes.name: git_configset_add_file
nodes.summary: Reads a config file and adds all of its entries to a configset.

nodes.name: git_configset_get
nodes.summary: Checks whether a key exists in a configset, returning 0 if found.

nodes.name: git_configset_get_bool
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in a configset and parses its last value as a boolean.

nodes.name: repo_config_get_string_tmp
nodes.summary: Returns a pointer to the repository config string value without copying it.

nodes.name: repo_config_get_int
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the repository configset and parses it as an int.

nodes.name: repo_config_get_bool
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the repository configset and parses it as a boolean.

nodes.name: repo_config_set_in_file_gently
nodes.summary: Sets or unsets one key in a given config file without dying, a thin wrapper over the multivar writer.

nodes.name: config_error_nonbool
nodes.summary: Reports a "missing value for key" error for a config variable that needs a value.

nodes.name: copy.c
nodes.summary: Small helpers to copy a file descriptor or a whole file, optionally preserving the modification time. Used for copying files such as sparse-checkout patterns and config between locations.

nodes.name: copy_fd
nodes.summary: Copies everything from one file descriptor to another in 8 KiB chunks, returning distinct read-error and write-error codes.

nodes.name: copy_times
nodes.summary: Copies the access and modification times from a source file to a destination file with utime().

nodes.name: copy_file
nodes.summary: Copies a file to a new path with O_EXCL, normalizing the mode to 0666 or 0777 depending on the execute bits, then applies the repository's shared permissions.

nodes.name: copy_file_with_time
nodes.summary: Copies a file with copy_file and then copies the timestamps from the source.

nodes.name: copy.h
nodes.summary: Declares the file copy helpers and the COPY_READ_ERROR and COPY_WRITE_ERROR codes.

nodes.name: daemon.c
nodes.summary: Implements `git daemon`, the anonymous git:// protocol server: it listens on TCP sockets (or runs under inetd), reads the initial request packet, checks access rules, and runs upload-pack, upload-archive or receive-pack as a child process.
nodes.languageNotes: Process-per-connection model: the parent poll()s listening sockets, re-executes itself for each connection and reaps children with waitpid.

nodes.name: hostinfo
nodes.summary: Per-connection state for the requested host: hostname, canonical name, IP address and TCP port, filled from the extended host= argument.

nodes.name: logreport
nodes.summary: Formats a message and writes it to syslog or to stderr with a pid prefix depending on whether syslog logging is enabled.

nodes.name: path_ok
nodes.summary: Maps the requested path to a repository directory, rejecting aliases, applying ~user, interpolated-path or base-path rules and then enter_repo with optional strictness.

nodes.name: daemon_service
nodes.summary: Describes one service the daemon can run: protocol name, config name, handler function and enabled and overridable flags.

nodes.name: daemon_error
nodes.summary: Sends an ERR pkt-line to the client with either the real message or a generic access denied text, depending on informative-errors.

nodes.name: run_access_hook
nodes.summary: Runs the configured --access-hook with service, path and host info, and turns a non-zero exit or its output into a rejection message for the client.

nodes.name: run_service
nodes.summary: Checks that a service is enabled (including daemon.<service> config), the repository exists and is exported, and the access hook allows it, then calls the service handler.

nodes.name: copy_to_log
nodes.summary: Reads a child's stderr line by line and forwards each line to the daemon log.

nodes.name: run_service_command
nodes.summary: Starts the service as a `git` child process on ".", closes stdio and relays the child's stderr to the log until it exits.

nodes.name: upload_pack
nodes.summary: Service handler that runs `git upload-pack --strict --timeout=N` to serve fetch and clone.

nodes.name: receive_pack
nodes.summary: Service handler that runs `git receive-pack` to accept pushes.

nodes.name: parse_host_and_port
nodes.summary: Splits a host[:port] string (including bracketed IPv6) into host and port parts.

nodes.name: parse_host_arg
nodes.summary: Parses the host= extended attribute from the request packet and fills in hostname and port, dying on an invalid request.

nodes.name: parse_extra_args
nodes.summary: Parses extra NUL-separated arguments after the request line, handling host= and collecting the rest into GIT_PROTOCOL (protocol v2 negotiation).

nodes.name: lookup_hostname
nodes.summary: Resolves the client-supplied hostname with getaddrinfo to fill canonical name and IP address for use in interpolation and hooks.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Per-connection entry: sets keepalive, reads the first pkt-line with a timeout, parses extra args and dispatches to the matching git-<service> handler, or logs a protocol error.

nodes.name: addrcmp
nodes.summary: Compares two socket addresses by family and address bytes for IPv4 and IPv6.

nodes.name: child
nodes.summary: Linked list node tracking a forked connection handler: its child_process and the client address.

nodes.name: add_child
nodes.summary: Registers a new connection child in the list, grouped next to other children from the same address.

nodes.name: kill_some_child
nodes.summary: Under connection pressure, sends SIGTERM to a child whose address matches another, to make room for new connections.

nodes.name: check_dead_children
nodes.summary: Reaps finished children with waitpid(WNOHANG), logs their disconnect and frees their list entries.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Accepts one connection: enforces max_connections, puts REMOTE_ADDR and REMOTE_PORT into the child's environment, spawns the daemon again in per-connection mode and registers the child.

nodes.name: setup_named_sock
nodes.summary: Creates, binds and listens on sockets for each address returned by getaddrinfo (IPv6-aware version).

nodes.name: socksetup
nodes.summary: Sets up listening sockets for every --listen address, or on all interfaces when none is given.

nodes.name: service_loop
nodes.summary: Main server loop: poll()s all listening sockets, accepts connections with retry on EINTR and passes each to handle, reaping children between rounds.

nodes.name: prepare_credentials
nodes.summary: Looks up the --user and --group accounts for privilege dropping, dying if they do not exist.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Sets up sockets, drops privileges after binding and runs the service loop.

nodes.name: cmd_main
nodes.summary: Entry point of git-daemon: parses the many options (--listen, --port, --inetd, --base-path, --enable, --detach, --user and others), validates incompatible combinations and runs either one request (inetd) or the server.

nodes.name: date.h
nodes.summary: Public API for Git date handling: the date_mode formatting modes, formatting a timestamp with show_date, parsing date strings (including approximate dates such as "2 weeks ago") and expiry dates. The implementations live in date.c.

nodes.name: date_mode_type
nodes.summary: Enumeration of output date formats (normal, human, relative, short, ISO 8601, strict ISO, RFC 2822, strftime, raw, unix).

nodes.name: date_mode
nodes.summary: Selects how show_date formats a timestamp: the mode type, local-time flag and an optional strftime format.

nodes.name: date_mode_release
nodes.summary: Frees the strftime format string that parse_date_format may have allocated.

nodes.name: date_overflows
nodes.summary: Returns whether a timestamp is too large to be represented safely.

nodes.name: diagnose.h
nodes.summary: Declares the diagnose API that collects repository information and statistics into a zip archive for bug reports (used by `git diagnose` and `git bugreport --diagnose`).

nodes.name: diagnose_mode
nodes.summary: Enumeration of how much a diagnostics archive contains: none, stats only, or all (including packs and loose objects).

nodes.name: dir-iterator.c
nodes.summary: A stack-based recursive directory iterator that yields every path below a start directory with its lstat data, optionally sorted and optionally stopping on errors (pedantic mode).

nodes.name: dir_iterator_level
nodes.summary: One level of the iteration stack: the open DIR handle or a sorted list of names, the index into it and the path prefix length.

nodes.name: dir_iterator_int
nodes.summary: Internal iterator state that wraps the public dir_iterator with the level stack, its allocation count and the flags.

nodes.name: next_directory_entry
nodes.summary: Reads the next directory entry skipping . and .., returning 1 at the end and -1 with a warning on read errors.

nodes.name: push_level
nodes.summary: Opens the directory at the current path as a new stack level and, in sorted mode, reads and sorts all entry names up front.

nodes.name: pop_level
nodes.summary: Closes the top stack level and releases its entry list.

nodes.name: prepare_next_entry_data
nodes.summary: Appends an entry name to the path buffer, resets relative_path and basename pointers and lstat()s the new path.

nodes.name: dir_iterator_advance
nodes.summary: Advances to the next entry, descending into directories by pushing a level and popping when a directory is exhausted, and returns ITER_OK, ITER_DONE or ITER_ERROR.

nodes.name: dir_iterator_free
nodes.summary: Closes every open directory and frees the level stack, path buffer and iterator.

nodes.name: dir_iterator_begin
nodes.summary: Creates an iterator for a directory after lstat checking that it exists and is a directory.

nodes.name: dir-iterator.h
nodes.summary: Declares the directory iterator API (begin, advance, free), the struct dir_iterator exposed to callers and the PEDANTIC and SORTED flags.

nodes.name: dir_iterator
nodes.summary: Public iterator record that callers read: current path, path relative to the start, basename and lstat result.

nodes.name: editor.c
nodes.summary: Finds and launches the user's text editor for commit messages and rebase todo lists: chooses between GIT_EDITOR, core.editor, VISUAL and EDITOR, runs it through the shell and reads the edited file back into a strbuf.

nodes.name: is_terminal_dumb
nodes.summary: Returns true when TERM is unset or "dumb".

nodes.name: git_editor
nodes.summary: Selects the editor command by precedence GIT_EDITOR, core.editor, VISUAL (not on a dumb terminal), EDITOR and a compiled default, or NULL on a dumb terminal with none set.

nodes.name: git_sequence_editor
nodes.summary: Selects the editor for sequence files from GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR, sequence.editor and then the normal editor.

nodes.name: launch_specified_editor
nodes.summary: Runs the editor on a file through the shell with SIGINT and SIGQUIT ignored in the parent, optionally prints a waiting hint, re-raises a signal that killed the editor and reads the result into a buffer.

nodes.name: launch_editor
nodes.summary: Launches the configured editor on a path and optionally reads the file back.

nodes.name: launch_sequence_editor
nodes.summary: Launches the sequence editor (used for interactive rebase todo files).

nodes.name: strbuf_edit_interactively
nodes.summary: Writes a buffer to a file under the git dir (or an absolute path), opens it in the editor and reads the edited text back into the buffer, then removes the file.

nodes.name: environment.c
nodes.summary: Holds global and per-repository settings derived from the environment and from the core.*, branch.*, push.*, pack.*, i18n.*, sparse.* and related config variables, plus accessors such as namespace handling for refs. git_default_config is the common callback that most commands chain to.
nodes.languageNotes: Settings that used to be loose globals are being moved into struct repo_config_values, reached via repo_config_values(repo).

nodes.name: getenv_safe
nodes.summary: Reads an environment variable and stores a copy in a strvec so the pointer stays valid after later setenv calls.

nodes.name: is_bare_repository
nodes.summary: Returns true if core.bare is set and the repository has no work tree.

nodes.name: repo_protect_ntfs
nodes.summary: Returns the NTFS path protection setting for an initialized repository, or the platform default.

nodes.name: repo_protect_hfs
nodes.summary: Returns the HFS+ path protection setting for an initialized repository, or the platform default.

nodes.name: repo_ignore_case
nodes.summary: Returns core.ignorecase for an initialized repository, otherwise 0.

nodes.name: repo_trust_executable_bit
nodes.summary: Returns core.filemode (trust executable bit) for an initialized repository, otherwise 1.

nodes.name: repo_has_symlinks
nodes.summary: Returns core.symlinks for an initialized repository, otherwise the platform capability.

nodes.name: repo_excludes_file
nodes.summary: Returns core.excludesFile, falling back to the XDG ignore file path when unset.

nodes.name: get_git_namespace
nodes.summary: Builds the ref namespace prefix `refs/namespaces/<a>/refs/namespaces/<b>/` from GIT_NAMESPACE, validating the resulting ref name and caching it.

nodes.name: strip_namespace
nodes.summary: Removes the active ref namespace prefix from a ref name, or returns NULL if it does not have it.

nodes.name: get_log_output_encoding
nodes.summary: Returns i18n.logOutputEncoding, falling back to the commit output encoding.

nodes.name: get_commit_output_encoding
nodes.summary: Returns i18n.commitEncoding or UTF-8.

nodes.name: use_optional_locks
nodes.summary: Returns whether GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS allows commands like status to take optional locks such as the index refresh lock.

nodes.name: parse_fsync_components
nodes.summary: Parses a core.fsync value like `committed,-loose-object` into a bitmask of components (loose-object, pack, index, reference and so on), supporting negation and "none".

nodes.name: git_default_core_config
nodes.summary: Large callback handling core.* variables: filemode, symlinks, ignorecase, bare, abbrev, compression levels, fsync, autocrlf, whitespace, sparse checkout and many others, storing them in repo_config_values or globals.

nodes.name: git_default_sparse_config
nodes.summary: Handles sparse.* variables such as sparse.expectFilesOutsideOfPatterns.

nodes.name: git_default_i18n_config
nodes.summary: Handles i18n.commitEncoding and i18n.logOutputEncoding.

nodes.name: git_default_branch_config
nodes.summary: Handles branch.autoSetupMerge (always, inherit, simple, bool) and branch.autoSetupRebase (never, local, remote, always).

nodes.name: git_default_push_config
nodes.summary: Handles push.default and validates it against nothing, matching, simple, upstream, current.

nodes.name: git_default_attr_config
nodes.summary: Handles attr.tree, the tree from which gitattributes are read.

nodes.name: git_default_config
nodes.summary: The shared config callback: dispatches by key prefix to core, user/identity, i18n, branch, push, attr, advice, pager, pack and sparse handlers and handles index.maxpathlen.

nodes.name: repo_config_values_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a repo_config_values struct with the built-in defaults for compression, tracking, symlinks, file mode and other settings.

nodes.name: repo_config_values_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the string settings held in a repo_config_values struct.

nodes.name: exec-cmd.c
nodes.summary: Locates Git's own installation: finds the running executable (per-OS methods) to support RUNTIME_PREFIX, computes system paths, manages the exec path where git-* programs live, puts it first on PATH and executes `git` subcommands.
nodes.languageNotes: Large #ifdef blocks pick an executable-path method (procfs, sysctl, Darwin, z/OS, Windows) at compile time.

nodes.name: git_get_exec_path
nodes.summary: Finds the absolute path of the running executable by trying platform-specific methods in order of reliability (BSD sysctl, Darwin, procfs, Windows, z/OS) and falling back to argv[0], then normalizes it.

nodes.name: git_resolve_executable_dir
nodes.summary: Computes the directory containing the git executable and stores it for RUNTIME_PREFIX builds; a no-op without runtime prefix.

nodes.name: system_path
nodes.summary: Returns a path under the installation prefix (absolute paths pass through), used for system config and locale directories.

nodes.name: git_set_exec_path
nodes.summary: Sets the exec path and exports it as GIT_EXEC_PATH for child processes.

nodes.name: git_exec_path
nodes.summary: Returns the directory with git-* programs, from the value set earlier, GIT_EXEC_PATH or the compiled default.

nodes.name: add_path
nodes.summary: Appends an absolute directory and a path separator to a PATH-building buffer if the path is non-empty.

nodes.name: setup_path
nodes.summary: Prepends the exec path to the PATH environment variable so git-* commands are found first.

nodes.name: prepare_git_cmd
nodes.summary: Builds an argv with "git" as the first element followed by the given arguments.

nodes.name: execv_git_cmd
nodes.summary: Executes `git` with the given NULL-terminated argv, tracing the call; returns -1 if the exec fails.

nodes.name: execl_git_cmd
nodes.summary: Variadic wrapper that collects arguments up to NULL and calls execv_git_cmd.

nodes.name: exec-cmd.h
nodes.summary: Declares the exec path and path setup API used to find and run Git's own subcommands.

nodes.name: gettext.c
nodes.summary: Internationalization support: sets up the gettext text domain and locale, determines the locale charset and whether it is UTF-8, reads the preferred language list and computes display width of translated strings.

nodes.name: locale_charset
nodes.summary: Fallback that derives the locale charset from LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE or LANG when libcharset and langinfo are unavailable.

nodes.name: get_preferred_languages
nodes.summary: Returns the user's language list from LANGUAGE or the LC_MESSAGES locale (ignoring C and POSIX), such as "ko:ja:en".

nodes.name: init_gettext_charset
nodes.summary: Binds the text domain to the locale charset and works around an old glibc vsnprintf bug by switching LC_CTYPE to C when it triggers.

nodes.name: git_setup_gettext
nodes.summary: Initializes gettext: finds the locale directory (GIT_TEXTDOMAINDIR or the system path), binds the "git" domain, sets LC_MESSAGES and LC_TIME and enables translations.

nodes.name: gettext_width
nodes.summary: Returns the display width in columns of a string, using UTF-8 width tables in a UTF-8 locale and byte length otherwise.

nodes.name: is_utf8_locale
nodes.summary: Returns whether the current locale charset is UTF-8, recomputing it from the environment when gettext is compiled out.

nodes.name: gpg-interface.c
nodes.summary: Interface to signing and signature verification for commits, tags and push certificates through three formats: OpenPGP (gpg), X.509 (gpgsm) and SSH (ssh-keygen). It signs buffers, runs the external program to verify a detached signature, parses its status output and applies the minimum trust level.
nodes.languageNotes: A table of struct gpg_format entries holds per-format function pointers, giving a small strategy pattern over external programs.

nodes.name: gpg_interface_lazy_init
nodes.summary: Reads gpg.* and user.signingkey settings once on first use via repo_config.

nodes.name: gpg_format
nodes.summary: Describes one signature format: program name, verify arguments, signature header markers and function pointers for verify, sign, default key and key id.

nodes.name: get_format_by_name
nodes.summary: Finds a signature format by name (openpgp, x509, ssh).

nodes.name: get_format_by_sig
nodes.summary: Detects the format of a signature block by matching its BEGIN header line against each format's markers.

nodes.name: get_signature_format
nodes.summary: Returns the format name of a signature in a buffer, or "unknown".

nodes.name: valid_signature_format
nodes.summary: Checks that a string names a known signature format or "unknown".

nodes.name: signature_check_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the allocated fields of a signature_check result.

nodes.name: parse_gpg_trust_level
nodes.summary: Maps a gpg trust name (UNDEFINED, NEVER, MARGINAL, FULLY, ULTIMATE) to the signature_trust_level enum.

nodes.name: parse_gpg_output
nodes.summary: Parses gpg's `[GNUPG:]` status lines (GOODSIG, BADSIG, ERRSIG, VALIDSIG, TRUST_*) to fill result code, signer, key id, fingerprints and trust level.

nodes.name: verify_gpg_signed_buffer
nodes.summary: Writes the detached signature to a temp file, runs gpg or gpgsm with --verify on the payload via a pipe, captures status and stderr and parses the result.

nodes.name: parse_ssh_output
nodes.summary: Parses ssh-keygen verify output ("Good git signature for ...") to set the result, signer principal, key and fingerprint.

nodes.name: verify_ssh_signed_buffer
nodes.summary: Verifies an SSH signature: finds matching principals in gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile with ssh-keygen -Y find-principals, then runs -Y verify with the signing time and checks the revocation file.

nodes.name: parse_payload_metadata
nodes.summary: Extracts the committer or tagger timestamp from the signed payload so SSH key validity can be checked at signing time.

nodes.name: check_signature
nodes.summary: Verifies a signature over a payload: detects the format, reads payload metadata, runs that format's verifier and fails unless the result is good and the trust level meets gpg.minTrustLevel.

nodes.name: print_signature_buffer
nodes.summary: Prints a verification result: raw status or human output, and the payload in verbose mode.

nodes.name: parse_signed_buffer
nodes.summary: Scans a buffer line by line and returns the offset where the last signature block begins, or the buffer size when there is none.

nodes.name: parse_signature
nodes.summary: Splits a buffer into the signed payload and the trailing signature, removing the signature from the payload.

nodes.name: set_signing_key
nodes.summary: Records the configured signing key id, replacing any earlier value.

nodes.name: git_gpg_config
nodes.summary: Config callback for user.signingkey, gpg.format, gpg.minTrustLevel, gpg.ssh.* and the per-format program settings.

nodes.name: is_literal_ssh_key
nodes.summary: Recognizes a literal public key given as `key::...` or an `ssh-*` string rather than a file path.

nodes.name: get_ssh_key_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Computes the fingerprint of an SSH signing key by running `ssh-keygen -lf`.

nodes.name: get_default_ssh_signing_key
nodes.summary: Runs gpg.ssh.defaultKeyCommand and takes the first literal key line as the default signing key.

nodes.name: get_signing_key_id
nodes.summary: Returns the key id for the active format, using its get_key_id callback or the signing key.

nodes.name: get_signing_key
nodes.summary: Returns the configured signing key, the format's default key, or the committer identity as a last resort.

nodes.name: sign_buffer
nodes.summary: Signs a buffer with the selected format, optionally substituting the default key when none is given.

nodes.name: strip_cr_before_lf
nodes.summary: Removes carriage returns that precede a newline from a signature buffer, in place.

nodes.name: sign_buffer_gpg
nodes.summary: Signs a buffer by running gpg or gpgsm with -bsau and piping the payload in, requires a SIG_CREATED status and normalizes line endings of the signature.

nodes.name: sign_buffer_ssh
nodes.summary: Signs a buffer with `ssh-keygen -Y sign` using a key file or a literal key written to a temp file, then reads back the generated signature file.

nodes.name: parse_sign_mode
nodes.summary: Parses a signed-tag handling mode name such as abort, strip, warn-verbatim or sign-if-invalid=<keyid> into an enum and optional key id.

nodes.name: hook.c
nodes.summary: Discovers and runs Git hooks: traditional executables under `$GIT_DIR/hooks`, and hooks defined in config (`hook.<name>.command` bound to events with `hook.<name>.event`). It builds a per-repository hook config cache, honors enabled and parallel settings and runs hook lists through the parallel process runner.
nodes.languageNotes: Hook config is gathered in one repo_config pass into several strmaps, then frozen into a cache of per-event string lists whose util pointers carry hook_config_cache_entry records.

nodes.name: is_known_hook
nodes.summary: Returns true if a name appears in the generated hook_name_list of official hook events.

nodes.name: find_hook
nodes.summary: Finds an executable traditional hook in the hooks directory of a repository, returning NULL (with an advice message when it is merely not executable).

nodes.name: hook_free
nodes.summary: Frees a hook entry including its traditional path or configured name and command and any feed-pipe data.

nodes.name: list_hooks_add_default
nodes.summary: Appends the traditional hook for an event to the list, making its path absolute if the hook runs in another directory and allocating per-hook pipe data.

nodes.name: hook_config_cache_entry
nodes.summary: Cached data for one configured hook: its command, config scope and disabled and parallel flags.

nodes.name: hook_all_config_cb
nodes.summary: Collects every hook.* config key in one pass: command map, event to friendly-name lists, disabled set, parallel flags and job counts.

nodes.name: hook_config_lookup_all
nodes.summary: repo_config callback that interprets hook.jobs, hook.<name>.event, .command, .enabled, .parallel and .jobs, validating values and rejecting names that collide with known events.

nodes.name: hook_cache_clear
nodes.summary: Frees the cached hook lists and entries and clears the map.

nodes.name: is_friendly_name
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name was seen as a hook friendly-name in the commands, parallel or event maps.

nodes.name: warn_jobs_on_friendly_names
nodes.summary: Warns when hook.<name>.jobs is set on something that looks like a friendly-name rather than an event name.

nodes.name: build_hook_config_map
nodes.summary: Reads all hook config, derives event-level disables, and builds the event to ordered hook cache lists, dying when an event-bound hook has no command.

nodes.name: get_hook_config_cache
nodes.summary: Returns the repository's hook config cache, building and storing it on first use, or a throwaway cache when there is no repository.

nodes.name: list_hooks_add_configured
nodes.summary: Adds hooks configured for an event to the list as configured hook records copied from the cache, including scope and disabled state.

nodes.name: list_hooks
nodes.summary: Returns the ordered list of hooks for an event: configured hooks first, then the traditional hook from the hooks directory.

nodes.name: hook_exists
nodes.summary: Returns whether any hook for an event would actually run, ignoring disabled configured hooks.

nodes.name: pick_next_hook
nodes.summary: Parallel runner callback that sets up the next child_process for the next enabled hook: env, stdin source, working dir and command (shell for configured hooks).

nodes.name: notify_start_failure
nodes.summary: Parallel runner callback that marks the run as failed when a hook could not be started.

nodes.name: notify_hook_finished
nodes.summary: Parallel runner callback that ORs a finished hook's exit status into the overall result and calls the invoked_hook callback.

nodes.name: warn_non_parallel_hooks_override
nodes.summary: Warns when hooks not marked parallel run in parallel anyway because of an explicit job count.

nodes.name: resolve_hook_config_jobs
nodes.summary: Reads a hook.jobs style config integer (with -1 meaning all CPUs) into a job count.

nodes.name: get_hook_jobs
nodes.summary: Determines how many hooks may run in parallel from options, hook.jobs and per-event settings, forcing serial when any configured hook is not parallel.

nodes.name: run_hooks_opt
nodes.summary: Main hook runner: lists hooks, resolves the job count, runs them through run_processes_parallel with stdin, env and output options, and returns the combined exit status.

nodes.name: run_hooks
nodes.summary: Runs hooks of an event with default options.

nodes.name: run_hooks_l
nodes.summary: Runs hooks of an event with a NULL-terminated list of arguments.

nodes.name: hook.h
nodes.summary: Public API for running Git hooks: structs describing a hook (traditional script in the hooks directory or a hook configured via hook.<name>.event), the options for running them (env, args, parallel jobs, stdin feeding callbacks), and functions to list, find, test for and run hooks for an event.
nodes.languageNotes: Optional C header documented with doc comments; the struct hook uses an anonymous enum plus a union so that traditional and configured hooks share one type.

nodes.name: hook
nodes.summary: One hook to run: a kind tag (traditional or configured) selecting either a script path or a friendly name, command, config scope and disabled flags, plus a parallel flag and per-hook feed_pipe callback state with its free function.

nodes.name: run_hooks_opt
nodes.summary: Options for a hook run: extra env and args (strvec), error_if_missing, job count for parallel execution, working dir, invoked_hook out-flag, stdout_to_stderr, a stdin file path and the feed_pipe callbacks with their alloc/free hooks.

nodes.name: hook_cb_data
nodes.summary: State shared across the run-command callbacks while hooks execute: cumulative return code, event name, the list of hook commands with a cursor to the next one, and the run options.

nodes.name: http-backend.c
nodes.summary: The CGI program behind Git's smart and dumb HTTP serving (`git http-backend`): it matches the request path against a table of GET/POST routes, checks that the repository is exported and the service enabled, and either serves ref advertisements and loose/pack files (dumb protocol) or pipes the request body (optionally gzip-inflated) into upload-pack, receive-pack or upload-archive (smart protocol).
nodes.languageNotes: A CGI program: all input comes from environment variables (REQUEST_METHOD, PATH_INFO, QUERY_STRING, CONTENT_LENGTH...) and the response is a header block written to fd 1, followed by the body.

nodes.name: rpc_service
nodes.summary: Describes one smart-protocol service (upload-pack, receive-pack, upload-archive): its name, the http.<name> config key, whether to buffer the input and its enabled state (-1 means enabled only for authenticated users).

nodes.name: service_cmd
nodes.summary: One row of the routing table: HTTP method, a POSIX regex for the path and the handler function (get_head, get_info_refs, get_loose_object, service_rpc, ...).

nodes.name: get_parameters
nodes.summary: Lazily decodes the QUERY_STRING into a string_list of name/value pairs (later values replace earlier ones).

nodes.name: get_parameter
nodes.summary: Looks up one decoded query parameter by name.

nodes.name: format_write
nodes.summary: printf-style write to a file descriptor through a fixed 1024-byte buffer that dies on overlong output.

nodes.name: not_found
nodes.summary: Emits a "404 Not Found" header block with no-cache headers, prints the formatted message on stderr and exits successfully (the CGI has already reported the failure).

nodes.name: forbidden
nodes.summary: Emits a "403 Forbidden" header block with no-cache headers, logs the message on stderr and exits.

nodes.name: send_local_file
nodes.summary: Opens a file below the repository git dir, sends Content-Length, Content-Type and Last-Modified headers and then streams the file to stdout in 8 KiB chunks; 404 if it cannot be opened.

nodes.name: get_text_file
nodes.summary: Handler for plain text files such as objects/info/alternates: requires getanyfile, sets no-cache and sends the file as text/plain.

nodes.name: get_loose_object
nodes.summary: Handler for loose object requests: sends the file with a forever-cache header and the application/x-git-loose-object type.

nodes.name: get_pack_file
nodes.summary: Handler for objects/pack/pack-*.pack: sends the packfile with forever caching and type application/x-git-packed-objects.

nodes.name: get_idx_file
nodes.summary: Handler for objects/pack/pack-*.idx: sends the pack index with forever caching and type application/x-git-packed-objects-toc.

nodes.name: http_config
nodes.summary: Reads http.getanyfile, http.maxrequestbuffer and the http.uploadpack/receivepack/uploadarchive settings from the repository config to set which services are enabled.

nodes.name: select_service
nodes.summary: Maps a "git-<name>" request name to an rpc_service, replying 403 if unknown or disabled; receive-pack and upload-archive default to enabled only when REMOTE_USER is set.

nodes.name: read_request_eof
nodes.summary: Reads the whole request body into a growing buffer until EOF, dying if it exceeds max_request_buffer (protects against huge requests).

nodes.name: read_request_fixed_len
nodes.summary: Reads exactly CONTENT_LENGTH bytes of the request body into a buffer, dying when the length exceeds max_request_buffer.

nodes.name: inflate_request
nodes.summary: Streams a gzip-compressed request body through zlib inflate and writes the plain bytes to the child process stdin, either buffering input fully or reading it in 8 KiB pieces.

nodes.name: copy_request
nodes.summary: Reads the full request body and writes it unchanged to the child process stdin, then closes it.

nodes.name: pipe_fixed_length
nodes.summary: Copies exactly req_len bytes from stdin to the child process in 8 KiB chunks without buffering the whole body.

nodes.name: run_service
nodes.summary: Spawns `git <service> --stateless-rpc .` as a child process with committer identity derived from REMOTE_USER and REMOTE_ADDR, feeds it the request body (inflated, buffered or piped) and waits for it to finish; its stdout becomes the HTTP response.

nodes.name: show_text_ref
nodes.summary: refs iterator callback that appends "<oid>\t<refname>" lines for the dumb info/refs file, adding a peeled "refname^{}" line for annotated tags.

nodes.name: get_info_refs
nodes.summary: Handles GET /info/refs. With ?service= it sends the smart-protocol advertisement (a "# service=" pkt-line for protocol v0/v1) by running the service with --http-backend-info-refs; otherwise it builds the dumb text listing of refs.

nodes.name: show_head_ref
nodes.summary: refs callback that writes HEAD for the dumb protocol: "ref: <target>" for a symbolic ref, otherwise the oid.

nodes.name: get_head
nodes.summary: Handler for GET /HEAD: sends the text form of HEAD built by show_head_ref.

nodes.name: get_info_packs
nodes.summary: Handler for GET /objects/info/packs: lists the local packfiles as "P pack-xxx.pack" lines for dumb clients.

nodes.name: check_content_type
nodes.summary: Verifies CONTENT_TYPE equals the type expected for an RPC POST and replies "415 Unsupported Media Type" otherwise.

nodes.name: service_rpc
nodes.summary: Handles POST /git-upload-pack, git-receive-pack and git-upload-archive: selects the service, checks the request content type, writes result headers and runs the service with --stateless-rpc.

nodes.name: die_webcgi
nodes.summary: die() routine installed for the CGI: prints the message, then emits a "500 Internal Server Error" header block (once) before exiting normally.

nodes.name: getdir
nodes.summary: Computes the repository directory from GIT_PROJECT_ROOT plus PATH_INFO (rejecting aliased paths) or from PATH_TRANSLATED.

nodes.name: bad_request
nodes.summary: Replies 405 (with an Allow header) under HTTP/1.1 or 400 otherwise when the route matched but the HTTP method did not.

nodes.name: cmd_main
nodes.summary: Program entry: installs the CGI die handlers, matches REQUEST_METHOD and the translated path against the services table with regexec, enters the repository, checks the export-ok marker, loads http config, forwards the Git-Protocol header and calls the selected handler.

nodes.name: read_request
nodes.summary: Reads the request body either until EOF or for a known CONTENT_LENGTH, choosing between the two readers.

nodes.name: hdr_nocache
nodes.summary: Adds Expires, Pragma and Cache-Control headers that forbid caching of the response.

nodes.name: hdr_cache_forever
nodes.summary: Adds Date, Expires (one year ahead) and a public max-age header for immutable objects such as loose objects and packs.

nodes.name: select_getanyfile
nodes.summary: Rejects the request with 403 when http.getanyfile is disabled, guarding all dumb-protocol file handlers.

nodes.name: files-backend.c
nodes.summary: Implements the default 'files' ref backend: loose refs as one file per ref under .git/refs, layered over the packed-refs store, with lockfile-based transactions, reflogs under logs/, pack-refs, rename/copy and fsck. This is how a stock repository stores branches, tags and HEAD.
nodes.languageNotes: C source that implements a vtable of function pointers (ref_storage_be) so the generic refs layer can dispatch to this backend.

nodes.name: clear_loose_ref_cache
nodes.summary: Frees the in-memory loose ref cache so the next read rescans the refs directory.

nodes.name: files_read_raw_ref
nodes.summary: Backend read_raw_ref entry that reads a ref from its loose file and falls back to packed-refs.

nodes.name: unlock_ref
nodes.summary: Drops one user of a ref lock and rolls back and frees it when the count reaches zero.

nodes.name: prune_refs
nodes.summary: Prunes every loose ref in a list of refs that were just packed.

nodes.name: files_ref_store_reparent
nodes.summary: chdir-notify callback that rewrites the relative gitdir and common-dir paths of a files ref store after the process changes its working directory.

nodes.name: files_ref_store_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads core.preferSymlinkRefs and core.logAllRefUpdates into the lazily loaded write options of the files ref store.

nodes.name: files_ref_store_write_options
nodes.summary: Returns the write options (reflog policy, symlink preference), loading them from the repository config the first time they are needed.

nodes.name: files_ref_store_init
nodes.summary: Backend init: computes the refdir and common ref dir, initializes the base ref_store and creates the nested packed-refs store that holds the packed half of the files backend.

nodes.name: files_downcast
nodes.summary: Casts a generic ref_store to files_ref_store and BUGs if the backend type is wrong or the store lacks the required capability flags.

nodes.name: files_reflog_path
nodes.summary: Builds the path of a ref reflog under logs/, choosing the current worktree, common dir or another worktree directory from the refname.

nodes.name: files_ref_path
nodes.summary: Builds the filesystem path of a loose ref, mapping per-worktree and shared refs to the right gitdir or common dir.

nodes.name: add_per_worktree_entries_to_dir
nodes.summary: Adds placeholder directory entries for refs/bisect, refs/worktree and refs/rewritten to the cache for refs/ so per-worktree ref directories are always seen.

nodes.name: loose_fill_ref_dir_regular_file
nodes.summary: Resolves one loose ref file, flags it broken if unreadable, null or badly named, and adds the resulting entry to the ref cache directory.

nodes.name: loose_fill_ref_dir
nodes.summary: Fills one level of the loose-ref cache by reading a refs directory with readdir, skipping dotfiles and .lock files and adding subdirectories as lazily filled entries.

nodes.name: for_each_root_ref
nodes.summary: Scans the top of the gitdir for regular files whose names look like root refs (HEAD, ORIG_HEAD and so on) and calls a callback for each.

nodes.name: add_root_refs
nodes.summary: Adds every root ref found in the gitdir to the loose ref cache directory.

nodes.name: get_loose_ref_cache
nodes.summary: Lazily creates the in-memory loose ref cache with an incomplete refs/ directory, optionally pre-adding root refs.

nodes.name: read_ref_internal
nodes.summary: Reads a ref from its loose file (lstat, readlink or open), retrying around races, then falls back to packed-refs when the loose file or directory is missing.

nodes.name: files_read_symbolic_ref
nodes.summary: Reads a symbolic ref through read_ref_internal without consulting packed-refs, since packed-refs cannot hold symrefs.

nodes.name: parse_loose_ref_contents
nodes.summary: Parses the content of a loose ref file as either "ref: target" (symbolic) or a hex object id, flagging the ref as broken when the content is malformed.

nodes.name: transaction_has_case_conflicting_update
nodes.summary: Checks whether another update in the same transaction has a refname that differs only by case, which matters on case-insensitive filesystems.

nodes.name: lock_raw_ref
nodes.summary: Creates leading directories and takes the .lock file for a ref without following symrefs, reads the ref under the lock, and classifies failures such as name or case conflicts, with retries against concurrent directory cleanup.

nodes.name: files_ref_iterator_advance
nodes.summary: Advances the merged loose and packed iterator while filtering by worktree scope, dangling symrefs and refs whose object does not exist.

nodes.name: files_ref_iterator_begin
nodes.summary: Creates the files backend iterator by overlaying the loose-ref cache iterator on top of the packed-refs iterator, reading loose refs first to avoid a pack-refs race.

nodes.name: raceproof_create_file
nodes.summary: Runs a file-creating callback, creating missing parent directories or removing empty directories in the way, and retrying when another process cleans up concurrently.

nodes.name: lock_ref_oid_basic
nodes.summary: Locks a loose ref for modification, checks packed-refs for name conflicts when the ref is new, and records the old oid. Used by reflog expiry.

nodes.name: try_remove_empty_parents
nodes.summary: Walks up from a deleted ref or reflog and rmdirs empty parent directories, sparing refs/ and its immediate subdirectories.

nodes.name: prune_ref
nodes.summary: Deletes one loose ref after it has been packed, by running a REF_IS_PRUNING transaction that checks the ref is unchanged.

nodes.name: should_pack_ref
nodes.summary: Decides whether a loose ref is eligible for packing: shared, non-symbolic, resolving to an object and matching the include and exclude patterns.

nodes.name: should_pack_refs
nodes.summary: Implements the auto-pack heuristic that decides whether the number of loose refs is large enough, relative to the size of packed-refs, to justify packing.

nodes.name: files_optimize
nodes.summary: Implements pack-refs: iterates loose refs, writes eligible ones to packed-refs through a locked packed transaction, then prunes the loose copies.

nodes.name: rename_tmp_log_callback
nodes.summary: Callback that renames the temporary logs/refs/.tmp-renamed-log file into place, mapping ENOTDIR to EISDIR for the retry logic.

nodes.name: rename_tmp_log

nodes.summary: Arguments for writing an expiry table.

nodes.name: refs_be_reftable
nodes.summary: The ref_storage_be vtable named "reftable" wiring the reftable backend into the generic refs layer.

nodes.name: ref_update
nodes.summary: One pending reference update inside a transaction: new and old oid or target, flags (REF_HAVE_NEW, REF_HAVE_OLD, REF_LOG_ONLY), reflog message, rejection error and backend data.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_state
nodes.summary: Enum of the lifecycle states of a ref transaction: open, prepared and closed.

nodes.name: ref_transaction_rejections
nodes.summary: Indices of updates rejected in a batched transaction so backends can skip them.

nodes.name: ref_transaction
nodes.summary: Opaque ref transaction: the target ref_store, array of ref_update, state, rejections and backend-specific data.

nodes.name: ref_iterator
nodes.summary: Base type of every ref iterator: a vtable pointer and the current reference being yielded.

nodes.name: ref_iterator_vtable
nodes.summary: Function table (advance, seek, release) that each iterator type implements.

nodes.name: ref_store_init_options
nodes.summary: Options passed to backend init functions, chiefly the access flags describing allowed operations.

nodes.name: ref_storage_be
nodes.summary: The backend interface: init, release, transaction prepare/finish/abort, optimize, rename/copy, iterators, raw and symbolic ref reads, reflog operations and fsck. Each ref format (files, reftable, packed) provides one.

nodes.name: ref_store
nodes.summary: Base type of all reference stores: the backend vtable, owning repository and gitdir.

nodes.name: reftable-iterator.h
nodes.summary: Public header of the reftable library that declares the generic iterator used to walk ref and log records stored in reftable files. It defines the vtable-backed struct and the seek/next/destroy API shared by tables, merged tables and stacks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a hand-rolled vtable (ops pointer plus opaque iter_arg) to get polymorphism in C.

nodes.name: reftable_iterator
nodes.summary: Generic iterator handle for the reftable backend: a vtable pointer plus an opaque argument, so the same API can walk a single table, a merged table or a stack.

nodes.name: reftable-stack.h
nodes.summary: Public header of the reftable library describing a stack of reftables: opening a stack, adding tables inside a locked transaction, iterating merged refs and logs, compaction and statistics. It is the main API the reftable ref backend uses to read and write refs.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutations go through a reftable_addition transaction that holds the stack lock until commit or destroy.

nodes.name: reftable_stack_options
nodes.summary: Options for opening a stack: hash id, an on_reload callback with payload to invalidate caches, and a flag to suppress deletions.

nodes.name: reftable_log_expiry_config
nodes.summary: Reflog expiry policy for compaction: drop entries older than a timestamp or below a minimum update index.

nodes.name: reftable_compaction_stats
nodes.summary: Counters describing past compactions: bytes and entries written, attempts and failures caused by concurrent updates.

nodes.name: repo-settings.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct repo_settings, the per-repository cache of lazily loaded config values (commit-graph, sparse index, pack, fsmonitor, index version, big file threshold, shared repository) plus the accessors for them. Defaults live in REPO_SETTINGS_INIT.
nodes.languageNotes: REPO_SETTINGS_INIT uses designated initializers for sentinel defaults like -1 meaning "not yet read".

nodes.name: repo_settings
nodes.summary: Per-repository settings cache holding commit-graph, pack, index, fsmonitor, hooks path, shared-repository and big-file-threshold values so config is parsed once and reused.

nodes.name: untracked_cache_setting
nodes.summary: Enum choosing whether to keep, remove or write the untracked cache in the index.

nodes.name: fetch_negotiation_setting
nodes.summary: Enum selecting the fetch negotiation algorithm: consecutive, skipping or noop.

nodes.name: repository.c
nodes.summary: Implements struct repository lifecycle: initializing the global the_repository, setting gitdir/commondir/worktree/hash algorithm/ref storage format, opening a repository or a submodule, loading the index and tearing everything down in repo_clear. It is the object that ties the object database, refs, config and index together.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps a single static the_repo and exposes the_repository as a global; repo_config_values enforces that only that instance may read config values.

nodes.name: set_default_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Reads GIT_TEST_DEFAULT_HASH_ALGO and, if set to a known hash name, sets that hash algorithm on the repo as an escape hatch for code running outside a repository.

nodes.name: repo_config_values
nodes.summary: Returns the private config values of a repository, aborting if called on a repository other than the_repository or before it is initialized.

nodes.name: initialize_repository
nodes.summary: Marks a repository as initialized and allocates its remote state, parsed-object pool and in-memory index, setting defaults and the fallback hash algorithm for the_repository.

nodes.name: expand_base_dir
nodes.summary: Replaces a path field with the explicit value if given, otherwise with base_dir plus a default relative name such as info/grafts or index.

nodes.name: repo_get_git_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the repository gitdir, calling BUG if the repository has not been set up.

nodes.name: repo_get_common_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the common directory shared by all worktrees of a repository, with a BUG check for an unset repo.

nodes.name: repo_get_object_directory
nodes.summary: Returns the path of the primary object source (the objects directory) of the repository.

nodes.name: repo_get_index_file
nodes.summary: Returns the path of the index file of the repository, with a BUG check if unset.

nodes.name: repo_get_graft_file
nodes.summary: Returns the path of the grafts file used for commit graph rewriting.

nodes.name: repo_get_work_tree
nodes.summary: Returns the work tree path of the repository, or NULL for a bare repository.

nodes.name: repo_set_commondir
nodes.summary: Sets the common directory either from an explicit argument or by reading the commondir file of the gitdir, and records whether it differs from the gitdir.

nodes.name: repo_set_gitdir
nodes.summary: Sets the gitdir (following a .git file if present), derives the common dir, and fills in default graft and index file paths and the disable_ref_updates flag.

nodes.name: repo_set_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Selects the repository hash algorithm (SHA-1 or SHA-256) from the global hash_algos table.

nodes.name: repo_set_compat_hash_algo
nodes.summary: Sets the compatibility hash algorithm for transitions between hash functions, or dies if Rust support is not compiled in.

nodes.name: repo_set_ref_storage_format
nodes.summary: Records the ref storage backend (files or reftable) and its payload on the repository.

nodes.name: repo_init_gitdir
nodes.summary: Resolves a gitdir path to a real absolute path, validates it as a git directory or gitfile and applies it to the repository.

nodes.name: repo_set_worktree
nodes.summary: Sets the work tree to the real path and tells trace2 about the repo definition.

nodes.name: read_repository_format_from_commondir
nodes.summary: Reads the repository format (version and extensions) from the config file in the common directory.

nodes.name: repo_init
nodes.summary: Initializes a struct repository from a gitdir: resolves it, reads and applies the repository format, creates the object database and optionally sets the work tree, clearing on failure.

nodes.name: repo_submodule_init
nodes.summary: Opens a submodule as its own repository, first at path/.git and, if the submodule is not checked out, from the superproject modules directory located via submodule config.

nodes.name: repo_clear_path_cache
nodes.summary: Frees the cached paths of well-known files such as MERGE_HEAD, FETCH_HEAD, squash and merge messages and the shallow file.

nodes.name: repo_clear
nodes.summary: Releases everything a repository owns: paths, object database, parsed objects, settings, config, submodule cache, in-memory index, hook and promisor config, remote state and all ref stores.

nodes.name: repo_read_index
nodes.summary: Loads the on-disk index into repo->index, expands a sparse index if the command needs the full index and clears skip-worktree bits for paths present in the work tree.

nodes.name: repo_hold_locked_index
nodes.summary: Takes the lock file for updating the repository index file so that the index can be rewritten atomically.

nodes.name: repository
nodes.summary: The static the_repo instance and the the_repository pointer to it: the main repository of the running process.

nodes.name: setup.c
nodes.summary: Core of repository discovery and initialization: finds the git directory and work tree from the current directory, GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE, reads and verifies the repository format and extensions, enforces ownership (safe.directory) and bare-repository policy, and implements the work of git init (templates, config, refs and object database creation).
nodes.languageNotes: The discovery code is heavily annotated with test case numbers from t1510; state is passed through struct repo_discovery instead of globals.

nodes.name: abspath_part_inside_repo
nodes.summary: Given a normalized absolute path, returns the part that lies inside the work tree by stripping the work tree prefix or by resolving symlinks level by level, rewriting the path in place; returns -1 if outside.

nodes.name: prefix_path_gently
nodes.summary: Normalizes a path argument relative to a prefix, or an absolute one against the work tree, returning NULL if it escapes the repository.

nodes.name: prefix_path
nodes.summary: Like prefix_path_gently but dies with a message naming the repository when the path is outside it.

nodes.name: path_inside_repo
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path, interpreted relative to the prefix, lies inside the repository work tree.

nodes.name: check_filename
nodes.summary: Checks whether an argument names an existing file, honoring the :/ and :! pathspec magic prefixes and the current prefix, and dies on stat errors other than missing file.

nodes.name: die_verify_filename
nodes.summary: Dies with the right diagnostic for an argument that is neither a path nor an unambiguous revision, optionally diagnosing a misspelt object name.

nodes.name: looks_like_pathspec
nodes.summary: Heuristically decides whether an argument that is not an existing file still looks like a pathspec because it has glob characters or long-form magic.

nodes.name: verify_filename
nodes.summary: Verifies that an argument can be treated as a file or pathspec, dying if it is an option or a nonexistent non-pathspec, to disambiguate revisions from paths.

nodes.name: verify_non_filename
nodes.summary: Verifies that an argument parsed as a refname is not also an existing file, dying with an ambiguity message if both interpretations exist.

nodes.name: get_common_dir
nodes.summary: Appends the common dir from GIT_COMMON_DIR if set, otherwise from the commondir file of the gitdir.

nodes.name: get_common_dir_noenv
nodes.summary: Reads the commondir file of a worktree gitdir and appends the resolved path to the buffer, or the gitdir itself when there is no such file; returns whether it differs.

nodes.name: validate_headref
nodes.summary: Checks that HEAD is a symlink into refs/, a "ref:" symbolic ref to refs/, or a detached HEAD holding a valid object id.

nodes.name: is_git_directory
nodes.summary: Decides whether a directory looks like a git directory: valid HEAD, an objects directory (or GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY) and a refs directory in the common dir.

nodes.name: is_nonbare_repository_dir
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path holds a non-bare repository or submodule by looking at .git as a gitfile or directory, erring on the side of yes on read errors.

nodes.name: is_inside_git_dir
nodes.summary: Returns whether the current directory is inside the repository git directory.

nodes.name: is_inside_work_tree
nodes.summary: Returns whether the current directory is inside the repository work tree.

nodes.name: setup_work_tree
nodes.summary: Changes into the work tree (dying if there is none or config is bogus) and normalizes GIT_WORK_TREE so child processes find the same tree.

nodes.name: setup_original_cwd
nodes.summary: Records the original working directory as a path relative to the work tree in startup_info so that commands avoid removing the directory the user is in.

nodes.name: read_worktree_config
nodes.summary: Config callback that picks up core.bare and core.worktree into a repository_format.

nodes.name: handle_extension_v0
nodes.summary: Handles extensions honored even in v0 repositories (noop, preciousObjects, partialClone, worktreeConfig) for historical compatibility.

nodes.name: parse_reference_uri
nodes.summary: Splits a ref storage value of the form format://payload into the format name and payload.

nodes.name: handle_extension
nodes.summary: Parses version-1 extensions such as objectformat, compatobjectformat, refstorage, relativeworktrees and submodulepathconfig into the repository_format.

nodes.name: check_repo_format
nodes.summary: Config callback that reads core.repositoryformatversion and extensions.*, tracking known v1-only and unknown extensions, then falls through to worktree config.

nodes.name: read_and_verify_repository_format
nodes.summary: Reads the repository format from the common config, verifies it, merges per-worktree config.worktree and decides bareness and core.worktree depending on whether a common dir is shared.

nodes.name: upgrade_repository_format
nodes.summary: Raises core.repositoryformatversion to a target version if the current format is valid and has no unknown extensions.

nodes.name: init_repository_format
nodes.summary: Resets a repository_format struct to the REPOSITORY_FORMAT_INIT defaults.

nodes.name: read_repository_format
nodes.summary: Reads a config file into a repository_format, returning the version or -1 when none is present.

nodes.name: clear_repository_format
nodes.summary: Frees the allocated members of a repository_format and reinitializes it.

nodes.name: verify_repository_format
nodes.summary: Checks that a repository format is readable: supported version, no unknown extensions in v1 and no v1-only extensions in v0, building an error message otherwise.

nodes.name: read_gitfile_error_die
nodes.summary: Maps a READ_GITFILE_ERR_* code to a fatal error message, except for the benign missing/not-a-file cases.

nodes.name: read_gitfile_gently
nodes.summary: Reads a .git file, resolves a relative target, verifies it is a git directory and returns the real path from a shared buffer, or an error code.

nodes.name: read_gitfile_raw
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the "gitdir: " line of a .git file with size and type checks, returning an error code without resolving the path.

nodes.name: apply_gitdir_and_environment
nodes.summary: Applies a gitdir to the repository using GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_GRAFT_FILE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the quarantine environment.

nodes.name: update_relative_gitdir
nodes.summary: chdir-notify callback that rewrites a relative GIT_DIR after the process changes directory and re-exports it.

nodes.name: apply_and_export_relative_gitdir
nodes.summary: Sets the gitdir on the repository, exports it as GIT_DIR and registers for chdir notification when the path is relative.

nodes.name: repo_discovery_release
nodes.summary: Frees the format and path strings held by a repo_discovery state.

nodes.name: repo_discovery_set_gitdir
nodes.summary: Stores the discovered gitdir in the discovery state, optionally as a real path.

nodes.name: repo_discovery_set_worktree
nodes.summary: Stores the real path of the discovered work tree in the discovery state.

nodes.name: repo_discover_explicit_gitdir
nodes.summary: Handles GIT_DIR set explicitly: validates it, reads the repository format and decides the work tree from GIT_WORK_TREE, core.worktree or the cwd, then computes the prefix.

nodes.name: repo_discover_implicit_gitdir
nodes.summary: Handles a .git found while walking up from the cwd: verifies the format, honors work tree overrides and bare config, and sets the work tree and prefix.

nodes.name: repo_discover_bare_gitdir
nodes.summary: Handles a directory that itself is a bare git directory: verifies the format and sets the gitdir and implicit work tree behaviour.

nodes.name: get_device_or_die
nodes.summary: Returns st_dev of a path or dies with a descriptive message, used to stop discovery at filesystem boundaries.

nodes.name: canonicalize_ceiling_entry
nodes.summary: filter_string_list callback that canonicalizes GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES entries, dropping unusable ones.

nodes.name: safe_directory_cb
nodes.summary: Protected-config callback that evaluates safe.directory entries (*, ., absolute paths and trailing /*) against the repository path.

nodes.name: ensure_valid_ownership
nodes.summary: Checks that the gitfile, work tree and gitdir are owned by the current user, or that safe.directory lists the repository.

nodes.name: die_upon_dubious_ownership
nodes.summary: Dies with advice to add a safe.directory exception when ensure_valid_ownership fails.

nodes.name: allowed_bare_repo_cb
nodes.summary: Protected-config callback that parses safe.bareRepository as explicit or all.

nodes.name: get_allowed_bare_repo
nodes.summary: Returns the bare-repository policy from protected config, defaulting to all (or explicit with breaking changes).

nodes.name: allowed_bare_repo_to_string
nodes.summary: Converts the bare-repository policy enum to "explicit" or "all" for messages.

nodes.name: is_implicit_bare_repo
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path is a .git, a worktrees entry or a submodule modules directory, which are acceptable as implicit bare repositories.

nodes.name: repo_discovery_find_dir
nodes.summary: Walks from a directory upward looking for .git (file or directory) or a bare repository, honoring GIT_DIR, ceiling directories, filesystem boundaries, ownership and bare policy; returns a discovery_result.

nodes.name: discover_git_directory_reason
nodes.summary: Finds the commondir and gitdir of the repository containing the cwd without changing global state, validating the repository format and returning a reason code.

nodes.name: apply_repository_format
nodes.summary: Applies a verified repository_format to a repository: bareness, shallow file, hash algorithms, ref storage and extension flags.

nodes.name: enter_repo
nodes.summary: Used by servers to chdir into a repository given a path, trying suffixes like /.git and .git, checking ownership and applying the repository format and object database.

nodes.name: set_git_work_tree
nodes.summary: Sets the repository work tree once, dying if a different one was already set.

nodes.name: repo_discover
nodes.summary: Discovers the repository for the cwd and dispatches on the result (explicit, implicit, bare, ceiling, mount point, ownership, bare policy), setting discovery state or dying/setting nongit_ok.

nodes.name: setup_git_directory_gently
nodes.summary: Main entry for finding and entering the repository: runs discovery, sets work tree, gitdir, ref storage format and object database, exports GIT_PREFIX and returns the prefix.

nodes.name: git_config_perm
nodes.summary: Parses core.sharedRepository values (umask, group, all, octal filemodes, booleans) into permission constants.

nodes.name: setup_git_directory
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that calls setup_git_directory_gently and dies if no repository is found.

nodes.name: resolve_gitdir_gently
nodes.summary: Returns the path itself if it is a git directory, otherwise follows it as a gitfile.

nodes.name: sanitize_stdfds
nodes.summary: Ensures stdin, stdout and stderr are open by pointing missing ones at /dev/null.

nodes.name: daemonize
nodes.summary: Forks into the background, makes the child a session leader, closes standard descriptors and hands tempfile ownership to the child.

nodes.name: template_dir_cb
nodes.summary: Protected-config callback that reads init.templatedir.

nodes.name: get_template_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the template directory from the option, GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR, init.templatedir or the compiled default.

nodes.name: copy_templates_1
nodes.summary: Recursively copies the files, symlinks and directories of a template directory into a new git directory without overwriting existing entries.

nodes.name: copy_templates
nodes.summary: Copies the template directory into the common dir after verifying the template format version.

nodes.name: needs_work_tree_config
nodes.summary: Returns whether core.worktree must be set because the gitdir is not simply work_tree/.git.

nodes.name: initialize_repository_version
nodes.summary: Writes core.repositoryformatversion and the objectformat, refstorage and submodulepathconfig extensions that a new or reinitialized repository needs.

nodes.name: is_reinit
nodes.summary: Returns whether HEAD already exists, meaning git init is reinitializing a repository.

nodes.name: create_reference_database
nodes.summary: Creates the ref store on disk and, for a new repository, points HEAD at refs/heads/<initial branch> after validating the name.

nodes.name: create_default_files
nodes.summary: Copies templates, writes core.* defaults and probes the filesystem for filemode, symlink and case-insensitivity support during git init.

nodes.name: create_object_database
nodes.summary: Creates the objects directory in the common dir and instantiates the object database source on disk.

nodes.name: separate_git_dir
nodes.summary: Moves an existing gitdir to a separate location, writes a gitfile linking to it and repairs worktrees.

nodes.name: read_default_format_config
nodes.summary: Config callback reading init.defaultObjectFormat, init.defaultRefFormat and feature.experimental defaults.

nodes.name: repository_format_configure
nodes.summary: Decides hash algorithm and ref storage format for a new repository from command line, environment, config and defaults, rejecting changes on reinit.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Implements repository creation for git init: sets up gitdir and work tree, applies the repository format, creates default files, refs and object database, and prints the message.

nodes.name: repo_discovery
nodes.summary: State collected during repository discovery: the repository format, gitdir, worktree and prefix.

nodes.name: safe_directory_data
nodes.summary: Callback data for safe.directory evaluation: the normalized path and whether it was found safe.

nodes.name: template_dir_cb_data
nodes.summary: Callback data holding the template directory path read from init.templatedir.

nodes.name: default_format_config
nodes.summary: Callback data for the default hash and ref storage format read from config during git init.

nodes.name: extension_result
nodes.summary: Enum returned by extension handlers: error, unknown extension or ok.

nodes.name: setup.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the repository setup code: discovery results, gitfile error codes, repository_format and its extensions, git init helpers, shared-repository permission constants and startup_info. Most commands call setup_git_directory from here at startup.
nodes.languageNotes: The READ_GITFILE_ERR_* values are plain macros, and read_gitfile/resolve_gitdir are macro wrappers passing NULL for the error pointer.

nodes.name: discovery_result
nodes.summary: Enum describing the outcome of repository discovery: explicit, discovered or bare on success, and several negative error reasons (ceiling, mount point, ownership, bare disallowed).

nodes.name: repository_format
nodes.summary: Describes the on-disk repository format: version, hash algorithms, ref storage format and payload, extension flags, work tree and lists of unknown and v1-only extensions.

nodes.name: apply_repository_format_flags
nodes.summary: Flags for applying a repository format; HONOR_ENV makes object-database related environment variables count.

nodes.name: sharedrepo
nodes.summary: Enum of core.sharedRepository permission modes whose numeric values are preserved for old repositories.

nodes.name: startup_info
nodes.summary: Process-wide startup state: forced bare mode, whether a repository was found and the original working directory.

nodes.name: discover_git_directory
nodes.summary: Inline wrapper over discover_git_directory_reason that returns 0 on success and -1 if no repository is found.

nodes.name: shell.c
nodes.summary: Implementation of git-shell, the restricted login shell that only allows git-receive-pack, git-upload-pack and git-upload-archive, plus user scripts from ~/git-shell-commands in interactive mode. cmd_main validates the -c command and dispatches it.
nodes.languageNotes: Accepts "git foo" as "git-foo" and rejects any command name containing . or / to avoid path traversal.

nodes.name: do_generic_cmd
nodes.summary: Runs the allowed git-* server command (receive-pack, upload-pack, upload-archive) after dequoting the single argument and rejecting options.

nodes.name: is_valid_cmd_name
nodes.summary: Checks that a command name has no dot or slash so it cannot escape git-shell-commands.

nodes.name: make_cmd
nodes.summary: Builds the path git-shell-commands/<prog> for a user command.

nodes.name: cd_to_homedir
nodes.summary: Changes the working directory to $HOME, dying if it is unset or cannot be entered.

nodes.name: run_shell
nodes.summary: Runs the interactive git-shell loop: honors the no-interactive-login script, prints help, reads bounded command lines, parses them and executes valid commands from git-shell-commands.

nodes.name: cmd_main
nodes.summary: Entry point of git-shell: starts the interactive shell without arguments, or with -c dispatches an allowed git command or a user command from git-shell-commands.

nodes.name: commands
nodes.summary: Table entry type pairing an allowed git command name with its executor, used for the cmd_list whitelist.

nodes.name: strvec.h
nodes.summary: Declares the strvec API for building NULL-terminated string arrays suitable for argv, where the array owns duplicated copies of its strings. It is used throughout Git to assemble child-process arguments and environments.
nodes.languageNotes: The empty array points at the shared empty_strvec sentinel so v is never NULL.

nodes.name: strvec
nodes.summary: Dynamic NULL-terminated array of owned strings with element count and allocation size, directly usable as argv.

nodes.name: tempfile.c
nodes.summary: Implements the tempfile API: temporary files and directories that are tracked in a global signal-safe list and removed on exit or on a fatal signal by the process that created them. Callers can close, reopen, rename into place or delete them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a volatile linked list and async-signal-safe unlink/rmdir in the signal handler; the owner pid prevents a forked child from deleting the parent files.

nodes.name: remove_template_directory
nodes.summary: Removes the temporary directory created for a tempfile, using the signal-safe rmdir in a handler and the warning variant otherwise.

nodes.name: remove_tempfiles
nodes.summary: Walks the global tempfile list and closes and unlinks every active file owned by this process, with a variant safe for signal handlers.

nodes.name: remove_tempfiles_on_exit
nodes.summary: atexit handler that removes all active tempfiles.

nodes.name: remove_tempfiles_on_signal
nodes.summary: Signal handler that removes tempfiles, restores the previous handler and re-raises the signal.

nodes.name: new_tempfile
nodes.summary: Allocates a tempfile object in its initial inactive state.

nodes.name: activate_tempfile
nodes.summary: Registers cleanup handlers once, adds the tempfile to the global list and records the owner pid.

nodes.name: deactivate_tempfile
nodes.summary: Removes a tempfile from the global list and frees it.

nodes.name: repo_create_tempfile_mode
nodes.summary: Creates a new tempfile at an absolute path with O_EXCL and the given mode, then fixes permissions for shared repositories.

nodes.name: register_tempfile
nodes.summary: Registers an existing path as a tempfile so it is removed on exit.

nodes.name: mks_tempfile_sm
nodes.summary: Creates a tempfile from a mkstemp-style template with suffix length and mode.

nodes.name: mks_tempfile_tsm
nodes.summary: Creates a tempfile from a template inside $TMPDIR (default /tmp).

nodes.name: mks_tempfile_dt
nodes.summary: Creates a private temporary directory from a template and a named file inside it, both removed on cleanup.

nodes.name: xmks_tempfile_m
nodes.summary: Creates a tempfile with a mode and dies if it cannot.

nodes.name: fdopen_tempfile
nodes.summary: Opens a FILE stream on the tempfile descriptor.

nodes.name: get_tempfile_path
nodes.summary: Returns the filename of an active tempfile.

nodes.name: get_tempfile_fd
nodes.summary: Returns the file descriptor of an active tempfile.

nodes.name: get_tempfile_fp
nodes.summary: Returns the FILE pointer of an active tempfile.

nodes.name: close_tempfile_gently
nodes.summary: Closes the descriptor or stream of a tempfile, reporting write errors, and keeps the file on disk.

nodes.name: reopen_tempfile
nodes.summary: Reopens a closed tempfile for writing with truncation.

nodes.name: rename_tempfile
nodes.summary: Closes the tempfile and renames it to its final path, deleting it on failure; the basis of atomic file replacement.

nodes.name: delete_tempfile
nodes.summary: Closes and unlinks a tempfile, removes its directory and frees the object.

nodes.name: reassign_tempfile_ownership
nodes.summary: Changes the owner pid of tempfiles from one process to another, used when daemonizing.

nodes.name: tempfile.h
nodes.summary: Public header of the tempfile API with the struct tempfile definition and the documented lifecycle (create, write, close, rename or delete) used for lock-free atomic writes and cleanup on exit.

nodes.name: tempfile
nodes.summary: Tracks a temporary file: a volatile list node, descriptor, stream, owner pid, filename and optional directory.

nodes.name: tmp-objdir.c
nodes.summary: Implements temporary (quarantine) object directories: a tmp_objdir_* directory inside the object store that receives incoming objects, is advertised to child processes via environment variables, and is either migrated into the main object database or discarded. Used by receive-pack for quarantining pushes.
nodes.languageNotes: Allows only one tmp_objdir per process and removes it with atexit; migration copies packs in keep, pack, rev, idx order.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir
nodes.summary: State of a temporary object directory: repository, path, child environment variables, previous primary source and will_destroy flag.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_free
nodes.summary: Frees the path, environment and struct of a tmp_objdir without touching the filesystem.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_reparent
nodes.summary: chdir-notify callback that rewrites a relative tmp_objdir path after the process changes directory.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_destroy
nodes.summary: Restores the previous primary object source, recursively removes the temporary directory and unregisters callbacks.

nodes.name: remove_tmp_objdir
nodes.summary: atexit handler that destroys the process-wide tmp_objdir.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_discard_objects
nodes.summary: Deletes everything inside the temporary object directory but keeps the directory itself.

nodes.name: env_append
nodes.summary: Appends a value to an environment variable list separated by PATH_SEP, quoting only when needed, for GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES.

nodes.name: env_replace
nodes.summary: Adds a KEY=value string that overrides an environment variable in the child environment.

nodes.name: setup_tmp_objdir
nodes.summary: Creates the pack subdirectory in the new temporary object directory.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_create
nodes.summary: Creates a unique tmp_objdir-<prefix> directory in the object store, installs cleanup, and prepares GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, alternates and quarantine variables for child processes.

nodes.name: pack_copy_priority
nodes.summary: Ranks file names so packfile pieces are copied in the safe order: keep, pack, rev, then idx.

nodes.name: pack_copy_cmp
nodes.summary: Comparator ordering names by pack_copy_priority.

nodes.name: read_dir_paths
nodes.summary: Reads the non-dot entries of a directory into a string list.

nodes.name: migrate_one
nodes.summary: Moves one entry into the main object store, recursing into directories and finalizing files with collision handling.

nodes.name: is_loose_object_shard
nodes.summary: Returns whether a name is a two-hex-digit loose object fan-out directory.

nodes.name: migrate_paths
nodes.summary: Sorts directory entries in pack-safe order and migrates each, skipping collision checks for loose object shards.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_migrate
nodes.summary: Moves all objects from the temporary directory into the main object database and then destroys the directory.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_env
nodes.summary: Returns the environment strings to pass to child processes so they use the temporary object directory.

nodes.name: tmp_objdir_replace_primary_odb
nodes.summary: Makes the temporary directory the primary writable object source of the current process and keeps the old one as an alternate.

nodes.name: tmp-objdir.h
nodes.summary: Public API of temporary object directories: create, get the child environment, migrate into the main object database, destroy, discard objects, or swap in as the process primary object source. The header comment shows the typical child-process usage.

nodes.name: trace.c
nodes.summary: Implements the GIT_TRACE family: trace keys selecting stderr, a descriptor or an absolute file path via environment variables, timestamped trace lines, argv tracing, performance timers with nested indentation, and the setup trace that prints gitdir, worktree and prefix.
nodes.languageNotes: Chooses clock_gettime, QueryPerformanceCounter or gettimeofday at compile time and keeps a fixed-size stack of start times for nested performance traces.

nodes.name: get_trace_fd
nodes.summary: Lazily resolves a trace key from its environment variable into a file descriptor: disabled, stderr, a numeric fd or an absolute path opened for append.

nodes.name: trace_override_envvar
nodes.summary: Reinitializes a trace key from an explicit value instead of the environment variable.

nodes.name: trace_disable
nodes.summary: Disables a trace key, closing its file if it opened one.

nodes.name: prepare_trace_line
nodes.summary: Starts a trace line with timestamp, file and line number aligned to a column, unless the key is off or bare mode is requested.

nodes.name: trace_write
nodes.summary: Writes a buffer to the trace fd, disabling the key with a warning on error.

nodes.name: trace_verbatim
nodes.summary: Writes raw bytes to a trace key with no formatting if tracing is on.

nodes.name: print_trace_line
nodes.summary: Terminates the buffer with a newline and writes it to the trace fd.

nodes.name: trace_vprintf_fl
nodes.summary: Formats a va_list message into a prepared trace line and prints it.

nodes.name: trace_argv_vprintf_fl
nodes.summary: Prints a trace line with a message plus a shell-quoted argv to the default trace key.

nodes.name: trace_strbuf_fl
nodes.summary: Prints the contents of a strbuf as a trace line.

nodes.name: trace_performance_enter
nodes.summary: Pushes a start timestamp for nested performance tracing and returns it.

nodes.name: trace_performance_vprintf_fl
nodes.summary: Prints a performance line with elapsed seconds and an indented message.

nodes.name: trace_printf_key_fl
nodes.summary: Variadic wrapper that prints a formatted trace line for a given key.

nodes.name: trace_argv_printf_fl
nodes.summary: Variadic wrapper that traces a message followed by argv.

nodes.name: trace_performance_fl
nodes.summary: Variadic wrapper that prints a performance trace for a given duration.

nodes.name: trace_performance_leave_fl
nodes.summary: Pops the performance stack and prints elapsed time since the matching enter.

nodes.name: quote_crnl
nodes.summary: Escapes backslashes, newlines and carriage returns in a path for single-line trace output.

nodes.name: trace_repo_setup
nodes.summary: Traces the discovered git_dir, common dir, worktree, cwd and prefix when GIT_TRACE_SETUP is on.

nodes.name: trace_want
nodes.summary: Returns whether a trace key is enabled.

nodes.name: highres_nanos
nodes.summary: Returns a monotonic nanosecond reading from clock_gettime.

nodes.name: gettimeofday_nanos
