nodes.name: run-command.c
nodes.summary: Child process and async execution layer: start_command and finish_command fork/exec subprocesses with pipe redirection, signal-safe cleanup and trace2 events, with async threads, pipe_command I/O pumping, run_processes_parallel, auto-maintenance and background daemon startup.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains separate pthread and fork based implementations of async selected by NO_PTHREADS, plus Windows-specific branches under GIT_WINDOWS_NATIVE.

nodes.name: child_process_init
nodes.summary: Zero-initializes a child_process and its args and env string vectors.

nodes.name: child_process_clear
nodes.summary: Releases the args and env vectors of a child_process so it can be reused.

nodes.name: cleanup_children
nodes.summary: Walks the list of registered children, runs clean_on_exit handlers, kills them with a signal and waits for them (not waiting when called from a signal handler).

nodes.name: mark_child_for_cleanup
nodes.summary: Registers a spawned child on the cleanup list and installs the atexit and signal-chain handlers once.

nodes.name: clear_child_for_cleanup
nodes.summary: Removes a finished child from the cleanup list by pid.

nodes.name: is_executable
nodes.summary: Checks that a path is a regular, executable file (on Windows by extension and shebang inspection).

nodes.name: exists_in_PATH
nodes.summary: Returns whether a command can be found in PATH.

nodes.name: sane_execvp
nodes.summary: Wraps execvp with trace2 exec events and normalizes the errno (EACCES to ENOENT) when the command is not found.

nodes.name: wait_or_whine
nodes.summary: Waits for a child pid with waitpid and converts exit status or signal into an exit code, reporting errors and 127 for exec failures.

nodes.name: trace_add_env
nodes.summary: Formats the environment changes of a command (unset and VAR=value) into a trace string.

nodes.name: trace_run_command
nodes.summary: Writes a "trace: run_command:" line with directory, env and quoted argv when tracing is on.

nodes.name: start_command
nodes.summary: Spawns a child process: sets up stdin/stdout/stderr pipes, forks (or uses the Windows spawn path), execs the prepared command in the child, handles setup errors through a notifier pipe, and registers cleanup.

nodes.name: finish_command
nodes.summary: Waits for a started child to exit, records the trace2 exit, clears the process struct and returns its exit code.

nodes.name: finish_command_in_signal
nodes.summary: Variant of finish_command safe for signal handlers: waits for the child without printing messages.

nodes.name: run_command
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that starts a command and waits for it, refusing configurations that could deadlock on pipes.

nodes.name: check_pipe
nodes.summary: Handles EPIPE by exiting quietly (thread-aware) or re-raising SIGPIPE with the default action.

nodes.name: start_async
nodes.summary: Runs a function asynchronously with piped input and output, using a thread (or fork when threads are unavailable).

nodes.name: finish_async
nodes.summary: Joins an async thread (or waits for its forked child) and returns the function's result.

nodes.name: async_with_fork
nodes.summary: Returns whether async tasks are implemented with fork rather than threads.

nodes.name: pump_io_round
nodes.summary: Runs one poll round over the pipes in an io_pump array, reading or writing buffers for each ready descriptor and closing finished ones.

nodes.name: pump_io
nodes.summary: Repeats poll rounds until all input and output buffers are fully transferred and reports the first error.

nodes.name: pipe_command
nodes.summary: Runs a child with optional in-memory stdin, stdout and stderr buffers, pumping all pipes without deadlock and waiting for the child.

nodes.name: pp_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the parallel process pool: validates options, allocates child slots and pollfds, installs signal cleanup handlers.

nodes.name: pp_cleanup
nodes.summary: Releases child slots, flushes buffered output and restores signal handlers at the end of a parallel run.

nodes.name: pp_start_one
nodes.summary: Takes a free slot, asks get_next_task for a new command, and starts it (reporting failures through start_failure).

nodes.name: pp_buffer_stdin
nodes.summary: Feeds queued data to child stdin pipes through the feed_pipe callback in ungroup mode.

nodes.name: pp_buffer_io
nodes.summary: Polls the stderr pipes of running children and appends their output to per-child buffers for grouped output.

nodes.name: pp_output
nodes.summary: Flushes the buffered stderr of the child that currently owns the output to the real stderr.

nodes.name: pp_collect_finished
nodes.summary: Reaps children waiting for cleanup, calls the task_finished callback, frees slots and picks the next output owner.

nodes.name: pp_handle_child_IO
nodes.summary: Dispatches child I/O handling for grouped or ungrouped mode of the pool.

nodes.name: run_processes_parallel
nodes.summary: Runs many child processes concurrently with a bounded pool: starts tasks, pumps their I/O, groups output and collects results until all tasks are done.

nodes.name: prepare_auto_maintenance
nodes.summary: Fills a child_process for "git maintenance run --auto" if maintenance.auto or gc.auto enable it, setting quiet and detach flags.

nodes.name: run_auto_maintenance
nodes.summary: Prepares and runs automatic repository maintenance as a subprocess if enabled.

nodes.name: sanitize_repo_env
nodes.summary: Adds env entries that unset all repository-local environment variables (like GIT_DIR) except config injection variables.

nodes.name: prepare_other_repo_env
nodes.summary: Prepares a child environment to operate on another repository by sanitizing and setting GIT_DIR.

nodes.name: start_bg_command
nodes.summary: Starts a background command (e.g. a daemon), then polls with a callback and timeout until it is ready, failed or timed out.

nodes.name: locate_in_PATH
nodes.summary: Searches each PATH entry for an executable file and returns the first full path.

nodes.name: git_shell_path
nodes.summary: Returns the path of the shell (SHELL_PATH, or sh found in PATH on Windows).

nodes.name: prepare_shell_cmd
nodes.summary: Turns a command into a shell invocation (sh -c ...) when it contains shell metacharacters, otherwise leaves it as a plain argv.

nodes.name: child_die
nodes.summary: Reports a child setup error (error code plus errno) over a notifier pipe to the parent and exits with _exit.

nodes.name: child_err_spew
nodes.summary: Prints the parent-side error message for a failure that the forked child reported through the notifier pipe (chdir, dup2, exec, etc.).

nodes.name: prepare_cmd
nodes.summary: Builds the final argv of a child: the shell fallback, git subcommand prefix or shell command, and a PATH-resolved command name.

nodes.name: prep_childenv
nodes.summary: Builds the environment array of a child by merging the current environ with the delta (add or unset) entries in sorted order.

nodes.name: atfork_prepare
nodes.summary: Blocks all signals and disables thread cancellation before fork so the child starts in a clean state.

nodes.name: atfork_parent
nodes.summary: Restores the signal mask and thread cancellation state in the parent after fork.

nodes.name: run_thread
nodes.summary: Thread entry for async tasks: blocks SIGPIPE if requested, records the async in thread-local storage and runs the user function.

nodes.name: die_async
nodes.summary: die routine for async threads that exits only the thread, printing the die message first.

nodes.name: in_async
nodes.summary: Returns whether the current thread is an async worker thread rather than the main thread.

nodes.name: git_atexit
nodes.summary: Registers an atexit-style handler in git's own handler list and installs a dispatcher once.

nodes.name: child_to_clean
nodes.summary: Node of the linked list of live children that must be killed and reaped on exit or signal.

nodes.name: io_pump
nodes.summary: One pipe endpoint for pump_io: descriptor, direction, buffer and position, error state.

nodes.name: parallel_child
nodes.summary: One slot of the parallel process pool with its child_process, stderr buffer and state.

nodes.name: parallel_processes
nodes.summary: Whole state of a run_processes_parallel call: child slots, pollfds, counters and buffered output.

nodes.name: parallel_processes_for_signal
nodes.summary: Minimal pool view that the signal handler uses to kill and reap children.

nodes.name: run-command.h
nodes.summary: Declares struct child_process (command, stdio redirection, env, cleanup flags), struct async, the parallel process runner options, and the functions to start, wait for and run subprocesses.

nodes.name: child_process
nodes.summary: Describes a subprocess to run: args and env, stdin/stdout/stderr redirection, git_cmd and shell flags, working directory, cleanup and trace2 settings.

nodes.name: async
nodes.summary: Describes a function to run asynchronously (thread or fork) with input and output pipes.

nodes.name: run_process_parallel_opts
nodes.summary: Options of run_processes_parallel: process count, task, failure, feed and finished callbacks, trace2 labels, ungroup mode.

nodes.name: start_bg_result
nodes.summary: Enum of outcomes of start_bg_command (ready, error, timeout, died, cb_error).

layers.name: Commands and CLI (builtin/)
layers.description: The git.c dispatcher, the builtin/ implementation of each porcelain and plumbing command, and command-line support such as option parsing, help, aliases, pager, color and progress.

layers.name: Configuration and Repository Setup
layers.description: Config parsing and lookup, repository discovery and initialization, environment, git-dir paths, hooks, tracing and gettext, which every command bootstraps from.

layers.name: Object Database
layers.description: Git object model (blob, tree, commit, tag), object IDs and hashing, loose object storage and the odb/ source abstraction that reads and writes objects, plus fsck, notes and replace objects.

layers.name: Packfiles, Bitmaps and Repack
layers.description: Packfile and pack index reading and writing, delta compression, multi-pack-index, reachability bitmaps, cruft packs and the repack and prune machinery that keeps storage compact.

layers.name: Refs and Reftable
layers.description: Reference storage and transactions (files, packed and reftable backends, the reftable/ library), reflogs, ref filtering and branch bookkeeping.

layers.name: Index and Working Tree
layers.description: The staging area (read-cache, cache-tree, sparse and split index), tree unpacking, checkout, ignore and pathspec handling, attributes and conversion, fsmonitor, linked worktrees and submodules.

layers.name: Revision Walk, History and Output
layers.description: Commit graph traversal (revision, reachability, commit-graph, bloom filters, shallow), bisect, blame, log formatting, tree-to-archive output and grep.

layers.name: Diff, Merge and History Rewriting
layers.description: The diff engine and diffcore, xdiff algorithms, apply and combine-diff, merge-ort and three-way merge, rerere, rebase, the sequencer and replay.

layers.name: Transport, Protocols and Remotes
layers.description: Fetch, push and clone plumbing: remote and refspec handling, pkt-line wire protocol v0 to v2, upload-pack and send-pack, smart and dumb HTTP, bundles, credentials and partial clone filters.

layers.name: Low-level Utilities
layers.description: Foundation code with no Git semantics: strbuf, string-list, hashmap, wrapper and I/O helpers, subprocess and lockfile handling, quoting, UTF-8, wildmatch and portability headers.

tour.title: Where Every Command Starts
tour.description: Every git program begins in common-main.c, which holds the real main(), runs init_git, calls the program-specific cmd_main and exits through the exit wrapper. For the git binary, cmd_main lives in git.c: it parses global options, expands aliases (alias.c), then looks the command up in the builtin command table together with its setup flags such as RUN_SETUP and NEED_WORK_TREE. builtin.h lists the cmd_* entry point of every built-in command, and parse-options.c is the shared parser each of those commands uses for its own options. If no builtin matches, git.c falls back to an external git-<cmd> program.
tour.languageLesson: C programs have one main() per executable. Git keeps it in common-main.c and lets each program supply only cmd_main, so initialization is written once for all of them.

tour.title: Finding the Repository
tour.description: Before most commands do any work, setup.c discovers the git directory and work tree from the current directory, GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE, checks the repository format and extensions, and enforces ownership rules such as safe.directory. setup.h exposes setup_git_directory, which most commands call at startup, and builtin/init-db.c shows the other direction: git init resolves directories, template, object format and ref format and then creates the layout. The result of all this is struct repository, defined in repository.h and managed by repository.c, which ties the object database, refs, config and index together.

tour.title: Configuration and Environment
tour.description: Once the repository is known, config.c supplies the configuration subsystem: a parser for config files and -c parameters, include handling, typed value accessors and an in-memory config set per repository. config.h is the public API you will see in nearly every command, with repo_config_get_* lookups and git_config callbacks. environment.c then holds the global and per-repository settings derived from core.*, pack.*, push.* and similar variables, and its git_default_config is the common callback most commands chain to.

tour.title: Utility Foundations
tour.description: Almost everything above sits on a small base of utilities with no Git semantics. git-compat-util.h is the portability and safety header included first by nearly every file, with die/error helpers, overflow-checked arithmetic and the BUG() macro. strbuf.c provides the growable string buffer used for nearly all string building, wrapper.c wraps libc calls so allocation and I/O failures die with a message, and hashmap.c is the generic hash table. lockfile.c adds the path.lock mechanism that later steps rely on for atomic updates of refs, the index and config.
tour.languageLesson: Because C has no built-in growable strings or checked allocation, Git wraps them (strbuf, xmalloc and friends) so that callers rarely handle allocation failure or buffer sizes by hand.

tour.title: The Object Model
tour.description: Git stores four kinds of objects, and object.h defines the shared model: enum object_type, struct object, and the per-repository table of parsed objects that object.c maintains. Objects are named by hashes, so hash.h and hash.c abstract the SHA-1 and SHA-256 algorithms behind struct object_id. commit.c and tree.c then show two concrete types: parsing commit objects (including from the commit-graph) and creating new ones, and parsing and reading tree objects recursively.

tour.title: The Object Database Layer
tour.description: odb.h and odb.c implement the object database of a repository. It owns a list of object sources (the primary objects directory, alternates and an in-memory source) and dispatches reads, existence checks, enumeration and writes to them. odb/source.h defines the abstract source as a table of backend callbacks, and odb/source-files.c is the default backend that pairs a loose-object source with a packed source. This split explains why the same read call works whether an object sits in its own file or inside a pack.
tour.languageLesson: A struct of function pointers, as in odb_source and later in the ref backends, is the C idiom for a vtable: callers go through the table and never need to know which backend is behind it.

tour.title: Loose Objects
tour.description: The simplest storage form is the loose object, one zlib-compressed file per object. object-file.c formats object headers, hashes content, builds loose paths, reads and unpacks loose objects and moves written objects into place with collision checks, while odb/source-loose.c is the backend that reads, enumerates and writes them. To see this from the command line, builtin/hash-object.c computes an object id for file contents and can write the object, and builtin/cat-file.c prints an object's type, size or contents.

tour.title: Reading and Writing Packfiles
tour.description: Packfiles store many objects together and use deltas to stay compact. packfile.c opens and validates .idx and .pack files, maps pack windows with LRU eviction, decodes object headers and delta chains, and finds objects by binary search in the index. diff-delta.c creates binary deltas with a rolling hash and patch-delta.c applies them, pack-write.c writes the .idx index and pack headers, and builtin/index-pack.c reads an incoming pack and resolves its delta chains. Read these together to see how an object becomes a delta against a base and is rebuilt on demand.

tour.title: Building Packs and Speeding Lookups
tour.description: builtin/pack-objects.c decides what goes into a pack: it enumerates objects (by revision walk, bitmaps or stdin), picks delta bases with a sliding window across threads and writes the pack and index. builtin/repack.c drives it to consolidate existing packs and then removes redundant ones. The structures around them make large repositories fast: midx.c reads the multi-pack-index, pack-bitmap.c reads reachability bitmaps that shortcut a revision walk, and pack-revindex.c maps between index position, pack position and offset.

tour.title: References
tour.description: Refs give names such as branches, tags and HEAD to object ids. refs.h is the public interface, and refs.c is the backend-independent part: it validates names, resolves symbolic refs, iterates refs and implements atomic transactions by dispatching to a backend vtable defined in refs/refs-internal.h. Three backends sit behind it: refs/files-backend.c stores one file per loose ref over a packed store, refs/packed-backend.c reads and rewrites the sorted packed-refs file, and refs/reftable-backend.c keeps refs and reflogs in stacked binary tables.

tour.title: The Index
tour.description: The index is the staging area, and read-cache.c is its core: it reads and writes .git/index, keeps the sorted array of cache entries, does stat-based change detection and refreshes entries against the working tree. read-cache-ll.h defines struct cache_entry and struct index_state, the structures you meet whenever code touches the index. cache-tree.c stores a tree of cached tree object ids so write-tree can skip unchanged directories. builtin/add.c and builtin/update-index.c are the porcelain and plumbing commands that stage files into it.

tour.title: Making a Commit
tour.description: Here the earlier pieces meet. builtin/commit.c chooses which index to commit, runs the pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg and commit-msg hooks, builds the message, writes the commit object with commit_tree_extended (from commit.c) and moves HEAD with a reflog entry. wt-status.c collects the staged, unstaged and untracked paths that both git status and the commit message template show. builtin/write-tree.c and builtin/commit-tree.c are the plumbing versions of the same two steps, writing the index out as trees and creating a commit from a tree and parents.

tour.title: Checkout and the Working Tree
tour.description: Going the other way, from objects back to files, is the job of unpack-trees.c: unpack_trees() walks several trees in parallel with the index, applies a merge function per path, checks the work tree can be changed safely and then updates it. tree-walk.c provides the low-level tree iteration it depends on, and entry.c writes index entries out as files, symlinks and submodules. builtin/checkout.c implements git checkout, switch and restore on top of this, and dir.c handles the untracked and ignore-pattern side of walking the work tree.

tour.title: Walking History
tour.description: revision.c is the revision walking machinery behind log, rev-list and many other commands: it parses revision arguments into struct rev_info, limits and orders commits and returns them one at a time through get_revision (see revision.h for the calling sequence). commit-graph.c adds an on-disk cache of parents, dates and generation numbers that speeds the walk, and list-objects.c extends the traversal from commits to the trees and blobs they reach. builtin/rev-list.c is the plumbing front end, and builtin/log.c shows the same walk feeding the log output pipeline.

tour.title: The Diff Engine
tour.description: diff.c holds the diff options, the queue of file pairs and every output format, and drives the diffcore pipeline through diffcore_std and diff_flush. diffcore-rename.c adds rename and copy detection, xdiff/xdiffi.c is the line-level engine implementing the Myers algorithm (with patience and histogram variants), and diff-lib.c compares the index against the working tree or a tree. builtin/diff.c ties them together, classifying its arguments and choosing which comparison to run.

tour.title: Merging and Rewriting History
tour.description: Merging builds on the tree and diff machinery. merge-ort.c is the default merge strategy: it walks three trees at once, detects renames, merges contents, records conflicts and writes the result tree. builtin/merge.c is the command that resolves the commits, handles fast-forward and up-to-date cases, tries strategies and writes the merge commit. sequencer.c powers cherry-pick, revert and interactive rebase through a todo script, and builtin/rebase.c offers the merge backend built on it and the older apply backend.

tour.title: Remotes and the Wire Protocol
tour.description: To talk to another repository, remote.c reads remote and branch configuration and matches refs against refspecs, which refspec.c parses and applies. transport.c chooses a transport for a URL and implements the smart transport over fetch-pack and send-pack. Underneath it, pkt-line.c is the framing used by every git transport, connect.c opens git, ssh and local connections and parses ref advertisements, and protocol.c selects the protocol version.

tour.title: Fetch, Push and the Server Side
tour.description: The last step follows data moving between repositories. builtin/fetch.c builds the ref map, downloads objects through a transport and updates remote-tracking refs. On the other end, upload-pack.c negotiates wants and haves and streams a pack from pack-objects, while fetch-pack.c is the client that receives it. Pushing is the mirror image: builtin/push.c sets up the transport, send-pack.c streams a pack and ref update commands, and builtin/receive-pack.c unpacks, runs hooks and applies the ref updates. Every piece here reuses the object, pack, ref and revision code from the earlier steps.
